APSH-125.cause: It was detected that the Process was DISABLED at the start of this production program. A choice (or setup selection) has indicated that the Process should be FORCED to the enabled state.
APSH-125.remedy: - Don't choose to FORCE the process enable. - Change Prog Select-Production Check Process ready setup to NOT Force Condition. - Ensure that Process Enabled input is on at the start of the next production cycle.

APSH-127.cause: The joint velocity limit has changed. This parameter change requires you to cycle controller power in order to take effect.
APSH-127.remedy: Turn off the controller, then turn it on again.

APSH-128.cause: Tryout mode state has CHANGED from disabled to enabled. This is only a status message, it is not a fault. Note: tryout mode is a test function - part thickness value is ignored, when tryout mode is enabled.

APSH-129.cause: Tryout mode state has CHANGED from enabled to disabled. This is only a status message, it is not a fault. Note: tryout mode is a test function - part thickness value is ignored, when tryout mode is enabled.

APSH-130.cause: Error occurred while accessing the FR: device. No.dt files found.
APSH-130.remedy: .DT files must exist on the FR: device.

APSH-131.cause: I/O port defined wrong: Illegal type, Default data is used.
APSH-131.remedy: .DT file on the FR: device must be corrected.

APSH-132.cause: The program name that the shell was requested to run is not loaded on the controller.
APSH-132.remedy: Check PLC->Robot style communication. Verify that specified Program name was requested by PLC. Load or create the specified Program program.

APSH-133.cause: The robot has been jogged away from the position where the teach pendant was enabled.
APSH-133.remedy: Move the robot back to the position where the teach pendant was enabled, abort the program, or continue (in linear motion) from position where the robot is currently positioned.

APSH-141.cause: The robot has been jogged away from the position where the teach pendant was enabled.
APSH-141.remedy: Move the robot back to the position where the teach pendant was enabled, abort the program, or continue (in linear motion) from position where the robot is currently positioned.

APSH-142.message: WARNING - System is in dry run
APSH-142.cause: This is a warning to notify you that a production job is running with the process disabled.

APSH-143.cause: Robot motion and/or program execution cannot occur unless UOP input 8 is ON.
APSH-143.remedy: Check UOP I/O setup. UOP input 8 must be ON.

APSH-144.message: WARNING - Process Complete manually turned on at end of %s
APSH-144.cause: A 'Force Process Complete' was performed from the Soft Panel
APSH-144.remedy: This is just a warning to let the operator know that Process Complete was manually turned on.

APSH-150.cause: A production job is running with the gun set to NOSTROKE.

APSH-151.cause: A production job is running with weld set to NOWELD.

APSH-152.cause: The robot must be in full automatic mode with the PLC before production operation can occur.
APSH-152.remedy: Go to the SOFT PANEL menu and set Robot mode=AUTO.

APSH-153.cause: The shift key must be pressed when accessing this teach pendant hardkey.

APSH-154.cause: Because the system is currently configured for one equipment with a single gun, there is no need to set the equiopment that that GUN and BACKUP hardkeys will operate on; they will always operate on the one gun.

APSH-155.cause: The HOME position has not been recorded yet. The HOME position is contained in Reference Position menu.
APSH-155.remedy: 1. Go to the SETUP menu. 2. Select Reference Position from the [TYPE] menu. 3. Jog the robot to the HOME position. 4. Record your reference position, and then verify that it is a valid home position.

APSH-156.message: Specify Home in Ref Pos Menu
APSH-156.cause: The HOME position has not been recorded yet. The HOME position is contained in Reference Position menu.
APSH-156.remedy: Go to the SETUP menu, select Reference Position from the [TYPE] menu. Jog the robot to the HOME position. Record your reference position, then specify it is a valid HOME position.

APSH-157.cause: The teach pendant must be enabled when accessing this teach pendant hardkey.

APSH-158.message: No group output for weld sched
APSH-158.cause: The group output that contains the weld schedule has not been configured yet.
APSH-158.remedy: Go to the Weld Intface Output menu, and edit the index of the Weld Schedule I/O point. Make sure the group output has been properly configured from the Group Output menu. You must cold start the controller when changing this index, or redefining the group output.

APSH-159.cause: The servos are not ready, so operation requested cannot be performed.
APSH-159.remedy: When resetting a fault, wait for the servos to click on before attempting to execute a program.

APSH-160.cause: The robot is not at the POUNCE position, so the operation requested cannot be performed.
APSH-160.remedy: Re-issue this request when the robot is AT POUNCE.

APSH-161.cause: The robot is not currently running a production style, so the operation requested cannot be performed.
APSH-161.remedy: Re-issue the request when the robot is running a production style.

APSH-162.cause: The group output that contains the setting for the multi-pressure valving has not been configured yet.
APSH-162.remedy: Go to the Spot Equipment Intface Output menu, and edit the index of the Valve pressure I/O point. Make sure the group output has been properly configured from the Group Output menu. You must cold start the controller when changing this index, or redefining the group output.

APSH-163.cause: No motion can occur because the gun is closed. This prevents the user from jogging or running a program while the gun is closed, and damaging parts and/or tooling.

APSH-164.cause: The HOME I/O program as specified from the Cell Setup menu does not exist and was not run.
APSH-164.remedy: Go to the Cell Setup menu and either check the name of the HOME I/O macro name menu item. Make sure the file specified exists on the controller. Either create a program by that name or change this menu item to a program that already exists on the controller.

APSH-165.cause: There I/O configuration for the proper studwelding gun has not been initialized.
APSH-165.remedy: Proceed to the Spot Equipment I/O setup screen and configure the digital inputs Gun Present = On/Off, Gun in Nest = On/Off for the 2 stud guns. Proper configuration if gun 1 is on the robot is for Gun 1 (Gun Present = ON, Gun in Nest = OFF and for Gun 2 (Gun Present = OFF, Gun in Nest = ON. Proper configuration if gun 2 is on the robot is for Gun 1 (Gun Present = OFF, Gun in Nest = ON and for Gun 2 (Gun Present = ON, Gun in Nest = OFF.

APSH-166.cause: The robot was aborted or interrupted during the studgun change sequence.
APSH-166.remedy: Manually change the stud guns and move the robot to the home position. Press cycle start to run production.

APSH-167.cause: The stud gun change program was interrupted.
APSH-167.remedy: To resume production the robot must be manually returned home and cycle start must be pressed to continue.

APSH-168.cause: The group output that contains the setting for the equalization pressure has not been configured yet.
APSH-168.remedy: Go to the Spot Equipment Intface Output menu, and edit the index of the Equal pressure I/O point. Make sure the group output has been properly configured from the Group Output menu. You must cold start the controller when changing this index, or redefining the group output.

APSH-169.cause: A macro program to dropoff or pickup studgun 1 or 2 has not been initialized.
APSH-169.remedy: Proceed to Spot Equipment Menu under MENUS-SETUP and initialize the studwelding macros which will only appear if STUD BACKUP is ENABLED at CONTROLLED START.

APSH-170.cause: The inputs on the studwelder nest do not appear to be set up correctly.
APSH-170.remedy: Verify on the Spot Equip I/O menu that the Head in Nest inputs are set up correctly.

APSH-171.cause: HOME_IO has not completed successfully, so new program cannot be run.
APSH-171.remedy: Check HOME_IO and see if it is looping on some I/O. Check HOME_IO and see if it has a motion group mask enabled. If so, disable the mask for all motion groups.

APSH-174.cause: An SCR overtemp signal has been received.

APSH-175.message: Req. Press. Not mapped for WC:%s
APSH-175.cause: The Request Pressure digital input is not mapped.
APSH-175.remedy: Map request pressure input on Weld Interface Menu.

APSH-176.message: GIN For Weld Press. Not mapped for WC:%s
APSH-176.cause: The GIN for Weld Pressure is not mapped.
APSH-176.remedy: Map Weld Pressure pressure input on Weld Interface Menu.

APSH-177.message: Read Press. Not mapped for WC:%s
APSH-177.cause: Read pressure input is not mapped on weld interface Menu.
APSH-177.remedy: Map read pressure input on Weld Interface Menu.

APSH-178.message: Map I/O in Weld Interface Menu
APSH-178.cause: There is not cause, this is a help code

APSH-179.cause: The weld controler did not set Read Pressure input in time.
APSH-179.remedy: Check if weld controler is functioning correctly, or increase Weld Pres time-out at CTRL start menu.

APSH-180.cause: Could not read any I/O from the Weld controller. Device may be offline.
APSH-180.remedy: Check if weld controler is functioning correctly, or powered on.

APSH-202.cause: Automatic Collision recovery was attempting to run the recovery program.
APSH-202.remedy: Make sure the program is loaded, and retry the operation.

APSH-203.cause: The task could not run or continue.
APSH-203.remedy: Check the associated error message for the task error and follow the recovery procedure.

APSH-204.cause: Automatic Collision recovery is about to run the recovery program.

APSH-205.cause: Automatic Collision recovery is about to run the original program.

APSH-206.cause: The group specified to get_home does not exist.
APSH-206.remedy: Verify the specified group number exists, and retry the operation.

APSH-207.cause: The reference position specified to get_home.
APSH-207.remedy: Verify the specified Reference position exists.

APSH-208.cause: This error is related to production setup check screen. This item should not be checked on the present configuration.
APSH-208.remedy: Press F6,REDO and cycle power to update items.

APSH-209.cause: This is a warning message to log that the user chose to disable fault checking for one cycle.

APSH-210.cause: This is a warning message to log that the user chose to disable fault checking for multiple cycles.

ARC-001.cause: An attempt was made to add or use more equipment than permitted.
ARC-001.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-002.cause: An arc instruction contained an illegal schedule number.
ARC-002.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-003.cause: No gas flow was detected during an arc start.
ARC-003.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-004.cause: The gas fault input was not ON after the gas output was set to OFF.
ARC-004.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-005.cause: A gas fault input was detected during welding.
ARC-005.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-006.cause: A wire fault input was detected during welding.
ARC-006.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-007.cause: A water fault input was detected during welding.
ARC-007.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-008.cause: A power fault input was detected during welding.
ARC-008.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-010.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-011.cause: A wirestick was detected and wirestick reset was not performed. Wirestick reset may be disabled. Wirestick reset is not done during TIG welding or if welding is stopped by turning weld enable off.
ARC-011.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-012.cause: A wirestick was detected and the automatic wirestick reset failed to break the wirestick.
ARC-012.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-013.cause: The arc detect input did not stabilize during an arc start.
ARC-013.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-014.cause: The weld enable or a wire inch hardkey was pressed with the teach pendant enable switch OFF.
ARC-014.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-015.cause: The weld enable or a wire inch hardkey was pressed without holding the shift key.
ARC-015.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-016.message: Weld by Shift FWD is disabled
ARC-016.cause: A program executing from the teach pendant attempted an Arc Start with welding from the teach pendant disabled.
ARC-016.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-017.cause: An Arc Start instruction was executed with welding disabled.
ARC-017.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-018.cause: The arc detect signal was lost during a weld.
ARC-018.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-019.cause: The arc detect input could not be read.
ARC-019.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-020.cause: Insufficient memory exists to plan an arc instruction.
ARC-020.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-021.cause: A program was aborted while welding.
ARC-021.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-022.cause: The programmed analog output is beyond the equipment limits.
ARC-022.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-023.cause: The arc instruction register is not an integer type.
ARC-023.remedy: Check if the weld controller is functioning correctly, or powered on.

ARC-024.cause: The equipment min to max range is too small.
ARC-024.remedy: Enter new min or max values for the equipment.

ARC-025.cause: The binary range data for the A/D or D/A is too small.
ARC-025.remedy: Modify the correct system variable fields within $AWEPRR.

ARC-026.cause: An analog scaling limit was modified while welding. The scaling was not changed.
ARC-026.remedy: Turn off the controller and turn it on again.

ARC-027.cause: Free space on Memory Device is insufficient, so cannot save the log file for Arc Weld Log function.
ARC-027.remedy: Arrange the contents of Memory Device and get enough free space on Memory device for Arc Weld Log function.

ARC-028.cause: Free space on Memory Device is insufficient, so auto deletion of log files is performed.
ARC-028.remedy: Arrange the contents of Memory Device and get enough free space on Memory device for Arc Weld Log function.

ARC-029.cause: The number of weld I/O is illegal; more than maxmum, less than minimum or uninitialized, so cannot weld.
ARC-029.remedy: Set up weld I/O again at controlled start.

ARC-030.cause: A wire stick is still detected after a system RESET.
ARC-030.remedy: Secure the robot and equipment. Cut the wire.

ARC-031.cause: Motion has stopped longer than $arc_los_tim while welding.
ARC-031.remedy: If no motion is needed during welding, increase the arc loss time in the Weld Equipment SETUP screen or disable arc loss detection in the Weld System SETUP screen.

ARC-032.cause: Welding was stopped by entering single step mode after welding began.
ARC-032.remedy: To continue welding you must exit single step mode.

ARC-033.cause: The speed override is less than 100%.
ARC-033.remedy: Set the speed override to 100% to weld or disable welding to continue at a low speed.

ARC-034.cause: A task which does not have weld control attempted to execute an Arc Start or an Arc End instruction. Only one task is permitted to have weld control.
ARC-034.remedy: Allow the task which has weld control to end or abort before attempting to weld with another task.

ARC-035.cause: The arc instruction does not have the equipment number
ARC-035.remedy: Please set the equipment number to the program attribute data or the arc instruction

ARC-036.cause: An attempt was made to add or use more equipment than permitted.
ARC-036.remedy: Please set the equipment number to the program attribute data or the arc instruction

ARC-037.cause: Another equipment is wire inching now.
ARC-037.remedy: Please stop wire inching for another equipment by releasing the shift key or user key

ARC-038.cause: This program(task) has already held the another equipment A task can only use a equipment.
ARC-038.remedy: Please control the equipment by the another task

ARC-039.cause: The named weld analog output signal is not scaled properly.
ARC-039.remedy: Adjust the weld analog output scaling in the Weld I/O screen using the CONFIG function key.

ARC-040.cause: The named weld I/O signal is not detected or configured properly.
ARC-040.remedy: Verify the I/O hardware is connected and the signal is assigned a port number in the Weld I/O screen. Use the CONFIG function key if the signal is unassigned.

ARC-041.cause: The weld equipment has been configured to use DeviceNet by setting the fields $VENDOR_ID, $DEV_TYPE, and $PROD_CODE in the system variable $AWEPRR to non-zero values. However, the DeviceNet option is not installed.
ARC-041.remedy: Add the DeviceNet option or choose a weld equipment model which does not require DeviceNet. If the weld equipment model is correct and does not require DeviceNet then set the $AWEPRR fields mentioned above to zero and cycle power.

ARC-042.message: Weld EQ needs Expl Msg option
ARC-042.cause: The weld equipment has been configured to use DeviceNet by setting the fields $VENDOR_ID, $DEV_TYPE, and $PROD_CODE in the system variable $AWEPRR to non-zero values. However, the Explicit Messaging option is not installed.
ARC-042.remedy: Add the Explicit Messaging option or choose a weld equipment model which does not require DeviceNet. If the weld equipment model is correct and does not require DeviceNet then set the $AWEPRR fields mentioned above to zero and cycle power.

ARC-043.cause: The weld equipment has been configured to use DeviceNet by setting the fields $VENDOR_ID, $DEV_TYPE, and $PROD_CODE in the system variable $AWEPRR to non-zero values. However, DeviceNet hardware was not detected.
ARC-043.remedy: Add DeviceNet hardware or choose a weld equipment model which does not require DeviceNet. If the weld equipment model is correct and does not require DeviceNet then set the $AWEPRR fields mentioned above to zero and cycle power.

ARC-044.cause: The weld equipment has been configured to use DeviceNet by setting the fields $VENDOR_ID, $DEV_TYPE, and $PROD_CODE in the system variable $AWEPRR to non-zero values. A DeviceNet device definition could not be found for that product.
ARC-044.remedy: You can add a DeviceNet definition for this product or if the weld equipment you are using does not support DeviceNet you can set the $AWEPRR fields mentioned above to zero and cycle power.

ARC-045.cause: ArcTool attempted to communicate with the Welding Equipment using the DeviceNet network, but could not because the link was not properly established.
ARC-045.remedy: Verify the Weld Equipment is ON. Verify the DeviceNet cable is connected. Check the DeviceNet I/O screen board status and device status.

ARC-046.cause: There was a communication error detected between ArcTool and the Weld Equipment.
ARC-046.remedy: Verify the Weld Equipment is ON. Verify the DeviceNet cable is connected. Check the DeviceNet I/O screen board status and device status.

ARC-047.cause: An operation was attempted which is not permitted while a weld is executing or paused.
ARC-047.remedy: Try the operation after the program ends or is aborted.

ARC-048.cause: Auto AI/O setup for the mounted I/O module is not supported. So parameters are not set automatically.
ARC-048.remedy: Verify mounted I/O module and set system variables of $AWEPRR[] in system variable screen manually if need.

ARC-049.cause: ArcTool failed to switch weld processes.
ARC-049.remedy: The weld power supply may be OFF, unconnected, or data in the second process may be incorrect.

ARC-050.cause: ArcTool failed to find this process on the weld power supply.
ARC-050.remedy: Enter a different number or use the SEARCH parameters and function key.

ARC-051.cause: ArcTool is communicating with the weld power supply. The version number of the power supply is shown.
ARC-051.remedy: This message is for notification and information. It does not indicate a problem.

ARC-052.cause: The indicated parameter is out of range.

ARC-053.cause: Ramping is not allowed when switching weld processes.
ARC-053.remedy: Complete the process switch first, then ramp with another arc start instruction.

ARC-054.cause: A weld was automatically shutdown because motion had stopped while welding longer than the time specified in $awsemgoff.$chk_time. This feature is intended to protect the welder from accidentally burning through a part.
ARC-054.remedy: You can increase the $awsemgoff.$chk_time to allow a longer welding time without motion. You can also disable this feature by setting $awsemgoff.$nofltr_off = FALSE. Both changes require you to turn off the controller then turn it on again.

ARC-055.cause: An Arc Start instruction specified synchronizing with an Equipment that is not also doing an Arc Start.
ARC-055.remedy: Determine why the sync Equipment is not starting, or do not use synchonization.

ARC-056.cause: An Arc Start instruction specified synchronizing with an Equipment that is not also synchronized.
ARC-056.remedy: Check the synchronization equipment number specified in the Arc instruction or in the specified weld schedule SYNCDT detail menu. Refer to the Arc Start Synchronization section in the ArcTool Setup and Operations Manual.

ARC-057.cause: The Arc process ramping cannot execute because the delay (t1) to communicate with the welder is larger than the ramping loop time (t2). This might occur with ramping or HeatWave $awwv_mode 2.

ARC-058.cause: A wire stick is still detected after a system RESET.
ARC-058.remedy: Secure the robot and equipment. Cut the wire.

ARC-060.cause: The voltage or current command do not exist, so Arc Welding Monitor cannot decide the WARN and STOP Limit range.
ARC-060.remedy: If you want to use Arc Welding Monitor without voltage and current command, please set ABS(V,A) to Monitoring Method and input the absolute values to WARN and STOP Limit ranges in Arc Welding Monitor screen. If you do not want to monitor feedback values, please set DISABLED to Arc Welding Monitor.

ARC-072.remedy: Sometimes this error requires cycling the controller power.

ARC-084.message: Application process is changed during welding

ARC-085.cause: Imcomplete the analog signal conversion factor.

ARC-086.message: Invalid of binary data in conversion factor
ARC-086.cause: The binary data($AWEPRR.$io_min/max_bin) is invalid. The difference is zero.

ARC-087.cause: The conversion factor data is invalid. It must be filled more than 2 tables at least. But the value of the second table is zero.
ARC-087.remedy: Please set conversion factor more than 2 tables

ARC-088.cause: The selected number of AO conversion factor data is over the number of the actual data array
ARC-088.remedy: Please select the correct number of AO conversion factor data

ARC-090.cause: In this situation, the welding is disalbled by the following reason 1: In Single step mode 2: In Machine lock mode 3: In Dry run mode 4: No I/O board exist 5: No I/O assignment for welding 6: In Flush AMR status 7: In Application disabled mode 8: In Arc disabled status 9: In Skip welding status 10: In disable status mode by AWDBG
ARC-090.remedy: Please remove the specified reason to perform the welding.

ARC-091.message: Arc End cannot ramp to position (%s^4,%d^5)
ARC-091.cause: An Arc End weld schedule specified a time of 99.0 seconds. This time value is sometimes used with Arc Starts to indicate ramping during an entire motion. This type of ramping is not available for an Arc End. A time of 99.0 seconds for an Arc End craterfill time is very long and is not recommended. If a long time is needed then 98.0 seconds will work without this error.
ARC-091.remedy: Use a different weld schedule for the Arc End or change the time value to a smaller value.

ARC-100.cause: The selected wire material is not supported for Servo Torch.
ARC-100.remedy: Please select the correct wire materal.

ARC-101.cause: The selected wire size is not supported for Servo Torch.
ARC-101.remedy: Please select the correct wire size.

ARC-102.cause: The selected unit of inching speed is not supported for Servo Torch.
ARC-102.remedy: Please select the correct unit of inching speed

ARC-103.cause: Failed to convert weld schedule to wire feed speed command for Servo Torch.
ARC-103.remedy: If another alarm is also occured at the same time, please check it and remove the cause of the alarm. If no other alarm is occured, some internal error is occured.

ARC-104.cause: Internal error. Invalid sequence mode command is sent to Servo Torch.
ARC-104.remedy: Internal error. Cycle power to recover.

ARC-105.cause: Cannot received WSTK signal from serial communication power supply.
ARC-105.remedy: Confirm which type of weld equip is used. Confirm the connection with serial communication power supply. Confirm the setting of serial port.

ARC-106.cause: Configuration of Roboweld was invalid. So data for Robowelds were set inappropriately.
ARC-106.remedy: Remove all Robowelds by selecting other equip in weld equip select screen. Then select and setup Roboweld again, if you want to use Roboweld.

ARC-108.cause: Wire touching before Touch Retract Start sequence starts.
ARC-108.remedy: Check the wire touches to the work at the arc start position.

ARC-109.cause: Feedback voltage fell down to displayed value over Arc Loss Error Time. Therefore, robot judges that arc is lost.
ARC-109.remedy: Remove the cause of lower voltage. If the weld has no problem, the voltage threshold for arc loss detect may be high. Then, set $AWEUPR.$ARC_LOSS_V to lower value.

ARC-110.cause: Feedback current fell down to displayed value over Arc Loss Error Time. Therefore, robot judges that arc is lost.
ARC-110.remedy: Remove the cause of lower current. If the weld has no problem, the voltage threshold for arc loss detect may be high. Then, set $AWEUPR.$ARC_LOSS_A to lower value.

ARC-111.cause: ServoTorch I/O assignment is invalid. This assignment is automatically executed after cycle power.
ARC-111.remedy: Please confirm the assignment of signals for arc welding.If you find a wrong assignment, please correct it. After that, please cycle power.

ARC-120.cause: The necessary signals for Simulation mode cannot be detected.
ARC-120.remedy: Verify that AI/O and WDI/O signals are assigned appropriately.

ARC-121.cause: Simulation mode is enabled. Actual welding is not performed.

ARC-122.cause: I/O signals were not set to sim/unsim appropriately when Simulation mode was enabled/disabled.
ARC-122.remedy: Verify that the AI/O and WDI/O signals are assigned appropriately.

ARC-123.cause: The memory size is too small to get the memory area for the necessary data.
ARC-123.remedy: Change the memory module into the one which has appropriate size, and perform an INIT start.

ARC-124.cause: The weld equipment has reported an error.
ARC-124.remedy: Refer to the weld equipment manual for more information.

ARC-125.message: Cannot start stitch in a weld
ARC-125.cause: An Arc Stitch instruction was executed while welding. Stitch welds begin with an Arc Stitch and end with an Arc End. Arc Stitch cannot execute between Arc Start and Arc End.
ARC-125.remedy: Edit the program so the Arc Stitch instruction is not between an Arc Start and Arc End.

ARC-126.message: Bad stitch weld or pitch length
ARC-126.cause: An Arc Stitch instruction could not execute because the stitch weld length or the pitch length were invalid or the stitch weld length was larger than the pitch length.
ARC-126.remedy: Modify the stitch weld length or pitch length. $aweupr[eq].$st_weld_len or $aweupr[eq].$st_ptch_len

ARC-127.cause: An Arc Stitch instruction could not execute because a stitch weld was already executing. Stitch welds cannot include weld schedule changes.
ARC-127.remedy: Edit the program so the Arc Stitch instruction does not follow an Arc Stitch.

ARC-128.cause: Joint motions are not permitted in a Stitch Weld.

ARC-130.cause: Term-type is changed to FINE automatically
ARC-130.remedy: Please choose FINE term-type when an arc end instruction is added.

ARC-131.cause: The weld procedure number entered in a Weld Start or a Weld End instruction is not found on the controller.
ARC-131.remedy: Enter the number of an existing weld procedure or create or load the missing weld procedure.

ARC-132.cause: The weld schedule number entered in a Weld Start or a Weld End instruction is not found on the controller.
ARC-132.remedy: Enter the number of an existing weld schedule or increase the number of weld schedules in the weld procedure.

ARC-133.cause: This error is reported after ARC-57 Cannot ramp t1 > t2. ARC-133 indicates the variable $aweramp[1].$time_factor was automatically increased to remedy a ramp timing problem. The weld can often be resumed immediately with this new setting.
ARC-133.remedy: Resume the program. If the ARC-57 error occurs without an ARC-133 error the $awscfg.$loop_time may need to be increased. This must be done during a controlled start.

ARC-134.cause: This error is related to Production Monitor operation.
ARC-134.remedy: Refer to the manual for details on the specific error reported.

ARC-135.cause: This error is related to Production Monitor macro operation.
ARC-135.remedy: Refer to the manual for details on the specific error reported.

ARC-136.cause: execute because the delay (t1) to communicate with the welder is larger than the pulsing loop time (t2). This may occur with Low-Frquency pulse welding.
ARC-136.remedy: Resume the program. If the ARC-136 error occurs without an ARC-133 error the $awscfg.$loop_time may need to be increased. This must be done during a controlled start.

ARC-137.cause: Low-Frequency Pulse Welding is clamped because pulse waveform exceeds the available range.
ARC-137.remedy: Adjust Pulse Frequency or Pulse Duty Cycle for Low-Frequency Pulse Welding again. Decrease Frequency value, or bring Duty Cycle close to 50%.

ARC-138.cause: Intenal error of ArcTool software. Normally this is not occurred.
ARC-138.remedy: Contact tech support for further investigation. Then, don't forget to inform the ID number in the error message.

ARC-139.cause: The specified Weld ID has already been used in the current TP program.
ARC-139.remedy: Enter other Weld ID which has not been used in this TP program.

ARC-140.cause: Setup parameter for MMC I/O assignment are wrong.

ARC-141.cause: The MCC was stuck but has been turned ON.

ARC-142.cause: MCC is OFF even though the MCC request is ON.
ARC-142.remedy: Check the MCC and signal line for MCC.

ARC-143.cause: In the power supply, the communication between the operation board and the control board was disconnected.
ARC-143.remedy: 1. Check the fuses [For feeder: 3A(FU2)/8A(FU3)]. If the fuses were blown, please perform the following remedy. Change the encoder cable and fuses Change the encoder board in the wire feeder, and change fuses. 2. Change the Gabana board. 3. Change operation board in the welding power supply.

ARC-144.cause: In Power supply, the communication alarm between GABANA CPU and Main CPU occured.
ARC-144.remedy: Cycle power of the power supply by pressing E-STOP then pressing RESET.

ARC-145.cause: In the Power supply, the communication data between GABANA CPU and Main CPU was abnormal.
ARC-145.remedy: Cycle power of the power supply by pressing E-STOP then RESET.

ARC-146.cause: In CO2 setup, you cannot use Pulse mode.
ARC-146.remedy: Set pulse mode to disabled in the weld schedule detail menu. If you use the direct command AS instruction, AS[20V, 200A], the pulse mode is always ON. So use the AS instruction with the weld schedule number.

ARC-147.message: Can't use Pulse in this setup(E:%d)
ARC-147.cause: In CO2 setup, you cannot use Pulse mode.
ARC-147.remedy: Set pulse mode to disabled in the weld schedule detail menu. If you use the direct command AS instruction, AS[20V, 200A], the pulse mode is always ON. So use the AS instruction with the weld schedule number.

ARC-148.cause: In CO2 setup, you cannot use Pulse mode.
ARC-148.remedy: Set pulse mode to disabled in the weld schedule DETAIL menu. If you use the direct command AS instruction, AS[20V, 200A], the pulse mode is always ON. Therefore, use the AS instruction with the weld schedule number.

ARC-149.message: Can't use Pulse in this setup
ARC-149.cause: In CO2 setup, you cannot use Pulse mode.
ARC-149.remedy: Set pulse mode to disabled in the weld schedule detail menu. If you use the direct command AS instruction, AS[20V, 200A], the pulse mode is always ON. So use the AS instruction with the weld schedule number.

ARC-150.cause: Detect invalid signal operation in welding.
ARC-150.remedy: Reset and try again after Arc OFF.

ARC-154.cause: Arc loss time is invalid range.

ARC-155.cause: Communication with RoboWeld power source is timeout.
ARC-155.remedy: Confirm port setup and connection cable.

ARC-157.cause: Receive invalid data from Power Source.

ARC-166.cause: Communication with RoboWeld power source stopped in welding.
ARC-166.remedy: Confirm another error message and port, cable setup.

ARC-167.cause: I/O space for RoboWeld is already in use.
ARC-167.remedy: Confirm another I/O device and $IO_START in $RBWLD.

ARC-168.remedy: Confirm another I/O device and $IO_START in $RBWLD.

ARC-169.cause: An invalid wire FWD/BWD operation was detected.

ARC-170.remedy: Confirm welding device and workpiece status.

ARC-171.remedy: Confirm port setup, noise environment, cable status.

ARC-172.cause: Receive invalid command from power source.

ARC-173.cause: Retry to send the command to power source.

ARC-175.cause: Communication with power source is stopped.
ARC-175.remedy: Confirm welding setup, cable connection, then reset.

ARC-176.cause: Sysvar $RBWLD is not setup for new EQ number.

ARC-179.cause: This alarm occurs when communication between the welding equipment control board and the robot controller stops.
ARC-179.remedy: 1. If this alarm occurred with ARC-143, please perform the remedy for ARC-143. 2. If this alarm is still occurred after restarting the system, check the wiring between the controller and welding power supply. If problem is not found, check the power supply control board.

ARC-180.cause: Wire feeder motor speed is over the limited speed.
ARC-180.remedy: Check the wire feeder motor. After check try the operation again. If the same alarm occurs, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

ARC-181.cause: Wire feeder motor sensor line was connected off or wire feeder motor did not rotate correctly.
ARC-181.remedy: Check the wire feeder motor sensor line. After check try again. If the same alarm occurs, inform of the service.

ARC-182.cause: While the motor should stop, the motor rotation was detected.
ARC-182.remedy: If the motor was rotated actually, the control board in wire feed controller may be broken.

ARC-188.cause: An ESTOP signal was input from an external source.
ARC-188.remedy: Turn off controller power, remove the cause for the error, reset the ESTOP, then turn on the controller again.

ARC-189.cause: An Exernal1 hold signal was input from an external source.
ARC-189.remedy: Turn off controller power, remove the cause for the error, reset the ESTOP, then turn on the controller again.

ARC-190.cause: An Exernal1 hold signal was input from an external source.
ARC-190.remedy: Turn off controller power, remove the cause for the error, reset the ESTOP, then turn on the controller again.

ARC-191.remedy: Turn off the power then try again. If the same alarm occurs again, inform of the service.

ARC-192.cause: A Weld power supply CPU error has occurred.
ARC-192.remedy: Perform a Cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

ARC-193.cause: The Torch switch was turned ON but the arc could not started within 4sec.
ARC-193.remedy: By turning off the Torch switch, the alarm will disappear. Confirm that the weld power lines are connected correctly.

ARC-195.cause: The specified weld type has not been supported for this power supply.
ARC-195.remedy: Check the setup of process type, wire size, wire material in weld equipment setup screen and pulse mode in weld schedule. Then change them.

ARC-196.cause: Loading weld type data now. Please wait for a moment.

ARC-198.cause: The specified weld type has not been supported for this power supply.
ARC-198.remedy: Check the setup of process type, wire size, wire material in weld equipment setup screen and pulse mode in weld schedule. Then change them.

ARC-199.cause: The connected weld equipment is not supported.

ARC-200.cause: The welding equipment connected on the Arclink is not responding to queries.
ARC-200.remedy: Check the power and Arclink connections to the welding equipment.

ARC-201.cause: A welding equipment component on the Arclink failed to respond to a request issued by the controller.
ARC-201.remedy: Check the power and Arclink connections between the controller and welding equipment.

ARC-202.cause: A welding equipment component returned an error in response to a request from the controller.
ARC-202.remedy: Turn the controller and welding equipment off then on again.

ARC-203.cause: The Arclink network was reset by a request from the welding equipment.
ARC-203.remedy: None. This usually happens as a result of an error detected by the welder.

ARC-204.cause: This is an informational message indicating that the Arclink network has been initialized and is ready for normal operation.

ARC-205.cause: The high speed event message expected during welding failed to arrive in time.
ARC-205.remedy: The Arclink network is automatically reset. If this error persists, it indicates a problem with the communications network or welding equipment.

ARC-206.cause: The Arclink CAN interface is detecting a high rate of errors on the connection to the welder. This is usually caused by electical noise on the Arclink network.
ARC-206.remedy: Check all Arclink connections and wiring to eliminate the electical noise.

ARC-207.cause: The Arclink interface on the controller cannot detect any power or other equipment on the network connections. This indicates that there is no Arclink network connected, or that the welding equipment is turned off or has been disconnected.
ARC-207.remedy: Make sure that all Arclink connections are properly made and that the connected welding equipment is also connected and turned on.

ARC-208.message: Arclink ch%d no nodes on bus
ARC-208.cause: No other equipment can be detected on the Arclink network.
ARC-208.remedy: Check to make sure that the Arclink network is properly connected and that the attached welding equipment is turned on.

ARC-209.cause: The Arclink interface is detecting unexpected errors on the network, indicating possible electrical noise or other interference. If these errors continue, a network failure could occur.
ARC-209.remedy: Check all Arclink connections and wiring to eliminate the source of the noise.

ARC-210.cause: The Arclink interface on the controller is unable to communicate due to too many messages flooding the network.
ARC-210.remedy: Reduce the message traffic by running fewer utility program sessions to the same controller.

ARC-211.cause: An unexpected communications error has occurred on the Arclink CAN interface.
ARC-211.remedy: Check all Arclink connections and wiring, then turn off the controller, and restart it.

ARC-212.cause: A CANbus card has been detected for an Arclink communications channel that has already been assigned as an Arclink-over-Ethernet channel.
ARC-212.remedy: Assign the Ethernet connection to a different channel to make this channel available for use by the CANbus card.

ARC-249.cause: The weld table number could not be selected on the weld equipment.
ARC-249.remedy: Check the weld table in the Weld Eq setup screen. The Powerwave may need another weld table.

ARC-250.cause: After the weld ended the process active input remained ON longer than the specified maximum time.
ARC-250.remedy: Increase the process active timeout on the robot ($aweupr[eq].$max_end_time [seconds]) or decrease the weld end time values on the power supply.

ARC-251.cause: After the weld ended the arc detect input remained ON longer than the specified maximum time.
ARC-251.remedy: Increase the process active timeout on the robot ($aweupr[eq].$max_end_time [seconds]) or decrease the weld end time values on the power supply.

ARC-252.cause: Constant Deposition ramping could not be used. This is because the constant deposition option is not loaded or because of using incompatible features such as HeatWave, Low Freq Pulse, TAST/AVC.
ARC-252.remedy: Check that the constant deposition option is loaded. If not, turn off CDep ramp in the weld schedule. Do not use CDep ramping with the incompatible options.

ARC-253.cause: Some I/O polarities are set to Inverse. This is need cycle power.

ARC-255.cause: Weld EQ setup has not been completed yet.
ARC-255.remedy: Please complete Weld EQ setup for Digital Weld EQ on ArcTool Setup screen with Controlled Start.

ARC-256.cause: First connection with weld EQ is failed.
ARC-256.remedy: Please check follows. 1. All programs are aborted. 2. Alarm of Weld EQ is not posted.

ARC-257.cause: Torch collision is detected. This is judged by the state of specified signal($aweioex[x].$torch_colli).
ARC-257.remedy: Remove the cause of torch collision. This alarm can be reset by reset key.

ARC-258.cause: Wirestick detect is not executed correctly at welder because voltage for detecting wirestick is not applied.
ARC-258.remedy: Check follows and push reset button. 1. If ARC-008 and ARC-124 occurred at same time, remove the cause of them. 2. Check the voltage detection cable setting.

ARC-259.cause: Weld start instruction was performed during communication with weld equipment.
ARC-259.remedy: Program execution can be resumed. Basically, it is recommended that you do not perform communication during weld program execution.

ARC-263.cause: The adaptive welding program was not found.
ARC-263.remedy: Check the program name is correct and check the adaptive welding KAREL program.PC file is loaded.

ARC-270.message: Fail to set Weld EQ parameter
ARC-270.cause: 1. Weld EQ is OFFLINE. 2. Now welding. 3. This parameter is not availavle.
ARC-270.remedy: 1. Establish communication with Weld EQ. 2. Set after welding. 3. Use Weld EQ which supports this parameter.

ARC-280.message: E%d EMG Arc Off time too short
ARC-280.cause: The Emergency Arc Off time specifies how long welding is permitted without any motion group moving. The time ($AWSEMGOFF.$CHK_TIME) is shorter than the delay during the Weld Start.
ARC-280.remedy: Reduce the weld start time on the welder or increase the allowable welding time with no motion by setting $AWSEMGOFF.$CHK_TIME. The units of $CHK_TIME are milliseconds.

ARC-281.cause: The Motion Release DI was not ON when the weld start time completed.
ARC-281.remedy: Resume the program. If this alarm happens repeatedly, check the power supply settings.

ARC-282.cause: A problem occurred during a Weld Start using the motion release feature. 1. Motion release port is not defined. 2. Motion release port read failed. 3. Start time port is not defined. 4. Start time port read failed. 5. Motion release DI ON before start.

ARC-300.cause: The argument for Adjust Start Height macro is not an integer.
ARC-300.remedy: Use an integer value for the Adjust Start Height macro.

ARC-301.cause: The specified equipment number for Arc Start Height Adjust is invalid.
ARC-301.remedy: Specify the existed equipment number by Adjust Start Height macro.

ARC-302.cause: The specified robot group number for Arc Start Height Adjust is invalid.
ARC-302.remedy: Specify the proper robot group number in Arc Start Height Adjust setup screen.

ARC-303.cause: The specified I/O assignment for Arc Start Height Adjust is invalid.
ARC-303.remedy: Specify the proper I/O assignment in Arc Start Height Adjust setup screen.

ARC-304.cause: In Arc Start Height Adjust function, You cannot use same PR number for both Touch Command Signal and Touch Detect Signal.
ARC-304.remedy: Use different PR number for Touch Command Signal and Touch Detect Signal.

ARC-305.cause: Other task has already start Arc Start Height Adjust for the specified equipment.
ARC-305.remedy: Do not perform Arc Start Height Adjust for one equipment at the same timing.

ARC-306.cause: Arc Start Height Adjust is ignored because of Single Step, Dry Run. Or because of Weld Disabled when $AWSTHOF.$CHK_WLD_ENB is TRUE. If Lincoln welder is used, ArcLink may be disconnect.
ARC-306.remedy: Release Single Step or Dry Run or set Weld Enabled to perform Arc Start Height Adjust. If you are using Lincoln welder, establish the ArcLink connection. If you do not want to post the warning message, set $AWSTHOF.$POST_WARN to FALSE.

ARC-307.cause: Contact has already detected before search is started for Arc Start Height Adjust function.
ARC-307.remedy: Perform Arc Start Height Adjust at the position which the torch never touch the work. If you want to continue Arc Start Height Adjust in this situation, set Contact Before Search item in Arc Start Height Adjust setup screen to WARN.

ARC-308.cause: Contact is not detected during the search motion for Arc Start Height Adjust function.
ARC-308.remedy: Perform search motion from closer position against the work. Or change Search Speed or Search Max Distance.

ARC-309.cause: Arc Start Height Adjust is failed by some reason.
ARC-309.remedy: Confirm that the settings for Arc Start Height Adjust is proper. If other alarm is posted at the same time, solve the other alarm first. If this problem persists, contact tech support.

ARC-310.cause: The motion for Arc Start Height Adjust function is too long.
ARC-310.remedy: If Arc Start Height Adjust is performed with very low override, the alarm may be posted. If you encounter the alarm with 100% override,

ASBN-305.cause: Other task has already start Arc Start Height Adjust for the specified equipment.
ASBN-305.remedy: Do not perform Arc Start Height Adjust for one equipment at the same timing.

ASBN-309.cause: Arc Start Height Adjust is failed by some reason.

ASBN-310.cause: The motion for Arc Start Height Adjust function is too long.
ASBN-310.remedy: If Arc Start Height Adjust is performed with very low override, the alarm may be posted. If you encounter the alarm with 100% override,
