FORC-634.message: Can't use WCG in case of fixed FS
FORC-634.cause: In case of fixed force sensor, Tool weight and center of gravity can't be calculated.
FORC-634.remedy: In order to use WCG, Attach force sensor to wrist and change attachment from fixed to hand

FORC-635.message: Can't use WCG with this robot
FORC-635.cause: In case of this robot, there is no force sensor to be attached, Tool weight and center of gravity can't be calculated.
FORC-635.remedy: In order to use WCG, change robot type that can have force sensor

FORC-641.cause: Recording positions failed. The real cause is the alarm just below this one in alarm history.
FORC-641.remedy: Please check the alarm history and then retry again.

FORC-642.remedy: Please reduce total recording time, or increase the monitoring interval.

FORC-643.cause: Recording positions not finished, or NO enough recorded positions.
FORC-643.remedy: Please finish recording, or increase total recording time.

FORC-644.cause: iRVision Debur. Line Output vision process has not been executed, or NO enough edge points detected.
FORC-644.remedy: 1. Please finish running iRVision Debur. Line Output vision process. 2. Please check the setting of iRVision Debur. Line Output vision process.

FORC-645.cause: Too many edge points detected by iRVision Debur. Line Output vision process.
FORC-645.remedy: 1. Please check maximum available number of edge points. 2. Please check the setting of iRVision Debur. Line Output vision process.

FORC-646.cause: Failed to update initial data. The real cause is the alarm just below this one in alarm history.
FORC-646.remedy: Please check the alarm history and then retry.

FORC-647.cause: Generating TP program failed. The real cause is the alarm just below this one in alarm history.
FORC-647.remedy: Please check the alarm history and retry.

FORC-648.remedy: Please increase values of parameters Distance Threshold, Angle Threshold or Orient Change Thres.

FORC-649.cause: Parameter setting not initialized or it is not correct. The real cause is the alarm just below this one in alarm history.
FORC-649.remedy: Please check the alarm history and retry.

FORC-650.message: NOT for robot with Ext axes
FORC-650.cause: Robots with extended axes are NOT supported.
FORC-650.remedy: Please change to robot without extended axes to use this function.

FORC-651.cause: Cannot find an edge line detected by iRVision Debur. Line Output vision process matches to that in the initial data.
FORC-651.remedy: If the parameter Non Stop When Gen. Fail is FALSE, the start point, and end point of the detected longest line of the edge were saved in the TP program ERR_PTP_EDG. Please check the setting of iRVision Debur. Line Output vision process near them.

FORC-652.cause: The setting of the specified contouring schedule data is wrong.
FORC-652.remedy: Please set the specified contouring schedule correctly. If you manually set the specified schedule from UNUSED to CONTOURING, please reset it to UNUSED and try again.

FORC-653.cause: The data file is missing or it is invalid.

FORC-655.remedy: Please confirm all target distance are greater than 15mm.

FORC-656.cause: The detected target distance does not match the taught target distance.
FORC-656.remedy: Please confirm the vision data of target.

FORC-658.cause: Some edge position is not reachable.
FORC-658.remedy: Please adjust the workpiece position, start point of edge or TCP and then try again.

FORC-659.cause: Approach point setting of the edge is wrong.
FORC-659.remedy: On the ROBOGUIDE edge property page, enable the parameter Add approach point, and set Acr to a minus value and then try again.

FORC-660.remedy: Please set the part name to be no longer than 18 characters and try again.

FORC-661.cause: All edge point in the data file are not in the same plane.
FORC-661.remedy: Please teach the edge in the same plane and then generate data files again.

FORC-662.cause: The orientation of some edge points in the data file are wrong.
FORC-662.remedy: Please teach the orientation of the edge points correctly and then generate data files again.

FORC-663.cause: The edge line in the data file overlapped.
FORC-663.remedy: Please do not overlap the edge while teaching it and generate data files again.

FORC-681.cause: In the hand guidance operation, two or more Cartesian Position Limits with Inside motion area are enabled.
FORC-681.remedy: Please enable only one Cartesian Position Limit with inside motion area. in the hand guidance operation.

FORC-682.cause: In the hand guidance operation, two or more Cartesian Position Limits with Outside motion area are enabled.
FORC-682.remedy: Please enable only one Cartesian Position Limit with Outside motion area. in the hand guidance operation.

FORC-683.remedy: Please finish a hand guidance operation within two minutes.

FORC-684.cause: During the direct teaching process, the position configuration has been changed.
FORC-684.remedy: During the direct teaching process, please do not change the position configuration between Flip and Non-flip, or between Up and Down, or between Back and Front.

FORC-685.remedy: Please check the hand guidance initial setting screen. 1. To use the custom button, please set as follows. (a) Lever Mounted -> Yes. (b) Custom Switch Output -> Enable. (c) Output To -> a correct DO/RO/F. 2. To use Hand Open/Close SW, please set as follows (a) Hand Open/Close SW -> Enable. (b) Open Program/Close Program -> Correct programs.

FORC-686.cause: Hand guidance I/O Signal setting error.
FORC-686.remedy: Please check the hand guidance I/O Signal setting in the Cartesian Pos. Limit Detail screen.

FORC-687.remedy: Please reduce total recording time, or increase the Distance Threshold or Orient Change Thres. and do the Direct Teaching again.

FORC-688.cause: Too many TP program teach points.
FORC-688.remedy: Please reduce total recording time, or increase the Distance Threshold or Orient Change Thres. and do the Direct Teaching again.

FORC-689.message: H/G System is in error Status
FORC-689.cause: System is in error status, therefore the hand guidance can not be started.
FORC-689.remedy: Please clear the error by pressing RESET button, and then try the hand guidance again.

FORC-690.cause: ENBL input is OFF, therefore the hand guidance can not be started.
FORC-690.remedy: Please set the ENBL input to ON and try the hand guidance again.

FORC-691.cause: HOLD input is ON, therefore the hand guidance can not be started.
FORC-691.remedy: Please set the HOLD input to OFF and try the hand guidance again.

FORC-692.message: H/G Force Sensor Initial Force Error
FORC-692.cause: The initial force of hand guidance force sensor is error.
FORC-692.remedy: Stop the robot for more than 10 seconds, and then try hand guidance again.

FRSY-001.cause: The FROM disk does not have enough available memory to perform the specified command.
FRSY-001.remedy: Delete all unnecessary files and then purge the device. If the device is still full, then backup the files to an off-line device and reformat the device.

FRSY-002.remedy: Format the device before using it.

FRSY-003.remedy: Verify all the parameters for the requested command are correct.

FRSY-004.cause: Copying a file to the FROM disk requires that the RAM disk be mounted with enough memory available to temporarily contain the file.
FRSY-004.remedy: Mount the RAM disk before specifying the command.

FRSY-005.remedy: Mount the device before using it.

FRSY-006.remedy: This is a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

FRSY-007.cause: The specified device is not valid.

FRSY-008.remedy: Delete the file first or specify overwrite if available with the command.

FRSY-009.cause: The maximum number of files is already open. THerefore the requested command cannot be performed
FRSY-009.remedy: Either close one or more of the files or set $OPEN_FILES to a larger number and perform a cold start.

FRSY-010.cause: An invalid file position is specified. The position is beyond the end of the file or a negative position.

FRSY-011.cause: No more files are allowed on the device.
FRSY-011.remedy: Delete any unnecessary files or dismount and remount MF: device which will increase the maximum number of files allowed.

FRSY-012.cause: The requested command cannot be performed because the file is not opened with the proper access mode. This error is also caused by trying to update or append to an existing file on the FROM disk or to an existing compressed file on the RAM disk. Update and append are only allowed with uncompressed files on the RAM disk.
FRSY-012.remedy: Open the file with the proper access mode.

FRSY-013.cause: The file cannot be created on the device because not enough consecutive blocks are available.
FRSY-013.remedy: Delete all unnecessary files and then purge the device. For more information on purging, refer to the PURGE_DEV Built-in in the KAREL Reference Manual. If the device is still full, then backup the files to an off-line device and reformat the device.

FRSY-014.cause: The specified file is not found.
FRSY-014.remedy: Verify the file name and the specified or default device is correct.

FRSY-015.cause: The file name contains an invalid character or is blank.
FRSY-015.remedy: Verify the file name is correct.

FRSY-016.cause: The file type contains an invalid character.
FRSY-016.remedy: Verify the file type is correct.

FRSY-017.cause: File not open The file is not open.

FRSY-018.cause: The requested command cannot be performed because the file is already opened.
FRSY-018.remedy: Close the file before specifying the command.

FRSY-019.cause: The specified command is not supported for the device.
FRSY-019.remedy: This is a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

FRSY-020.cause: The RAM disk does not have enough available memory to perform the specified command. Note that copying a file to the FROM disk requires that the RAM disk be mounted with enough memory available to temporarily contain the file.
FRSY-020.remedy: Delete all unnecessary files and then purge the device. For more information on purging, refer to the PURGE_DEV Built-in in the KAREL Reference Manual. If the device is still full, then back up the files to an off-line device and reformat the device after setting $FILE_MAXSEC to a larger number.

FRSY-021.cause: The end of the file is detected.
FRSY-021.remedy: This is a notification. Your do not have to do anything for this warning message.

FRSY-022.cause: The file identification number has reached the maximum number for the device.
FRSY-022.remedy: You must backup all your files, reformat the device, and restore the files. Refer to the File System chapter in the KAREL Reference Manual for more information.

FRSY-023.cause: No blocks were purged for one of the following reasons: 1. No garbage blocks exist. 2. No spare blocks exist because the FROM disk is full.
FRSY-023.remedy: If you require more blocks, you must back up all your files, reformat the device, and restore the files. Refer to the File System chapterin the KAREL Reference Manual for more information.

FRSY-024.cause: You are not allowed to purge the FROM disk because purge is disabled.
FRSY-024.remedy: Set $PURGE_ENBL to TRUE and retry the purge operation. You may wish to set $PURGE_ENBL to FALSE before running a program or application which requires fast cycle time.

FRSY-026.cause: One or more files on the FROM disk are corrupted. This may occur if the FROM is wearing out.
FRSY-026.remedy: You should backup all your files, reformat the device, and restore the files. Refer to the File System chapter in the KAREL Reference Manual for more information. If the problem persists, the FROM might need to be replaced.

FRSY-028.cause: The FROM disk is wearing out.
FRSY-028.remedy: The system will continue to operate as long as enough blocks are available. When too many blocks become bad, the FROM will need to be replaced.

FXTL-001.cause: A file parsing error has occurred. An error exists in one of the model files.
FXTL-001.remedy: Correct the model file and copy it to the controller.

FXTL-002.cause: Not enough values on line. There are not enough values on a line in one of the model files.
FXTL-002.remedy: Correct the model file and copy it to the controller.

FXTL-003.cause: A numeric conversion error has occurred. A value on a line in a model file is not a valid numeric value.
FXTL-003.remedy: Correct the model file and copy it to the controller.

FXTL-004.cause: The output buffer is too small. A file output line exceeds the size of the buffer.
FXTL-004.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

FXTL-005.cause: An unexpected internal library error has occurred.
FXTL-005.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

FXTL-006.cause: An invalid unit number was specified in a command or within a model file.
FXTL-006.remedy: Specify a unit number that is valid for the particular tray.

FXTL-007.cause: An invalid CPU number was specified in the mapping assignment.
FXTL-007.remedy: Specify a CPU number that is valid for this controller configuration. The range is 0 - 2, depending on the hardware.

FXTL-008.cause: Invalid motion group. An invalid motion group was specified in the mapping assignment.
FXTL-008.remedy: Specify a motion group that is valid for this controller configuration. The range is 1 - 6, depending on the hardware.

FXTL-009.cause: Loop number out of range. A LOOP number in a model program is out of range.
FXTL-009.remedy: Correct the model file and copy it to the controller. A valid loop number range is 1 - 20.

FXTL-010.cause: There are too many offsets or no offsets specified on a SENSOR_READ line.
FXTL-010.remedy: Correct the model file and copy it to the controller. The maximum number of offsets is 20.

FXTL-011.cause: A payload was specified that exceeds the maximum for the particular unit.
FXTL-011.remedy: Correct the model file and copy it to the controller.

FXTL-012.cause: An invalid sensor slot was specified in an OFFSET line in a model file.
FXTL-012.remedy: Correct the model file and copy it to the controller. Slot numbers must be in the range of 1 - 20.

FXTL-013.cause: An invalid model name was specified in a MODEL line in a model file.
FXTL-013.remedy: Correct the model file and copy it to the controller. Model names can be up to 18 characters long.

FXTL-014.cause: An invalid model number was specified in a MODEL_NUM line in a model file.
FXTL-014.remedy: Correct the model file and copy it to the controller. Model numbers must be in the range of 1 - 99.

FXTL-015.cause: A NEWMODEL.PTS file was not found in the tray's root directory or could not be opened.
FXTL-015.remedy: Correct the model file and copy it to the controller.

FXTL-016.cause: An invalid index file exists: T%d. An entry in the NEWMODEL.PTS file could not be processed.
FXTL-016.remedy: Correct the model file and copy it to the controller.

FXTL-017.cause: Memory for the tray data structures could not be allocated.
FXTL-017.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

FXTL-018.cause: A file specified in the NEWMODEL.PTS file could not be found and/or opened.
FXTL-018.remedy: Correct the model files and copy them to the controller.

FXTL-019.cause: No cell data file exists: T%d. A cell data file was not found in the tray's root directory or could not be opened.
FXTL-019.remedy: Correct the model file and copy it to the controller.

FXTL-020.cause: No model program file exists: T%d. A model program file that was specified in the NEWMODEL.PTS file was not found in the tray's root directory or could not be opened.
FXTL-020.remedy: Correct the model file and copy it to the controller.

FXTL-021.cause: There was an error during processing the set of model files for the tray.
FXTL-021.remedy: Check the error log and listing for more details about the specific error.

FXTL-022.cause: An invalid mechanical unit type was specified in a command or within a model file.

FXTL-023.message: Error in cell data file: T%d
FXTL-023.cause: An error was found in the cell data file for the tray.
FXTL-023.remedy: Check the error log and listing for more details about the specific error.

FXTL-024.cause: An unrecognized keyword was found when reading one of the model files.
FXTL-024.remedy: Correct the model file and copy it to the controller.

FXTL-025.cause: The unit cpu/group mapping file was not found in the tray's root directory or could not be opened.

FXTL-026.cause: The unit cpu/group mapping file contains incorrect entries and could not be opened.
FXTL-026.remedy: Check the error log and listing for more details about the specific error.

FXTL-027.message: Wrong number of units in prog
FXTL-027.cause: A model program has the wrong number of units vs. the number specified in the cell data file.
FXTL-027.remedy: Correct the model file and copy it to the controller.

FXTL-028.cause: A model program file has incorrect or invalid lines and could not be processed.
FXTL-028.remedy: Check the error log and listing for more details about the specific error.

FXTL-029.cause: Model numbers must all be specified or all set to the defaults.
FXTL-029.remedy: Correct the model files and copy them to the controller.

FXTL-030.cause: More than one model program has the same model number specified.
FXTL-030.remedy: Correct the model files and copy them to the controller.

FXTL-031.cause: A POSITIONER_MOVE statement was not followed by any move command subkeys.
FXTL-031.remedy: Correct the model files and copy them to the controller.

FXTL-032.cause: More than one BUILD_BEGIN or BUILD_END line was found in a model file.
FXTL-032.remedy: Correct the model files and copy them to the controller.

FXTL-033.cause: More than one LOOP_BEGIN/END statement specifies the same loop number.
FXTL-033.remedy: Correct the model files and copy them to the controller.

FXTL-034.cause: A subkey following a POSITIONER_MOVE is invalid or in the wrong place.
FXTL-034.remedy: Correct the model files and copy them to the controller.

FXTL-035.cause: A BUILD_BEGIN did not have a BUILD_END, a LOOP_BEGIN did not have a LOOP_END, or there was some other error in matching looping statements.
FXTL-035.remedy: Correct the model files and copy them to the controller.

FXTL-036.cause: An error occurred while creating or writing a new version of one of the model files.
FXTL-036.remedy: Check the error log and listing for more details about the specific error.

FXTL-037.cause: The tray has one or more units that have not been mapped to a CPU and motion group.
FXTL-037.remedy: Assign or correct the unit mappings and restart.

FXTL-038.cause: The tray has one or more units that are mapped to the same CPU and the motion group as another unit on the controller.
FXTL-038.remedy: Assign or correct the unit mappings, and restart.

FXTL-039.cause: The specified unit has not been mapped to a CPU and motion group.
FXTL-039.remedy: Assign or correct the unit mappings and restart.

FXTL-040.cause: The specified units have the same CPU and group mapping.
FXTL-040.remedy: Assign or correct the unit mappings and restart.

FXTL-041.cause: There were errors in the assignment of positioners to specific CPUs and motion groups. The specified units have the same CPU and group mapping.
FXTL-041.remedy: Check the error log for more specific details, then assign or correct the unit mappings and restart.

FXTL-042.cause: Verification of the tray model files failed due to an error in the files or in the system configuration.
FXTL-042.remedy: Check the error log for more specific details, then make the required corrections.

FXTL-043.cause: An error occurred in the process of converting the model programs to their internal TPP form.
FXTL-043.remedy: Check the error log for the specific details.

FXTL-044.cause: The mechanical variant type specified in the cell data does not match the actual positioner for the specified tray and unit.
FXTL-044.remedy: Correct the model files or the physical unit configuration.

FXTL-045.cause: The tray has one or more mismatches of mechanical variants specified in the cell data file vs. the actual configuration.
FXTL-045.remedy: Check the error log for more specific details, then make the required corrections.

FXTL-046.cause: An error occurred while creating or writing a new TPP file for a model program for a particular unit.
FXTL-046.remedy: Check the error log and listing for more details about the specific error.

FXTL-047.cause: An invalid unit number was specified in a command.
FXTL-047.remedy: Specify a tray number that is valid for the particular configuration. The valid range is 1 - 2.

FXTL-048.cause: An invalid program number was specified in a command or by the PLC.
FXTL-048.remedy: Specify a program number that is valid for the configuration.

FXTL-049.cause: An error occurred while converting the model program to the internal TPP format.
FXTL-049.remedy: Check the error log and listing for more details about the specific error.

FXTL-050.cause: No CPU RIPE communications exist. There are no internal network communication connections with one or more of the CPU boards in the controller cabinet.
FXTL-050.remedy: Verify that the internal network connections and the Ethernet switch are correctly connected and powered on. Turn off the controller and then turn it on again.

FXTL-051.cause: Program conversion timed out. A request to convert a model program to a TP program has taken too long to complete.
FXTL-051.remedy: Turn off the controller and then turn it on again. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC Representative.

FXTL-052.cause: A TP program converted from a model program failed to be copied to its destination location.
FXTL-052.remedy: Check the error log and listing for more details about the specific error.

FXTL-054.cause: The model move command has specified a program or step number that does not exist.
FXTL-054.remedy: Correct the command data or the model program files and retry the operation.

FXTL-055.cause: One or more units on the tray that are required for the model move are not enabled.
FXTL-055.remedy: Enable all units and retry the operation.

FXTL-056.cause: The tray is not in a valid position in order to do a legal model step move.
FXTL-056.remedy: Check the positions of the units. Use the model move OVERRIDE option if the move can be safely performed.

FXTL-057.cause: The requested model move is out of sequence according to the model program.
FXTL-057.remedy: Correct the command data or use the OVERRIDE option to force the move.

FXTL-058.cause: The requested model move has been rejected. The move was not initiated.
FXTL-058.remedy: Check the error log for more details on the exact cause.

FXTL-059.cause: The command is rejected because the tray or one or units on the tray are busy completing a previous operation that cannot be interrupted.
FXTL-059.remedy: Wait for the tray to finish the previous operation, and retry the operation again.

FXTL-060.cause: One or more units on the tray that are required for the model move do not have the proper programs loaded and verified.
FXTL-060.remedy: Initiate a full initialization or data verification for the tray.

FXTL-061.cause: The PLC interface has put the tray into AUTO mode and the requested operation can not be executed.
FXTL-061.remedy: Use the PLC to put the tray into MANUAL mode, and retry the operation.

FXTL-062.cause: The PLC did not clear the CR bit within the allowable time after the controller accepted the command.
FXTL-062.remedy: Check and correct the PLC program.

FXTL-063.cause: An invalid axis number was specified in a command.
FXTL-063.remedy: Specify an axis number that is valid for the particular positioner.

FXTL-064.cause: The specified positioner has been disabled or bypassed.
FXTL-064.remedy: Undo the bypass or change the unit number.

FXTL-065.cause: The tray is in a HOLD state because the PLC NOHLD bit is OFF.
FXTL-065.remedy: Clear the HOLD condition from the PLC, and retry.

FXTL-066.cause: An invalid positioner group number was specified in a GROUP statement.
FXTL-066.remedy: Specify a valid group number in the range from 1 - 20.

FXTL-067.cause: A duplicate positioner group number was specified in a GROUP statement.
FXTL-067.remedy: Edit the file so that each GROUP specifies a unique number in the range from 1 - 20.

FXTL-068.cause: The PLC sent a command that is invalid or not supported.
FXTL-068.remedy: Correct the PLC logic to send only valid command codes.

FXTL-069.cause: A data value sent by the PLC is not valid, such as the unit number, program number, or step number.
FXTL-069.remedy: Correct the PLC logic to send only valid command values.

FXTL-070.cause: Error state recovery is not possible for this tray at this time. The previous commanded state cannot be determined.
FXTL-070.remedy: Put the tray into a valid state by using the model move override feature, and proceed from there.

FXTL-071.cause: There is an invalid value assigned for the rack and/or slot number for the fieldbus I/O device for the tray.
FXTL-071.remedy: Assign the correct rack and slot for the fieldbus interface that is actually installed and configured on the controller.

FXTL-072.cause: An invalid program step number was specified. The step number is out of range or is not a valid step for the specified operation.
FXTL-072.remedy: Use the correct step number for the specified program.

FXTL-073.cause: A model file processing error occurred in the file as shown at the specified line number.
FXTL-073.remedy: Check the other entries in the alarm log for the type of error that was detected, then correct the file, copy it to the model file directory, and retry the operation.

FXTL-074.cause: A step number in the model file is out of sequence. Steps must be numbered sequentially with no missing numbers.
FXTL-074.remedy: Correct the model file by fixing or renumbering the cell step lines.

FXTL-075.cause: An invalid program number was specified.
FXTL-075.remedy: Specify a program number that is valid for the configuration.

FXTL-076.cause: A shim was calculated or specified that is out of range of the limits specified for this unit.
FXTL-076.remedy: Specify a smaller shim value, change the limits in the celldata.pts file, or use the TEACH function to change the nominal position value for this step.

FXTL-077.cause: A forward/backward shim search cannot be done for a rotational shim.
FXTL-077.remedy: Do not do a shim search if the current shim has a rotational component.

FXTL-078.cause: A position that was specfied as IDLE in the model points file cannot be directly shimmed.
FXTL-078.remedy: Shim the previous actual move step and the IDLE position will also get the new position data. A move step has the JOINT, LINEAR, or MOVE keyword.

FXTL-079.cause: One or more of the sub-CPUs did not start up or was not detected on the internal network. The tray(s) that depend on the positioners on that CPU could not be auto data-verified.
FXTL-079.remedy: Determine the reason for the CPU startup failure, or try cycling power on the controller.

FXTL-080.cause: The model files for the specified tray have been successfully converted and the tray is ready for manual or PLC operations.

FXTL-081.cause: A PATH_END statement was found without a matching PATH_BEGIN statement.
FXTL-081.remedy: Make sure that PATH_BEGIN and PATH_END are used in matching pairs in the proper sequence.

FXTL-082.cause: A PATH_BEGIN statement was found without a matching PATH_END statement.
FXTL-082.remedy: Make sure that PATH_BEGIN and PATH_END are used in matching pairs in the proper sequence.

FXTL-083.cause: There must be at least three POSITIONER_MOVE statements between a PATH_BEGIN and a PATH_END statement.
FXTL-083.remedy: Make sure that there are the correct number of steps within a path-move block.

FXTL-084.cause: The requested path move has been rejected. The move was not initiated.
FXTL-084.remedy: Check the error log for more details on the exact cause.

FXTL-085.message: Requested step is not a path
FXTL-085.cause: The requested step is not a valid step for a path move.
FXTL-085.remedy: A path move can only be made to the last step or first step within the path block. Modify the program or change the command accordingly.

FXTL-086.cause: The units are not at a valid position or are not at a valid step for doing a path move.
FXTL-086.remedy: All units on the tray must be at a move step that is within the defined path move block. Move the tray to a valid position using a model move or model move with override and then issue the path move command.

FXTL-087.cause: The requested vision or sensor command has been rejected.
FXTL-087.remedy: Check the error log for more details on the exact cause.

FXTL-088.cause: A vision or sensor operation was commanded, but there is no vision or sensor application running. The command cannot be executed.
FXTL-088.remedy: Take action to start the vision or sensor application when the controller starts.

FXTL-089.cause: The requested vision or sensor operation failed.
FXTL-089.remedy: Check the error log for more details on the exact cause.

FXTL-090.cause: The vision or sensor user application did not respond to the command in the allowed time.
FXTL-090.remedy: Make sure that the program is running and is correctly written.

FXTL-091.cause: A vision or sensor offset was specified that is out of range of the limits specified for this unit.
FXTL-091.remedy: Correct the vision offset value, change the limits in the celldata.pts file, or use the TEACH function to change the nominal position value for this step.

FXTL-092.cause: A model move for a single unit or a group of units requires the override flag (MMO) to be set.
FXTL-092.remedy: Issue an override (MMO) command before trying the move command again.

FXTL-093.cause: An invalid value was specified in a LIN_SPEED, JNT_SPEED, DEF_LIN_SPEED, or DEF_JNT_SPEED statement. Linear speed must be from 10-180 (mm/sec) and joint speed must be from 10-100 (percent).

FXTL-099.cause: Signature file for wall mount units have been copied. Cycle Power to take effect.

FXTL-100.cause: Wall mount units cannot find sig file in its FR: Hex data: 00 00 00 00 has 4 bytes. only lower 3 bytes are used to indicate status for cpu3 cpu2 cpu1 each bit is for a group in that cpu. LSB is G1 e.g. 00 00 04 00 indicates cpu2 G3 wall mount unit cannot find its sig file in FR: of cpu2
FXTL-100.remedy: Indentify which unit's sig file is missing. Copy sig file again in flextool setup menu.

FXTL-101.message: CPU Hex:%x miss sig file chk
FXTL-101.cause: Error occurred during sig file checking. CPU mask is in Hex. LSB is cpu1. e.g. CPU Hex:3 means CPU-2 and CPU-1 both has error during sig file check
FXTL-101.remedy: Check that sig files for all wall mount units are copied to FR: of each cpu in flextool setup menu

FXTL-102.cause: Warning indicating the available MBE memory size is substantially low, and is affecting the performance. This may be due to excessive activities on the Network.
FXTL-102.remedy: Wait until MBE memory comes back, or you may need to cycle power if the warning does not go away for one minute.

FXTL-103.cause: Some units are not ready for motion. The error text shows the CPU number and group number whose servo is not ready.
FXTL-103.remedy: Visit the error history page to find related servo error. You may also need to log on the CPU to see if any servo error exist local to the CPU

FXTL-151.cause: The shift key is not pressed

FXTL-152.remedy: Use this menu to map a unit number with a physical unit.

FXTL-153.remedy: Check the hardware to make sure the mapping is correct.

FXTL-155.cause: The Step number is not valid.
FXTL-155.remedy: Perform a data verify first, then select the valid step number.

FXTL-156.cause: Not all units are in the correct position for a model move. The Tray cannot determine which program it is in.
FXTL-156.remedy: Go to the model move menu and move the tray to a model move position.

FXTL-157.message: Cannot copy file to same dev
FXTL-157.cause: You cannot copy a file back to its device.
FXTL-157.remedy: Select a different device for the file copy operation.

FXTL-158.cause: No unit in the Tray. No unit is defined for the tray.
FXTL-158.remedy: Check the unit mapping and Unit enable menu. Then check the celldata.pts and do a data verify.

FXTL-159.cause: The program has no motion step.
FXTL-159.remedy: Check the model file offline and copy the file to the controller. Then do a data verify.

FXTL-160.cause: Non-Zero mastering has been applied. Zero mastering must be performed before running model move.
FXTL-160.remedy: Move all axes to their zero mastering position. Perform a Zero Mastering before running model move.

FXTL-161.cause: Cannot open shim log file in FR: directory.
FXTL-161.remedy: Check memory status to make sure space is available for a shim log file.

FXTL-162.cause: Cannot restore this shim in the shim log because it is no longer valid due to TEACH.

FXTL-163.cause: An error has occurred in reading the shim log file.
FXTL-163.remedy: The shim log file has been corrupted. Load the shim log file from a backup, or delete the log from FR:.

FXTL-164.cause: Invalid shim data. Cannot display the shim item.
FXTL-164.remedy: Select a valid item on the shim log.

FXTL-165.cause: New shim data is all zero. No shim is applied.

FXTL-166.remedy: Move the units to the first or last step of the model program before switching.

FXTL-167.cause: The cursor is not on a unit.
FXTL-167.remedy: Move the cursor to a unit, then press the ENTER key.

FXTL-168.cause: The jog keys are disabled in C-flex axis jog or frame jog menu.
FXTL-168.remedy: Exit from the C-flex axis jog or C-flex frame jog menu to enable jog keys.

FXTL-171.cause: Invalid shim move has occurred. Yoc cannot execute a shim move due to mismatch of tray number, program number, or step number with the current tray state.
FXTL-171.remedy: Use Model Move to move the units to the shim step before shimming the particular step.

FXTL-201.cause: Inverse Kinematic Error. The calibrated inverse kinematics does not converge to a solution. The unit is close or at a singular position.
FXTL-201.remedy: Jog the robot or teach the position away from the singular position.

FXTL-202.cause: The wrist type is not supported.
FXTL-202.remedy: Turn off/on the controller to get correct wrist type.

FXTL-203.cause: The motion group is either not available or it is not a C-flex unit.
FXTL-203.remedy: Make sure the group number is valid.

FXTL-204.cause: The program is not in the model program list.
FXTL-204.remedy: Make sure to do a data verify before running the program.

FXTL-205.cause: The teach pendant program has an invalid position data type.
FXTL-205.remedy: Make sure to do a data verify before running the program.

FXTL-206.cause: The robot is close to a singularity point where there is no solution for the inverse kinematics.
FXTL-206.remedy: Jog the unit away from singular position and continue the operation.

FXTL-207.remedy: Make sure the tool vector is defined.

HOST-001.cause: Your listing has reached the end of the directory. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

HOST-002.cause: The file name you are trying to create or copy to already exists on this device.
HOST-002.remedy: Delete the file on this device or choose a different file name.

HOST-003.cause: The file you are trying to open or copy does not exist on this device.
HOST-003.remedy: Open or copy a file that exists on the device.

HOST-004.cause: The requested operation is not supported.
HOST-004.remedy: Use only supported operations, or check command syntax.

HOST-005.cause: The disk file capacity has been reached.
HOST-005.remedy: Delete some unneeded files or use a disk with sufficient free space.

HOST-006.cause: The end of the file was reached while reading.
HOST-006.remedy: Do not attempt to read beyond the end of a file.

HOST-008.message: Only one file may be opened
HOST-008.cause: An attempt was made to open more than one file.
HOST-008.remedy: Do not attempt to open more than one file at a time.

HOST-009.cause: ZDT Client/iRConnect option is not loaded or demo option expired.
HOST-009.remedy: You may not use ZDT/iRConnect features without the option. Please purchase and load the ZDT/iRConnect option.

HOST-010.remedy: Use the SETUP ZDT Client/iRConnect menu to enable feature. You will have to cycle power to enable the first time.

HOST-011.cause: An attempt was made to send an iRConnect email when To Addr is not set.
HOST-011.remedy: Use the SETUP iRConnect menu to set the To Addr.

HOST-012.cause: An attempt was made to send an iRConnect alert when Alert Addr is not set.
HOST-012.remedy: Use the SETUP iRConnect menu to set the Alert Addr.

HOST-013.cause: ZDT/iRConnect message was not sent because too many messages per minute are being sent by a particular task.
HOST-013.remedy: If possible, configure the messages so they are sent at longer intervals.

HOST-014.cause: ZDT/iRConnect message was not sent because the size is too large.

HOST-015.remedy: Try again later or try increasing $FILESETUP.$FILE_TD_SEC and recycle power.

HOST-017.cause: Web server did not respond to PING request.
HOST-017.remedy: Please check web server IP/name is valid.

HOST-018.remedy: Please check error number for details.

HOST-019.cause: ZDT/iRConnect is busy processing other requests.

HOST-020.cause: The concurrent limit for this message type has been reached.
HOST-020.remedy: Increase the maximum concurrency count for this message type in the ZDT/iRConnect configuration file.

HOST-021.cause: The maximum amount of memory dedicated for sending ZDT messages has been reached.
HOST-021.remedy: Reduce the number of messages being sent or increase the amount of memory allocated to the ZDT messaging task.

HOST-022.cause: The supplied message exceeds the maximum allowed size for an individual message.
HOST-022.remedy: Eliminate unnecessary information in your message or split it into multiple message types.

HOST-023.cause: The messaging library was unable to instantiate a message of the supplied type or an inconsistency was found between the calling arguments and the message's type information.
HOST-023.remedy: Verify the supplied message's program and variable name are spelled correctly, the program containing the message was loaded and the supplied message type's size is correct.

HOST-024.cause: The maximum number of file attachments has exceeded the systems allowable limit.
HOST-024.remedy: Reduce the number of file attachments being sent or stagger the timing of when the file attachments are sent.

HOST-025.message: ZDT No msg create from higher task
HOST-025.cause: Messages cannot be created from a task with priority higher than memory manager.
HOST-025.remedy: Preallocate messages if continue calling create from a task higher them memory manager.

HOST-026.message: ZDT Fields count mismatch src %d dst %d
HOST-026.cause: Field count in source and destination mismatch
HOST-026.remedy: Create same number of fields in destination as SOURCE array size

HOST-027.cause: Field sizes mismatch in source and destination
HOST-027.remedy: Please correct definition of destinations to match source types

HOST-028.remedy: Please check the sub-error code and correct url.

HOST-029.cause: Data Collector/Server did not send correct authorization code
HOST-029.remedy: Please use a FANUC Data Collector for your server.

HOST-030.remedy: Use the SETUP ZDT Client menu to enable [Use XML Config]. You don't need to reload RCMCFG.XML.

HOST-031.message: ZDT MBE memory is low, no messages
HOST-031.cause: MBE memory is low when checked
HOST-031.remedy: Power must be cycled to regain MBE memory if ZDT message continueto not be sent. MBE memory leak is possible if issue persist.

HOST-032.remedy: ZD file has been removed. Cycle power is required to take effect.

HOST-033.message: Cannot send data now. Robot running.
HOST-033.cause: Active Support cannot send data. Robot is in busy or running mode.
HOST-033.remedy: Verify robot is not in busy or running mode and retry the operation.

HOST-034.cause: Active Support has just sent the files before

HOST-035.cause: Diagnostic files are sent by Active Support

HOST-036.cause: Active Support starts sending diagnostic files

HOST-100.remedy: Verify protocol field in the setup menu and retry the operation.

HOST-101.cause: The directory information is corrupted and unreadable.
HOST-101.remedy: Clean the disk drive,try another disk or reformat the disk.

HOST-102.cause: The checksum data is bad. Data is corrupted on the disk and can not be read.
HOST-102.remedy: Try another disk, or reformat the disk

HOST-103.cause: There is a bad sector or track on the disk.
HOST-103.remedy: Clean the disk drive, try another disk, or reformat the disk.

HOST-104.cause: The drive did not respond to a command.
HOST-104.remedy: Check the cable to the drive and make sure drive power is on.

HOST-105.cause: The disk has write protection enabled.
HOST-105.remedy: Remove write protection from the disk or use a disk that is not write protected.

HOST-106.cause: Protocol Entry structure ($PROTOENT) is invalid. It should be reset to default values.
HOST-106.remedy: Return Protocol Entry structure to initial values from Setup and Operations manual.

HOST-107.cause: Server Entry structure ($SERVENT) is invalid. It should be reset to default values.
HOST-107.remedy: Return Server Entry structure to initial values from Setup and Operations manual.

HOST-108.cause: Either the robot controller's Internet Address is invalid, or the robot controller is trying to access a remote Internet Address or Host Name that is invalid or doesn't exist.
HOST-108.remedy: Correct the invalid Internet Address. The robot's Internet Address can be configured in the Setup Host Comm TCP/IP Protocol Menu.

HOST-109.cause: Host Name needs to be set.
HOST-109.remedy: Set Host Name and Internet Address in the Host Comm TCP/IP Protocol Setup Menu.

HOST-110.cause: The Remote Node Name needs to be set. 9
HOST-110.remedy: Set Remote Node Name in the Host Comm TCP/IP Protocol Setup Menu.

HOST-111.cause: ER-1 or ER-2 Ethernet hardware is already running and can not be restarted without cycling power.
HOST-111.remedy: Turn off and then turn on the controler.

HOST-112.cause: The TCP/IP Stack has encountered a situation that may result in corruption or disruption in normal network activity.
HOST-112.remedy: Copy ETHERNET.DG file from MD: and save it. Note the PANIC string. Cycle power to the controller and contact the Support hotline and provide them with that information.

HOST-113.cause: The robot controller Proxy was not able to bind a TCP network socket.
HOST-113.remedy: This alarm generally implies that either the Proxy or the TCP/IP interface is not set up correctly. Verify network connectivity to the robot controller using the ping utility (on the robot, and also on the local PC). Check for abnormal activity with all installed Internet options. Obtain the ethernet.dg file from the MD: device, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-114.cause: A new TCP/IP socket cannot be allocated because all system resources are in use.
HOST-114.remedy: Check for abnormal activity with all installed internet options. Obtain the ethernet.dg file from the MD: device and contact the FANUC America Corporation Hotline.

HOST-115.cause: The robot controller Proxy was not able to listen on a TCP network socket.
HOST-115.remedy: This alarm generally implies that either the Proxy or the TCP/IP interface is not set up correctly. Verify network connectivity to the robot controller using the ping utility (on the robot, and also on the local PC). Check for abnormal activity with all installed Internet options. Obtain the ethernet.dg file from the MD: device, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-116.cause: The External Proxy Server is not configured with a valid Hostname or IP Address.
HOST-116.remedy: Configure the External Proxy Server with a valid Hostname or IP Address. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-117.cause: The Ethernet address needs to be set.
HOST-117.remedy: Set the Ethernet address in Configuration Menu.

HOST-126.cause: The Ethernet address needs to be set.
HOST-126.remedy: Set the Ethernet address in Configuration Menu.

HOST-127.cause: The Ethernet Board firmware is not loaded.
HOST-127.remedy: Load the Ethernet Board firmware in BMON.

HOST-128.cause: The Ethernet Board needs to be reinitialized.
HOST-128.remedy: Install or reseat the Ethernet Board.

HOST-129.cause: Data received from external device is invalid. Most likely caused by electrical noise on receivers.
HOST-129.remedy: The error can be cleared by Stopping and Starting the Tag in Host Comm Setup Menu.

HOST-130.cause: A buffer was passed to the Serial Port Driver which can not be accessed.
HOST-130.remedy: Ensure program can run on this version of controller. You might need to retranslate your program.

HOST-131.cause: The Host Comm system can not execute the requested command in the present operating mode.
HOST-131.remedy: Stop and Start the Host Comm Tag in the Host Comm Setup Menu to reset the operating mode.

HOST-132.cause: The Host Comm system can not allocate memory buffers for receiving or transmitting messages
HOST-132.remedy: Either add more memory to the controller or reduce the number of simultaneous connections.

HOST-133.cause: The Host Comm system is receiving messages but can not decode them.
HOST-133.remedy: Correct port settings: data rate, data size, stop bits, etc to match external device.

HOST-134.cause: The Host Comm system is receiving checksum errors on all messages.
HOST-134.remedy: Ensure that the external device is using the same protocol.

HOST-135.cause: There has not been any network activity on the Comm Tag for a period specified by Inactivity Timeout. The Comm Tag has been stopped as a result.

HOST-136.cause: The remote device is connected but is not responding to requests.
HOST-136.remedy: Check cabling between the devices and/or insure the device is powered.

HOST-137.cause: The remote device indicates the operation was successfully terminated.

HOST-138.cause: The remote device did not indicate operation was terminated.
HOST-138.remedy: The command might have been completed before the cancel command was received.

HOST-139.cause: The Host Comm Protocol does not support the requested function.
HOST-139.remedy: Check the Host Comm Protocol to ensure the function is supported.

HOST-140.cause: The remote device is connected but it is not online.

HOST-141.cause: The Host Comm Protocol could not be started (Mounted) or stopped (dismounted) on the selected comm tag.
HOST-141.remedy: Either use another Comm Tag or Stop and Undefine the selected Comm Tag under Menus-Setup-HostComm-Show

HOST-142.cause: The Host Comm Protocol could not establish communication with the remote device. Possible software mismatch.
HOST-142.remedy: Ensure both local and remote are using compatible software versions.

HOST-143.cause: The selected hardware port defined for the Comm Tag could not be closed.
HOST-143.remedy: Power the controller OFF and then ON and try again. If the error occurs again a cabling or hardware problem might exist with the port.

HOST-144.cause: The Comm Tag either does not have a protocol defined or if required does not have a port assigned.
HOST-144.remedy: DEFINE a protocol to the Comm Tag or assign a port.

HOST-145.cause: An attempt has been made either to read a file opened for write access only or to write a file opened for read access only.
HOST-145.remedy: If possible, close and reopen the file with the correct access parameters.

HOST-146.cause: A bad address has been detected.
HOST-146.remedy: Verify the tag has a supported protocol then UNDEFINE and DEFINE the Comm Tag

HOST-147.cause: The selected protocol requires a device port.
HOST-147.remedy: First ensure the Port has No Use from Port Init Setup. Then assign it to the selected Comm Tag.

HOST-148.cause: Either the Comm Tag is STARTED or it is presently in use.
HOST-148.remedy: Either STOP the Comm Tag or select another Tag.

HOST-149.cause: The passed Device Type is not a Comm Tag type (Cx or Sx).
HOST-149.remedy: Only Comm Tags can be used with this command.

HOST-150.cause: The system does not support selected protocol.
HOST-150.remedy: Either select another protocol or install the selected protocol.

HOST-151.cause: The System has run out of buffers to communicate with the Ethernet Remote PCB.
HOST-151.remedy: Reduce the number of simultaneous connections as there is not enough memory.

HOST-158.cause: An error occurred in the networking software.
HOST-158.remedy: Consult your network administrator. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-159.cause: The Comm Tag does not have a valid username and password.
HOST-159.remedy: Enter a valid username and password for the Comm Tag.

HOST-160.cause: An error occurred in the networking software.
HOST-160.remedy: Consult your network administrator. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-161.cause: The Comm Tag does not have a remote host defined.
HOST-161.remedy: Enter a remote host name in SETUP TAGS menu Current Remote and Startup Remote fields.

HOST-162.cause: The Ethernet PCB isn't initialized properly.
HOST-162.remedy: Ensure both Ethernet PCB firmware and Main PCB Ethernet tasks are activated.

HOST-164.remedy: Make a read call after write before making a new write call.

HOST-167.remedy: Check cable and remote device. Close connection and open again.

HOST-168.cause: Invalid Channel specified. Channel may not be online.
HOST-168.remedy: Make sure the channel specified is online or specify the correct channel

HOST-169.remedy: Verify Path format specified EM:/DNET/1/10/40 DNET-Protocol, 1-Channel,10-MAC Id 40-buffer size Also verify values are legal.

HOST-170.remedy: Verify Explicit Messaging mapping system variables are correctly set and the values are legal.

HOST-171.remedy: Reopen connection with correct buffer size.

HOST-172.remedy: Make sure your host name and local domain name are correct. Your DNS server may not have the. current host listed.

HOST-173.remedy: Verify that you DNS server is running. Check with your DNS administrator to verify that the server is working properly.

HOST-174.remedy: Verify that the host name and local domain name and formated correctly. Verify that your server supports recursive queries. Verify that your server grants access to your robot.

HOST-175.cause: Server has no IP address listed.
HOST-175.remedy: Your host name is valid and is recognized by the DNS server. The server has no IP address for the host queried on. Have your DNS administrator provide the server with an IP address for the host queried on.

HOST-176.remedy: Go to the DNS configuration menu and verify that the server IP address and local domain name are correct.

HOST-177.cause: No router name has been defined. The router name has been set to the robot name.
HOST-177.remedy: If your network has a router, then define a router in the TCP/IP set up menu.

HOST-178.cause: The router does not have an address listed in the local host table.
HOST-178.remedy: If your network has a router, then define an address for it in the TCPIP SETUP screen.

HOST-179.cause: The entered IP address is invalid.
HOST-179.remedy: Reconfigure the Ethernet interfaces such that each interface is on a different subnet, or only configure a single interface.

HOST-180.cause: Internal software problem. Network memory service request occurs before any memory is not created.
HOST-180.remedy: Network memory should be created before accessing.

HOST-181.cause: Timeout occured at getting memory access right.
HOST-181.remedy: Network may overload if this error occurs frequently.

HOST-182.cause: Internal software problem. Specified network memory buffer descriptor was not correct.
HOST-182.remedy: Verify that correct buffer descriptor is specified.

HOST-183.message: NETMEM: buffer is auto ack mode
HOST-183.cause: Internal software problem. Network memory update request issued to automatic acknowledge transmit memory.
HOST-183.remedy: Verify that correct buffer descriptor is specified.

HOST-184.cause: Internal software problem. Specified buffer descriptor is not for transmit buffer.
HOST-184.remedy: Verify that correct buffer descriptor is specified.

HOST-185.cause: Internal software problem. Specified buffer descriptor is not for receive buffer.
HOST-185.remedy: Verify that correct buffer descriptor is specified.

HOST-186.cause: UDP open for datagram sending was failed.
HOST-186.remedy: Confirm that UDP port was consumed by another network application.

HOST-187.cause: UDP open for datagram receiving was failed.
HOST-187.remedy: Verify that there is RLSYNC entry in $SERVENT system variable. Verify that port number for RLSYNC is correct.

HOST-188.remedy: Verify that a correct port number is specified

HOST-189.remedy: Verify that a correct port number is specified

HOST-190.remedy: Verify that a correct port number is specified

HOST-191.remedy: Verify that a correct port number is specified

HOST-192.remedy: Verify that a correct port number is specified

HOST-193.cause: login made to a device using telnet

HOST-194.cause: logout made out of device using telnet

HOST-195.cause: TELNET connection attempt rejected. Please look at cause code for further information
HOST-195.remedy: Correct the cause of failure and try again

HOST-196.remedy: ensure the device is not connected and try again

HOST-197.remedy: ensure the login id is valid and try again

HOST-198.remedy: ensure the password is valid and try again

HOST-199.cause: the inactivity timer for the device expired
HOST-199.remedy: log in again or increase the timer value for the device from the TELNET screens

HOST-200.cause: the FSAC security feature is enabled and the client PC doesn't have sufficient privileges
HOST-200.remedy: make an entry for the PC in the FSAC table

HOST-201.remedy: check the access level for the device from the TELNET screens

HOST-202.cause: valid port not configured for device
HOST-202.remedy: configure a valid port for device from Port Init screens first

HOST-204.message: SM: Remote Client Name is invalid
HOST-204.cause: The host name in the Client tag is not set correctly. If DNS is enabled, DNS server did not resolve the name.
HOST-204.remedy: Change the host name to be a valid name in the client tags.

HOST-205.cause: A request to mount a tag which was already mounted was received.
HOST-205.remedy: Do not try to remount a tag without dismounting it.

HOST-206.cause: The system variable $server_port in the Client tag or the host tag was invalid.
HOST-206.remedy: Set the $hosts_cfg[n].$server_port sysvar for the server tag or $hostc_cfg[n].$server_port for the client to a valid number

HOST-207.cause: The requested tag is not mounted
HOST-207.remedy: Mount the tag before using it

HOST-208.cause: The requested tag is not yet connected to the remote host/device
HOST-208.remedy: Use MSG_CONNECT to connect the tag before opening it.

HOST-209.cause: The connection was aborted by remote host
HOST-209.remedy: Check the remote host and reconnect to it

HOST-210.cause: Connection was timed out by remote.

HOST-211.message: SM: Connection Write Buffer is full
HOST-211.cause: Write buffer is full. The remote host may not be responding or the network is down.
HOST-211.remedy: Check remote host and network connection.

HOST-212.message: SM: Write Direction shut down by Peer
HOST-212.cause: Write direction was shutdown by remote.
HOST-212.remedy: Check remote and reconnect to remote host

HOST-213.message: SM: Read Direction shut down by Peer
HOST-213.cause: Read direction was shutdown by remote.
HOST-213.remedy: Check remote and reconnect to remote host

HOST-214.cause: Remote host has not yet connected.

HOST-215.cause: The requested tag is in use.
HOST-215.remedy: Stop using the remote tag. If necessary close any open file to the tag and disconnect the tag by using MSG_DISCO.

HOST-216.cause: A request was received for a socket which is invalid

HOST-217.cause: A socket error was returned by the tcpip library.
HOST-217.remedy: Retry the operation. All sockets may be use. Free some resources by closing some connections to telnet, ftp or socket mesg If that is not feasible, the same error may occur again.

HOST-218.cause: A diagnostic TP session was connected in interactive mode. Input is allowed.

HOST-219.cause: A diagnostic TP session was connected in monitor mode. Input is not allowed.

HOST-220.cause: A diagnostic TP session was disconnected.

HOST-223.cause: A response from the DHCP server was detected.

HOST-224.cause: No response exists from the DHCP server.
HOST-224.remedy: Check your cable and server configuration, and retry the operation.

HOST-225.cause: The DHCP server returned an IP address which is already in use.
HOST-225.remedy: Check the DHCP server configuration. Identify the device that is using the same IP address that the DHCP server assigned to the robot controller. This is strictly a DHCP server configuration/IP address management problem.

HOST-226.cause: The DHCP lease time expired and the robot could not renew the DHCP lease on the robot controller's IP address.
HOST-226.remedy: Check the Ethernet cables and make sure the robot controller is still connected to the Ethernet network. Check that the DHCP server is online. Check the DHCP server configuration and verify it is able to assign IP address to the robot controller.

HOST-227.cause: The Ethernet interface was shut down.
HOST-227.remedy: The lease might have expired. Check the cabling/server configuration and start DHCP again from the DHCP screens.

HOST-228.cause: this may be normal protocol operation

HOST-230.cause: The robot tried to renew IP address, but the renew attempt failed.
HOST-230.remedy: Check the network cabling and DHCP server setup.

HOST-232.cause: The DHCP operation is in progress.

HOST-233.remedy: Check the network cabling for defects, or the DHCP server setup for possible errors.

HOST-234.remedy: This is a status message. No remedy is required.

HOST-235.remedy: This is a status message. No remedy is required.

HOST-236.cause: After loading the FTP option, the FTP servers could not be automatically started.
HOST-236.remedy: Start the FTP servers from the Hostcomm Server SETUP screen.

HOST-237.cause: The system was unable to start the FTP servers because no free server tags were found.

HOST-239.cause: A web page tried to issue a KCL command, but KCL is not loaded on the robot controller.
HOST-239.remedy: Load the KCL option on the robot controller at Controlled Start.

HOST-240.cause: An SMTP server failure has occurred.
HOST-240.remedy: Check and verify your SMTP configuration. On an iPendant, this is done using the DRC menus. Otherwise, see the $SMTP_CTRL system variable. It is likely that $SMTP_CTRL.$SERVER was not set with the IP address of an SMTP server.

HOST-241.remedy: This warning can be disabled from the DRC menus: Data Services Setup. The warning can also be disabled by setting the system variable $SMTP_CTRL.$POST_DLVR to FALSE.

HOST-242.cause: No packets were received from NTP server.
HOST-242.remedy: Check to make sure the NTP server IP address is correct. If it is not, correct the address and try the operation again.

HOST-243.cause: The Address Conflict Detection has detected a duplicate IP address on the network.
HOST-243.remedy: Change the configured IP address to an IP address not on the network. If using DHCP, consult your network administrator.

HOST-244.cause: Important robot operations might be effected by the high level of traffic on the Ethernet network.
HOST-244.remedy: Contact your system administrator to fix the network problem.

HOST-245.cause: The robot name configured for the TCP/IP interface is illegal.
HOST-245.remedy: Change the robot Hostname in the Host Comm TCP/IP screen to a legal name. A legal Hostname is a text string of characters drawn from the alphabet (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and minus sign (-). No blank or space characters are permitted as part of a name, nor is the underscore character (_). The first character must be an alpha character. The last character must not be a minus sign.

HOST-246.cause: A Hosttable entry is configred with an illegal name. If n1 = 1, the illegal name is in the local host table. If n1 = 2, the illegal name is in the shared host table. n2 indicates the entry number of the name in the respective table.
HOST-246.remedy: Change the robot Hosttable entry in the Host Comm TCP/IP screen to a legal name. A legal Hostname is a text string of characters drawn from the alphabet (A-Z, a-z), digits (0-9), and minus sign (-). No blank or space characters are permitted as part of a name, nor is the underscore character (_). The first character must be an alpha character. The last character must not be a minus sign.

HOST-260.cause: The camera handle was not found.
HOST-260.remedy: Be sure the camera is initialized.

HOST-261.cause: Could not get access rights to camera. Some other device might be using it.
HOST-261.remedy: Be sure the robot can get exclusive rights to the camera.

HOST-265.remedy: This could be caused by a temporary network issue See PIPC:GIGE_LOG.DT.

HOST-266.cause: The camera IP address is not on same subnet as the robot.
HOST-266.remedy: The camera and the robot should be on same subnet.

HOST-267.cause: The Mac address does not match camera. The camera might have been swapped.

HOST-268.remedy: See PIPC:GIGE_LOG.DT. There might be too many.CAM files.

HOST-279.cause: The GigE command to the camera failed.

HOST-280.cause: The PC responded to a robot PC Share request in a way the robot couldn't understand.
HOST-280.remedy: Verify your PC is running a supported platform. Supported operating systems include Windows XP, Windows Vista, and Linux running Samba 3.2. If problems persist on supported platforms, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-281.cause: The robot timed-out while waiting for the PC to respond to a PC Share request.
HOST-281.remedy: Verify the PC is properly connected to the network, and can be pinged on the network. Verify the PC Share client tag is properly configured, and the PC has properly shared the location/directory being accessed. The default timeout value can be changed in System Variables. If the PC is too slow for the default timeout, set a more reasonable timeout value in seconds in $SMB_CLNT[X].$RSPTMOUT, and power-cycle the controller. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-282.cause: The requested file operation can not be performed unless the client tag is configured with a share.
HOST-282.remedy: Configure the client tag with a shared drive to perform the requested file operation. Make sure the shared drive is porperly configured on the remote PC. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-283.cause: NetBios name resolution is not properly configured.
HOST-283.remedy: Either configure a valid WINS server, or enable broadcast name resolution. Both settings can be configured in the PC Share protocol page in the HOST COMM screen. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-284.message: SMB: Secure Signature from PC failed
HOST-284.cause: The Secure Signature failed on a network message sent from the PC to the robot controller.
HOST-284.remedy: The PC server has message signing enabled. This forces the robot controller to perform Secure Signatures to verify communication integrity. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-285.message: SMB: DOS error: File not found
HOST-285.cause: The PC server was unable to find the requested file.
HOST-285.remedy: Verify the Remote Path/Share field is properly configured in the client tag setup screen. Verify the requested file exists on the remote PC server by performing a directory listing from the robot controller FILE menu. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-286.message: SMB: DOS error: Path not found
HOST-286.cause: The PC server was unable to find the requested path.
HOST-286.remedy: Verify the Remote Path/Share field is properly configured in the client tag setup screen. Verify the requested path exists on the remote PC server by performing a directory listing from the robot controller FILE menu. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-287.message: SMB: DOS error: Too many open files
HOST-287.cause: The PC server was unable to open the requested file, because the robot controller has too many files opened to the remote PC.
HOST-287.remedy: Close some files that the robot controller has opened on the PC Share client tag associated with the remote PC. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-288.cause: The PC server denied the robot controller access to a file, share, or directory path.
HOST-288.remedy: Verify your username and re-enter your password in the robot controller client tag setup screens. Verify permissions have been properly set on the shared folder on the remote PC. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-289.message: SMB: DOS error: Requested share does not exist
HOST-289.cause: The PC server cannot find the Share requested by the robot controller.
HOST-289.remedy: Verify on the remote PC that a folder has been properly shared. Verify that the share name is configured in the robot controler client tag setup screen. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-299.cause: The PC responded to a PC share request with a DOS File Error.
HOST-299.remedy: First, check for an alarm cause code for more information on the specific DOS error. If no alarm cause code exists, note the DOS error code. Lookup the DOS error code in the PC Share manual. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

HOST-301.remedy: Connect the CNC to the robot controller.

HOST-302.remedy: Connect the CNC to the robot controller.

HOST-303.remedy: Change the CNC to a supported type.

HOST-304.remedy: Cycle power on the robot controller to activate the change.

HOST-305.cause: Starting the communication with the specified CNC.

HOST-306.message: Input I/O number for CNC No.

HOST-306.remedy: Enter the proper I/O number for the selected CNC.

HOST-308.cause: The CNC number is greater than the maximum number allowed.

HOST-309.cause: The CNC No. is not set.

HOST-311.cause: You press the OPR enable button but interlock signal is off.

HOST-313.cause: You try to jog machine tool but Machine Tool Operation in Setup Machine I/F isn't available.
HOST-313.remedy: Set the Machine Tool Operation available.

HOST-380.remedy: Power-down and up the controller. There may be other error messages that shows the cause of this alarm. Open alarm history screen and report all to FANUC. Select the alarms and press DETAIL to see all message displayed in two lines. If the problem occurs again, write down the error message, record the software version and any significant events leading up to this problem and contact FANUC. There may be other error messages that shows the cause of this alarm. Open alarm history screen and report all to FANUC. Select the alarms and press DETAIL to see all message displayed in two lines. Report all messages to track the problem.

HOST-390.cause: ONLYSEND in RSI configuration XML is other than TRUE

HOST-391.cause: 1st argument in RSI_WRXML_I is not supported.
HOST-391.remedy: Change 1st argument in RSI_WRXML_I to supported one.

HOST-392.message: RSI: 2nd argument in RSI_WRXML_I should be 1 character
HOST-392.cause: 2nd argument in RSI_WRXML_I is not 1 character.
HOST-392.remedy: Change 2nd argument in RSI_WRXML_I to 1 character.

HOST-401.cause: HSSB board is not found in option board slot of robot.

HOST-410.message: TLIF_READ timeout in KAREL for Tool Interface function
HOST-410.cause: KAREL built-in function TLIF_READ for Tool Interface function is timed out.
HOST-410.remedy: This warning is just for information. Data received until timeout is read and the size is returned to 2nd argument of TLIF_READ. You may have to greater the timeout value, which is 1st argument of TLIF_READ.

HOST-411.message: Requested size from TLIF_READ is larger than $TLIF.$RCV_BUF_SZ in KAREL
HOST-411.cause: Requested size of KAREL built-in function TLIF_READ for Tool Interface function is greater than $TLIF.$RCV_BUF_SZ.
HOST-411.remedy: Greater $TLIF.$RCV_BUF_SZ or decrease request size, which is 2nd argument of TLIF_READ.

HOST-412.message: Internal error for Tool Interface function %s
HOST-412.cause: An internal error was occured in Tool Interface function.
HOST-412.remedy: Contact FANUC service representative and tell the the last number of this alarm if exists and tell the alarm messages which is occured with this alarm.

HOST-413.message: Receive buffer overflow for Tool Interface function
HOST-413.cause: Receive buffer for KAREL built-in function TLIF_READ in Tool Interface function is overflowed.
HOST-413.remedy: Greater $TLIF.$RCV_BUF_SZ or decrease the size of receive data.

HOST-414.message: 1st argument of TLIF_WRITE in KAREL is invalid for Tool I/F function
HOST-414.cause: 1st argument of TLIF_WRITE for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function isn't initialized or less than 1.
HOST-414.remedy: Fix 1st argument, which means send length, of TLIF_WRITE.

HOST-415.message: 1st argument of TLIF_WRITE in KAREL is greater than 2nd argument size
HOST-415.cause: 1st argument of TLIF_WRITE for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is greater than 2nd argument size.
HOST-415.remedy: Fix 1st argument, which means send length, or fix the array length of the 2nd argument, which is an array of BYTE for send data, in TLIF_WRITE.

HOST-416.message: 2nd argument of TLIF_READ is uninit or less than 1 in KAREL
HOST-416.cause: 2nd argument of TLIF_READ for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function isn't initialized or less than 1.
HOST-416.remedy: Fix 2nd argument, which means size of read data, of TLIF_READ.

HOST-417.message: 2nd argument of TLIF_READ in KAREL is greater than 3rd argument size
HOST-417.cause: 2nd argument of TLIF_READ for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is greater than 3rd argument size.
HOST-417.remedy: Fix 2nd argument, which means size of read data, or fix the array length of the 3rd argument, which is read array of BYTE where read data is set, in TLIF_READ.

HOST-418.message: 1st argument of TLIF_READ is uninit or less than -1 in KAREL for Tool
HOST-418.cause: 1st argument of TLIF_READ for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is uninit or less than -1.
HOST-418.remedy: Fix 1st argument, which means timeout of TLIF_READ.

HOST-419.message: 2nd argument of TLIF_CRC16 is illegal in KAREL for Tool I/F function
HOST-419.cause: 2nd argument of TLIF_CRC16 for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is uninit or less than 1 or larger than 32767.
HOST-419.remedy: Fix 2nd argument, which means length of the data, of TLIF_CRC16.

HOST-420.message: 2nd argument of TLIF_CRC16 in KAREL is greater than 1st argument size
HOST-420.cause: 2nd argument of TLIF_CRC16 for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is greater than the array length of the 1st argument.
HOST-420.remedy: Fix 2nd argument, which means length of the data, or fix 1st argument array length of BYTE of TLIF_CRC16.

HOST-421.message: 3rd argument size of TLIF_CRC16 in KAREL for Tool I/F is smaller than 2
HOST-421.cause: 3rd argument size of TLIF_CRC16 for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is smaller than 2.
HOST-421.remedy: Fix 3rd argument array size of BYTE larger than 1 in TLIF_CRC16.

HOST-422.message: 2nd argument of TLIF_READ is less than 1 in KAREL for Tool I/F function
HOST-422.cause: 2nd argument of TLIF_READ for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is less than 1.
HOST-422.remedy: Fix 2nd argument, which means size of read, in TLIF_READ.

HOST-423.message: Send buffer overflow by TLIF_WRITE in KAREL for Tool Interface function
HOST-423.cause: Send buffer for TLIF_WRITE for KAREL built-in function in Tool Interface function is overflowed.
HOST-423.remedy: Greater $TLIF.$SND_BUF_SZ or make more interval of calling TLIF_WRITE.

HOST-424.message: IO is not updated during $TLIF.$IO_TIMEOUT [ms] for Tool I/F function
HOST-424.cause: IOs for Tool Interface function are not updated durting $TLIF.$IO_TIMEOUT [ms].
HOST-424.remedy: Greater $TLIF.$IO_TIMEOUT or check cables for Tool Interface function.

HOST-425.cause: Tool answer may later than $TLIF.$TLANS_TMOUT [ms] or communication error happens.
HOST-425.remedy: Greater $TLIF.$TLANS_TMOUT or faster the answer of tool or check cables for Tool Interface function. Pay attention that I/O update is done after tool answers by RS485 if robot controller send data to tool by RS485. If tool answers later, I/O update becomes later.

HOST-426.message: Tool Interface board major version error. Board = %d, Controller = %d
HOST-426.cause: Tool Interface board version is old.
HOST-426.remedy: Contact FANUC service representative and tell this alarm message and version number in this alarm.

HOST-427.message: ROBOGUIDE doesn't support KAREL built-in for Tool Interface function
HOST-427.cause: ROBOGUIDE doesn't support KAREL built-in for Serial Communication of Tool Interface Communication Function.
HOST-427.remedy: This warning is just for notification.

IFPN-013.cause: Another pane is displaying detail screen of the button that you tried to display or change setup.

IFPN-021.cause: Button of I/F panel cannot be pressed. It is because check of condition signal is specified and it cannot be read.
IFPN-021.remedy: Check if specified signal is correct.

IFPN-023.cause: Button of I/F panel cannot be pressed. It is because check of condition signal is specified and its value is ON.

IFPN-028.remedy: Please check KAREL variable name and its data type. INTEGER, SHORT, BYTE, REAL BOOLEAN and STRING are supported. You cannot specify structure or array as a whole.
