INTP-287.cause: It failed to execute MAINT program
INTP-287.remedy: Confirm the MAINT program name is correct or MAINT program exist in acutual.

INTP-288.cause: The parameter designated by AR register does not exist.
INTP-288.remedy: Please confirm the index of AR register and the parameter in CALL/MACRO command in main program.

INTP-289.message: Can't save ffast point at program change
INTP-289.cause: When fast fault is enabled, the program was paused at the part of program change
INTP-289.remedy: Check whether the CONT terminaton exists at end of sub-program If exist, please change it to FINE. This is the limitation of the fast fault recovery function.

INTP-290.message: Fast fault recovery position is not saved
INTP-290.cause: During fast fault recovery sequence, any alarm occurs. So the fast fault recovery position is not saved.
INTP-290.remedy: Check whether the CONT terminaton exists at end of sub-program If exist, please change it to FINE. This is the limitation of the fast fault recovery function.

INTP-291.message: (%s^4, %d^5) Index for AR is not correct
INTP-291.cause: The parameter designated by AR register does not exist. But this error does not occur at present.
INTP-291.remedy: Please confirm the index of AR register and the parameter in CALL/MACRO command in main program.

INTP-292.message: more than 6 motion with DB executed
INTP-292.cause: More than six Distance Before (DB) motion options were processed at the same time.
INTP-292.remedy: Either change the termination type from CNT to FINE as in the example below, or reduce the number of DB motion options being used consecutively: 1: L P[1] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[1] = ON 2: L P[2] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[2] = ON 3: L P[3] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[3] = ON 4: L P[4] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[4] = ON 5: L P[5] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[5] = ON 6: L P[6] 2000mm/sec FINE 7: L P[7] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[7] = ON 8: L P[8] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[8] = ON 9: L P[9] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[9] = ON 10: L P[10] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[10] = ON 11: L P[11] 2000mm/sec CNT 100 DB 10mm DO[11] = ON

INTP-293.cause: A Distance Before condition was not established.
INTP-293.remedy: Change the program so that the TCP moves into the trigger region or increase the size of trigger region in order for the Distance Before condition to take effect.

INTP-294.cause: The parameter designed in CALL/MACRO instruction is not correct. This error is internal error.
INTP-294.remedy: Document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

INTP-295.cause: A Distance Before condition was not established.
INTP-295.remedy: Change the program so that the TCP moves into the trigger region or increase the size of trigger region in order for the Distance Before condition to take effect.

INTP-296.cause: Distance Before doesn't work if $SCR_GRP[ ].$M_POS_ENB is FALSE.

INTP-297.cause: Motion completed before trigger of DB condition.

INTP-300.cause: KAREL program error. This KAREL statement cannot be executed.
INTP-300.remedy: Check the KAREL translater software version.

INTP-301.cause: KAREL program error. Execution entered into a FOR loop by the GOTO statement.
INTP-301.remedy: A GOTO statement cannot be used to enter or exit a FOR loop. Check the label of the GOTO statement.

INTP-302.cause: The program stack overflowed. Too many local variables were declared or too many routines were called.
INTP-302.remedy: For KAREL programs, refer to the KAREL Reference Manual, Stack Usage and the %STACKSIZE Translator Directive.

INTP-303.cause: KAREL program error. The specified value exceeds the maximum limit.

INTP-304.cause: KAREL program error. The dimensions of the arrays are not the same.
INTP-304.remedy: Check the dimensions of the arrays.

INTP-305.cause: KAREL program error. A condition handler error occurred.
INTP-305.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-306.cause: KAREL program error. The ATTACH statement failed.
INTP-306.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-307.cause: KAREL program error. The DETACH statement failed.
INTP-307.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-308.cause: KAREL program error. The CASE statement does not match any branches.
INTP-308.remedy: Check the CASE value and branches.

INTP-309.cause: KAREL program error. The specified parameter cannot be used in the with clause of the condition handler.

INTP-310.cause: KAREL program error. The index of the array is invalid.
INTP-310.remedy: Check the length of the array and index value.

INTP-311.cause: KAREL program error. Untaught or uninitialized data was used.
INTP-311.remedy: Teach or initialize the data before using it.

INTP-312.cause: KAREL program error. The wrong axis number was used.
INTP-312.remedy: Check the axis number and the data value.

INTP-313.cause: KAREL program error. The MOTION statement cannot be executed.
INTP-313.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-314.cause: KAREL program error. Execution cannot be returned from the routine.
INTP-314.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-315.cause: KAREL program error. A built-in routine error occurred
INTP-315.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-316.cause: KAREL program error. The routine cannot be called.
INTP-316.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen. Verify the routine is loaded.

INTP-317.cause: KAREL program error. The specified condition was invalid.

INTP-318.cause: KAREL program error. The specified action was invalid.

INTP-319.cause: KAREL program error. The data type was invalid.

INTP-320.cause: KAREL program error. The built-in routine is not defined.
INTP-320.remedy: Check the appropriate option is loaded.

INTP-321.message: (%s^4, %d^5) END stmt of a func rtn
INTP-321.cause: KAREL program error. The END statement was executed in a function routine instead of a RETURN statement.
INTP-321.remedy: Add a RETURN statement to the function routine.

INTP-322.cause: KAREL program error. The argument value of a built-in routine was wrong.

INTP-323.cause: KAREL program error. The data value for the variable was too large.
INTP-323.remedy: Check the variable's type and data value.

INTP-324.cause: KAREL program error. The usage string in the OPEN FILE statement was invalid.
INTP-324.remedy: Check the usage string in the OPEN FILE statement.

INTP-325.cause: KAREL program error. The file string in the OPEN FILE statement was invalid.
INTP-325.remedy: Check the file string. If no device is specified, the default device is used.

INTP-326.cause: KAREL program error. The FILE variable is already being used.
INTP-326.remedy: Close the file before reusing the FILE variable or add a new FILE variable.

INTP-327.cause: KAREL program error. The file could not be opened.
INTP-327.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-328.cause: KAREL program error. The specified file was not opened before operation.

INTP-329.cause: KAREL program error. The value cannot be written to the variable.
INTP-329.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-330.cause: KAREL program error. Writing to the file failed.
INTP-330.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-331.cause: KAREL program error. Reading the variable failed.
INTP-331.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-332.cause: KAREL program error. Data read from the file is too short.
INTP-332.remedy: Make sure the data in the file is valid.

INTP-333.cause: KAREL program error. The string read from the file is wrong.
INTP-333.remedy: Check the data of the file.

INTP-334.cause: KAREL program error. Reading from the file failed.
INTP-334.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-335.cause: KAREL program error. A file pre-defined by the system cannot be opened.
INTP-335.remedy: Use the file defined by the system without opening it.

INTP-336.cause: KAREL program error. A file pre-defined by the system cannot be closed.
INTP-336.remedy: Do not try to close it.

INTP-337.cause: KAREL program error. This routine cannot be used.
INTP-337.remedy: Make sure you have the correct routine type and name.

INTP-338.cause: KAREL program error. Closing the file failed.
INTP-338.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-339.cause: KAREL program error. The program name is invalid.
INTP-339.remedy: Make sure you have the correct program name.

INTP-340.cause: KAREL program error. The variable name is invalid.
INTP-340.remedy: Make sure you have the correct variable name.

INTP-341.cause: KAREL program error. The variable cannot be found.
INTP-341.remedy: Verify the program name and variable name.

INTP-342.cause: KAREL program error. The data type defined by the BYNAME function and the variable type are mismatched.
INTP-342.remedy: Make sure you have the correct data type and variable type.

INTP-343.cause: KAREL program error. Too many variables are passed using the BYNAME function.
INTP-343.remedy: Decrease the number of BYNAME functions.

INTP-344.cause: KAREL program error. The buffer to read ahead from the device overflowed.

INTP-345.cause: KAREL program error. The PAUSE statement cannot be executed.
INTP-345.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-346.cause: KAREL program error. The ABORT statement cannot be executed.
INTP-346.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-347.cause: KAREL program error. The digital input signal cannot be input.
INTP-347.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-348.cause: KAREL program error. The digital output signal cannot be output.
INTP-348.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-349.cause: KAREL program error. The HOLD statement cannot be executed.
INTP-349.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-350.cause: KAREL program error. The UNHOLD statement cannot be executed.
INTP-350.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-351.cause: KAREL program error. The STOP statement cannot be executed.
INTP-351.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-352.cause: KAREL program error. The CANCEL statement cannot be executed.
INTP-352.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-353.cause: KAREL program error. The RESUME statement cannot be executed.
INTP-353.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-354.cause: KAREL program error. The break point function cannot be executed.
INTP-354.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-355.cause: KAREL program error. The AMR operated by the RETURN_AMR built-in routine was not found.

INTP-356.cause: KAREL program error. The RETURN_AMR built-in routine cannot be used for an unoperated AMR.
INTP-356.remedy: Operate the AMR using the WAIT_AMR built-in routine.

INTP-357.cause: KAREL program error. The execution of the WAIT_AMR built-in routine was cancelled.
INTP-357.remedy: The program executing the WAIT_AMR must be restarted.

INTP-358.cause: KAREL program error. The READ statement timed out.

INTP-359.cause: KAREL program error. Another READ statement was executed while a READ statement was waiting for input.

INTP-360.cause: KAREL program error. The vector value was invalid.

INTP-361.cause: KAREL program error. The X-axis direction cannot be calculated in the FRAME built-in routine because P1 and P2 are the same point.
INTP-361.remedy: Teach P1 and P2 as different points.

INTP-362.cause: KAREL program error. The X-Y plane cannot be calculated in the FRAME built-in routine because P1 and P3 are the same point.
INTP-362.remedy: Teach P1 and P3 as different points.

INTP-363.cause: KAREL program error. The X-Y plane cannot be calculated in the FRAME built-in routine because P3 is located in the X-axis direction.
INTP-363.remedy: Teach P3 out of the X-axis direction.

INTP-364.cause: KAREL program error. The target string was too short.

INTP-365.cause: KAREL program error. A FILE pre-defined by the system is not opened.
INTP-365.remedy: Check the use of this file.

INTP-366.cause: KAREL program error. The last file operation failed.
INTP-366.remedy: Reset the error using the CLR_IO_STAT built-in routine.

INTP-367.cause: KAREL program error. I/O mode operates only from binary to hexdecimal.

INTP-368.cause: KAREL program error. The specified program cannot be used.
INTP-368.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-369.cause: KAREL program error. The WAIT_AMR built-in routine timed out.
INTP-369.remedy: If an AMR was expected within the time-out value check logic in the task that sould have posted the AMR

INTP-370.cause: KAREL program error. The vision CPU board is not plugged in.
INTP-370.remedy: Plug in the vision CPU board.

INTP-371.cause: KAREL program error. The operation overflowed in the vision built-in routine.
INTP-371.remedy: Modify program so fewer vision builtins are executing at the same time.

INTP-372.cause: KAREL program error. The vision built-in routine is not defined.
INTP-372.remedy: Check the appropriate option is loaded.

INTP-373.cause: KAREL program error. The parameter to the vision built-in routine is invalid.
INTP-373.remedy: Check the parameter of the vision built-in routine.

INTP-374.cause: KAREL program error. The return value from the vision built-in routine is invalid.
INTP-374.remedy: Check the return value from the vision built-in routine.

INTP-375.cause: KAREL program error. System variables cannot be passed using the BYNAME function.
INTP-375.remedy: Pass without using BYNAME or use GET_VAR and SET_VAR instead.

INTP-376.cause: A MOVE statement was executed in an interrupt routine while a motion in the interrupted program was still in progress.
INTP-376.remedy: One (or both) of the following should correct this problem: 1. Add CANCEL or STOP condition handler action before the call to the interrupt routine in the condition handler. 2. Add a DELAY 500 statement before the first move in the interrupt routine to allow the motion to complete.

INTP-377.cause: This local condition can't be recovered.
INTP-377.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

INTP-378.cause: Local variable or parameter is used for the condition.
INTP-378.remedy: Use global variable to recover local condition.

INTP-379.cause: An invalid condition handler number was used in a condition handler definition, or an ENABLE, DISABLE, or PURGE statement or action
INTP-379.remedy: Correct the condition handler number. Condition handler numbers must be in the range 1-1000.

INTP-380.cause: A invalid program number has been specified in an ABORT PROGRAM, PAUSE PROGRAM, or CONTINUE PROGRAM condition or action.
INTP-380.remedy: Use a valid program number. Prorgam numbers must be in the range 1..$SCR,$MAXNUMTASK + 2.

INTP-381.cause: An invalid delay time has been specified in DELAY statement.
INTP-381.remedy: Use a valid delay time. Delay time must be in the range 0..86400000.

INTP-382.cause: An invalid value has been specified in bit field
INTP-382.remedy: Use a valid value for the bit field.

INTP-383.cause: The specified path node is out of range.

INTP-384.cause: The indicated value cannot be used for the CNT instruction.

INTP-400.cause: Too many motions are executed at the same time.
INTP-400.remedy: Decrease the number of motions executed at the same time. Execute the next motion after the completion of the last motion.

INTP-401.cause: Paused motion exists after the motion was resumed.
INTP-401.remedy: Resume the motion that was previously paused.

INTP-410.cause: Loading/Running optimized program without OPTM loaded.
INTP-410.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Check program and options.

INTP-420.remedy: Please check motion type and options

INTP-422.remedy: Please turn on stitch enable signal

INTP-424.cause: Setting of Stitch speed is illegal.

INTP-425.cause: Please check motion type The motion statement is JOINT motion.
INTP-425.remedy: Change the motion statement to LINEAR motion.

INTP-426.cause: Another program is in stitch mode.
INTP-426.remedy: Please force abort another program if it is executing stitch or it paused in stitch area.

INTP-427.cause: Master/Slave/SlaveAlone program cannot call KAREL program
INTP-427.remedy: Master/Slave/SlaveAlone program cannot call KAREL program

INTP-428.cause: Analog I/O with conversion data can not use in condition program.
INTP-428.remedy: Please delete AI/O instructions in the condition program.

INTP-429.cause: When analog I/O conversion fuction is used, mixed logic has to be used for WAIT condition.
INTP-429.remedy: Please use mixed logic instruction for WAIT condition.

INTP-430.cause: The program does not have all motion groups. All motion groups are required for Dry Run.
INTP-430.remedy: Enable all motion groups for the program. If some groups should not be affected by Dry Run, set $DRYRUN.$GRP_MASK to indicate which motion groups should be affected. 1 = affect this group; 0 = do not affect this group.

INTP-431.cause: Dry Run cannot start in an incremental motion statement.
INTP-431.remedy: Exit the incremental motion statement by moving the cursor to another line, or do backward execution.

INTP-432.cause: Dry Run cannot start in a circular motion statement.
INTP-432.remedy: Exit the circular motion by moving the cursor to another line, or perform backward execution.

INTP-433.cause: Dry Run is activated on interruption routine. Dry Run can not start from an interruption routine.
INTP-433.remedy: Perform a backward execution to exit the interrupt routine.

INTP-434.message: Please do BWD to exit P-SPS
INTP-434.cause: This is used as a cause code for INTP-433, to recommend backward execution.

INTP-435.cause: An error occurred in Dry Run execution.
INTP-435.remedy: Refer to additional errors for more information.

INTP-436.cause: The item specified in left side of assignment statement is not available for output.
INTP-436.remedy: Do not use the item for output.

INTP-437.cause: Depth of Marker nesting is greater than 10.
INTP-437.remedy: Reduce the nesting level of Marker.

INTP-438.cause: The Marker being read is not defined by any expression.

INTP-439.cause: Multiple tasks are attempting to execute the same Marker at the same time.

INTP-440.cause: Program is paused by TC_ONLINE, because the result of the defined expression is FALSE.

INTP-441.cause: The setting of Background Logic cannot be changed when the Background Logic is running.

INTP-442.cause: The Background Logic that was running at power down was changed before this COLD start. This Background Logic is stopped.

INTP-443.cause: There is an operator or data that cannot be used in Mixed Logic. Mixed Logic statements are those that have parentheses.
INTP-443.remedy: Use the operator or data in a normal Logic instruction.

INTP-444.cause: There is an operator or data that cannot be used in Fast mode Background Logic. Fast Mode Background Logic can have only I/O ports and logical operators.
INTP-444.remedy: Remove the operator or data, or execute this program in Normal mode Background Logic

INTP-445.cause: There is an indirection of index, (ex. DI[R[1]]), in Fast mode Background Logic. Fast mode Background Logic cannot use indirection.
INTP-445.remedy: Remove the indirection, or execute this program in Normal mode Background Logic

INTP-446.cause: The parentheses nesting is too deep. The maximum number of nesting is 11.
INTP-446.remedy: Divide the expression into two lines.

INTP-447.cause: The combination of parentheses is wrong.

INTP-448.cause: Total size of Fast mode programs is greater than 4000 steps. 4000 steps is approx. 4000 operands.
INTP-448.remedy: Set execution mode of some Background programs to Normal

INTP-449.cause: There is a recursive reference of a Marker.

INTP-450.cause: Master/Slave/SlaveAlone program cannot call KAREL program
INTP-450.remedy: Master/Slave/SlaveAlone program cannot call KAREL program

INTP-451.cause: Master/Slave/SlaveAlone program cannot call Normal program which has motion group.
INTP-451.remedy: Master/Slave/SlaveAlone program can call Normal program which does not have motion group.

INTP-452.cause: Master/Slave/SlaveAlone program can call different type of program.
INTP-452.remedy: Master/Slave/SlaveAlone program can call only same type of program.

INTP-453.cause: Slave program cannot be execute without remote status.

INTP-454.cause: Program type is different between caller program and called program.

INTP-455.cause: Master program does not have the same motion group which is specified by the link pattern of robot link data.
INTP-455.remedy: Master program must have the same motion group which is specified by the link pattern of robot link data.

INTP-456.cause: Slave program does not have the same motion group which is specified by the slave group of robot link data.
INTP-456.remedy: Slave program must have the same motion group which is specified by the slave group of robot link data.

INTP-457.cause: Current tool frame number of master robot is different from the master tool No of robot link data of the slave program.
INTP-457.remedy: Current tool frame number of master robot and the master tool No of robot link data of the slave program must be same number.

INTP-458.cause: Since robot is still moving, it is impossible to synchronize.
INTP-458.remedy: After robot stops completely, countinue the program again.

INTP-459.cause: The motion statement of slave program is JOINT motion.
INTP-459.remedy: Change the motion statement of slave program to LINEAR motion.

INTP-460.message: (%s^4, %d^5) Cannot use JOINT pos for Slave
INTP-460.cause: The position data of slave program is JOINT type.
INTP-460.remedy: Change the position data of slave program to LINEAR type.

INTP-461.cause: Master program is executed by TP.
INTP-461.remedy: Slave program is paused, when master program is executed by TP.

INTP-462.cause: Master program is executed by TP.
INTP-462.remedy: Slave program is paused, when master program is executed by TP.

INTP-463.cause: The motion group of specified program becomes to be master.
INTP-463.remedy: Change the robot to normal from master. Then, please try to execute again.

INTP-464.cause: The motion group of specified program becomes to be slave.
INTP-464.remedy: Change the robot to normal from slave. Then, please try to execute again.

INTP-465.cause: Tracking of slave program is failed.
INTP-465.remedy: Change the robot to normal from slave. Then, please try to execute again.

INTP-466.cause: Robot link calibration has not been done yet.

INTP-467.cause: The slave program cannot use Incremental instruction.

INTP-468.cause: The slave program cannot use Offset instruction.

INTP-469.cause: Synchronize of Master is falid for BWD.
INTP-469.remedy: Change the Slave robot to be synchronize waiting state.

INTP-470.cause: BWD of Slave program is not supported.
INTP-470.remedy: BWD of Slave program is not supported.

INTP-471.cause: Current status of the robot is Master(Manual).
INTP-471.remedy: When robot is Master(Manual), you cannot use external program execution. To use external program execution, please change the status to Master(Alone) at the manual operation screen.

INTP-472.cause: Current status of the robot is Slave(Manual).
INTP-472.remedy: When robot is Slave(Manual), you cannot execute other Slave program. To execute other Slave program execution, please hold the program to exit Slave(Manual) status.

INTP-473.cause: The synchro ID of the specified program is zero.
INTP-473.remedy: Synchro ID 0 is not available number. Please set another synchro ID.

INTP-474.cause: The program whose synchro ID is different from current synchro ID is executed.
INTP-474.remedy: Please change the synchro ID to fit the current synchro ID.

INTP-477.cause: Slave program cannot be executed directly.
INTP-477.remedy: Slave program must be called by normal program.

INTP-478.message: This group can not be MASTER
INTP-478.cause: This motion group is not specified as master in SETUP.
INTP-478.remedy: Use another group as master or change SETUP.

INTP-479.cause: HOSTNAME, IP Address or group number about MASTER is not correct.
INTP-479.remedy: Confirm RobotLink and HOST Comm TCP/IP SETUP.

INTP-480.cause: HOSTNAME, IP Address or group number about SLAVE is not correct.
INTP-480.remedy: Confirm RobotLink and HOST Comm TCP/IP SETUP.

INTP-481.cause: Synchronization ID in program is invalid.
INTP-481.remedy: Modify Synchronization ID at Program List Screen.

INTP-482.cause: Link Pattern Number in program is invalid.
INTP-482.remedy: Modify Link Pattern Number at Program List Screen.

INTP-483.cause: Master Number in program is invalid.
INTP-483.remedy: Modify Master Number at Program List Screen.

INTP-484.cause: Specified group number about MASTER is invalid.
INTP-484.remedy: Confirm group number setup about MASTER.

INTP-485.cause: Specified group number about SLAVE is invalid.
INTP-485.remedy: Confirm group number setup about SLAVE.

INTP-487.message: No Valid SLAVE in Link Pattern
INTP-487.cause: No valid SLAVE is specified in Link Pattern data.
INTP-487.remedy: Confirm Link Pattern at RobotLink SETUP screen.

INTP-488.cause: At comm-buffer init, comm-processor is too busy.

INTP-489.cause: Hostname or IP Address, Group number setup is invalid.
INTP-489.remedy: Check HOST Comm TCP/IP and RobotLink SETUP.

INTP-490.remedy: Check another robot and robot link program

INTP-491.remedy: Check another robot is paused or communication status

INTP-494.cause: Schedule number for PROC_SYNC is not initialized
INTP-494.remedy: Use SYNC_SCHED instruction prior to using INPOS, PROC_STRT or PROC_SYNC instructions

INTP-495.cause: PROC_END statement is not found after PROC_START
INTP-495.remedy: Use PROC_END instruction after a PROC_START instruction or use PROC_SYNC instruction

INTP-530.cause: PS statement is not available for this system.

INTP-531.cause: Number of PS motions has reached the limit.

INTP-532.cause: Number of PS items per one motion has reached the limit.

INTP-533.cause: PS logic statement is not valid.

INTP-534.cause: PS time is not available for this motion type.

IRPK-072.remedy: Please select the action for real robot.

IRPK-073.remedy: Don't power off controllers during the login. Please retry login and if the problem persists, please contact FANUC.

IRPK-074.cause: Failed to synchronize the data of iRPickTool.
IRPK-074.remedy: Please do [F6: SYNC DATA] again. If the problem persists, please contact FANUC.

IRPK-075.message: This operation is not allowed during production.
IRPK-075.cause: There is a controller that is running a TP program.
IRPK-075.remedy: Stop the TP program and retry the operation.

IRPK-076.message: There are already all controllers which can be added to treeview.
IRPK-076.cause: There are already all controllers which can be added to treeview.
IRPK-076.remedy: You need not to add any more robots.

IRPK-077.message: There is already the robot of the selected controller and group number.
IRPK-077.cause: There is already the robot of the selected controller and group number.
IRPK-077.remedy: Please select the unique controller and group number.

IRPK-078.cause: There might be a controller that is powered on or off during logging in.
IRPK-078.remedy: Confirm that the all contollers have finished the boot and retry login. If the problem persists, please contact FANUC.

IRPK-079.cause: There is a controller which has different setup data of iRPickTool from this controller.
IRPK-079.remedy: Login to the controller that has the correct setup data and click [F6: SYNC DATA] on the setup page of iRPickTool. The setup data is synchronized.

IRPK-080.message: Can't use Action of '%s^1' with load balance for each model ID.
IRPK-080.cause: Sensor action cannot be used with load balance for each model ID.
IRPK-080.remedy: Please specify the load balance for all model IDs in the parent conveyor setup page.

IRPK-081.message: UPDATE TREE is necessary because data has been changed in runtime.
IRPK-081.cause: Data has been changed in runtime.
IRPK-081.remedy: Please perform UPDATE TREE in workcell setup page.

IRPK-082.message: Can't update configuration because there is a data difference.
IRPK-082.cause: Can't update configuration because there is a data difference among controllers.
IRPK-082.remedy: Please synchronize the data for all robots by [SYNC DATA] in workcell setup page.

IRPK-083.cause: Another recipe process is already running.
IRPK-083.remedy: Please try again after the running recipe process finishes.

IRPK-084.cause: Recipe operation of iRPickTool timed out.
IRPK-084.remedy: Please retry after a while and if the problem persists, please contact FANUC.

IRPK-085.remedy: This function cannot be used in circular tracking.

IRPK-086.cause: Buffer is not enabled in fixed station.
IRPK-086.remedy: Please enable buffer in fixed station.

IRPK-087.message: This is dedicated instruction for pre-grouping.
IRPK-087.cause: This is dedicated instruction for pre-grouping.

IRPK-088.message: There is an invalid pre-grouping setting.
IRPK-088.cause: There is an invalid pre-grouping setting.
IRPK-088.remedy: Please check the settings of pre-grouping.

IRPK-089.message: Sensor cannot be used in conveyor used for pre-grouping.
IRPK-089.cause: Sensor cannot be used in conveyor used for pre-grouping.
IRPK-089.remedy: Please remove the sensor in the conveyor used for pre-grouping.

IRPK-090.message: Reference cell is not set up.
IRPK-090.cause: Reference cell is not set up.
IRPK-090.remedy: Set the reference cell of tray

IRPK-091.message: Data for newer version software is used.
IRPK-091.cause: There are some controllers which do not support some functions.

IRPK-092.cause: The shift key was released while the program is executing.
IRPK-092.remedy: Hold the shift key and press the FWD key to resume execution.

IRPK-093.remedy: Check the selected and current group number.

IRPK-094.remedy: Check the selected and current conveyor.

IRPK-202.cause: There was an error running the named task.
IRPK-202.remedy: See the associated cause code posted with this error.

IRPK-203.cause: An error was encountered while getting the value of a KAREL or system variable.
IRPK-203.remedy: Check the associated cause code. Make sure that the variable exists, and is spelled correctly.

IRPK-204.cause: An error was encountered while setting the value of a KAREL or system variable.
IRPK-204.remedy: Check the associated cause code. Make sure that the variable exists, and is spelled correctly.

IRPK-205.cause: An error occured while trying to simulate an I/O Input port
IRPK-205.remedy: Make sure that all the I/O inputs are cofigured correctly and assigned to a valid input port.

IRPK-206.cause: An option which was required was not installed.

IRPK-207.cause: A notification that data recording for collecting profiler data with PickPRO - duty, cycle time, power consumption or life estimation has started.

IRPK-208.cause: A notification that data recording for collecting profiler data with PickPRO - duty, cycle time, power consumption or life estimation has ended.

IRPK-209.cause: Invalid data was received for Profiler recording.
IRPK-209.remedy: Specify a valid value for duration, parts or cycles to record profiler data.

IRPK-210.cause: Sending or receiving data between one or more controllers failed because the those controllers were offline (Ethernet).
IRPK-210.remedy: Check the Ethernet cables and connections and ensure the controllers are on-line.

IRPK-211.cause: An invalid Recipe id or name was encountered.
IRPK-211.remedy: Specify a valid recipe id (1-99) or a valid name.

IRPK-212.cause: An invalid conveyor id or name was encountered.
IRPK-212.remedy: Specify a valid conveyor id (1-32) or a valid name.

IRPK-213.cause: An invalid tray id or name was encountered.
IRPK-213.remedy: Specify a valid tray id (1-16) or a valid name.

IRPK-214.cause: An invalid Conveyor station id or name was encountered.
IRPK-214.remedy: Specify a valid conveyor station id (1-84) or a valid name.

IRPK-215.cause: An invalid sensor id or name was encountered.
IRPK-215.remedy: Specify a valid sensor id (1-32) or a valid name.

IRPK-216.cause: An invalid Fixed station id or name was encountered.
IRPK-216.remedy: Specify a valid fixed station id (1-84) or a valid name.

IRPK-217.cause: An invalid robot id or name was encountered.
IRPK-217.remedy: Specify a valid robot id (1-32) or a valid name.

IRPK-218.cause: An invalid gripper id or name was encountered.
IRPK-218.remedy: Specify a valid gripper id (1-32) or a valid name.

IRPK-219.cause: An invalid Gripper zone id was encountered.
IRPK-219.remedy: Specify a valid gripper zone id (1-20)

IRPK-220.cause: An invalid Activation I/O for a gripper zone was encountered.
IRPK-220.remedy: Specify a valid and configured I/O port for the gripper zone activation.

IRPK-221.cause: An invalid Part presence I/O for a gripper zone was encountered.
IRPK-221.remedy: Specify a valid and configured I/O port for the gripper zone part presence.

IRPK-222.cause: An invalid motion group number was encountered.

IRPK-223.cause: The UTOOL for a gripper zone is NILPOS
IRPK-223.remedy: This is only a warning. It is not typical that the gripper zone utool is nilpos. Ensure the zone utool is correct.

IRPK-224.remedy: Specify a valid tracking schedule (1-8) for the conveyor station.

IRPK-225.cause: The RIPE index for a robot is invalid.
IRPK-225.remedy: Specify a valid RIPE id based on RIPE setup for the Robot.If RIPE setup was not done, it must be setup first.

IRPK-226.remedy: A valid operation is Pick=1 or Drop=2. Make sure that the operation argument in your TP program calls is correct and ensure that the proper operation is selected in the iRPick Setup UI.

IRPK-227.cause: An invalid pick or drop quantiy was encountered.
IRPK-227.remedy: A valid pick or drop quantity should match with the number of zones used in the gripper. Its valid range is 1-20.

IRPK-228.cause: An invalid I/O type was encountered.
IRPK-228.remedy: Specify a valid I/O type such as DO or RDO based on the definitions in kliotyps.kl

IRPK-229.cause: An invalid I/O value was encountered.
IRPK-229.remedy: Specify a valid I/O value such as ON=1, OFF=2 or PULSE=3

IRPK-230.cause: An invalid I/O port number was encountered.
IRPK-230.remedy: Specify a valid I/O port number

IRPK-231.cause: An invalid pulse time was specified for I/O
IRPK-231.remedy: Specify a valid integer I/O pulse time (ms).

IRPK-232.cause: An invalid position register number was encountered.
IRPK-232.remedy: Specify a position register value that is available in the DATA Position Registers menu.

IRPK-233.cause: An invalid numeric register number was encountered.
IRPK-233.remedy: Specify a numeric register value that is available in the DATA Numeric Registers menu.

IRPK-234.cause: An invalid vision register number was encountered.
IRPK-234.remedy: Specify a vision register value that is available in the DATA Vision Registers menu.

IRPK-235.cause: An invalid string register number was encountered.
IRPK-235.remedy: Specify a string register value that is available in the DATA String Registers menu.

IRPK-236.cause: An invalid name was encountered for an iRPick object such as conveyor, fixed. station, sensor, etc.
IRPK-236.remedy: Specify a valid name in the User interface for the object. Also verify the String Register that has a valid string.

IRPK-237.cause: A validation of I/O port that exists in another controller failed (timed out)
IRPK-237.remedy: This check is performed over RIPE. Check if all controllers are on-line or if the CPU load on the other controller is high.

IRPK-238.cause: The parameter passed to TP program was expected to be an integer but is not.
IRPK-238.remedy: Specify a valid integer value for the appropriate argument of the call statement.

IRPK-239.cause: The parameter passed to TP program was expected to be a REAL but is not.
IRPK-239.remedy: Specify a valid REAL value for the appropriate argument of the call statement.

IRPK-240.cause: The UTOOL for a gripper zone is invalid
IRPK-240.remedy: Ensure the zone utool is initialized and is correct.

IRPK-241.cause: The Uframe number for a Fixed Station is invalid.
IRPK-241.remedy: Ensure a Valid Uframe number is specified in the Fixed Station menu and also in the PKFSGETUF call in the fixed stn TP program.

IRPK-242.cause: An uninit value was encountered while executing a routine or a program.
IRPK-242.remedy: You should not generally see this error. Try to trace the execution history of the program to find an input value that is that is uninitialized. Else, contact FANUC.

IRPK-243.cause: A reallocation or resizing of a KAREL or system variable failed.
IRPK-243.remedy: You should not generally see this error. iRPick attempts to keep memory size optimal using only as many indexes of an array as possible. If it failed, contact FANUC.

IRPK-244.cause: An invalid encoder id was encountered.
IRPK-244.remedy: Specify a valid I/O encoder number in the tracking schedule.

IRPK-245.cause: There is problem to sync this encoder

IRPK-246.remedy: This is just a message to indictate encoder has been synced

IRPK-247.cause: There is problem to sync this enthernet Encoder

IRPK-248.cause: QMGR global variable does not exist

IRPK-249.cause: Can not find reference system variable

IRPK-250.cause: An error occurred while getting data from the indicated position register.
IRPK-250.remedy: Check the data type in the position and make sure it is cartesian type. Check if all controllers are on-line because an attempt to get a Pos Reg from a different controller could have been made.

IRPK-251.cause: An error occurred while setting data to the indicated position register.
IRPK-251.remedy: From related error messages, check the source of the position data. Check if all controllers are on-line because an attempt to set a Pos Reg in a different controller could have been made.

IRPK-252.cause: An error occurred while getting CONFIG.
IRPK-252.remedy: From related error messages, check the source of the position data. Check if all controllers are on-line because an attempt to get a Pos Reg in a different controller could have been made.

IRPK-253.cause: A routine was called with an invalid iRPickTool object type such as CStn, FStn, conveyor, etc.
IRPK-253.remedy: Check that all setup was done correctly. Each robot must have a pick and drop stn. Each conveyor must have at least one sensor and one Conveyor station.

IRPK-254.cause: An invalid part id or name was encountered.
IRPK-254.remedy: Specify a valid part id for the Conveyor or Fixed Station where the part is used. Also, make sure that the part has a valid name.

IRPK-255.cause: Part presence check failed for gripper zone. The part was either not detected during pick or was detected after a place operation.
IRPK-255.remedy: Check why the part is not getting picked or placed during pick and place operations. Also check part presence sensors and if there is a problem with vacuum or activation system

IRPK-256.message: Insufficient gripper zones to pick or drop
IRPK-256.cause: There are not enough gripper zones to pick or place the specified quantity of parts.
IRPK-256.remedy: Add zones to the gripper in the Gripper menu or reduce the quantity of parts to pick or place.

IRPK-257.cause: A new recipe is being created

IRPK-258.cause: A new recipe was successfully created

IRPK-259.cause: The active recipe is being saved.

IRPK-260.cause: The active recipe was successfully saved

IRPK-265.cause: Recipes are being exported to the default file device.

IRPK-266.cause: Recipe export to the default file device completed successfully.

IRPK-267.cause: Recipes are being imported from the default file device.

IRPK-268.cause: Recipe import from the default file device completed successfully.

IRPK-269.cause: An attempt to switch recipes is being made

IRPK-270.cause: An attempt to restore the active recipe is being made

IRPK-271.cause: A recipe Export was attempted but there are no saved or created recipes to export.
IRPK-271.remedy: First create at least one recipe.

IRPK-272.cause: A recipe Import was attempted but there are no recipes on the default file device.
IRPK-272.remedy: Check that the IRPICKTOOL directory with the individual RECIPEx directories exist in the default file device.

IRPK-273.remedy: This was an unusual error. Contact FANUC for this error and the status number that is included in this message.

IRPK-274.cause: An attempt was made to delete the active recipe.
IRPK-274.remedy: You are not allowed to delete the active recipe. You can switch to a different recipe and then delete this recipe.

IRPK-275.message: Invalid device for Recipe Import or Export
IRPK-275.cause: An attempt was made to import recipes from or export recipes to an invalid file device.
IRPK-275.remedy: The valid devices for import and export are MC:, UD1:, UT1: and RD:.

IRPK-276.cause: A notification that the controller received a DI signal to initiate a recipe change.

IRPK-277.cause: An attempt to switch recipes was made when there were recent changes to setup data that have not yet been saved to the current recipe.
IRPK-277.remedy: You must either Save the recent changes to the current recipe or Restore last saved data before switching recipes.

IRPK-278.cause: The existing object sizes are inadequate to initialize the recipe that you are trying to load.
IRPK-278.remedy: This error is posted with other error messages that indicate which objects require expansion. Check the error log and then use the Object Config menu in the Workcell to expand the sizes of the required objects.

IRPK-279.cause: The size of the robot object is inadequate to initialize the recipe that you are trying to load.
IRPK-279.remedy: Use the Object Config menu in the Workcell to expand the size of the robot object.

IRPK-280.cause: The size of the tray object is inadequate to initialize the recipe that you are trying to load.
IRPK-280.remedy: Use the Object Config menu in the Workcell to expand the size of the tray object.

IRPK-281.cause: The size of the gripper object is inadequate to initialize the recipe that you are trying to load.
IRPK-281.remedy: Use the Object Config menu in the Workcell to expand the size of the gripper object.

IRPK-282.cause: The size of the zone object is inadequate to initialize the recipe that you are trying to load.
IRPK-282.remedy: Use the Object Config menu in the Workcell to expand the size of the zone object.

IRPK-283.cause: The size of the sensor object is inadequate to initialize the recipe that you are trying to load.
IRPK-283.remedy: Use the Object Config menu in the Workcell to expand the size of the sensor object.

IRPK-284.cause: The size of the Conveyor Station object is inadequate to initialize the recipe that you are trying to load.
IRPK-284.remedy: Use the Object Config menu in the Workcell to expand the size of the Conveyor Station object.

IRPK-285.cause: The size of the Fixed Station object is inadequate to initialize the recipe that you are trying to load.
IRPK-285.remedy: Use the Object Config menu in the Workcell to expand the size of the Fixed Station object.

IRPK-286.cause: The size of the conveyor object is inadequate to initialize the recipe that you are trying to load.
IRPK-286.remedy: Use the Object Config menu in the Workcell to expand the size of the conveyor object.

IRPK-287.cause: You changed setup data that requires cycle power of the controller to take effect.
IRPK-287.remedy: Cycle the power on the controller.

IRPK-288.cause: A recipe Move was attempted but there are no recipes in the recipe controller
IRPK-288.remedy: Check that the iRPICKTOOL directory with the individual RECIPEx directories exist in the recipe controller from which you wish to move the recipe to another controller.

IRPK-289.cause: A recipe load was disallowed due to saved robot id not matching with the actual assigned RIPE Id for it now. This could happen if you changed the RIPE ring size by adding new members after you saved the recipe.
IRPK-289.remedy: The only way to recover the original recipe is to edit the PKROBxx.xml file which has the RIPE mismatch.

IRPK-290.cause: A recipe load was disallowed because the actual controllers have RIPE setup but the recipe does not or vice versa.
IRPK-290.remedy: This is an invalid unsupported configuration. You should abandon using the old recipe. Create a new recipe instead.

IRPK-291.message: Program with group mask zero is run
IRPK-291.cause: A non-motion program that has a group mask of zero was run.
IRPK-291.remedy: This is only a warning message. When this is posted, it means that Dynamic load balance function is not available. Dynamic load balance works only with production programs that have a non-zero group mask. For example, if you run PNS0001.tp with group mask zero from which you RUN your actual production program AMAIN.TP which has a group mask of 1, then you will see this message. To avoid the error, you can change PNS0001.tp to have group mask of 1 and then CALL AMAIN.TP instead of RUN AMAIN.TP.

IRPK-292.cause: A layer number which does not exist in the specified tray has been encountered.
IRPK-292.remedy: Check the KAREL macro call in which the invalid layer number was specified and correct it.

IRPK-293.message: Only some controllers support Plug & Play
IRPK-293.cause: Not all controllers contain the J945 (iRPickTool).
IRPK-293.remedy: Ensure that all controllers in the workcell have J945. You cannot have this option in only some controllers.

IRPK-294.cause: PLC initiated recipe operation failed due to timeout or other reasons.Timeout means that the robot did not receive the expected signal - a GI or DI on time from the PLC.
IRPK-294.remedy: PLC should respond to the controller's signal requests within 30 seconds.Refer to the program PK_PLC_RECIPE_OPERATION.TP for a detailed understanding of the handshake process.

IRPK-295.cause: A notification that the controller received a DI signal to initiate a recipe operation.

ISD-000.cause: This error is displayed when the ISD system encounters a problem that it is unable to solve internally.
ISD-000.remedy: Write down the exact error number and message displayed. Write down exactly what your robot was doing at the time of the failure. Make sure you include: Program name, line number, the robot's location in the workcell, any cell I/O or other communication activity. This fault is usually fixed when you perform a COLD start. If that does not work, contact your supervisor or call the FANUC America Corporation Hot Line.

ISD-001.cause: This error is posted when the system detects excessive pressure in the dispensing material. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: • The dispenser line (gun nozzle, hose, etc.) is clogged. • The dispensing rate is too high. • The high pressure limit value is too low. • The high pressure time out value is too short.
ISD-001.remedy: Perform the following operations: 1. Make sure no clogs exist in the dispensing tubing. 2. Make sure the dispensing flow rate is not too high. 3. Make sure the high pressure limit value is appropriate.

ISD-002.cause: This error is posted when the system detects low pressure in the dispensing material. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: • The dispenser line (gun nozzle, hose, and so forth) was removed. • The dispensing rate is too low. • The low pressure limit value was set too high. • The low pressure time out value was set too short.
ISD-002.remedy: Check the following items: • Make sure that the dispensing line is ok. • Make sure that the dispensing flow rate is not too low. • Make sure that the low pressure limit value is appropriate.

ISD-003.cause: This error is posted when the system detects excessive pressure in the material supply line. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: • The supply pressure was set too high. • The high pressure limit value was set too low. • The high pressure time out value was set too short.
ISD-003.remedy: Check the following items: • Make sure that the pressure is appropriate at the supply pump. • Make sure that the high pressure limit value is appropriate. • Make sure that the high pressure time out value is appropriate.

ISD-004.cause: This error is posted when the system detects low pressure in the material supply. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: • The supply line (hose, and so forth) was removed. • A low pressure limit value was set too high. • A low pressure time out value was set too short.
ISD-004.remedy: Check the following items: • Make sure that the supply line is ok. • Make sure that the low pressure limit value is appropriate. • Make sure that the low pressure time out value is appropriate.

ISD-005.cause: This warning is posted when the meter has reached its stroke limit during dispensing. After this occurs, the system automatically reverses the meter direction, and resumes dispensing. However, the quality of the dispensed bead might not be acceptable, because of the transition during meter direction reversal.
ISD-005.remedy: Perform the following operations: 1. Modify your program and use the provided macros to reposition the meter before you start dispensing for the seam. 2. Lower the flow rate so that it can cover the entire seam without meter direction.

ISD-006.cause: The motor velocity has reached its maximum limit.
ISD-006.remedy: Lower the flow rate to within the acceptable motor velocity limit.

ISD-007.cause: This error is posted when the meter has tripped the overtravel limit switch.
ISD-007.remedy: Continuously press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys on the teach pendant at the same time while you jog the meter away from overtravel position. Be sure to keep the SHIFT key pressed during this operation so that overtravel condition can be bypassed until it is cleared.

ISD-008.cause: The meter has tripped the overtravel limit switch.
ISD-008.remedy: Press and hold the SHIFT key and then press the RESET button on the teach pendant. While you are still pressing the SHIFT key, jog the meter away from overtravel position. Be sure to keep the shift button pressed during the above operation so that overtravel condition can be bypassed until it is cleared.

ISD-009.cause: The meter has reached its stroke limit during prepressuring. This typically occurs when the meter has traveled in the reverse direction to decrease pressure.
ISD-009.remedy: 1. Make sure supply pressure is not too high. 2. Slightly increase the $isd_config[].$repos_ofst value.

ISD-010.cause: The digital servo system for the process axis has detected an error.

ISD-011.cause: The index value or I/O port type is incorrectly assigned.
ISD-011.remedy: If you want to use this I/O port, set the port index and I/O type to the correct values. Verify that a valid value is shown on the I/O menu for this I/O port instead. If you do not want to use this I/O point

ISD-012.cause: This error is posted when the ISD servo is not ready.
ISD-012.remedy: Usually, this error occurs when the servo power is turned off because of a strapped OT sensor, the machine is locked or an EMERGENCY STOP has occurred. Determine the cause and turn on the power.

ISD-013.cause: This error is posted when the SS[] instruction is executed while the meter is doing the reposition operation.
ISD-013.remedy: Insert the check repos macro in the program so that the program waits for a reposition to complete before starting the dispensing operation.

ISD-014.cause: The meter has reached its stroke limit while trying to decrease the pressure during prepressurization.
ISD-014.remedy: 1. Make sure supply pressure is not too high. 2. Increase the $isd_config[eq].$repos_ofst value..

ISD-015.cause: The meter has travelled its maximum distance allowed for prepressurization.
ISD-015.remedy: 1. Increase the $isd_config[eq].$maxprp_strk value to allow for a longer travel distance. 2. Check for a material leak in the dispensing line.

ISD-016.cause: The analog input tick of pressure transducer has exceeded the max value of the specific I/O module. This error maybe caused by disconnection of the transducer.
ISD-016.remedy: Check the wiring of the pressure transducers.

ISD-017.cause: The material pressure did not build up within the specified time (in SETUP/ISD menu) after the meter has moved to the reload position.
ISD-017.remedy: 1. Check for material supply system to the meter. 2. Set a larger value in Reload time out item in SETUP/ISD menu. The units are in msec.

ISD-018.cause: This error is posted when the system detects excessive pressure in the second dispensing material. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: A dispenser line (gun nozzle, hose, for example) is clogged.
ISD-018.remedy: Check the following: • Make sure that there is no clog in the dispensing tubing. • Make sure dispensing flow rate is not too high. • Make sure high pressure limit value is appropriate.

ISD-019.cause: This error is posted when the system detects inadequate pressure in the second dispensing material. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: • The dispenser line (gun nozzle, hose, etc.) has been removed.
ISD-019.remedy: • Make sure dispensing line is ok. • Make sure the dispensing flow rate is not too low. • Make sure the low pressure limit value is appropriate. • Make sure the low pressure time out value is appropriate.

ISD-020.cause: This error is posted when the system detects excessive pressure in the second material supply. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: • The supply pressure was set too high. • The high pressure limit value was set too low. • The high pressure time out value was set too short.
ISD-020.remedy: • Make sure the pressure is appropriate at the supply pump. • Make sure the high pressure limit value is appropriate. • Make sure the high pressure time out value is appropriate.

ISD-021.cause: This error is posted when the system detects inadequate pressure in the second material supply. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: • The supply line (hose, etc.) has been removed. • The low pressure limit value was set too high. • The low pressure time out value was set too short.
ISD-021.remedy: • Make sure the supply line is ok. • Make sure the low pressure limit value is appropriate. • Make sure the low pressure time out value is appropriate.

ISD-022.cause: This warning is posted when the inactive meter could not finish reloading before the active meter reaches the Pre-Near-Empty position. This is where the sub-meter should start adjusting the pressure value for meter switching. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: • The supply pressure was not high enough. • The Pre-Near-Empty location is set too early. • The PLC did not send RELOAD_OK early enough.
ISD-022.remedy: • Make sure the material supply pressure is high enough. • Make sure Pre-Near-Empty location is set properly. • Make sure PLC sends RELOAD_OK on time.

ISD-023.cause: This warning is posted when the inactive meter could not finish reloading before the active meter reaches the Near-Empty position. This is where the sub-meter should start dispensing for meter switching. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: • The supply pressure was not high enough. • The Near-Empty location is set too early. • The PLC did not send the RELOAD_OK early enough.
ISD-023.remedy: • Make sure material supply pressure is high enough. • Make sure the Near-Empty location is set properly. • Nake sure the PLC sends the RELOAD_OK on time.

ISD-024.cause: This warning is posted when both meters are within the Near-Empty area when the meters are switched. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: • The supply pressure was not high enough. • The Near-Empty location is set too early. • The PLC did not send the RELOAD_OK early enough.
ISD-024.remedy: • Make sure the material supply pressure is high enough. • Make sure the Near-Empty location is set properly. • Make sure the PLC sends the RELOAD_OK on time.

ISD-025.cause: This warning is posted when the previous reload did not finish when the meter was switched. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: • The supply pressure was not high enough. • The Near-Empty location is set too early. • The PLC did not send RELOAD_OK early enough. • The RELOAD_OK signal was not cleared early enough.
ISD-025.remedy: • Make sure the material supply pressure is high enough. • Make sure Near-Empty location is set properly. • Make sure PLC sends RELOAD_OK on time. • Make sure the RELOAD_OK is cleared on time.

ISD-026.cause: The number of Dual ISD dispenser does NOT match the number specified within the SEAL Config menu.
ISD-026.remedy: Display NumCFG menu under SEAL Config menu, and make sure the number of Dual ISD is correctly specified.

ISD-027.cause: The number of the Dual ISD dispenser does NOT match the number specified within the SEAL Config menu.
ISD-027.remedy: Display the NumCFG menu under SEAL Config menu, and make sure the number of Dual ISD is correctly specified.

ISD-028.cause: This error is displayed when the system detects an excessive pressure difference between the two dispensing materials. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: 1. The dispenser line (gun nozzle, hose, etc.) is clogged. 2. The dispensing rate is too high. 3. The high pressure limit value was set too low. 4. The high pressure time out value was set too short.
ISD-028.remedy: Check the following: 1. Make sure that no clogs exist in the dispensing tubing. 2. Make sure that the dispensing flow rate is not set too high. 3. Make sure that the high pressure limit value is appropriate. 4. Make sure that the high pressure time out value is appropriate.

ISD-029.cause: This error is posted when the system detects too low of a pressure difference between the two dispensing materials. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: 1. The dispenser line (gun nozzle, hose, etc.) is removed 2. The dispensing rate is too low 3. The low pressure limit value was set too high 4. The low pressure time out value was set too short
ISD-029.remedy: Check the following: 1. Make sure dispensing line is ok 2. Make sure that the dispensing flow rate is not set too low. 3. Make sure that the low pressure limit value is appropriate. 4. Make sure low pressure time out value is appropriate.

ISD-030.message: Disp pressure diff too high warn(ISD%d)
ISD-030.cause: This error is posted when the system detects an excessive pressure difference between the two dispensing materials. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: 1. The dispenser line (gun nozzle, hose, etc.) is clogged. 2. The dispensing rate is too high. 3. The high pressure limit value was set too low. 4. The high pressure time out value was set too short.
ISD-030.remedy: Make sure there is no clog in the dispensing tubing. Make sure that the dispensing flow rate is not too high. Make sure high pressure limit value is appropriate. Make sure the high pressure time out value is appropriate.

ISD-031.cause: This error is posted when the system detects excessive pressure in the dispensing material. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: 1. The dispenser line (gun nozzle, hose, etc.) is clogged. 2. The dispensing rate is too high. 3. The high pressure limit value was set too low. 4. The high pressure time out value was set too short.
ISD-031.remedy: Please make sure there is no clog in the dispensing tubing. Make sure dispensing flow rate is not too high. Make sure high pressure limit value is appropriate. Make sure high pressure time out value is appropriate.

ISD-032.cause: This error is posted when the system detects too low pressure in the dispensing material. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: 1. The dispenser line (gun nozzle, hose, etc.) is removed. 2. The dispensing rate is too low 3. The low pressure limit value was set too high. 4. The low pressure time out value was set too short.
ISD-032.remedy: Make sure the dispensing line is ok. Make sure the dispensing flow rate is not too low. Make sure the low pressure limit value is appropriate. Make sure the low pressure time out value is appropriate.

ISD-033.cause: This error is posted when the system detects excessive pressure in the second dispensing material. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: 1. The dispenser line (gun nozzle, hose, etc.) is clogged. 2. The dispensing rate is too high. 3. The high pressure limit value was set too low. 4. The high pressure time out value was set too short.
ISD-033.remedy: Check the following: • Make sure there is no clog in the dispensing tubing. • Make sure dispensing flow rate is not too high. • Make sure high pressure limit value is appropriate. • Make sure high pressure time out value is appropriate.

ISD-034.cause: This error is posted when the system detects too low pressure in the second dispensing material. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: 1. The dispenser line (gun nozzle, hose, etc.) is removed 2. The dispensing rate is too low. 3. The low pressure limit value was set too high. 4. The low pressure time out value was set too short.
ISD-034.remedy: Check the following: • Make sure the dispensing line is ok. • Make sure dispensing flow rate is not too low. • Make sure low pressure limit value is appropriate. • Make sure low pressure time out value is appropriate.

ISD-035.cause: This error is posted when the system detects too low pressure in the second dispensing material. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: 1. The dispenser line (gun nozzle, hose, etc.) is removed. 2. The dispensing rate is too low. 3. The low pressure limit value was set too high. 4. The low pressure time out value was set too short.
ISD-035.remedy: Check the following: 1. Make sure the dispensing line is ok. 2. Make sure the dispensing flow rate is not too low. 3. Make sure the low pressure limit value is appropriate. 4. Make sure the low pressure time out value is appropriate.

ISD-040.cause: The minimum recovery pressure was not reached within the specified time in the ISD SETUP menu.
ISD-040.remedy: If the gap between the rods is not closed increase the recovery time, or increase the recovery speed. If the gap is closed, check the pressure transducers, or check for leaks in the system.

ISD-041.cause: Dispense pressure is below the minimum recovery pressure.

ISD-042.cause: Dispense pressure increased above the minimum recovery pressure after dropping below the minimum value.

ISD-050.cause: This error is caused when the Integral Pneumatic System (IPS) encounters a problem that it is unable to solve internally.
ISD-050.remedy: This fault is usually fixed when you perform a COLD start. If the error is not cleared, contact your supervisor or call the FANUC America Corporation Hot Line with the following information: • The exact error number and message shown. • Information documenting exactly what the robot was doing at the time of the failure. • Program name, line number, robot's location in the workcell, any cell I/O or other communication activity.

ISD-051.cause: The commanded velocity for the indicated pneumatic servo axis is too high.
ISD-051.remedy: The commanded velocity is limited to $IPS_CONFIG[n].$CMDSPD_MIN or $IPS_CONFIG[n].$CMDSPD_MAX, where n is the number specified in the alarm. Modify your application instruction or data to reduce the velocity demand on the pneumatic servo axis.

ISD-052.cause: A sudden change in load, inadequate air supply, malfunctioning servo-valve or poor servo tuning caused an excessive error in the pneumatic servo position. This warning is posted when the positional error (in mm.) of that axis exceeds $IPS_CONFIG[n].$POSERR_MAX1, where n is the number specified in the alarm.
ISD-052.remedy: Verify that adequate air supply is available. See if air pressure dips considerably during meter operation: this indicates that the air cylinder is starved for air.

ISD-053.cause: A sudden change in load, inadequate air supply, malfunctioning servo-valve or poor servo tuning caused excessive error in the pneumatic servo position. This alarm is posted when the positional error (in mm.) of that axis, when stationary, exceeds $IPS_CONFIG[n].$POSERR_MAX2, where n is the number specified in the alarm.
ISD-053.remedy: Press RESET to continue the operation. Verify that adequate air supply is available. See if the air pressure dips considerably during meter operation. This indicates that the air cylinder is starved for air..

ISD-054.cause: A sudden change in load or poor servo tuning caused an excessive error in the pneumatic servo position. This alarm is posted when the positional error (in mm.) of that axis exceeds $IPS_CONFIG[n].$POSERR_MAX2, where n is the number specified in the alarm.
ISD-054.remedy: Press RESET to continue the operation. Verify that adequate air supply is available. See if the air pressure dips considerably during meter operation. This indicates that the air cylinder is starved for air..

ISD-055.cause: A digital output that is used to provide power to the servo valve for the specified axis number has not been assigned.
ISD-055.remedy: 1. Perform a Controlled start and display the IPS Config screen. 2. Set up the servo enable digital output port number and type. 3. Perform a Cold Start.

ISD-056.cause: The analog output required to control the servo valve for the specified axis number has not been assigned.
ISD-056.remedy: 1. Perform a Controlled start and display the IPS Config screen. 2. Assign the servo control output port number and type. 3. Perform a Cold Start.

ISD-057.cause: The digital input required to detect air pressure loss to pneumatic servo valve(s) has not been assigned.
ISD-057.remedy: 1. Perform a Controlled start and display the IPS Config screen. 2. Assign the input port number and type for the Air Pressure Check item. 3. Perform a Cold start.

ISD-058.cause: The pressure switch monitoring the air supply to pneumatic servo valves is switched off because the air supply is too low.
ISD-058.remedy: If the gauge indicates adequate pressure, verify that the Air Supply Pressure digital input is not simulated. Also verify that the air pressure transducer settings are correct and operational.

ISD-059.cause: The specified pneumatic servo is unable to reset because of an external condition such as an Emergency Stop. This external condition is forcing the digital servo ready input to stay off.
ISD-059.remedy: Verify that when RESET is pressed, the digital output configured as servo enable comes on briefly. Determine and rectify the external condition (e-stop, blown fuse) causing the problem and then press RESET again. Check whether the servo enable digital output turns on. Verify that the servo ready digital input and the servo enable digital output are properly set up and assigned. Increase the value of $IPS_SETUP.$SRDY_TMOUT (number of scans that the pneumatic servo system waits before checking the servo ready digital input, after RESET is pressed) if required.

ISD-060.cause: Meter hydraulic running input signal is not assigned.
ISD-060.remedy: Assign Meter hydraulic running input signal to a valid port.

ISD-061.cause: Meter hydraulic running input signal is OFF.
ISD-061.remedy: Make sure meter hydraulics are turned ON and the input signal is ON.

ISD-062.cause: Input power input signal is not assigned. Checked only on Power up.
ISD-062.remedy: Assign the Input power input signal to a valid port.

ISD-063.cause: Input power signal is OFF. Checked only on power up.
ISD-063.remedy: Make sure that the input power to the hydraulics is turned ON before powering up the controller.

ISD-064.cause: Control power output signal is not assigned. Checked only on Power up.
ISD-064.remedy: Assign the control power output signal to a valid port.

ISD-065.cause: Gun hydraulics running input signal is not assigned.
ISD-065.remedy: Assign gun hydraulics running signal to a valid port.

ISD-066.message: Mtr. can't run w/o gun hyd. (IPS%d)
ISD-066.cause: Meter hydraulics can not run if gun hydraulics are not running.
ISD-066.remedy: Start the gun hydraulics first and then start meter hydraulics.

ISD-067.cause: Gun hydraulics not low input signal is OFF.
ISD-067.remedy: Make sure gun hydraulics pressure is normal.

ISD-068.cause: Gun hydraulics not high signal is OFF.
ISD-068.remedy: Make sure gun hydraulics pressure is normal.

ISD-069.cause: Gun hydraulics overload input signal is ON.

ISD-070.cause: Meter hydraulics overload input signal is ON.

ISD-071.cause: Local dispense stop input signal is ON.
ISD-071.remedy: Check dispenser stop button on the dispenser's panel.

ISD-072.cause: System dispense stop input signal is OFF.
ISD-072.remedy: Check system dispense stop buttons / logic.

ISD-073.cause: Fire dispenser stop input signal is OFF.

ISD-074.cause: Spare dispenser stop input signal is OFF.

ISD-080.cause: The software has detected a high flow level for the ISO/POLY material.
ISD-080.remedy: The ISO/POLY flow rate has exceeded the “ISO/POLY Max Warn Flow” level for a period of time greater than the “Flow Lo/Hi Time Out” duration. Verify that the dispense equipment (pressure regulators, flow meters and spray modules, etc.) is functioning correctly. Verify that the settings on the Dispenser Setup screen are reasonable.

ISD-081.cause: The software has detected an excessively high flow level for the ISO/POLY material. This case is more severe than ISD-080, and may result in serious material application defects.
ISD-081.remedy: The ISO/POLY flow rate has exceeded the “ISO/POLY Max Fault Flow” level for a period of time greater than the “Flow Lo/Hi Time Out” duration. Verify that the dispense equipment (pressure regulators, flow meters and spray modules, etc.) is functioning correctly. Verify that the settings on the Dispenser Setup screen are reasonable.

ISD-082.cause: The software has detected a low flow level for the ISO/POLY material.
ISD-082.remedy: The ISO/POLY flow rate is less than the “ISO/POLY Min Warn Flow” level for a period of time greater than the “Flow Lo/Hi Time Out” duration. Verify that the dispense equipment (pressure regulators, flow meters and spray modules, etc.) is functioning correctly. Verify that the settings on the Dispenser Setup screen are reasonable.

ISD-083.cause: The software has detected an excessively low flow level for the ISO/POLY material. This case is more severe than ISD-082, and may result in serious material application defects.
ISD-083.remedy: The ISO/POLY flow rate was less than the “ISO/POLY Min Fault Flow” level for a period of time greater than the “Flow Lo/Hi Time Out” duration. Verify that the dispense equipment (pressure regulators, flow meters and spray modules, etc.) is functioning correctly. Verify that the settings on the Dispenser Setup screen are reasonable.

ISD-084.cause: The software has detected a high ratio for the ISO/POLY mixture.
ISD-084.remedy: The deviation of the ISO/POLY ratio is greater than the “ISO/POLY Max Warn Ratio” level for a period of time greater than the “ISO/POLY Hi Ratio Wrn T/O” duration. Verify that the dispense equipment (pressure regulators, flow meters and spray modules, etc.) is functioning correctly. Verify that the settings on the Dispenser Setup screen are reasonable.

ISD-085.cause: The software has detected an excessively high ratio for the ISO/POLY mixture. This is more severe than ISD-084, and may result in serious material application defects.
ISD-085.remedy: The deviation of the ISO/POLY ratio is greater than the “ISO/POLY Max Fault Ratio” level for a period of time greater than the “ISO/POLY Hi Ratio Flt T/O” duration. Verify that the dispense equipment (pressure regulators, flow meters and spray modules, etc.) is functioning correctly. Verify that the settings on the Dispenser Setup screen are reasonable.

ISD-086.cause: The software has detected a low ratio for the ISO/POLY mixture.
ISD-086.remedy: The deviation of the ISO/POLY ratio is greater than the “ISO/POLY Min Warn Ratio” level for a period of time greater than the “ISO/POLY Lo Ratio Wrn T/O” duration. Verify that the dispense equipment (pressure regulators, flow meters and spray modules, etc.) is functioning correctly. Verify that the settings on the Dispenser Setup screen are reasonable.

ISD-087.cause: The software has detected an excessively low ratio for the ISO/POLY mixture. This is more severe than ISD-086, and may result in serious material application defects.
ISD-087.remedy: The deviation of the ISO/POLY ratio is greater than the “ISO/POLY Min Fault Ratio” level for a period of time greater than the “ISO/POLY Lo Ratio Flt T/O” duration. Verify that the dispense equipment (pressure regulators, flow meters and spray modules, etc.) is functioning correctly. Verify that the settings on the Dispenser Setup screen are reasonable.

ISD-088.cause: The instantaneous material flow ratio exceeded the amount set in the dispenser setup menu.
ISD-088.remedy: Verify that the limit and timeout in the setup menu are reasonable or check equipment for the source of flow ratio problems.

ISD-089.cause: The instantaneous material flow ratio was less than the amount set in the dispenser setup menu.
ISD-089.remedy: Verify that the limit and timeout in the setup menu are reasonable or check equipment for the source of flow ratio problems.

ISD-090.cause: The material pressure differential (ISO minus POLY) exceeded the Max. differential fault limit set in the dispenser setup menu.
ISD-090.remedy: Verify that the limit and timeout in the setup menu are reasonable or check equipment for the source of differential problems.

ISD-091.cause: The material pressure differential (ISO minus POLY) exceeded the Max. differential warn limit set in the dispenser setup menu.
ISD-091.remedy: Verify that the limit and timeout in the setup menu are reasonable or check equipment for the source of differential problems.

ISD-092.cause: The material pressure differential (ISO minus POLY) was less than the Min. differential warn limit set in the dispenser setup menu.
ISD-092.remedy: Verify that the limit and timeout in the setup menu are reasonable or check equipment for the source of differential problems.

ISD-093.cause: The material pressure differential (ISO minus POLY) was less than the Min. differential fault limit set in the dispenser setup menu.
ISD-093.remedy: Verify that the limit and timeout in the setup menu are reasonable or check equipment for the source of differential problems.

ISD-094.cause: The iso pressure variation detected when transitioning from RECIRC to DISPENSE mode exceeded the Iso max. variation flt limit set in the dispenser setup menu.
ISD-094.remedy: Verify that the related limit and capture delay time in in the setup menu are reasonable or check equipment for the source of recirc to dispense mode transition pressure variation problems.

ISD-102.remedy: Verify that the related limit and capture delay time in in the setup menu are reasonable or check equipment for the source of the excessive SS to SE pressure difference
