ISD-110.message: F-P ctrl and mon not allowed (ISD%d)
ISD-110.cause: F-P stability mon and Use F-P control are mutually exclusive in the sealing schedule data menu. They cannot both be enabled at the same time.

ISD-111.cause: F-P shift factor has been adjusted to the maximum value as set in the ISD setup menu.
ISD-111.remedy: Ensure that the system is otherwise operating normally. Also check the material characteristics for undesired changes in temperature and viscosity. ISD setup menu Shift factor max may be increased if necessary but make sure that doing so does not cause excessive system pressure or too much material to be applied. Verify that the pressure transducers are functioning normally.

ISD-112.cause: F-P shift factor has been adjusted to the minimum value as set in the ISD setup menu.
ISD-112.remedy: Ensure that the system is otherwise operating normally. Also check the material characteristics for undesired changes in temperature and viscosity. ISD setup menu Shift factor min may be decreased if necessary but make sure that doing so does not cause insufficient system pressure or too little material to be applied. Verify that the pressure transducers are functioning normally.

ISD-113.cause: F-P shift factor has been adjusted by the maximum amount as set in the ISD setup menu for this check.
ISD-113.remedy: Ensure that the system is otherwise operating normally. Also check the material characteristics for undesired changes in temperature and viscosity. This error may also be part of normal operation if the system has been idle for a while. If so then this error will most likely not continue to be posted on every check for very long. ISD setup menu Shift factor max chg may be increased if necessary but make sure that doing so does not cause insufficient system pressure or too little material to be applied. Also make sure that doing so does not cause excessive system pressure or too much material to be applied. Verify that the pressure transducers are functioning normally.

ISD-114.cause: F-P shift factor has been adjusted to the maximum value as set in the ISD setup menu.
ISD-114.remedy: Ensure that the system is otherwise operating normally. Also check the material characteristics for undesired changes in temperature and viscosity. ISD setup menu Shift factor max may be increased if necessary but make sure that doing so does not cause excessive system pressure or too much material to be applied. Verify that the pressure transducers are functioning normally.

ISD-115.cause: F-P shift factor has been adjusted to the minimum value as set in the ISD setup menu.
ISD-115.remedy: Ensure that the system is otherwise operating normally. Also check the material characteristics for undesired changes in temperature and viscosity. ISD setup menu Shift factor min may be decreased if necessary but make sure that doing so does not cause insufficient system pressure or too little material to be applied. Verify that the pressure transducers are functioning normally.

ISD-116.cause: F-P shift factor has been adjusted by the maximum amount as set in the ISD setup menu for this check.
ISD-116.remedy: Ensure that the system is otherwise operating normally. Also check the material characteristics for undesired changes in temperature and viscosity. This error may also be part of normal operation if the system has been idle for a while. If so then this error will most likely not continue to be posted on every check for very long. ISD setup menu Shift factor max chg may be increased if necessary but make sure that doing so does not cause insufficient system pressure or too little material to be applied. Also make sure that doing so does not cause excessive system pressure or too much material to be applied. Verify that the pressure transducers are functioning normally.

ISD-117.cause: Data point #1 for the F-P calibration has a flow rate selected that is <= 0.0 percent.
ISD-117.remedy: Enter a flow rate for data point #1 that is greater than 0.0 percent and re-record the pressure value for that point.

ISD-118.cause: Data point #1 for the F-P calibration has a flow rate selected that when converted to cc/sec is <= 0.0 percent.
ISD-118.remedy: Enter a flow rate for data point #1 that is slightly larger and greater than 0.0 percent and re-record the pressure value for that point.

ISD-119.cause: Data point #2 for the F-P calibration has a flow rate selected that is <= 0.0 percent.
ISD-119.remedy: Enter a flow rate for data point #2 that is greater than 0.0 percent and re-record the pressure value for that point.

ISD-120.cause: Data point #2 for the F-P calibration has a flow rate selected that when converted to cc/sec is <= 0.0 percent.
ISD-120.remedy: Enter a flow rate for data point #2 that is slightly larger and greater than 0.0 percent and re-record the pressure value for that point.

ISD-121.cause: Data points for the F-P calibration have flow values that are not all increasing.
ISD-121.remedy: Enter flow rates for data points that are all increasing and re-record the pressure values for any points that have been changed.

ISD-122.cause: Data points for the F-P calibration have flow values (after being converted to cc/sec) that are not all increasing.
ISD-122.remedy: Enter flow rates for data points that are all increasing and re-record the pressure values for any points that have been changed.

ISD-123.cause: Data points for the F-P calibration have pressure values that are not all increasing.
ISD-123.remedy: Enter flow rates for data points that are all increasing and re-record the pressure values for any points that have been changed. Ensure that the pressure values are all increasing as well.

ISD-124.cause: Data points in the F-P curve that are not used should have pressure values set to (-)1.0 One or more data points were found not to be set this way.
ISD-124.remedy: Enter pressure values of (-)1.0 for data points that are not being used. Note that good calibration data points must be contiguous - with no unused points intermixed.

ISD-125.cause: Data points in the F-P curve that are not used should have flow rate values set to (-)1.0% One or more data points were found not to be set this way (when converted to cc/sec).
ISD-125.remedy: Enter flow rate values of (-)1.0% for data points that are not being used. Note that good calibration data points must be contiguous - with no unused points intermixed.

ISD-126.cause: This error is caused when ISD system encounters a problem that is unable to solve internally.
ISD-126.remedy: Write down the exact error number and message shown. Write down exactly what your robot was doing at the time of the failure. Make sure you include: Program name, line number, robot's location in the work cell, any cell I/O or other communication activity, and exactly what the robot was doing right before the fault occurred. This fault is usually fixed by doing a COLD start. If that does not work, contact your supervisor or call FANUC America Corporation for assistance.

ISD-127.cause: The Output Power OK input signal is not ON.
ISD-127.remedy: Reset the cell or troubleshoot why the Output Power OK input signal is not ON.

ISD-128.cause: The Output Power OK input signal is assigned but the port is invalid.
ISD-128.remedy: Verify that the Output Power OK input signal is assigned to a valid port on the ISD I/O INPUT menu. Cycle power after assigning.

ISD-129.cause: The AirSupply PressOK input signal is not ON.
ISD-129.remedy: Reset the cell or troubleshoot why the AirSupply PressOK input signal is not ON.

ISD-130.cause: The AirSupply PressOK input signal is assigned but the port is invalid.
ISD-130.remedy: Verify that the AirSupply PressOK input signal is assigned to a valid port on the ISD I/O INPUT menu. Cycle power after assigning.

ISD-131.cause: This error is caused when ISD system encounters a problem that is unable to solve internally.
ISD-131.remedy: Write down the exact error number and message shown. Write down exactly what your robot was doing at the time of the failure. Make sure you include: Program name, line number, robot's location in the work cell, any cell I/O or other communciation activity, and exactly what the robot was doing right before the fault occured. This fault is usually fixed by doing a COLD start. If that does not work, contact your supervisor or call FANUC Robotics for assistance.

ISD-132.cause: 'Wrn time left Max' has been set to a value greater than 'Flt time left Max' in the Dispenser setup menu
ISD-132.remedy: This is only a warning. To prevent this alarm, please set the 'Flt time left Max' to a value greater than 'Wrn time left Max' in the Dispenser setup menu.

ISD-133.cause: The MCSD Lifetime timer has exceeded the value as set 'Wrn time left Max' in the Dispenser setup menu. The cartridge should be exchanged soon.
ISD-133.remedy: This is just a warning. After the cartridge is exchanged, the Lifetime timer should be reset in order to clear this alarm and to begin Lifetime timing for the new cartridge.

ISD-134.cause: The MCSD Lifetime timer has exceeded the value as set 'Flt time left Max' in the Dispenser setup menu. The cartridge should be exchanged immediately because its lifetime has expired.
ISD-134.remedy: Change the cartridge immediately. Do not attempt to dispense with an expired cartridge as equipment may be damaged or personnel may be injured. After the cartridge is exchanged, the Lifetime timer should be reset in order to clear this alarm and to begin Lifetime timing for the new cartridge.

ISD-135.cause: The MCSD Lifetime timer has exceeded the max overflow value of 34560 minutes and the timer will not advance.
ISD-135.remedy: Cartridges may need to be changed. Reset and restart the MCSD timer.

ISD-136.cause: The MCSD Lifetime timer has exceeded the max overflow value of 34560 minutes upon powerup and the timer will not advance.
ISD-136.remedy: Cartridges may need to be changed. Reset and restart the MCSD timer.

ISD-137.cause: Upon powerup it has been determined that the robot has been powered off for a long period of time - exceeding 1000 minutes while a Lifetime timer was in the RUN state.
ISD-137.remedy: Cartridges may need to be changed. Reset and restart the MCSD timer.

ISD-138.cause: An invalid parameter has been passed into the MCSDMAC Karel program during a call to it. Other possible cause is that the controlled start MCSD setup and mapping has not been completed correctly.
ISD-138.remedy: Check that parameters being passed in during a call to the MCSDMAC Karel program are correct. Ensure that the controlled start MCSD setup and mapping has not been completed correctly.

ISD-139.cause: The MCSD is not in the requested Load position by the timeout value.
ISD-139.remedy: Verify the state of BOTH of the following MCSD inputs: MCSD in Load Pos must be ON. MCSD in Disp Pos must be OFF. If one or more of these inputs is not assigned then they can be ignored. Reset the robot and restart the program to try again.

ISD-140.cause: The MCSD is not in the requested Dispense position by the timeout value.
ISD-140.remedy: Verify the state of BOTH of the following MCSD inputs: MCSD in Load Pos must be OFF. MCSD in Disp Pos must be ON. If one or more of these inputs is not assigned then they can be ignored. Reset the robot and restart the program to try again.

ISD-141.cause: The MCSD ISD is not in the fully retracted position.
ISD-141.remedy: In order to run this macro, the ISD must be in the fully retracted position first. Move the ISD to the fully retracted position and try running the macro again. Verify that the variable used to define the fully retracted position has been set correctly.

ISD-142.cause: The MCSD Cart. 1 Present input is OFF indicating that cartridge 1 is not present.
ISD-142.remedy: Verify the state of the following MCSD input: Cart. 1 Present must be ON. Note: if this input is not assigned then it will be ignored. Reset the robot and restart the program to try again.

ISD-143.cause: The MCSD Cart. 2 Present input is OFF indicating that cartridge 2 is not present.
ISD-143.remedy: Verify the state of the following MCSD input: Cart. 2 Present must be ON. Note: if this input is not assigned then it will be ignored. Reset the robot and restart the program to try again.

ISD-144.cause: The referenced MCSD I/O item has been assigned to an I/O point that is not valid.
ISD-144.remedy: Verify that the I/O item is assigned to a valid point.

ISD-145.cause: The ISD used for the equipment number indicated has not been mastered yet.
ISD-145.remedy: Master the ISD used for the equipment number indicated.

ISD-146.message: MCSD bad min retract pos val (ISD%s)
ISD-146.cause: The MCSD minimum retract position value is less than the reposition offset for this ISD.
ISD-146.remedy: Change the minimum retract position value or the reposition offset for the ISD number indicated.

ISD-147.cause: MCSD Lifetime monitoring is disabled for this ISD and a request was received to RESET or RUN the timer.
ISD-147.remedy: Enable MCSD Lifetime monitoring for this ISD or do not request to RESET or RUN the timer.

ISD-148.cause: The MCSD Plunger1 NotFound input is ON indicating that the plunger has not been found.
ISD-148.remedy: Verify the state of the following MCSD input: Plunger1 NotFound must be OFF. Note: if this input is not assigned then it will be ignored. Reset the robot and restart the program to try again.

ISD-149.cause: The MCSD Plunger1 NotFound input is OFF indicating that the plunger has been found.
ISD-149.remedy: Verify the state of the following MCSD input: Plunger1 NotFound must be ON. Note: if this input is not assigned then it will be ignored. Reset the robot and restart the program to try again.

ISD-150.cause: The MCSD Plunger2 NotFound input is ON indicating that the plunger has not been found.
ISD-150.remedy: Verify the state of the following MCSD input: Plunger2 NotFound must be OFF. Note: if this input is not assigned then it will be ignored. Reset the robot and restart the program to try again.

ISD-151.cause: The MCSD Plunger2 NotFound input is OFF indicating that the plunger has been found.
ISD-151.remedy: Verify the state of the following MCSD input: Plunger2 NotFound must be ON. Note: if this input is not assigned then it will be ignored. Reset the robot and restart the program to try again.

ISD-152.message: MCSD in Load Pos is ON (E%s)
ISD-152.cause: The MCSD in Load pos input is ON indicating that the Cartridge Holder Mechanism is in the Load position.
ISD-152.remedy: Verify the state of the following MCSD input: MCSD in Load Pos must be OFF. Note: if this input is not assigned then it will be ignored. Reset the robot and restart the program to try again.

ISD-153.message: MCSD in Load Pos is OFF (E%s)
ISD-153.cause: The MCSD in Load pos input is OFF indicating that the Cartridge Holder Mechanism is not in the Load position.
ISD-153.remedy: Verify the state of the following MCSD input: MCSD in Load Pos must be ON. Note: if this input is not assigned then it will be ignored. Reset the robot and restart the program to try again.

ISD-154.message: MCSD in Disp Pos is ON (E%s)
ISD-154.cause: The MCSD in Disp pos input is ON indicating that the Cartridge Holder Mechanism is in the Disp position.
ISD-154.remedy: Verify the state of the following MCSD input: MCSD in Disp Pos must be OFF. Note: if this input is not assigned then it will be ignored. Reset the robot and restart the program to try again.

ISD-155.message: MCSD in Disp Pos is OFF (E%s)
ISD-155.cause: The MCSD in Disp pos input is OFF indicating that the Cartridge Holder Mechanism is not in the Disp position.
ISD-155.remedy: Verify the state of the following MCSD input: MCSD in Disp Pos must be ON. Note: if this input is not assigned then it will be ignored.

ISDT-001.cause: Joint can not rotate as fast as the input speed required.
ISDT-001.remedy: Even though this is just a warning, reference $IS_MRR.$JNTVELLIM to reduce velocity command.

ISDT-002.cause: Motor can not rotate as fast as the input speed required.
ISDT-002.remedy: Even though this is just a warning, reference $IS_MRR.$JNTVELLIM to reduce velocity command.

ISDT-003.cause: ISDT global variables are not loaded.

ISDT-004.cause: Failed to allocate memory for ISDT system variables.
ISDT-004.remedy: Check amount of memory being used by system.

ISDT-005.cause: ISDT recieves NULL AMR from AX.
ISDT-005.remedy: Check if isaxcold() is called during cold start.

ISDT-006.cause: Servo error occurs, ISDT failed to create AMR.
ISDT-006.remedy: Check if isaxcold() is called during cold start.

ISDT-007.cause: Attempted to start process axes when servo is not ready.

ISDT-008.cause: Process axes speed command is not initialized.

ISDT-009.cause: Severe servo errors. It requires remastering. ISDT ignores all speed commands.
ISDT-009.remedy: Set $IS_DMR.$ignore_motn = FALSE, and perform mastering procedure.

ISDT-010.message: Invalid Grp In for Ax%d Speed
ISDT-010.cause: Group Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-010.remedy: Specify a proper group input number in IS_MRR.IS_SPD_GI

ISDT-011.message: Invalid Grp Out for Ax%d Speed
ISDT-011.cause: Group Output specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-011.remedy: Specify a proper group output number in IS_MRR.IS_SPD_GO

ISDT-012.cause: Axis number specified in TP Instruction SET ISDT SPEED is not a valid ISDT axis
ISDT-012.remedy: Change the indicated axis number in the instruction on the line indicated

ISDT-013.cause: Axis number specified in TP instruction SET ISDT SPEED was used more than once
ISDT-013.remedy: Change one of the instances of this axis to be a different, unused valid axis

ISDT-014.cause: Torque Limit feature is enabled on indicated axis and the motor current has exceeded this level for the specified amount of time.
ISDT-014.remedy: 1. Check mechanical loading of axis 2. Increase current limit in setup menu 3. Increase time to fault in setup menu

ISDT-015.cause: Something is wrong with process axis.
ISDT-015.remedy: Refer to co-occurring servo alarm's remedy.

ISDT-016.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-016.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.STR_MOT_DI

ISDT-017.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-017.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.STR_USG_DI

ISDT-018.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-018.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.USG_GO

ISDT-019.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-019.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.SRV_RDY_DO

ISDT-020.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-020.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.MOT_ACT_DO

ISDT-021.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-021.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.SPD_CTR_DO

ISDT-022.message: Invalid Trq Grp Out for Ax%d
ISDT-022.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-022.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.TRQ_GO

ISDT-023.message: Invalid Trq Ctrl DO for Ax%d
ISDT-023.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-023.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.TRQ_CTR_DO

ISDT-024.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-024.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.INC_MOV_DI

ISDT-025.message: Invalid Pos Grp In for Ax%d
ISDT-025.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-025.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.IS_POS_GI

ISDT-026.message: Invalid Pos Grp Out for Ax%d
ISDT-026.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-026.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.IS_POS_GO

ISDT-027.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-027.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.MOV_CMP_DO

ISDT-028.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-028.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.POS_CTR_DO

ISDT-029.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-029.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.JOG_PER_DI

ISDT-030.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-030.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.MASTER_DI

ISDT-031.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-031.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.NOT_MST_DO

ISDT-032.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-032.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number in IS_MRR.AT_MST_DO

ISDT-033.cause: Digital Input specified for this axis is invalid
ISDT-033.remedy: Specify a proper digital input number

ISDT-034.cause: When the electrode wheel moved, the difference between speed command and feedback exceeded a specified value.
ISDT-034.remedy: 1. Check whether the duty and applied load exceed the rating. If so, reduce the duty or applied load. 2. Check whether the electrode wheel is pushed or pulled by external force. If so, remove the external force to the electrode wheel or decrease the teaching speed. 3. Check whether the power line of the electrode wheel connection cable or the cable in the mechanical unit are down. 4. Check whether the motor power cable/connector and brake cable/connector are connected correctly. Especially, check whether the power cable/connector aren't connected to other motors. 5. Measure the supplied voltage. Then, check whether the voltage is matched to the controller specification. 6. Check whether the motor brake is released properly when Reset. First of all, check whether the setting of brake number is correct. 7. When this alarm occurs on the auxiliary axis which brake is controlled by the aux. brake unit, check the fuse on the aux. brake unit.

ISDT-035.message: Brake number duplicated (Axs:%d Brk:%d G:%d A:%d)
ISDT-035.cause: The brake number of the process axis is duplicated with other axis. The 1st parameter Axs means the Process axis number that brake number is duplicated. The 2nd parameter Brk means the duplicated brake number. The 3rd parameter G means the group number that brake number is duplicated with Process axis. The 4th parameter A means the axis number that brake number is duplicated with Process axis.
ISDT-035.remedy: Change the brake number and the hardware connection to an independent brake number.

ISDT-038.cause: External source does not allow Jogging of this axis
ISDT-038.remedy: Wait for the Jog Permissive DI to turn ON, and make sure it is configured

ISDT-040.cause: A position command was attempted while the process axis has not been mastered

ISDT-041.cause: Distance for position move was too short to acheive at given speed. No motion was issued.
ISDT-041.remedy: Decrease the speed for the position command, or increase distance.

ISDT-042.cause: The process axis is or will be in violation of position limits
ISDT-042.remedy: Adjust external commands to avoid upper and lower bounds

ISDT-043.cause: Different Control mode requested or Master axis request while Start Motor Digital Input is ON
ISDT-043.remedy: Turn OFF the Start Motor Digital Input

ISDT-044.cause: Different Control mode requested or Master axis request while a non-zero value is in the Speed Command Group Input
ISDT-044.remedy: Set the value of the Speed Command Group Input to 0

ISDT-045.cause: Different Control mode requested or Master axis request while motor still in motion. May occur because axis is decelerating
ISDT-045.remedy: Wait for axis to come to a complete stop.

ISDT-046.cause: The teach pendant was ENABLED when an external request was recieved. This may include a change in control mode, or sart motion request.
ISDT-046.remedy: Disable the teach pendant to allow external commands to be processed.

ISDT-047.cause: Teach pendant was DISABLED when using the Jog/Master Teach Pendant screen to jog or master an axis
ISDT-047.remedy: Enable the teach pendant to allow jog and master requests from the UIF to be processed.

JOG-001.remedy: Use the MANUAL FCTNS OT release menu in to find out which axis is in an overtravel condition. Release overtravel by holding the SHIFT key and pressing the RESET key. At this time the servo power will be turnned on. If the SHIFT key is released, the servo power will be turnned off again. You can only use JOINT to jog the axis out of overtravel. If you want to jog the overtraveled axis further into the overtravel direction, you have to release the axis by moving the cursor to the axis direction you want, then press release function key in the OT release menu. At this point you can jog the axis to that direction.

JOG-002.remedy: Set the system variable $MASTER_ENB to 1. Select SYSTEM then Master/Cal, to display the Master/Cal menu. Select a method for calibrating the robot. If the robot can not be calibrated, mastering is required. If the robot has been master before, set the system variable $DMR_GRP[].$master_done to TRUE then calibrate the robot again. For more information on mastering and calibrating the robot, refer to the KAREL and TPP Setup and Operations Manual.

JOG-003.remedy: Abort the program that has motion control by pressing FCTN key then selecting ABORT.

JOG-004.cause: You cannot do more than one rotational jog at a time
JOG-004.remedy: Only press one rotational jog key at a time.

JOG-005.cause: The system call to clear hold flag failed. error

JOG-006.cause: No extended axis exist in this group with which to jog.
JOG-006.remedy: This is a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

JOG-007.cause: The SHIFT key is not pressed
JOG-007.remedy: You must press the SHIFT key when jogging the robot. Release the jog key then hold the SHIFT key and press the jog key to jog.

JOG-008.remedy: Hold the DEADMAN and turn on the teach pendant before jogging the robot.

JOG-009.cause: The DEADMAN switch is not pressed
JOG-009.remedy: Press the DEADMAN switch, then press the RESET key to clear the error

JOG-010.cause: The jog key was pressed before the shift key was pressed
JOG-010.remedy: Release the jog key. Then,hold the SHIFT key then press the jog key

JOG-011.cause: The selected tool frame changed while jogging
JOG-011.remedy: Release the SHIFT key and the JOG key. The new TOOL frame will take effect automatically. To start jogging, hold down the SHIFT key and press the JOG key.

JOG-012.remedy: Engage all the brakes by pressing EMERGENCY STOP button, then press the RESET key. To start jogging, press the shift and the jog key.

JOG-013.cause: Robot axis reaches its specified stroke limit
JOG-013.remedy: The robot already reach the stroke limit and cannot jog in the current direction any more. Extend the axis limit if it does not exceed the robot and software specifications.

JOG-014.cause: Robot reaches its vertical fixture position
JOG-014.remedy: To continue jogging, release the JOG key then press it again.

JOG-015.cause: Robot reaches its horizontal fixture position
JOG-015.remedy: To continue jogging, release the JOG key then press it again.

JOG-016.cause: Follow-up time is over when softfloat is ON

JOG-017.cause: Robot reaches its R-Theta posture position
JOG-017.remedy: To continue jogging, release the JOG key then press it again.

JOG-018.cause: Robot is not at R-Theta posture position
JOG-018.remedy: Jog J4 to reach R-Theta posture (0, +180, -180).

JOG-020.cause: PATH JOG has selected, but robot is not currently on a taught path, or tool Z direction is same teaching path, so Y direction can not be determined. Can not PATH JOG
JOG-020.remedy: Use shift-FWD to execute program path, or specify another jog frame.

JOG-021.cause: Use of multiple jog keys is not supported in PATH JOG
JOG-021.remedy: Use only one jog key at a time.

JOG-022.cause: PATH jog is disabled in JOINT path
JOG-022.remedy: PATH jog is available in LINEAR and CERCULAR path

JOG-023.cause: PATH jog is available only in PAUSE status
JOG-023.remedy: PATH jog is available only in PAUSE status

JOG-024.cause: This key is invalid at current jog mode

JOG-026.cause: J4 angle is zero. J4 joint jog is disabled.

JOG-027.cause: This direction is reverse direction from J4 = 0.

JOG-028.cause: Stroke limit with this TCP configuration.

JOG-031.cause: A locked multi-robot system requires you to use coordinated jogging. Refer to the Coordinated Motion Setup and Operations Manual for information on coordinated motion setup and jogging.
JOG-031.remedy: Use coordinated jogging, or unlock the multi-robot system. Refer to the Coordinated Motion Setup and Operations Manual for more information.

JOG-032.cause: The selected coordinate system (COORD) is not supported in Dual Arm Tracking Jog.
JOG-032.remedy: Select a supported Tracking Jog COORD: Joint, Jgfrm, World, Tool, or User.

JOG-033.cause: Wrist joint mode is not available in coordinated jog.

JOG-034.cause: JOG has been disabled by $SCR.$TPMOTNENABL setting.
JOG-034.remedy: Please set $SCR.$TPMOTNENABL to 0 or 2 in accordance with Operations Manual.

JOG-051.cause: Jog Retract request was received, but it could not be processed
JOG-051.remedy: The cause of the error is displayed in the next line on the screen. Perform the remedy accordingly

JOG-052.message: No program is running or paused
JOG-052.remedy: Do the operation while a program is running

JOG-053.cause: Robot Return request was received, but it could not be processed
JOG-053.remedy: The cause of the error is displayed in the next line on the screen. Perform the remedy accordingly

JOG-054.cause: Jog Retract operation is not in progress.
JOG-054.remedy: Request the Jog Retract operation prior to this operation

JOG-055.cause: Abort Jog Retract request was received, but it could not be processed
JOG-055.remedy: The cause of the error is displayed in the next line on the screen. Perform the remedy accordingly

JOG-056.message: Jog Retract recorded Max Num positions
JOG-056.cause: Jog Retract has recorded maximum number of jogged positions, and therefore, cannot record any more.
JOG-056.remedy: You may request Robot Return at this point. The robot can still be returned to the stopped position from this point.

JOG-057.cause: The system could not use the recorded jogged position in Cartesian space. The system is using the recorded position in Joint space for Robot Return operation.
JOG-057.remedy: None. It is just an informational

LANG-004.cause: (1) The wrong port is set to the port you want to use. (2) The device may be out of order.
LANG-004.remedy: (1) Set the currect port. (2) Check the device if it works fine.

LANG-005.cause: Only able to process teach pendant programs.

LANG-006.cause: A when loading.TP file, invalid data was found. This may occur if a.TP file has become corrupted or if some other type of file e.g., a.PE file, has been copied or renamed to a.TP file.
LANG-006.remedy: Generate (using SAVE, with $ASCII_SAVE = FALSE) and load a valid.TP file. Note: An existing TP program in the controller might have been corrupted as a result of your attempt to load the invalid file. You might have to reteach the teach pendant program, before you save it as a.TP file.

LANG-014.cause: The program that is being loaded already exists in the system.
LANG-014.remedy: Before you load the program, delete the program already in the system.

LANG-015.cause: Failure when writing data to the floppy.
LANG-015.remedy: Check the connection of the device.

LANG-016.cause: Failure when reading data from the floppy.
LANG-016.remedy: Check the connection of the device.

LANG-017.cause: The data you are trying to save to a file is either abnormal or broken, therefore the file cannot be loaded.
LANG-017.remedy: The file cannot be loaded with the data as it is. The data must be normal to load the file.

LANG-018.cause: When printing the program, there was an illegal position that did not match the group mask of the program.
LANG-018.remedy: Reteach the position data so that the group number matches the group mask of the program.

LANG-050.cause: The file name and the program name are not the same. Their names must match.
LANG-050.remedy: Rename the file to be same as the program name.

LANG-051.cause: The daughter program name is not matched with the parent program name.
LANG-051.remedy: Please verify the daughter program name.

LANG-052.cause: The loading of the daughter program failed.
LANG-052.remedy: Please check the contents of the specified file.

LANG-053.cause: The save/load/print operation cannnot be processed to a daughter program directly.

LANG-054.cause: The program that cannot be loaded needs J858 option. You might load wrong program to the robot where J858 is not ordered.
LANG-054.remedy: Please confirm if you are not loading wrong program. Please confirm J858 is ordered in the robot.

LANG-055.cause: The program that cannot be printed needs J858 option.
LANG-055.remedy: Please confirm J858 is ordered in the robot.

LANG-056.cause: The positions of program whose handle_part is ON are printed by reversed representation when J858 is ordered, but the print is failed because conversion to reversed representation of a position is failed.
LANG-056.remedy: Please correct position data and try again

LANG-057.cause: This program was created on a robot which supports groups that are not available on this robot
LANG-057.remedy: You must upgrade to a later software version

LANG-058.cause: This program was created on a robot which had the extended frame option.
LANG-058.remedy: You must load the extended frame option and try the program again.

LANG-075.cause: The Ascii Input encountered an error in the attribute section.
LANG-075.remedy: Fix the /ATTR section of the.LS file.

LANG-076.cause: The Ascii Input encountered a syntax error in the application section.
LANG-076.remedy: Fix the /APPL section of the.LS file.

LANG-077.cause: The Ascii Input encountered an error in the mnenonic section.
LANG-077.remedy: Fix the /MN section of the.LS file.

LANG-078.cause: The Ascii Input encountered an error in the position section.
LANG-078.remedy: Fix the /POS section of the.LS file.

LANG-079.cause: The Ascii Input encountered an invalid section in the program.
LANG-079.remedy: Fix the invalid section in the.LS file.

LANG-080.cause: The Ascii Input encountered an invalid filename.
LANG-080.remedy: Verify the program name matches the name of the.LS file.

LANG-081.cause: The Ascii Input encountered an error in the application section.
LANG-081.remedy: Fix the /APPL section of the.LS file.

LANG-090.cause: The Ascii Input encountered a program line with too many characters.
LANG-090.remedy: Shorten the line in the /MN section of the.LS file.

LANG-091.cause: Optimize data exists in the program and this cannot be printed.
LANG-091.remedy: Special handling may occur for programs which contain optmized data.

LANG-094.cause: The specified file already exists in the floppy.
LANG-094.remedy: Before you write the new file to the floppy, delete the file that already exists on the floppy.

LANG-095.cause: The specified file does not exist in the floppy.
LANG-095.remedy: Check the file name or content of the floppy.

LANG-096.cause: The floppy disk has reached its limit and is full.
LANG-096.remedy: Either use a new floppy disk or delete an unnecessary file in order to make room for saving to the floppy.

LANG-097.message: Only one file may be opened
LANG-097.cause: An attempt was made to open more than one file.
LANG-097.remedy: Do not attempt to open more than one file at a time.

LANG-098.cause: It could not access the disk.
LANG-098.remedy: Check if the correct device is set to port and it turns on.

LANG-100.remedy: Connect the correct device to the correct port.

LECO-017.cause: A message was sent to another part of the system through the digital communications link (ArcLink) but no response was received. This often occurs when a part of the system is turned OFF or disconnected.
LECO-017.remedy: Verify all devices in the system are properly powered. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation if problem persists.

LECO-019.cause: Machine settings that are saved during power down could not be restored because the data is corrupt. The two backup copies of the machine settings are not complete or do not contain valid data. Default values have been restored. Calibration of system needs to be verified.
LECO-019.remedy: Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation if problem persists after firmware update.

LECO-020.cause: Machine settings that are saved during power down could not be restored because the data is corrupt. The first of two copies did not verify correctly.
LECO-020.remedy: Cycle power on system. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation if problem persists after firmware update.

LECO-021.cause: Machine settings that are saved during power down could not be restored because the data is corrupt. The second of two copies did not verify correctly.
LECO-021.remedy: Cycle power on system. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation if problem persists after firmware update.

LECO-022.cause: Machine settings that are saved during power down could not be restored because the data does not match the current configuration. This can be caused if the software in the machine has been updated.
LECO-022.remedy: Cycle power on system. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation if problem persists after firmware update.

LECO-024.cause: An attempt to establish communications between the robot and a Lincoln PowerWave welding power supply failed.
LECO-024.remedy: Verify that the weld power supply is turned on. Verify the ArcLink communications cable is installed properly.

LECO-049.cause: The input current to the machine exceeded the safe limit. This is normally caused by low input voltage or a missing phase (with 3 phase input power) but it could be caused by a faulty switch board, output diode, or main transformer.
LECO-049.remedy: Check the input power (voltage and frequency). Verify the primary reconnect is properly configured for the input voltage. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation if problem persists after firmware update.

LECO-050.message: Cap A under voltage (Cap A volts, Cap B volts)
LECO-050.cause: The voltage on one of the two input capacitor banks (bank A) has fallen below the normal operating limit. This is normally caused by low input voltage or a missing phase (with 3 phase input power) but it could be caused by a faulty switch board, main capacitor, contactor, or V-to-F feedback signal.
LECO-050.remedy: Check the input power (voltage and frequency). Verify the primary reconnect is properly configured for the input voltage.

LECO-051.message: Cap B under voltage (Cap A volts, Cap B volts)
LECO-051.cause: The voltage on one of the two input capacitor banks (bank B) has fallen below the normal operating limit. This is normally caused by low input voltage or a missing phase (with 3 phase input power) but it could be caused by a faulty switch board, main capacitor, contactor, or V-to-F feedback signal.
LECO-051.remedy: Check the input power (voltage and frequency). Verify the primary reconnect is properly configured for the input voltage.

LECO-052.message: Cap A over voltage (Cap A volts, Cap B volts)
LECO-052.cause: The voltage on one of the two input capacitor banks (bank A) has exceeded the high voltage limit. This is normally caused by high input voltage but it could be caused by a faulty switch board, main capacitor, contactor, or V-to-F feedback signal.
LECO-052.remedy: Check the input power (voltage and frequency). Verify the primary reconnect is properly configured for the input voltage.

LECO-053.message: Cap B over voltage (Cap A volts, Cap B volts)
LECO-053.cause: The voltage on one of the two input capacitor banks (bank B) has exceeded the high voltage limit. This is normally caused by high input voltage but it could be caused by a faulty switch board, main capacitor, contactor, or V-to-F feedback signal.
LECO-053.remedy: Check the input power (voltage and frequency). Verify the primary reconnect is properly configured for the input voltage.

LECO-054.cause: The machine has shutdown because it has overheated. This will normally occur because the output duty cycle has been exceeded but it could be caused by insufficient air flow through the machine, a faulty fan, or a faulty thermostat.
LECO-054.remedy: Verify the welding procedure does not exceed the duty cycle limits of the machine. Check the setup for proper air flow around and through the system. Check that the system has been properly maintained, including removal of accumulated dust and dirt from the intake and outlet louvers and the cooling channels in the machine. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation if problem persists.

LECO-055.cause: During the start up sequence, the capacitor banks failed to reach an expected minimum voltage. This can be caused by a faulty contactor or low input voltage; this error is typically accompanied by other errors that should also be reviewed.
LECO-055.remedy: Check the input power (voltage and frequency). Verify the primary reconnect is properly configured for the input voltage. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation if problem persists.

LECO-065.cause: A high level of output current (long average) has caused an overload. This is commonly seen if the wrong output stud is used on an STT machine or if there is a missing phase (with 3 phase input power). When this fault occurs, the output current will be reduced to 100A and a welding condition referred to as "noodle welding" may occur.
LECO-065.remedy: For process related issues, verify the welding procedure does not exceed the output limits of the machine. Verify the stick out, wire size, and gas are correct for the process that is selected. Check the weld circuit for short circuits and other leakage paths. Verify all three legs of the input power are present at the input contactor. When the contactor closes, be sure all three legs are present on the output side as well (toward the rectifier). Machines equipped with an STT output stud use a lower secondary output limit to protect the STT circuitry. If the machine is equipped with an STT output stud, consider using the standard output stud for more demanding applications. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware.

LECO-067.cause: The voltage difference between the two input capacitor banks has exceeded the safe limit. This will normally occur when the power is turned ON (if the machine has not been used for a long period) or if there is a missing phase (with 3 phase input power) but it could also be caused by a faulty switch board, main capacitor, or main transformer.
LECO-067.remedy: Check input line voltage. Check reconnect links and cables. AC/DC Systems: Check for shorts in the welding circuit. Make sure feedhead is properly isolated.

LECO-069.cause: The machine detected that the welding voltage was to high. Verify the correct input voltage selection has be made on the main reconnect switch.

LECO-070.cause: A high level of output current (short average) has caused an overload. This is commonly seen when there is a short in the welding circuit outside of the machine. It can also be caused if the wrong output stud is used on an STT machine or if there is a missing phase (with 3 phase input power) and this can also occur when starting high current welding processes.
LECO-070.remedy: Verify that the welding circuit does not have a short in it. Verify stick out, wire size, and gas are correct for the process that is selected. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware.

LECO-073.cause: Single phase input power has been detected so the machine may operate at a reduced output level. Refer to the instruction manual of the machine for more information on single phase operation.
LECO-073.remedy: Verify all fuses are good. Verify all three legs of the input power are present at the input contactor. When the contactor closes, be sure all three legs are present on the output side as well (toward the rectifier). If single phase operation is intentional, and secondary over current errors are a problem, verify the welding procedure does not exceed the reduced output limits of the machine. Check the weld circuit for short circuits and other leakage paths.

LECO-098.cause: Weld settings could not be updated properly while the system was welding. This normally occurs when a device is not operating properly or it is busy handling other operations such as external communications.
LECO-098.remedy: Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation if problem persists after firmware update.

LECO-129.cause: The wire feeder drive motor has been overloaded. This can be caused by a wire tangle or a high resistance from pulling wire off of the spool or drum.
LECO-129.remedy: Check Drive tension. Check drive rolls alignment and gears. Check Wire feed ability and control cables are not run along current currying conduit. If the system is in a constant current welding mode and the feeder is operating at its upper limit then configure the to run at a faster gear ratio. Change the voltage sensing locating to be closer to the arc. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware.

LECO-130.cause: The wire feeder drive motor has been overloaded by exceeding the current limit. This can be caused by a wire tangle or a high resistance from pulling wire off of the spool or drum.

LECO-131.cause: Shutdown circuit #1 on the wire drive external I/O connector is open. This open circuit generates an error in order to stop the machine.
LECO-131.remedy: Verify the circuit "Shutdown1 Input" is closed. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware.

LECO-132.cause: Shutdown circuit #2 (typically a water cooler fault) on the wire drive external I/O connector is open. This open circuit generates an error in order to stop the machine.
LECO-132.remedy: Verify the circuit "Shutdown2 Input (Water Fault)" is closed. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware.

LECO-356.cause: The machine could not properly send an email. Verify the correct settings are entered into the email system and that there is a mail server on the Ethernet network.
LECO-356.remedy: Use Production Monitoring software to verify E-mail configuration. Verify Ethernet connection.

LECO-357.cause: Email settings could not be properly restored. All email settings need to be verified.
LECO-357.remedy: Use Production Monitoring software to verify E-mail configuration. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware.

LECO-769.cause: Production Monitoring weld totals could not be saved when the machine was turned OFF. The values for the weld totals displayed in the Weld Totals tab of the application and the information included in the summary email report may be incomplete.
LECO-769.remedy: Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation if problem persists after firmware update.

LECO-770.cause: Production Monitoring weld profiles configuration could not be saved when the machine was turned OFF.
LECO-770.remedy: Verify the configuration of Production Monitoring weld profiles. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation if problem persists after firmware update.

LECO-771.cause: Production Monitoring system configuration could not be saved when the machine was turned OFF.
LECO-771.remedy: Verify the configuration of Production Monitoring. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation if problem persists after firmware update.

LECO-772.cause: Production Monitoring weld totals could not be restored when the machine was turned ON. The values for the weld totals displayed in the Weld Totals tab of the application and the information included in the summary email report may be incomplete.
LECO-772.remedy: Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation if problem persists after firmware update.

LECO-773.cause: Production Monitoring weld profiles configuration could not be restored when the machine was turned ON.
LECO-773.remedy: Verify the configuration of Production Monitoring weld profiles. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation if problem persists after firmware update.

LECO-774.cause: Production Monitoring system configuration could not be restored when the machine was turned ON.
LECO-774.remedy: Verify the configuration of Production Monitoring. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation for flashing system with latest Firmware. Notify FANUC or FANUC America Corporation if problem persists after firmware update.

LECO-849.cause: The output current is outside the Production Monitoring weld profile limits. The output current was less than the Current Low Limit or was greater than the Current High Limit.
LECO-849.remedy: Verify welding set points, changes in setup, and work piece position. Setup includes but is not limited to: gas flow, wire type and size, stick out, welding cable length, spatter buildup, and tip wear. Verify the start delay and end delay are properly configured to remove the start and end of the weld.

LECO-850.cause: The output voltage is outside the Production Monitoring weld profile limits. The output voltage was less than the Voltage Low Limit or was greater than the Voltage High Limit.
LECO-850.remedy: Verify welding set points, changes in setup, and work piece position. Setup includes but is not limited to: gas flow, wire type and size, stick out, welding cable length, spatter buildup, and tip wear. Verify the voltage limits for the weld profile are a reasonable range for the application. This would also include "Seconds Until Voltage Limit" in the General Settings section. Verify the start delay and end delay are properly configured to remove the start and end of the weld.

LECO-851.cause: The wire feed speed (WFS) is outside the Production Monitoring weld profile limits. The wire feed speed was less than the WFS Low Limit or was greater than the WFS High Limit.
LECO-851.remedy: Verify the welding setting for wire feed speed is correct. Verify the wire feed limits for the weld profile are a reasonable range for the application. This would also include "Seconds Until WFS Limit" in the General Settings section. Verify the start delay and end delay are properly configured to remove the start and end of the weld.

LECO-853.cause: The welding time (arc time) is outside the Production Monitoring weld profile limits. The welding time was less than the Time Low Limit or was greater than the Time High Limit.
LECO-853.remedy: Verify the weld was made at the proper travel speed and for the correct amount of time. Verify the time limits for the weld profile.

LECO-865.cause: The output current is outside the Production Monitoring weld profile limits. The output current was less than the Current Low Limit or was greater than the Current High Limit.
LECO-865.remedy: Verify welding set points, changes in setup, and work piece position. Setup includes but is not limited to: gas flow, wire type and size, stick out, welding cable length, spatter buildup, and tip wear. Verify the current limits for the weld profile are a reasonable range for the application. This would also include "Seconds Until Current Limit" in the General Settings section. Verify the start delay and end delay are properly configured to remove the start and end of the weld.

LECO-867.cause: The wire feed speed (WFS) is outside the Production Monitoring weld profile limits. The wire feed speed was less than the WFS Low Limit or was greater than the WFS High Limit.

This would also include "Seconds Until WFS Limit" in the General Settings section. Verify the start delay and end delay are properly configured to remove the start and end of the weld.

LECO-869.cause: The welding time (arc time) is outside the Production Monitoring weld profile limits. The welding time was less than the Time Low Limit or was greater than the Time High Limit.
LECO-869.remedy: Verify the weld was made at the proper travel speed and for the correct amount of time. Verify the time limits for the weld profile.

LECO-881.cause: Production Monitoring could not perform limit checking on a weld because the welding time (arc time) was too short. The welding time was less than the combined time for the Start Delay and End Delay.
LECO-881.remedy: Verify the duration of the weld is greater then the combination of the start delay and end delay. Verify the time limits for the weld profile.

LECO-882.cause: The wire package weight has dropped below the Production Monitoring "Warning Package Weight" limit. The supply of wire should be checked and replaced if necessary. The welding time was less than the combined time for the Start Delay and End Delay.
LECO-882.remedy: Replenish the wire package and reset the current wire weight. Verify the following setup items have been correctly entered: Initial Package Weight, Warning Package Weight, Wire Diameter, and Metal Density.

LECO-897.cause: The output current is outside the Production Monitoring weld profile limits. The output current was less than the Current Low Limit or was greater than the Current High Limit.
LECO-897.remedy: Verify welding set points, changes in setup, and work piece position. Setup includes but is not limited to: gas flow, wire type and size, stick out, welding cable length, spatter buildup, and tip wear. Verify the current limits for the weld profile are a reasonable range for the application. This would also include "Seconds Until Current Limit" in the General Settings section. Setup includes but is not limited to: gas flow, wire type and size, stick out, welding cable length, spatter buildup, and tip wear. LECO-899.cause: The wire feed speed (WFS) is outside the Production Monitoring weld profile limits. The wire feed speed was less than the WFS Low Limit or was greater than the WFS High Limit.
LECO-899.remedy: Verify the welding setting for wire feed speed is correct. Verify the wire feed limits for the weld profile are a reasonable range for the application. This would also include "Seconds Until WFS Limit" in the General Settings section. Verify the start delay and end delay are properly configured to remove the start and end of the weld.
