NCBN-009.remedy: Correct the command syntax and load the program again

NCBN-010.cause: Commands are not placed in right order
NCBN-010.remedy: Correct the command syntax and load the program again

NCBN-011.message: Only one M-code allowed each line
NCBN-011.cause: Only one M-code per line is allowed
NCBN-011.remedy: Correct the command syntax and load the program again

NCBN-012.cause: A T-code is expected for this M-code
NCBN-012.remedy: Correct the command syntax and load the program again

NCBN-013.cause: NC conversion software is required to process this file type

NCBN-014.cause: Specified program was not loaded due to error this file type
NCBN-014.remedy: Look at the cause code on the 2nd line of the screen, and fix the error

NCBN-015.message: File Name must be Prog name
NCBN-015.cause: Program name and file name does not match
NCBN-015.remedy: The NC file name must be the same as the program name specified by the O-code Example: File name O1234.NC should be used for program 'O1234'

NCBN-016.cause: position field indicated is not initialized
NCBN-016.remedy: Make sure all position components are specified

OPTN-000.remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

OPTN-001.cause: The maximum number of software options/updates (50) is installed.
OPTN-001.remedy: None required. Options/updates will load but not be logged.

OPTN-002.cause: Installation of software option/update has finished successfully.
OPTN-002.remedy: This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

OPTN-003.cause: S/W option was skipped by installer.
OPTN-003.remedy: Some options cannot be overlayed, you may need to delete some options first.

OPTN-006.cause: The specified software option was not installed properly.

OPTN-007.cause: Software option has not been authorized for this configuration.
OPTN-007.remedy: Call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

OPTN-008.cause: The required floppy disk was not used.
OPTN-008.remedy: Reinstall the option using the required floppy disk.

OPTN-009.cause: Software option is now authorized for this configuration.
OPTN-009.remedy: This is a notification. No action is needed.

OPTN-010.cause: Setup Application has not been done

OPTN-011.cause: Power down and then up is needed
OPTN-011.remedy: Turn the controller off, and then back on

OPTN-012.cause: The LICENSE file, license.dat, is missing or corrupted
OPTN-012.remedy: Do a full load from the original distribution media.

OPTN-013.cause: The supplied PAC is not valid for this option.
OPTN-013.remedy: Obtain a valid PAC for this option.

OPTN-014.cause: The option nesting tree is too deep.

OPTN-015.cause: This option is not compatible with an option that is already installed.

OPTN-016.cause: The KEY file, keyfile.dat, is missing or corrupted
OPTN-016.remedy: Do a full load from the original distribution media.

OPTN-017.cause: The distribution media does not contain, update.tx, so there are no updates to install.

OPTN-018.cause: The distribution media does not contain, custom.tx, so there are no customizations to install.

OPTN-019.cause: The distribution media contains updates or customizations, but has a different release version than this core.

OPTN-020.cause: The maximum number of feature references in the.fd files is exceeded. These include: REQUIRE, INCLUDE, EXCLUDE
OPTN-020.remedy: If the alarm includes: Increase KAREL constant: CONFIG CLIMIT REQUIRE DLIMIT OPTION OLIMIT Robot REQUIRE RLIMIT STANDARD SLIMIT

OPTN-021.cause: One or more lines in orderfil.dat have Order Numbers for options that can not work for this ApplicationTool.
OPTN-021.remedy: Remove or correct the line that contains the specified Order Number.

OPTN-022.cause: The Demonstration version of the option provides 60 days of free operation. This message indicates that there are “%d” days that are left for this option to operate. Option operation will be restricted or eliminated after that. The Order No. of the specific option is provided in the Cause message.
OPTN-022.remedy: None is required. If use beyond the 60 days is required, then the option can be purchased and authorized for permanent operation.

OPTN-023.message: Max number of arms is exceeded.
OPTN-023.cause: The maximum number of robot arms allowed has been exceeded. The default max number of arms is 2.
OPTN-023.remedy: Load TQAP:Triple Quad Arm Package to increase the max number of robot arms to 4.

OPTN-024.cause: The maximum number of motion groups is installed.
OPTN-024.remedy: None required. All of the setup for the Motion Group might not be complete.

OPTN-025.cause: The 60-day use period of this DEMO option has expired.
OPTN-025.remedy: Choose Controlled Start for the controller and then choose MENUS, S/W INSTALL, Option, then DEMOS. Please authorize this option. Refer to the Controller Software Installation Manual or contact your FANUC America Corporation Representative for more information.

OPTN-026.cause: Software option is now demo authorized for this configuration.
OPTN-026.remedy: This is a notification. No action is needed.

OPTN-027.cause: Controller ID does not match license ID.
OPTN-027.remedy: Correct from Reserialize Page at CTRL Start.

OPTN-028.cause: The supplied LAC is not valid for this controller.
OPTN-028.remedy: Correct from Reserialize Page at CTRL Start.

OPTN-029.cause: The supplied LAC is valid for this controller.
OPTN-029.remedy: This is a notification. No action is needed.

OPTN-030.cause: A small number of retries is allowed to authorize an option or re-authorize a license file.
OPTN-030.remedy: Obtain a valid PAC or LAC, and enter the numbers accurately.

OPTN-031.cause: The KAREL option, R632, must be installed in order to load this file.

OPTN-032.cause: Extending the number of days to use a Demonstration options is not valid in this context.
OPTN-032.remedy: Only Demonstration options can be extended. Permanent options can NOT be extended. Authorized options can NOT be extended.

OPTN-033.cause: Controller Image should be backed up prior to installing options. This allows you to restore an image without the added options should you need to.
OPTN-033.remedy: Backup your controller image prior to installing. additional options.

OPTN-034.cause: The controller image cannot be backed up at this time. An AutoUpdate is needed to complete this option installation.
OPTN-034.remedy: Press AUTOUPDT to complete this option installation.

OPTN-035.cause: The controller image is already backed up.
OPTN-035.remedy: This is a notification. No action is needed.

OPTN-036.remedy: This is a notification. No action is needed.

OPTN-037.remedy: This is a notification. No action is needed.

OPTN-038.cause: Software option is NOT enabled for this configuration.
OPTN-038.remedy: This is a notification. No action is needed.

OPTN-039.cause: The supplied PEC is not valid for this demonstration option.
OPTN-039.remedy: Obtain a valid PEC for this demonstration option.

OPTN-040.cause: Disabling a Demonstration Options is not valid in this context.
OPTN-040.remedy: A Demonstration Option must be enabled before it can be disabled. For any other state, disabling is not valid.

OPTN-041.message: Must be run from COLD start.
OPTN-041.cause: Autoupdate must be run from COLD start.

OPTN-042.cause: There is a limit to how many options can be installed at once.
OPTN-042.remedy: Autoupdate to install current pending options, then install more.

OPTN-044.cause: The 90-day use period for evaluation options has expired.
OPTN-044.remedy: Choose Controlled Start for the controller and then choose MENU, S/W INSTALL, Option, then Evaluation Option. Please ENABLE any option. Refer to the Controller Software Installation Manual.

OS-002.cause: The function performed by the user is not supported or is invalid.
OS-002.remedy: Consult the appropriate manual and verify the useage of the attempted operation. Try it again, if possible. If you try again and still get this error, record the events that led to the error and contact your FRNA tech representative.

OS-144.remedy: Contact the FRNA hotline and provide the following information for further investigation. o Record the entire error message(s) that occurred including any program running at the time of the system error. o Retrieve the following files from the File Menu: md:histe.ls md:histr.ls md:hists.ls md:histp.ls md:conslog.ls md:errall.ls o In addition for a system V5.22 or greater, do a diagnostic backup from the file menu to send to FRNA.

OS-145.cause: Usually a result of previous unrecoverable system error.
OS-145.remedy: Cycle power on the controller. If error message persists, then contact the FRNA hotline for further investigation.

OS-147.cause: An assert occurred on the MAIN processor.
OS-147.remedy: Record and report the parameters following the 'Assert MAIN' text to the FANUC America Corporation Help Hotline.

OS-148.cause: An assert occurred on the MAIN processor.
OS-148.remedy: Record and report the parameters following the 'Assert MAIN' text to the FANUC America Corporation Help Hotline.

OS-149.cause: An assert occurred on the VMAIN processor.
OS-149.remedy: Record and report the parameters following the 'Assert MAIN' text to the FANUC America Corporation Help Hotline.

OS-150.cause: An assert occurred on the VCOMM processor.
OS-150.remedy: Record and report the parameters following the 'Assert MAIN' text to the FANUC America Corporation Help Hotline.

PALL-001.message: Length must be longer than width
PALL-001.cause: The length dimension must always be greater than the width.
PALL-001.remedy: If the specified length was less than the width, then the length is forced to the width dimension. If the specified width was greater than the length, then the width is forced to the length dimension. Specify the correct length or width.

PALL-002.cause: A layer number greater than the maximum allowed layers was specified.
PALL-002.remedy: Specify a layer number less than the allowed maximum.

PALL-003.message: Cannot Flip Lt or Wd for Unique
PALL-003.cause: The length or width flip was specified for a unique matrix which is not allowed.
PALL-003.remedy: Specify No flip or diagonal (length and width) flip for the unique matrix.

PALL-004.cause: Point P1 on the teaching aid was not taught.
PALL-004.remedy: Teach P1 on the teaching aid.

PALL-005.message: Layer Barrier on last cyc only.
PALL-005.cause: The layer barrier cannot be selected for anything but the last cycle of a layer.
PALL-005.remedy: Select the layer barrier for the last cycle only.

PALL-006.cause: The user selected * or Layer barrier without enabling Configure all layers from the Optimal Path menu.
PALL-006.remedy: Set Configure All Layers to TRUE in the Optimal Path menu before selecting * for the Sequence.

PALL-007.message: Layer Barrier invalid on top lyr
PALL-007.cause: The layer barrier cannot be specified for the top layer.

PALL-008.cause: The specified sequence number was not found.
PALL-008.remedy: The sequence should include all the items in the layer.

PALL-009.message: Lyr bar invalid w/ slipsheet enb
PALL-009.cause: You cannot break the layer barrier if you have a slip sheet between two layers.
PALL-009.remedy: If you want a layer barrier, remove the slip sheet between the layers by removing the layer spacing between the layers. Or do not use the layer barrier.

PALL-010.cause: The position the robot is trying to go to is not reachable. If the preceeding error is: 'Error: Pallet=x Unit=y', it means that the robot was working with pallet x and box y when the error occured.
PALL-010.remedy: Verify that the value of $UTOOL and/or $MNUTOOL are correct. If the robot stopped while heading towards the pallet, then check the value of Pallet approach length and width in Optimal path setup. You might have specified large pallet offsets or you might need to specify a correct pallet offset in the Optimal path setup.

PALL-011.cause: The position has not been taught.

PALL-012.cause: Motion control was not obtained for robot motion.
PALL-012.remedy: Check if another task is running, or if the teach pendant is enabled. The teach pendant should be disabled

PALL-013.cause: Data in a SETUP menu could not be set.
PALL-013.remedy: Cold start the controller, and retry the operation.

PALL-014.cause: Data in a SETUP menu could not be set.
PALL-014.remedy: Cold start the controller, and retry the operation.

PALL-015.cause: An error occurred while creating an infeed or pallet station file.
PALL-015.remedy: Cold start the controller, and retry the operation.

PALL-016.cause: The data in the sequence screen is valid.

PALL-017.cause: PalletTool allows initialization of palletizing data by allowing users to pass a cycle number to the CALL PMPROCDT(cycle_number) in some teach pendant programs. If the user passes an invalid cycle number which is less than or equal to zero, or higher than the maximum number of cycles which is 20, or a number higher than the number of cycles in the application, this error will result.
PALL-017.remedy: Make sure to pass a valid cycle number to the call to PMPROCDT in the teach pendant program used.

PALL-018.cause: The.VR file does not exist, or an error occurred in communication.
PALL-018.remedy: Check the communication line, and make sure that the file exists on the floppy.

PALL-019.message: Could not create unit load file
PALL-019.cause: An error occurred while creating unit load file.
PALL-019.remedy: Cold start the controller, and retry the operation.

PALL-020.message: Could not open.DT file for read
PALL-020.cause: An error occurred while opening a.DT file.
PALL-020.remedy: Cold start the controller, and retry the operation.

PALL-021.cause: An I/O error occurred during the data transfer.
PALL-021.remedy: Cold start the controller, and retry the operation.

PALL-022.cause: Error occurred while saving a.VR file.
PALL-022.remedy: Cold start the controller, and retry the operation.

PALL-024.cause: 1. An error occurred while loading a.VR file. 2. The gripper setup file from previous versions of PalletTool cannot be read. The number of grippers was increased and the structure of the data has change. The error: “VARS-014 Create type - xxxx failed” will be displayed.
PALL-024.remedy: Cold start the controller and retry the operation if you know you should be able to read the.vr file into PalletTool.

PALL-028.cause: An error occurred while accessing the floppy disk.
PALL-028.remedy: Make sure the communication is correct, and retry the operation.

PALL-029.cause: The file transfer was not successful. Some data might not have been transferred.
PALL-029.remedy: Cold start the controller, and retry the operation.

PALL-030.cause: No.DT files exist on the floppy.
PALL-030.remedy: .DT files must exist on the floppy in order to perform the transfer.

PALL-031.cause: The specified station number is not loaded.
PALL-031.remedy: Load the station file, or create one.

PALL-032.cause: The pallet station specified in PalletSystem setup has not been taught.
PALL-032.remedy: Teach the pallet station specified in PalletSystem setup.

PALL-033.cause: The unit load file is not loaded.
PALL-033.remedy: Perform one of the following: • Load the Unit load file. • Transfer the.DT file. • Create a new.DT file. Retry the operation.

PALL-035.cause: An invalid layer number was entered at cycle start or passed from the PLC. Or, PalletTool encountered an invalid layer number while doing its data processing.
PALL-035.remedy: Make sure to enter a valid layer for each cycle at cycle start or in passing the data to the PLC.

PALL-036.cause: The user is trying to select the multi-case gripper but the multi-case option is not installed.

PALL-037.cause: The user is trying to select fork gripper but the fork gripper option is not installed.

PALL-038.cause: The infeed station specified in PalletSystem setup has not been taught.
PALL-038.remedy: Teach the infeed station specified in the PalletSystem setup.

PALL-040.cause: The specified flip type is unknown to PalletTool.
PALL-040.remedy: Check the value of flip type in Unit load SETUP. It should be a known flip type.

PALL-041.cause: The specified infeed station is not taught or loaded.
PALL-041.remedy: Teach or load the infeed station.

PALL-044.cause: An orientation besides LT_ON_LT or WD_ON_LT for a box in a layer was encountered by PalletTool while either PalletTool PC or PalletPRO data was downloaded to the controller.
PALL-044.remedy: Make sure to visit the screen in PalletTool PC or PalletPRO where unit orientation for each unit in a layer is defined and make sure that there are no blanks. If this does not resolve the problem while downloading, re-enter the proper orientation for each unit in PalletTool PC or PalletPRO even though the screen might show valid values.

PALL-045.cause: The unit load data file was created using PalletMate PC.
PALL-045.remedy: Data created using PalletMate PC cannot be changed in PalletTool. You must go back to the PC to make the changes, and then retransfer the file.

PALL-046.cause: An error occurred while PalletTool was internally trying to run another program in multi-tasking mode.
PALL-046.remedy: Perform an ABORT ALL, and retry the operation.

PALL-048.cause: An error occurred while PalletTool was trying to open a.TP program.
PALL-048.remedy: Make sure that the.TP program is loaded, and retry the operation.

PALL-049.cause: An error occurred while PalletTool was trying to set a position in a.TP program.
PALL-049.remedy: Cold start the controller, and retry the operation.

PALL-050.cause: An error occurred while PalletTool was trying to open a.TP program.
PALL-050.remedy: Cold start the controller, and retry the operation.

PALL-051.cause: Slip sheet support is not provided.
PALL-051.remedy: Disable slip sheet in the PalletSystem menu.

PALL-052.cause: Some patterns from older versions of PalltetTool are no longer supported.
PALL-052.remedy: Create a new unitload, and select a different pattern.

PALL-053.cause: Depalletizing was chosen with a gripper other than single.
PALL-053.remedy: Choose single gripper for depalletizing, and retry the operation.

PALL-054.cause: A request for picking up 0 part was received.
PALL-054.remedy: Abort all and retry the operation.

PALL-055.remedy: Perform an ABORT ALL, and retry the operation.

PALL-057.cause: The specified gripper is unknown to PalletTool.
PALL-057.remedy: Check the value of the gripper-id in Optimal path setup. The valid range is 1-9. A value of 10 is also allowed if the multi-case option is loaded. A value of 11 and 12 are also allowed if the fork option is loaded.

PALL-058.cause: A PalletMate PC pattern cannot be selected while creating or modifying a unit load.
PALL-058.remedy: Single, Doubleside, DoubleTop, or Unique Other patterns can only be transferred from PalletMate PC.

PALL-059.cause: An error occurred while clearing a variable file. If a.vr file was loaded into memory at Controlled start, it can only be cleared at Controlled start.
PALL-059.remedy: 1. Wait until production is aborted and clear the unit load. 2. If the unitload was loaded at Controlled start, you will have to go to controlled start to clear it. At Controlled start, press MENUS, select Clear UnitLd. You will only be able to clear unitloads that were loaded at Controlled start from the Controlled start menu.

PALL-063.cause: Product-id is not set in the UL file.
PALL-063.remedy: Set the product_id in the UL file from Unit load SETUP.

PALL-064.cause: The motion to P1, P2 or P3 on the teaching aid was successful.

PALL-065.cause: An invalid register value was encountered.
PALL-065.remedy: From the DATA menu, verify that the register contains the correct value.

PALL-066.remedy: Check if the register is defined, if it is between 1-64, and if it has the right value. You must perform an ABORT ALL and retry the operation.

PALL-067.cause: Could not set an internally calculated value V to the register R.
PALL-067.remedy: From the DATA menu, verify that the register is defined, is in the range 1-64, and has the correct value. Must ABORT ALL and retry.

PALL-068.cause: The infeed on which the unit load enters the workcell was not assigned in the PalletSystem menu.
PALL-068.remedy: Make the infeed-unit load assignment in the PalletSystem SETUP menu. You must perform an ABORT ALL and retry the operation.

PALL-069.cause: A valid unit load number was not found at the layer indicated for the mixed unit load.
PALL-069.remedy: From the Mixed UnitLd menu, indicate valid unit load numbers for each unit layer. Perform an ABORT ALL and retry the operation.

PALL-071.cause: Not all the pallets have been assigned a unit load in PalletSystem menu.
PALL-071.remedy: This is only a warning message. Make sure in PalletSystem menu, that all the pallets have a corresponding unit load assigned.

PALL-072.cause: Not all of the infeeds have been assigned a unit load in the PalletSystem menu.
PALL-072.remedy: Make sure that in the PalletSystem menu, all of the infeeds have a corresponding unit load assigned.

PALL-073.cause: All the teaching aid points have been taught, and the teaching of the station is complete.

PALL-074.cause: The perch position is uninitialized (has not been taught).
PALL-074.remedy: 1. Select PM_MAIN from the SELECT screen. 2. Press DATA. 3. Jog the robot to the perch position. 4. Record the variable perch position. 5. Perform an ABORT ALL and retry the operation.

PALL-081.cause: This is a notification that the robot will move to the perch position.

PALL-082.cause: This is a notification that the pallet is being indexed.

PALL-083.cause: This is a notification that the slip sheet is being placed.

PALL-085.cause: The program cannot run with the operator panel EMERGENCY STOP button pressed.
PALL-085.remedy: 1. Release the operator panel EMERGENCY STOP button. 2. Press RESET. 3. Press CYCLE START.

PALL-086.cause: The program cannot run with the teach pendant EMERGENCY STOP button pressed.
PALL-086.remedy: 1. Release the teach pendant EMERGENCY STOP button. 2. Press RESET. 3. Press CYCLE START.

PALL-087.cause: The program cannot run with teach pendant enabled.
PALL-087.remedy: 1. Disable the teach pendant. 2. Press RESET. 3. Press CYCLE START.

PALL-088.cause: PALLET STOP is already on. You can only have either CYCLE STOP or PALLET STOP on, not both.
PALL-088.remedy: Disable PALLET STOP, then enable CYCLE STOP.

PALL-089.cause: CYCLE STOP is already on. You can only have either CYCLE STOP or PALLET STOP on, not both.
PALL-089.remedy: Disable CYCLE STOP, then enable PALLET STOP.

PALL-091.cause: One of the slip sheet stack doors is open.
PALL-091.remedy: Find out which slip sheet stack door is open, and close it. Press CYCLE START to resume.

PALL-101.message: File is in use by robot. Cannot transfer
PALL-101.cause: The robot is attempting to transfer a unit load file that is being used by the robot. It is being used in production, or is being edited using the SETUP UNITLOAD or SETUP OPTIMAL PATH menus.
PALL-101.remedy: 1. Stop the robot. 2. Peform an ABORT ALL. 3. Try the file transfer again.

PALL-105.cause: Either (P1,P2), (P1, P3), (P2, P3), or (P1,P2,P3) were all taught at the same point.
PALL-105.remedy: Use MODIFY under the Infeed Stn SETUP menu to reteach the frame points P1, P2 and P3 correctly.

PALL-106.cause: There is only one pallet in the workcell.
PALL-106.remedy: This is only a message. NOSWITCH is the only option allowed for one Pallet cell.

PALL-108.cause: The robot did not get part presence or faulty part presence sensor.
PALL-108.remedy: Check if the gripper is in contact with the part and determine why the part presence sensor is not turning on.

PALL-109.cause: Part presence sensor is still detecting part or faulty sensor
PALL-109.remedy: Check if part presence is OFF and if not if the sensor is ok.

PALL-112.cause: The number of pallets is greater than 1 (one) and the pallet switch was NOSWITCH. This is not allowed in PalletTool.
PALL-112.remedy: This is only a message. By default, PalletTool forces PER_PICK. You can change this to other values except NOSWITCH.

PALL-113.cause: The program cannot run if teach pendant is not enabled.
PALL-113.remedy: This if for safety reasons. Enable the teach pendant, and press the Tool 1 or Tool 2 hardkey if necessary.

PALL-114.message: Must index pallet before changing product
PALL-114.cause: A partial or completed pallet is present at the station where you want to change the product. If the existing pallet is not indexed, then the new product will crash with the existing pallet.
PALL-114.remedy: Choose the Index pallet from the menu and index the existing pallet first.

PALL-115.cause: Part of the application setup of a robot is done at the first Cold start. This can take up to 20 seconds. The teach pendant Hints menu will be displayed before PalletTool has loaded all of its.tp programs and macros. NOTE: PalletTool needs an additional Cold start after the application setup Cold start to set up its macros completely.

PALL-117.cause: An error occurred while creating a new file.
PALL-117.remedy: Check the available memory. If RAM is full, clear unneeded data and try the operation again. If necessary, Cold start the controller, and retry the operation.

PALL-118.cause: The robot could not find the requested data.
PALL-118.remedy: Teach or load the required data.

PALL-119.message: Stn file not loaded or created
PALL-119.cause: The specified station is not taught or loaded.

PALL-121.cause: Could not read the unitload.dt file. A Data error exists.
PALL-121.remedy: Check the MOTET communication and PTPC status.

PALL-122.cause: Not all the gripper information has been specified in the PalletSystem setup.
PALL-122.remedy: Display the Gripper MENU, and fill in the gripper information.

PALL-123.cause: The robot is in production. SETUP data cannot be changed during production.
PALL-123.remedy: Wait until production is aborted and then make the changes.

PALL-124.cause: The data was not set up properly but was corrected automatically.
PALL-124.remedy: Make sure the value is set as needed.

PALL-125.cause: The data was not set up properly, but was corrected automatically.
PALL-125.remedy: Make sure the value is set as needed.

PALL-126.cause: The data was not set up properly, but was corrected automatically.
PALL-126.remedy: Make sure the value is set as needed.

PALL-127.cause: The data was not set up properly, but was corrected automatically.
PALL-127.remedy: Make sure the value is set as needed.

PALL-128.cause: The data was not set up properly, but was corrected automatically.
PALL-128.remedy: Make sure the value is set as needed.

PALL-131.cause: Layer count cannot be more than 40 or less than 1.
PALL-131.remedy: Pick a legal layer, and retry the operation.

PALL-132.cause: The program cannot run because an error condition will not clear. When on the ALARM page, select this error and press HELP to see the error detail.
PALL-132.remedy: Fix the error condition, and press RESET.

PALL-133.cause: If the unitload is being used in production it cannot be cleared. If a unitload was loaded into memory at Controlled start, it can only be cleared at Controlled start.
PALL-133.remedy: 1. Wait until production is aborted and clear the unit load. 2. If the unitload was loaded at Controlled start, you will have to go to controlled start to clear it. At a Controlled start, press MENUS, select Clear UnitLd. 3. You will only be able to clear unitloads that were loaded at Controlled start from the Controlled start menu.

PALL-137.message: Unit load num out of range
PALL-137.cause: Specified Unit load number was out of range.
PALL-137.remedy: Specify a Unit load number in the range 1-999.

PALL-138.message: Only Pal OR Cycle stop allowed
PALL-138.cause: PALLET STOP or CYCLE STOP is already on. You can only have either cycle stop, or pallet stop on, not both.
PALL-138.remedy: Disable one before trying to enable the other.

PALL-139.cause: The routine that calculates the final destination position while moving from the current source position has failed. The preceeding error should be: 'Error: Infeed=x Pallet=y Unit=x'. This means that the robot was working with infeed x, pallet y and box z when the error occured.
PALL-139.remedy: Check that all positions are in range.

PALL-140.cause: An old smaller NUMREG.VR or POSREG.VR file was loaded onto the controller. The number of registers or position registers was changed to fewer than what the current version of PalletTool needs.
PALL-140.remedy: PalletTool logic has automatically set the number of registers to the necessary size again. But a Cold start is needed to increase the register or position register table size. Perform a Cold start.

PALL-141.cause: An old smaller SYSMACRO.SV file was loaded onto the controller. The number of macros was changed to fewer than what the current version of PalletTool needs.
PALL-141.remedy: PalletTool logic has automatically set the number of macros to the necessary size again. But it needs a Cold start in order for the macro table size to be increased. Perform a Cold start.

PALL-142.cause: To run a teach pendant program.tp in local mode, you must first select the program.
PALL-142.remedy: Press the SELECT key and choose a program to run. If you are trying to run PalletTool, the keyswitch must be set to REMOTE. If there is no remote/local keyswitch on the controller you have, go to the MENUS -> System -> Config page, and change the remote/local setting in that menu to Remote.

PALL-143.cause: The robot is in production. Set up data cannot be changed during production.
PALL-143.remedy: Wait until production is aborted and then make the changes.

PALL-144.cause: Number of layers in the unit load was changed.
PALL-144.remedy: This is only a warning message to remind you to visit the layer flips and layer spacing menus to make sure that flips and spacing are correct for all the layers.

PALL-145.cause: This error is a general purpose text message posted by PalletTool during production runs for displaying status of an event or to show debug information to the user.

PALL-146.cause: The operator selects which device can be used to start palletizing on the SETUP Pallet System menu. The start device can be set to SOP or UOP/PLC or PTPC.
PALL-146.remedy: The UOP/PLC must be set as the start device or the UOP signal will be ignored.

PALL-147.cause: The operator must select which device can be used to start palletizing on the SETUP Pallet System menu. The start device can be set to SOP or UOP/PLC or PTPC.
PALL-147.remedy: The SOP must be set as the start device on the SETUP Pallet System menu or the SOP signal will be ignored.

PALL-148.cause: The approach position the robot is trying to go to is not reachable. The preceeding error should be: 'Error: Pallet=x Unit=y'. This means that the robot was working with pallet x and box y when the error occured.
PALL-148.remedy: Verify that the value of $UTOOL and/or $MNUTOOL are correct. If the robot stopped while heading towards the pallet, then check the value of Pallet approach length and width in Optimal path setup. You might have specified large pallet offsets or you may need to specify a correct pallet offset in the Optimal path setup.

PALL-149.cause: The placement position the robot is trying to go to is not reachable.
PALL-149.remedy: Verify that the value of $UTOOL and/or $MNUTOOL are correct. If the robot stopped while heading towards the pallet, then check the value of Pallet approach length and width in Optimal path setup You may have specified large pallet offsets or you mamight need to specify a correct pallet offset in the Optimal path setup menu.

PALL-150.cause: There was a problem loading the specified file.
PALL-150.remedy: Check the communication line, and make sure that the file exists on the floppy.

PALL-151.cause: The specified file already exists on the controller.
PALL-151.remedy: Delete the file from the controller before trying to reload it.

PALL-152.cause: The gripper's setup information has an illegal (zero) case number.
PALL-152.remedy: Edit the gripper data and specify a valid case number.

PALL-154.cause: The robot could not read or write the gripper data.
PALL-154.remedy: Check the available memory. Remove unnecessary files, if possible. Try to reload a backup of the gripper data.

PALL-155.cause: This is just a debug message

PALL-156.cause: R[80] is not set up properly when SET UTOOL macros are used.
PALL-156.remedy: Make sure R[80] contains the number of the desired pallet.

PALL-157.cause: The UTOOL of the pallet requested in R[80] is not set up properly.
PALL-157.remedy: Make sure all the stations are completely set up.

PALL-158.cause: This is a warning message posted by PalletTool to help debug problems with unit placement on the pallet.

PALL-159.message: Can change UnitLd on palt %s only
PALL-159.cause: During product changeovers through the Cycle Stop menu, you are first prompted to enter the pallet number where you want to bring the new unitload. This is followed by another menu where you can enter the unitload for that pallet and also assign the infeed which brings the new unitload. If you enter this information for a pallet other than the one you chose first, you will get this error.
PALL-159.remedy: Change the unitload number of the selected pallet.

PALL-160.cause: PalletTool production is aborted because of an error.
PALL-160.remedy: Refer to other errors in the ALARM log for details.

PALL-161.cause: Each of the gripper's cases must have inputs and outputs defined for control.

PALL-162.message: Recvd PLC signal for indexing pallet %s
PALL-162.cause: This is a message to notify the user that PLC data for initiating product changeovers has been received.

PALL-163.cause: The infeed I/O must be set up.
PALL-163.remedy: Make sure the infeed I/O is set up properly: 1. Press MENUS. 2. Select SETUP. 3. Select INFEED STN. 4. SET IO.

PALL-164.message: Gripper number not set in register
PALL-164.cause: R[15] is not set up properly when gripper macros are used.
PALL-164.remedy: Make sure R[15] contains the number of the desired gripper.

PALL-165.message: Invalid Gripper number set in register
PALL-165.cause: R[15] is not set up properly when gripper macros are used. The Gripper numbers supported in PalletTool are: • Single = 1 • Double icc = 3 • Triple case = 5 • Custom 1 = 6 • Custom 2 = 7 • Custom 3 = 8 • Custom 4 = 9 • Multi case = 10 • Fork pick = 11 • Bag push = 12
PALL-165.remedy: Make sure R[15] contains the number of the desired gripper.

PALL-166.cause: Certain variable files can change with each release of PalletTool. Files saved with an older release are automatically updated as needed.

PALL-167.cause: Certain variable files can change with each release of PalletTool. Files saved with an older release are automatically updated as needed.

PALL-168.cause: One of the following has occurred: 1. The number of units in the unitload is less than the start unit entered. 2. The number of units is greater than the maximum allowed (50).
PALL-168.remedy: Enter a valid number of layers.

PALL-169.message: Number of layers %s exceeds allowed maximum
PALL-169.cause: One of the following has occurred: • The number of units in the unitload is less than the start unit entered. • The number of units is greater than the maximum allowed (50).
PALL-169.remedy: Enter a valid number of layers.

PALL-170.message: Invalid pattern type in data file
PALL-170.cause: An illegal matrix type was received from PalletTool PC.
PALL-170.remedy: Check the MOTET communication and PTPC status.

PALL-171.cause: An error condition exists such that the robot cannot be reset.
PALL-171.remedy: Fix the error condition, and press RESET.

PALL-172.cause: The PLC sent an invalid infeed number. The number must be greater than 0, and less than or equal to the 'number of infeeds' set up.
PALL-172.remedy: Make sure a valid infeed number was sent by PLC. Check the PLC communication status.

PALL-173.cause: PLC sent an invalid pallet number. The number must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to the 'number of pallets' set up.
PALL-173.remedy: Make sure a valid pallet number was sent by the PLC. Check the PLC communication status.

PALL-174.cause: This indicates that PalletTool Controlled start setup is complete.

PALL-175.message: Can't use labels-out for triple gripper
PALL-175.cause: Labels out is supported only for the single and double case gripper.

PALL-176.cause: An error occurred while attempting to upgrade an older variable file to the current release format.

PALL-177.message: Single or Double pattern not supported
PALL-177.cause: The selected unitload has the wrong matrix type (it is less than type 4). This very old data is no longer supported by PalletTool.

PALL-178.cause: To run in production, you must calculate each unitload's optimal path data.
PALL-178.remedy: Display the SETUP OPTIMAL PATH screen for this unitload, and press the CALC key.

PALL-179.cause: GETINF.TP returned an infeed number which is assigned ul = 0. In other words, PalletTool received an invalid infeed number, most likely 0 from GETINF.TP.
PALL-179.remedy: Check GETINF.TP for infeed/unitload data. Check production setup data. GETINF.TP is used to return an infeed number for the current cycle. You should modify this program if more than one infeed brought the same unitload to the workcell. In this case, you have to tell PalletTool which infeed to pickup a unit from when both the infeeds have units present. There is an error in the logic of GETINF.TP. Alternatively, you might have provided incorrect assignments at the Cycle Start menu.

PALL-180.cause: The optimal path data was automatically updated.
PALL-180.remedy: Check the labels out data for completeness.

PALL-181.cause: Labels out was selected for a gripper that is not supported.

PALL-182.message: Not allowed for this gripper type
PALL-182.cause: Labels out is supported only for the single and double case gripper. –OR– 'Place remaining boxes' is not allowed for single case grippers.

PALL-183.cause: The CYCLE STOP option has been disabled.

PALL-184.cause: The CYCLE STOP option has been enabled.

PALL-185.cause: The PALLET STOP option has been disabled.

PALL-186.cause: The PALLET STOP option has been enabled.

PALL-187.cause: CYCLE STOP and PALLET STOP functions are only available when the robot is palletizing.

PALL-188.cause: The STEP key was pressed before entering or while in palletizing mode.
PALL-188.remedy: None. The STEP mode is automatically cleared by the system.

PALL-189.cause: Unit load gripper data has not been completely set up.
PALL-189.remedy: Check the variable pick_ar_tc_n and pick_ar_tc_f in the unit load file. Also check the variables new_order_n and new_order_f. See the FANUC America Corporation PalletTool Setup and Operations manual for details on accessing these variables.

PALL-190.cause: During the transfer of data from the PC, the.VR data file could not be created.
PALL-190.remedy: Check the available memory. If RAM is full, clear the unneeded data and try again.

PALL-191.cause: Temporary memory is getting too low to download more unitload files.
PALL-191.remedy: Delete any unneeded data before downloading more unitload files.

PALL-192.cause: Temporary memory is too low to calculate a unitload.
PALL-192.remedy: Delete any unneeded data and perform a Cold start before attempting to calculate the unit load.

PALL-193.cause: The file was not copied. The file is either in use, or there's not enough memory to copy the file.
PALL-193.remedy: Cold start the controller, and retry the operation.

PALL-194.cause: All units must be picked up. Not all the units have been listed in the NEW column.
PALL-194.remedy: Check that no units have been listed twice, change the NEW info, and VERIFY again.

PALL-195.cause: The total number of PLACEs must add up to the number of PICKs for each row of the config table.
PALL-195.remedy: Make sure the sum of the PLACEs adds up to the same number of PICKs.

PALL-196.cause: The PICK size cannot be bigger than the gripper's number of grips.
PALL-196.remedy: Check the selected gripper's grip size, change the PICK info, and VERIFY again.

PALL-197.cause: The PLACE values must be placed into the PL1 column first, then PL2, then PL3. The total of the PLACEs must add up to the number of PICKs for each row of the config table.
PALL-197.remedy: Make sure the sum of the PLACEs adds up to the number of PICKs, and are in the proper columns.

PALL-198.cause: This is a general configuration table error.
PALL-198.remedy: In the Sequence menu, you need to make sure that for the total number of picks, you clearly indicate how all the units are put down. Ex: Pick 3, place_1_1_1.

PALL-199.message: All units not listed in FlipConfig
PALL-199.cause: All units must be picked up.
PALL-199.remedy: Check that no units have been listed twice, change the NEW info, and VERIFY again.

PALL-200.message: All units not listed in NoFlip
PALL-200.cause: All units must be picked up.
PALL-200.remedy: Check that no units have been listed twice, change the NEW info, and VERIFY again.

PALL-201.cause: The total of the PLACEs must add up to the number of PICKs for each row of the config table. And, the total number must add up to the number of units in a layer.
PALL-201.remedy: Make sure the sum of the PLACEs adds up to the number of PICKs.

PALL-202.cause: Part drop recovery: the selected option cannot be used when the robot is at perch or at the gripper maintenance position.

PALL-203.cause: Part drop recovery: the selected option must have boxes remaining in the gripper.
PALL-203.remedy: Choose another option, or check the gripper sensors.

PALL-204.cause: Part drop recovery: the selected option cannot have boxes remaining in the gripper.
PALL-204.remedy: Choose another option, or check the gripper sensors.

PALL-205.message: Error - Processing UL data NOT done
PALL-205.cause: There are errors in the unitload data that caused the CALC calculations failed.
PALL-205.remedy: Correct the unit load errors, and try the CALC operation again.

PALL-206.cause: The requested unitload gripper type cannot be run on this controller. That is, a multi-case gripper unitload can only be run if the multi- case option is loaded on the controller.

PALL-207.cause: There is something wrong with the data that was entered.
PALL-207.remedy: Retype the data, and try the operation again.

PALL-208.cause: The item in error is a duplicate of another entry on the menu.
PALL-208.remedy: Check the entered data. The duplicate will be ignored.

PALL-209.cause: This unitload cannot be calculated during production when PalletTool PC is set as the data device.
PALL-209.remedy: Try this operation again when you are not running production.

PALL-210.message: Xfer in process, cannot edit file
PALL-210.cause: The same unitload as being transferred from PalletTool PC cannot be edited.
PALL-210.remedy: Try the operation again when not transferring or running the unitload.

PALL-211.cause: The controller could not read the.dt file. This is a data error. However, a unitload with the same name still exists on the robot.
PALL-211.remedy: Check the MOTET communication and PTPC status.

PALL-212.cause: The unitload data file transferred from PalletTool PC was not read because there is not enough memory to save the unitload on the robot.
PALL-212.remedy: Delete any unneeded data, and perform a Cold start.

PALL-213.cause: A part was dropped during part drop recovery. PalletTool does not support further recovery.
PALL-213.remedy: Check why parts are being dropped. Continue normal restart of palletizing.

PALL-214.message: The tool pointer length is changed.
PALL-214.cause: You have changed the length of the station teaching tool. All station positions must be taught using the SAME tool length.
PALL-214.remedy: Make sure all station positions are taught with the same tool length.

PALL-215.cause: The robot is moving to the gripper maintenance position.

PALL-216.message: SlipSheet pos. must be cartesian representation
PALL-216.cause: The slip sheet position registers have positions that are taught in JOINT representation. For the slip sheet logic to work properly, the positions must be taught in Cartesian representation.
PALL-216.remedy: Change the position representation to CARTESIAN: 1. Press DATA. 2. Press F1, [TYPE]. 3. Select Position Regs. 4. Select the register. 5. Select POSITION. 6. Press [REPRE]. 7. Select Cartesian.

PALL-217.cause: The position the robot is trying to go to is not reachable.
PALL-217.remedy: Verify that the value of $UTOOL and/or $MNUTOOL are correct. If the robot stopped while heading towards the pallet, then check the value of Pallet approach length and width in the Optimal path SETUP menu. You might have specified large pallet offsets or you might need to specify a correct pallet offset in the Optimal path SETUP menu.

PALL-220.message: Message buffer to PC is full
PALL-220.cause: More than 20 messages have not been read by PTPC. The communication is slow, or has stopped.
PALL-220.remedy: Check the MOTET communication and PTPC status.

PALL-221.message: PTPC message type %s - illegal data received
PALL-221.cause: Message received from PalletTool-PC/MOTET was not in the proper format. The PT-PTPC message types are: • 1-start • 2-cycle stop • 3-pallet stop • 4-status • 5-go • 6-abort • 7-unit data • 8-pallet data • 9-part drop • 10-hold • 11-reset • 12-change done • 13-index • 14-op.grip • 15-cancel • 16-unitload • 17-setup • 18-monitor grip • 19-stop grip • 20-alarms
PALL-221.remedy: Check the MOTET communication and PTPC status.

PALL-222.message: PTPC command ignored, in wrong mode
PALL-222.cause: PalletTool is not in the correct mode to act on this message.

PALL-223.cause: PalletTool is busy and cannot act on this message.

PALL-224.cause: PTPC sent an invalid infeed number. The number must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to the 'number of infeeds' set up.
PALL-224.remedy: Make sure a valid infeed number was sent by PTPC. Make sure that the robot has current setup data from PTPC. Check the MOTET communication and PTPC status.

PALL-225.cause: PTPC sent an invalid pallet number. The number must be greater than 0 and less than or equal to the 'number of pallets' set up.
PALL-225.remedy: Make sure a valid pallet number was sent by PTPC. Make sure that the robot has current setup data from PTPC. Check the MOTET communication and PTPC status.

PALL-226.cause: PTPC sent an invalid gripper number. The Gripper numbers supported in PalletTool are: • Single = 1 • Double icc = 3 • Triple case = 5 • Custom 1 = 6 • Custom 2 = 7 • Custom 3 = 8 • Custom 4 = 9 • Multi case = 10 • Fork pick = 11 • Bag push = 12
PALL-226.remedy: Check the MOTET communication and PTPC status.

PALL-227.cause: PTPC sent the wrong unit load. The unitload that was expected is given in the error message.
PALL-227.remedy: Check the MOTET communication and PTPC status.

PALL-228.cause: PTPC did not send the requested unitload data.
PALL-228.remedy: Check the MOTET communication and PTPC status.

PALL-229.message: Setup data not recvd from PTPC
PALL-229.cause: PTPC did not sent the requested setup data.
PALL-229.remedy: Check the MOTET communication and PTPC status.

PALL-230.cause: PalletTool requested a unitload from PTPC that PTPC did not have. But PalletTool has a copy of the unitload which it will use.
PALL-230.remedy: Make sure the right unitload is being used. Consider changing the control so that Unitload - Use data from: is set to ROBOT/PTPC.

PALL-231.message: PTPC: must be PAUSED or ABORTED
PALL-231.cause: PalletTool is not in the correct mode to act on this message.
PALL-231.remedy: Pause or abort the robot, and try the operation again.

PALL-235.cause: The conveyor infeed positions must be taught in order to use the fork or bag gripper.

PALL-236.cause: The conveyor infeed positions must be taught correctly in order to use the fork or bag gripper.

PALL-237.message: Fork not big enough to pick box
PALL-237.cause: The boxes are too big for this fork gripper.
PALL-237.remedy: Check the conveyor infeed positions and gripper UTOOL values.

PALL-240.cause: MULTI_IO.TP logic received a signal to perform end of batch processing.

PALL-241.cause: Previous end of batch signal processing is still in progress, or a CYCLE STOP or PALLET STOP is still in progress.

PALL-242.cause: The robot is requesting pallet, unitload and infeed information from PLC.

PALL-243.message: End-of-batch PLC - wrong part ID method
PALL-243.cause: Part ID select method must be set to PLC.
PALL-243.remedy: Set the Part ID method to PLC: 1. Press MENUS. 2. Select SETUP. 3. Select PalletSystem. 4. Set the Part ID method to PLC.

PALL-244.cause: The end of batch is complete. The robot is waiting for the PLC to index the pallet.

PALL-245.cause: The end of batch request was ignored.

PALL-246.cause: Nothing exists at the infeed to pick up.

PALL-247.cause: During a product changeover with the End-of-Batch feature enabled, PalletTool expected fewer than needed boxes at infeed for that cycle. However, it detected more boxes than required.
PALL-247.remedy: The end of batch feature works only when there are fewer boxes than needed for that cycle.

PALL-248.cause: The robot dropped a box during the end of batch logic.
PALL-248.remedy: Replace the dropped box, and continue the operation.

PALL-252.cause: The bag gripper UTOOL is not set up in the Gripper SETUP menu.
PALL-252.remedy: Set up the bag gripper UTOOL in the gripper SETUP menu. Without this data, you cannot teach the downstream pick position for the bag on the infeed.

PALL-253.cause: A warning that is posted when you attempt to select a basic, alternate or top-cap pattern before selecting a Mixed layer load to edit.
PALL-253.remedy: Select or enter the Mixed layer load to edit

PALL-254.cause: A warning that is posted when you attempt to select an alternate or top-cap pattern before selecting a basic pattern to edit.
PALL-254.remedy: Select or create a ML first, then select a basic pattern and then select the alt or top pattern.

PALL-255.cause: An invalid ML number was detected such as ML 0 or a ML out of range.
PALL-255.remedy: Select or enter a valid Mixed layer load.

PALL-256.message: Alt pat not allowed for top layer
PALL-256.cause: A warning that is posted when you try to assign an alternate pattern to the top layer

PALL-257.message: Alt pat not allowed for bottom layer
PALL-257.cause: A warning that is posted when you try to assign an alternate pattern to the bottom layer

PALL-258.cause: While retrieving a ML when you made the selection, an invalid UL such as UL 0 or a UL out of range was detected for basic pat.
PALL-258.remedy: Select or enter a valid ML. You are unlikely to see this error.

PALL-259.cause: While retrieving a ML when you made the selection, an invalid UL such as UL 0 or a UL out of range was detected for alt pat.
PALL-259.remedy: Select or enter a valid ML. You are unlikely to see this error.

PALL-260.cause: While retrieving a ML when you made the selection, an invalid UL such as UL 0 or a UL out of range was detected for top pat.
PALL-260.remedy: Select or enter a valid ML. You are unlikely to see this error.

PALL-261.cause: While retrieving a ML, an invalid number of ULs such as 0 or more than 3 was detected.
PALL-261.remedy: Select or enter a valid ML that contains less than 3 unitloads but at least one unitload.

PALL-263.cause: You entered a Unitload for basic, alt or top pattern that does not exist.

PALL-264.message: Please assign Alt pat to Layers
PALL-264.cause: A reminder to the user to assign alternate patterns from the Assign alternate patterns menu.

PALL-265.message: Alt pat not assigned to any layer of ML
PALL-265.cause: If a ML already contained different basic and alternate patterns, but you selected unitload for basic or alt pattern such that they are the same, then this warning is posted.

PALL-266.message: Alt pat not found. Using basic pat for alt pat
PALL-266.cause: When you select a ML for editing, if it contains the same Unitload for all layers or all layers except the top layer, this warning is posted.

PALL-267.cause: A confirmation warning that a new Mixed layer load was created.

PALL-268.cause: A message posted to confirm that the ML that you newly selected or entered, is being retrieved.

PALL-269.message: ML %s cleared. No ULs defined in it.
PALL-269.cause: If you exit the ML setup menu when you have created a ML but did not select any basic, alternate or top patterns, that is, when the ML does not contain any patterns, it is cleared from the controller's memory.

PALL-270.message: Setting Alt Pat to Basic pat in ML %s
PALL-270.cause: If you exit the ML setup menu when you have selected an alternate pattern but did not assign it to any layer from the Assign Alt ULs to layers sub-menu, then this message is posted and the alternate pattern you selected is changed to the basic pattern.
PALL-270.remedy: Whenever you choose an alternate pattern in the main menu, make sure to visit the Assign ULs to layers sub-menu and enable the layers for which the alt pattern should be used.

PALL-271.cause: The mixed layer load that PalletTool is trying to retrieve does not exist.
PALL-271.remedy: Select a valid loaded Mixed Layer load. Make sure it is loaded.

PALL-272.message: ML %s not found in file device
PALL-272.cause: PalletTool could not find the PMMLxxx.vr file.
PALL-272.remedy: Typically, this error occurs when you try to load a ML file but it does not exist in the default file device. The message is just a warning.

PALL-273.cause: A notification that Save of a ML file succeeded.

PALL-274.cause: A notification that load of a ML file succeeded.

PALL-275.cause: A notification that clearing of a ML file succeeded.

PALL-276.cause: A notification that copy of a ML file succeeded.

PALL-277.message: Alt and Basic patterns are the same
PALL-277.cause: When Alt pattern and basic pattern are the same you cannot assign an alternate pattern to layers.
PALL-277.remedy: Choose an alternate pattern that is different from the basic pattern.

PALL-278.message: Alt pat not available for layers < 3
PALL-278.cause: Alt pattern is only available to assign to layers when there are at least 3 layers in the ML. If there is only one layer, then it is the basic pattern. If there are only 2 layers, then the bottom pattern is basic and the other pattern is the top pattern.
PALL-278.remedy: Increase the number of layers in the ML to 3 or greater.

PALL-279.cause: A notification that data recording for collecting profiler data with PalletPRO - duty, cycle time power consumption or life estimation has started.

PALL-280.cause: A notification that data recording for collecting profiler data with PalletPRO - duty, cycle time power consumption or life estimation has ended.

PALL-281.cause: A value other than 0 for off or 1 for on was used as the argument for the program PMPROF.KL which is used for profiler data collection with PalletPRO
PALL-281.remedy: Customers are not expected to use this program. If accidently changed, then restore the original program, or correct the CALL PMPROF to use an argument of 1 or 0.

PALL-282.cause: An attempt to collect profiler data (duty, cycle time, etc.) with PalletPRO was made but the Data Acquisition option which was required was not installed.
PALL-282.remedy: If you wish to collect profiler data with PalletPRO, you need to install the Data Acquisition option (R583).

PALL-283.message: Invalid station: Niether INFEED nor PALLET
PALL-283.cause: During a cycle start or end-of_batch data processing by PalletTool, an invalid station was found for either pick or place.
PALL-283.remedy: Make sure that the data is correct for pick and place station types. Pick = 3, Place = 4.

PALL-284.message: Invalid inf or pal station Id
PALL-284.cause: During a cycle start or end-of_batch data processing by PalletTool, an invalid station id was found for either pick or place.
PALL-284.remedy: Make sure that the data is correct for Infeed

PALL-285.cause: Servo Tool option was needed but was not installed.
PALL-285.remedy: Install the Servo Tool Option. Servo Tool option is required to use the

PALL-286.cause: A different pattern was chosen in the unit load setup menu.
PALL-286.remedy: N/A. This is just a informational message.

PALL-287.cause: An invalid command was sent to the HMI task.

PALL-288.cause: An infeed station was successfully taught using the HMI interface.
PALL-288.remedy: N/A. This is just a informational message.

PALL-289.cause: A pallet station was successfully taught using the HMI interface.
PALL-289.remedy: N/A. This is just a informational message.

PALL-290.cause: The value of the Pointer UTOOL was invalid. while teaching an infeed or pallet station using the HMI interface.
PALL-290.remedy: Set a valid value for pointer UTool

PALL-291.cause: The value of the arrow direction on the teach plate was not sent correctly using the HMI interface.
PALL-291.remedy: Set a valid value for the arrow direction.

PALL-292.cause: The robot was in an overtravel condition when
PALL-292.remedy: N/A. This is just a informational message.

PALL-293.message: Robot is in Motion Limit Error
PALL-293.cause: The robot was in a Motion Limit error condition
PALL-293.remedy: The station should be taught when the robot is not in any error condition.

PALL-294.cause: Invalid data for cycle start was sent through through the HMI Interface.
PALL-294.remedy: Set proper values for infeed id, pallet id,

PALL-295.cause: Valid and Complete data for cycle start was sent through the HMI Interface.
PALL-295.remedy: N/A. This is just a informational message.

PALL-296.cause: The value entered cannot be zero or exceed the maximum number of payloads. The value has been reset.
PALL-296.remedy: N/A. This is just an informational message.

PALT-004.cause: The increment value of the palletizing CONFIG screen is illegal.

PALT-010.remedy: Check the route pattern in the palletizing route pattern screen.

PALT-024.remedy: Verify that you have taught all the bottom points and route points.

PALT-030.cause: Do not teach more than 16 palletizing instructions.
PALT-030.remedy: Do not teach more than 16 palletizing instructions in this program. Reteach the program.

PALT-031.message: Can not be set FREE or INTER
PALT-031.cause: In FREE configuation, can not be set INTER over two directions.
PALT-031.remedy: In FREE configuation, can be set INTER only one direction (ROW, COLUMN or LAYER).

PALT-033.cause: The palletizing option does not support this speed type.

PALT-034.cause: The layer pattern number was 0. Because this is an illegal value, change the layer pattern number to 1.
PALT-034.remedy: Delete the pallet instruction and teach it again.

PALT-035.cause: If Motion group 1 is not set up, The Palletizing option is not avaiable.

PALT-036.cause: A palletizing internal error has occurred.

PALT-037.cause: This command can not be executed in palletizing.

PICK-002.cause: Data could not be obtained from the data source.

PICK-003.cause: Data could not be set in data source.

PICK-004.cause: The robot is in production. Setup data cannot be changed during production.
PICK-004.remedy: Wait until production is aborted, and then make the changes.

PICK-005.cause: The user is attempting to change groups but there is only one installed group.

PICK-006.cause: The user is attempting to set the master for more than one robot or robot group.
PICK-006.remedy: The user should first set Master = FALSE for the robot for which Master is already set to TRUE.

PICK-007.cause: The Host Comm setup is not done for this robot. The robot hostname and IP address are important for the part Queue manager to communicate with and between robots.
PICK-007.remedy: From the Host Comm setup menu, assign a name and a valid IP address for this robot. Also, enter the names and IP addresses of all the other robots on the network.

PICK-008.cause: An error occurred while this robot tried to get data from another robot over the robot ring or Ethernet.
PICK-008.remedy: Check if all robots have a valid IP address and PickTool software. If ok, then document the events that led to the error and provide information on the program and line number where this error occurred to your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

PICK-009.cause: No robot has been set as a master.
PICK-009.remedy: Set one of the robots as master in the Setup menu. Also make sure that there is only one master.

PICK-010.message: More than 1 robot is a master
PICK-010.cause: More than one robot has been set as master.
PICK-010.remedy: Check the setup menus of all the robots and set only one of them as master.

PICK-011.cause: An error occurred reading Line track boundary data.
PICK-011.remedy: Check the line track setup menu and ensure that for the schedule you intend to use, and the boundary set you intend to use, proper values exist. Also check the PK robot setup menu to see if you have entered the proper values for the schedule and the boundary number.

PICK-012.cause: An error occurred reading the Line tracking encoder scale.
PICK-012.remedy: Check the line track setup menu and ensure that for the schedule you intend to use, a proper value for encoder scale exists. If not, teach it. Also check the PK robot setup menu to see if you entered the proper line track schedule number.

PICK-013.cause: The maximum number of robots that Picktool can handle has been exceeded.
PICK-013.remedy: PickTool can handle a maximum of 10 robot groups. Reduce the number of groups or robots to less than 10.

PICK-014.cause: An error occurred while reading data from robot ROBOT_NAME in the robot ring.
PICK-014.remedy: Look at the cause code with the error. Make sure that Ethernet is set up correctly with all the robots. Check the Host Comm menu on each robot and make sure that all members are listed on each controller. Make sure ROSIPCFG.XML in FRS: refers to all members in the Host Comm menu.

PICK-015.cause: An error was encountered while trying to move to a taught position. It could be due to a motion limit error or an incorrectly taught point.
PICK-015.remedy: Make sure to record the position correctly. Check the associated cause code if available.

PICK-016.cause: Without completing frame teaching of all 3 positions, you cannot proceed to the next step.

PICK-017.cause: The robot completed a move-to operation.

PICK-018.cause: The position has not been taught yet.

PICK-019.cause: The position the robot is trying to move to is not reachable.
PICK-019.remedy: Verify that the value of $UTOOL and/or $MNUTOOL are correct

PICK-020.cause: The DOUT port number specified for the conveyor is invalid.
PICK-020.remedy: Check if the I/O point is configured correctly.

PICK-021.message: The ID # of the robot unknown.
PICK-021.cause: The ID# of the robot could not be determined.
PICK-021.remedy: Check the PK Robot setup menu and make sure the ID exists, and is unique amongst the set of robots.

PICK-022.cause: The utilization percent for each robot does not add up to 100 percent. This prevents load balancing from working properly.
PICK-022.remedy: In the PK Robot menu of each robot, specify percent utilization so that they add up to 100.

PICK-023.cause: The Picktool QMGR task global variable does not exist. No dynmaic load balancing can be done.
PICK-023.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

PICK-024.cause: The Picktool QMGR task can not get all the relevant system variables.
PICK-024.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

PICK-025.cause: The Encoder has not been set up yet.

PICK-035.cause: An invalid Encoder setting of $TRK_ENC_NUM is set in the $LNSCH[] system variable.

PICK-036.cause: An invalid motion group was specified.
PICK-036.remedy: PickTool only supports up to 2 motion groups.

PICK-037.remedy: Follow the process of setting the master count for the robot.

PICK-038.cause: The digital input port is already ON.
PICK-038.remedy: Move the target upstream ahead of the DIN location.

PICK-039.remedy: Change the line tracking schedule number to a validate one.

PICK-041.cause: Positions are recorded too closed to each other.
PICK-041.remedy: Make sure the recorded positions are at least 50 mm apart from each other.

PICK-042.cause: The Line Tracking Schedule has not been properly set up.
PICK-042.remedy: Set up the line tracking schedule before setting up the track frame.

PICK-043.cause: The track frame has been updated before.

PICK-044.cause: Some required steps have been skipped.

PICK-045.remedy: Go to controller of the reference robot, select PickTool track frame menu. Set the Calibration Type to Set Reference. Follow the wizard's procedure.

PICK-046.remedy: The track frame should have been set up before it can be used for reference. Select another robot that has its track frame done before for reference. Then come back to this robot and add this robot to the line.

PICK-061.remedy: One LBG can only have one ethernet master encoder, the rest of stations have to be ethernet slave encoder.

PICK-100.cause: The specified file could not be opened to read or write data. The file might be missing or the file device might be full.
PICK-100.remedy: Make sure that the file exists on the file device and/or that there is room to write the files to the file device.

PICK-103.cause: PickTool was asked to perform a function with an invalid object Id. For example, read data for a LBG that does not exist. Or, an uninitialized id was passed to an internal routine.
PICK-103.remedy: Make sure that a valid object id in the range of the array size of the system variable is used.

PICK-425.cause: A notification that data recording for collecting profiler data with PickPRO - duty, cycle time power consumption or life estimation has started.

PICK-426.cause: A notification that data recording for collecting profiler data with PickPRO - duty, cycle time power consumption or life estimation has ended.

PICK-428.cause: An attempt to collect profiler data (duty, cycle time, etc.) with PickPRO was made but the Data Acquisition option which was required was not installed.
PICK-428.remedy: If you wish to collect profiler data with PickPRO, you need to install the Data

PLUG-001.cause: An error is posted by the Plugin software
PLUG-001.remedy: Please refer to the information of the Plugin software.

PMON-001.cause: The PC Monitor task could not be notified.
PMON-001.remedy: Refer to the associated error code. OS -012 System error This error may be seen when attempting to monitor a variable or I/O point using the.StartMonitor method. It occurs when you have performed a restore from a controller that did not have the PCIF option installed. To fix this error, set system variable $SCR.$LPCOND_TIME to 40 and cycle power. This variable is set to zero on controllers that do not have the PCIF option installed. When set to zero, the task that performs monitoring is not started on powerup.

PMON-002.cause: Not enough memory to create client connection

PMON-003.cause: Failure to connect to PMON Server
PMON-003.remedy: Check physical connections and check to see if PMON server is running on the PC

PMON-004.cause: The PC Monitor task had an initialization failure..
PMON-004.remedy: Refer to the associated error code.

PMON-005.cause: The PC Monitor task had an internal timer failure.
PMON-005.remedy: Refer to the associated error code.

PMON-006.cause: The PC Monitor task had an internal task status read failure. The accompanying cause code identifies the failure.

PMON-007.cause: The PC Monitor Server lost a connection with the named client.
PMON-007.remedy: This is a warning and may be normal.

PMON-008.cause: The PC Monitor task had an internal CURPOS read failure.
PMON-008.remedy: Refer to the associated error code.

PMON-009.cause: The PC Monitor task had an internal monitoring failure. The requested monitor number was not found in the list of monitors.
PMON-009.remedy: Somehow, PMON is out of sync with the PC. In some cases, this may be normal if the PC is attempting to clean up after an internal error.

PNT1-001.cause: PaintTool has detected an unknown error.
PNT1-001.remedy: Refer to the teach pendant error log for the cause of the error.

PNT1-002.cause: The system is in an error condition.
PNT1-002.remedy: Press RESET to clear the error.

PNT1-003.remedy: Correct the error, if any, and try the reset operation again.

PNT1-004.cause: The robot servo disconnect is on.
PNT1-004.remedy: Turn off the robot servo disconnect.

PNT1-005.cause: The production mode input is off.

PNT1-006.cause: The remote switch is in the LOCAL position.
PNT1-006.remedy: Place the remote switch in the REMOTE position.

PNT1-007.cause: The machine lock is on going into production.
PNT1-007.remedy: Disable the machine lock on the teach pendant before entering production.

PNT1-008.cause: The UOP enable input is OFF.
PNT1-008.remedy: The UOP enable input must be ON.

PNT1-009.remedy: Press MENU->SETUP->Wait/Release to define robot and opener controller # and group # properly!.

PNT1-010.remedy: No action is required, robot will coast to a stop.

PNT1-011.cause: One or more of the Zero Down Time (ZDT) tests has issued an alert.
PNT1-011.remedy: Please click the ZDT help button (on the Paintworks ZDT alert screen) to display information about each ZDT test.

PNT1-014.cause: An invalid job number was received from the PLC. Therefore, the robot cannot put the job into the job queue.
PNT1-014.remedy: At the PLC, initialize the robot with a valid job number in order to receive a job read acknowledge from the robot.

PNT1-015.cause: An invalid color number was received from the PLC. The robot cannot put the color into the color queue.
PNT1-015.remedy: The PLC must initialize the robot with a valid job number in order to receive a color read acknowledge from the robot.

PNT1-016.remedy: Remove unneeded job(s) from the job queue before attempting to add more jobs to the queue.

PNT1-017.remedy: Remove color(s) from the color queue before attempting to add more colors to the queue.

PNT1-018.cause: Another task has detected that the main task has aborted or paused.
PNT1-018.remedy: Turn off the controller, then turn it on again.

PNT1-019.cause: Autoprocessing of the last editted program is still in process.
PNT1-019.remedy: Wait for autoprocessing to complete before entering production mode.

PNT1-020.cause: An invalid job type was received from the PLC.
PNT1-020.remedy: The PLC must initialize the robot with a valid job prefix.

PNT1-021.cause: There is an alarm that must be cleared before Test Cycle can be run.
PNT1-021.remedy: Press RESET to clear all system alarms.

PNT1-022.cause: The job is not run and the encoder counts indicate that the part is past the Start switch (plus tolerance). The robot deletes the job from the queue, posts this warning message and continues to operate in production.

PNT1-023.cause: The job is not run and the encoder counts indicate that the part has not made it to the Start switch (minus tolerance). The robot will hold onto that job for the next start signal, post this warning message, and will continue to operate in production.

PNT1-024.cause: The User Operator Panel (UOP) inputs are assigned, but have been disabled!
PNT1-024.remedy: If your system requires these UOP signals, you must enable these inputs on the Teach Pendant as follows: 1. Press MENUS. 2. Select SYSTEM. 3. Press F1 [TYPE]. 4. Select Config. 5. Move the cursor to Enable UI signals, and change them from FALSE to TRUE. If your system does not require these UOP signals, unassign these UOP signals in the I/O menu.

PNT1-025.cause: Indicates the ghost job override being used on the current ghost job being executed
PNT1-025.remedy: Please change the Ghost Job override to a value between 1 and 100.

PNT1-026.cause: The Paint Calibration option is loaded and enabled, but the Process TP program currently being edited does not have a TRKUFRAME instruction.
PNT1-026.remedy: Please insert the TRKUFRAME instruction using the appropriate PR # for this style.

PNT1-034.cause: An attempt was made to set an applicator parameter output beyond its min/max value.
PNT1-034.remedy: Verify the specified parameter's min/max output setting.

PNT1-039.cause: SETUP Applicators: The I/O information is correct and complete.

PNT1-040.cause: SETUP Applicators: The I/O information for an applicator was changed and is in error.
PNT1-040.remedy: Check that the output type, output number, rack and slot number, first bit location, and number of bits are all specified correctly.

PNT1-045.cause: The application is attempting to adjust the size of the color tables based on the configuration variable setting.

PNT1-046.message: Adj. color valves table size to %s
PNT1-046.cause: The application is attempting to adjust the size of the color valve table based on the configuration variable setting.

PNT1-047.message: Failed to adj. color table size
PNT1-047.cause: There is not enough memory available for the application to adjust the size of the color tables to the match requested setting.
PNT1-047.remedy: Use a smaller setting that is within the memory constraints of the controller.

PNT1-048.message: Failed to adj. color valve table size
PNT1-048.cause: There is not enough memory available for the application to adjust the size of the color valves table to match the requested setting.
PNT1-048.remedy: Use a smaller setting that is within the memory constraints of the controller.

PNT1-053.cause: An invalid parameter indicator value was sent from the PLC.
PNT1-053.remedy: Verfiy that the number of applicator control parameters set up in the robot matches the value sent from the PLC. This value should be between the range of 1 to 4.

PNT1-054.cause: The PLC sent a parameter indicator value of 0.
PNT1-054.remedy: Correct the parameter indicator value at the PLC.

PNT1-055.cause: On manual mode entry, all PLC manual mode input functions are enabled.

PNT1-056.cause: On manual mode exit, all PLC manual mode input functions are disabled.

PNT1-057.cause: Manual mode is being initiated during robot motion.
PNT1-057.remedy: Robot motion must complete before it enters manual mode.

PNT1-058.cause: Manual mode is being initiated during a color change cycle.
PNT1-058.remedy: The color change cyle must complete before the robot enters manual mode.

PNT1-059.cause: The teach pendant cannot be enabled when running a remote color change cycle.

PNT1-065.cause: For continuous line systems, a line tracking parameter is undefined and is required to run the system.
PNT1-065.remedy: Ensure that all tracking parameters have been set up on the SETUP Tracking menu.

PNT1-066.cause: For continuous line systems, a rail tracking parameter is undefined and is required to run the system.
PNT1-066.remedy: Ensure that all tracking parameters have been set up on the SETUP Tracking menu.

PNT1-067.cause: An attempt was made to use an invalid tracking frame number.
PNT1-067.remedy: The current software supports tracking frames 1-6. The tracking frame number must be greater than 0, and less than 7.

PNT1-068.cause: For continuous line systems, this warning indicates that the encoder counter has detected a rollover condition.

PNT1-070.cause: For continuous line systems, the robot has determined the conveyor is running in the wrong direction. Part detects will be ignored by the robot.
PNT1-070.remedy: Swap the leads on the encoder repeater board so that the encoder counts positive pulses instead of negative.

PNT1-072.cause: The robot is detecting a problem with the tracking encoder cable.
PNT1-072.remedy: Check the encoder cable, and replace it if necessary.

PNT1-073.message: Right-Hand Rule only for this robot
PNT1-073.cause: The robot being used is not supported in PaintTool line tracking for a left hand arm type. The robot is not a P-Series robot.
PNT1-073.remedy: If the robot library (setup) does not offer a selection for right or left hand robots, then no remedy is required. If the robot has been set up as a left hand robot, change it to a right hand robot.

PNT1-074.cause: The tracking encoder has been disconnected, or is faulty.
PNT1-074.remedy: Reconnect the tracking encoder or determine if the encoder connector is faulty. The robot controller power must be turned off, then turned on again before the system is allowed to reset.

PNT1-075.cause: The TCP (Line Tracking) or Extended Axis (Rail Tracking) has been commanded beyond the Entry Limit defined in the System parameter, $LNCFG.$ENTRY_XTRM.
PNT1-075.remedy: Adjust the Entry Limit ($LNCFG.$ENTRY_XTRM), or change the Tracking Boundary to be inside of this limit.

PNT1-076.cause: The TCP (Line Tracking) or Extended Axis (Rail Tracking) has been commanded beyond the Exit Limit defined in the System parameter, $LNCFG.$EXIT_XTRM.
PNT1-076.remedy: Adjust the Exit Limit ($LNCFG.$EXIT_XTRM) or change the Tracking Boundary to be inside of this limit.

PNT1-077.cause: Valid part travel distance could not be found or disabled from PLC.
PNT1-077.remedy: Review conslog.dg after power up for further information.

PNT1-080.cause: Ethernet Encoder Master power was cycled or encoder alarm.
PNT1-080.remedy: Refer to Ethernet Encoder Master alarm log.

PNT1-081.cause: Ethernet Encoder slave not communicating with master or error detected.
PNT1-081.remedy: Check communications status and encoder errors.

PNT1-085.cause: An unreachable position is detected in the adjustment precheck
PNT1-085.remedy: Check the alarm log to find out at which position motion error will occur, use CLR_Adj to clear the adj value

PNT1-086.cause: An interlock signal fault or PLC E-stop was detected.
PNT1-086.remedy: Correct the source of the fault, and RESET the controller.

PNT1-087.cause: The mechanical unit went beyond its normal travel limits and reached an overtravel limit switch.
PNT1-087.remedy: Follow the overtravel recovery procedure in Electrical Connection and Maintenance Manual.

PNT1-088.cause: The operator panel (SOP) EMERGENCY STOP has been detected.
PNT1-088.remedy: Release the SOP EMERGENCY STOP, and press RESET to clear the E-STOP condition.

PNT1-089.cause: The teach pendant EMERGENCY STOP has been detected.
PNT1-089.remedy: Turn the teach pendant EMERGENCY STOP button, and press RESET to clear the EMERGENCY STOP condition.

PNT1-090.cause: The teach pendant was enabled during production.
PNT1-090.remedy: The teach pendant cannot be enabled during production. Disable the teach pendant.

PNT1-091.remedy: Disable the teach pendant to continue the program.

PNT1-092.cause: Refer to SRVO-023 SERVO Stop error excess(G:x A:x) in the Error Code Manual.
PNT1-092.remedy: Refer to SRVO-023 SERVO Stop error excess(G:x A:x) in the Error Code Manual.

PNT1-093.cause: Refer to SRVO-024 SERVO Move error excess(G:x A:x) in the Error Code Manual.
PNT1-093.remedy: Refer to SRVO-024 SERVO Move error excess(G:x A:x) in the Error Code Manual.

PNT1-094.cause: The DEADMAN switch has been released during an operation. The operation has been discontinued.
PNT1-094.remedy: Press and hold the DEADMAN switch to restart the procedure.

PNT1-095.cause: The FENCE1 and FENCE2 circuits are open on the EMG control board.
PNT1-095.remedy: Determine the cause of the FENCE1 and FENCE2 open circuits, and correct the problem.

PNT1-096.cause: The IMSTP (immediate stop) UOP input was not asserted.
