PRIO-168.cause: The connection size of the device in the scanlist does not match the target device.
PRIO-168.remedy: Verify correct size and reload the scan-list using the config tool

PRIO-169.cause: The connection has not been scheduled
PRIO-169.remedy: Run a network configuration tool such as RSNetworx and configure the network.

PRIO-170.cause: The Product Type of the device in the scan-list and that of the actual device do not match.
PRIO-170.remedy: Use correct EDS file and reconfigure the scan-list of the CNET interface on the system.

PRIO-171.cause: The Major/Minor revison of the device in the scan-list and that of the actual device do not match.
PRIO-171.remedy: Use correct EDS file and reconfigure the scan-list of the CNET interface on the system.

PRIO-172.message: CNET Target App Out of Conn.
PRIO-172.cause: The target device does not have enough connections
PRIO-172.remedy: Close some connections to target device.

PRIO-173.cause: The connection has not been scheduled
PRIO-173.remedy: Run a network configuration tool such as RSNetworx and configure the network.

PRIO-174.cause: The connection to the remote device is lost.
PRIO-174.remedy: Check network connections. Check to see that the remote device is online. Check the status of the remote device.

PRIO-175.cause: The device is not in correct state to respond to this connection request.
PRIO-175.remedy: Run a network configuration tool such as RSNetworx and configure the network. Check if any other scanner has exisiting connection to the device.

PRIO-176.cause: Remote device refused the connection. This could be due to an invalid connection path.
PRIO-176.remedy: Verify that the correct EDS file is being used for the device. Check the target device configuration.

PRIO-177.cause: The Card has an invalid scan-list configuration.
PRIO-177.remedy: Check the configuration on the scanner config tool. Verify correct EDS files are used. Verify Input and Output sizes to devices.

PRIO-178.cause: A group of consecutive scans were lost; if n1=1, scans were lost on the main processor; if n1 = 2, scans were lost on the communications processor; if n1 = 3 or 4, scans were lost on FL-net register on the main processor; if n1 = 5 or 6, scans were lost on FL-net register on the communications processor; if n1 = 7 or 8, scans were lost on CC-Link IE Field Slv on main processor; if n1 = 9, scans were lost on CC-Link IE Field Slv on comm processor; n2 = number of lost scans; if n2 is less than 5, this may not be a serious problem; n3 = total scans since power-up. Generally indicates overloading of the indicated processor.
PRIO-178.remedy: Review software configuration to determine how loading can be reduced.

PRIO-179.cause: A group of scans were lost within a run of 100 scans. If n1=1, scans were lost on the main processor; if n1 = 2, scans were lost on the communications processor; n2 = number of lost scans; if n2 is less than 20, this may not be a serious problem; n3 = total scans since pwr up since power-up. Generally indicates overloading of the indicated processor.
PRIO-179.remedy: Review software configuration to determine how loading can be reduced.

PRIO-180.cause: An element could not be added to the system I/O scan When this error is posted, ControlNet I/O is not Operational. Possible causes are: * Invalid Configuration of scanner scan list * Too many I/O points for any given CNET device * Too many I/O points in the whole system
PRIO-180.remedy: Verify all I/O is valid. Check all CNET devices and ensure the sizes are resonable. Max I/O is limited by that allowed for the system.

PRIO-181.cause: Target device did not respond to the connection request.
PRIO-181.remedy: Verify that the target device is online and the status is OK. Verify that correct EDS file was used for the Scan-list configuration in the scanner configuration tool.

PRIO-182.cause: Network change was aborted. Connections will be restored and I/O will be exchanged.

PRIO-183.cause: Unrecognized port type name supplied to tpptnptc
PRIO-183.remedy: Supply name from element tp_daio_tp_names_c in tpdaio*.utx

PRIO-184.cause: The target (adapter) connection is idle. A scanner has not connected yet. All the ports corresponding to this device will be offline.
PRIO-184.remedy: Check the remote scanner configuration. Check the sizes and other configuration parameters such as vendor ID, product code, product type, revision and connection path and verify they are correct. Verify that the scanner is online.

PRIO-185.cause: There is an error with the Scan-list configuration.

PRIO-186.cause: The input header size in case of scanner mode or the output header size in case of adapter is invalid.
PRIO-186.remedy: Enter a valid header size. The valid header is less that or equal to the total connection size. The total connection size is a sum of the I/O size and the header size.

PRIO-187.cause: The number of slots for the device in the scan is invalid.
PRIO-187.remedy: Verify the configuration in the scanner config tool and reload the configuration. Verify that the EDS files are valid.

PRIO-188.cause: There is no output defined for the Simulated Input Skip featue and a WAIT instruction containing a skipped input is being executed.
PRIO-188.remedy: Define the Simulated Input Skip output using the System Config menu.

PRIO-189.cause: The input used in this WAIT instruction is simulated and is designated as Skip When Simulated. This WAIT instruction will time out and program exection will proceed with the next line.
PRIO-189.remedy: This is only a warning to indicate that a Simulated Input Skip will occur.

PRIO-190.cause: PMCADR.HTM has format error. Check the line of this file.

PRIO-191.cause: There was a problem initializing the AB-RIO hardware. The PRIO-191 alarm code will include a cause code with the reason.
PRIO-191.remedy: - No Board: check that board is installed and dip switches are set properly. - Failed to load/start/clear FW (firmware): firmware file is missing or corrupt or possibly a problem with the hardware.

PRIO-192.cause: There was a problem initializing the AB-RIO hardware. The PRIO-191 alarm code will include a cause code with the reason.
PRIO-192.remedy: - No Board: check that board is installed and dip switches are set properly. - Failed to load/start/clear FW (firmware): firmware file is missing or corrupt or possibly a problem with the hardware.

PRIO-193.cause: There was a problem initializing the AB-RIO hardware. The PRIO-191 alarm code will include a cause code with the reason.
PRIO-193.remedy: - No Board: check that board is installed and dip switches are set properly. - Failed to load/start/clear FW (firmware): firmware file is missing or corrupt or possibly a problem with the hardware.

PRIO-194.cause: There was a problem initializing the AB-RIO hardware. The PRIO-191 alarm code will include a cause code with the reason.
PRIO-194.remedy: - No Board: check that board is installed and dip switches are set properly. - Failed to load/start/clear FW (firmware): firmware file is missing or corrupt or possibly a problem with the hardware.

PRIO-195.cause: There was a problem initializing the AB-RIO hardware. The PRIO-191 alarm code will include a cause code with the reason.
PRIO-195.remedy: - No Board: check that board is installed and dip switches are set properly. - Failed to load/start/clear FW (firmware): firmware file is missing or corrupt or possibly a problem with the hardware.

PRIO-196.cause: There was a problem with a rack configuration. The slot will indicate which rack configuration. The problem may be -rack number not between 0 and 31 -rack size or ending rack boundary larger than the 128 I/O (full rack) maximum (eg. start group at 4 and a size of more than half a rack).
PRIO-196.remedy: Correct rack configuration on AB-RIO user interface.

PRIO-197.cause: The I/O connection associated with this slot is not actively exchanging I/O. Note that alarm severity (STOP or WARN) is effected by the error severity setting on the AB-RIO configuration screen. The last state setting on this screen effects state of the inputs
PRIO-197.remedy: Check the wiring, baud rate, and PLC configuration.

PRIO-198.cause: The plc is in test mode, program mode, or the connection may be inhibited in the PLC. Note alarm severity (STOP or WARN) is effected by the error severity setting on the AB-RIO configuration screen. The last state setting on this screen effects state of the inputs
PRIO-198.remedy: Check that PLC is in run mode and that connection is not inhibited in PLC setup

PRIO-200.remedy: Write down the number in the message and contact the FANUC service representative.

PRIO-201.cause: The FIPIO PC104 board is not mounted on the PC104 motherboard or the PC104 motherboard is not mounted into the option slot on the backplane.
PRIO-201.remedy: Mount the FIPIO PC104 board on the PC104 motherboard and install the PC104 motherboard into the option slot on the backplane.

PRIO-202.remedy: It is necessary to replace the circuit board. Please contact service.

PRIO-203.cause: Other device occupies the node address.
PRIO-203.remedy: Remove the device using the same address or change address from the FIPIO setup screen and turn off and on the controller.

PRIO-204.remedy: Cycle power the controller. Please contact servive if the problem persists.

PRIO-205.remedy: Cycle power the controller. Please contact servive if the problem persists.

PRIO-206.cause: Physical node is reset by PLC.
PRIO-206.remedy: To resume communication, press reset button on teach pendant or operation panel.

PRIO-207.cause: Error message from FIPIO PC104 agent board.
PRIO-207.remedy: Check whether the robot controller and PLC is wired correctly and try cold start. If the error still occurs, please contact service. Please inform the digit value(n) displayed. This data is needed to track the problem.

PRIO-208.cause: Bad communication status of FIPIO PC104
PRIO-208.remedy: Check board address of FIPIO PC104 board. The value must be equal to $FIPIOVAR.$IO_ADDRESS that is displayed as decimal number, not hexadecimal. By default setting, address is 0x330 (=816 in decimal). If the values are not same, change $FIPIOVAR.$IO_ADDRESS or address of FIPIO PC104 board to the same value. Next, make sure FIPIO PC104 board and PC104 motherboard are installed correctly. If all of above are right and this alarm occurs continuously when the robot controller and PLC are connected well, please contact service. Please inform the digit value(n) displayed. This data is needed to track the problem.

PRIO-209.cause: 1. Operating mode is changed to IDLE or STOP by PLC. 2. Disconnection of the cable or the connector which wire the robot controller and PLC.
PRIO-209.remedy: 1. Set operation mode to RUN by PLC 2. Check whether the robot controller and PLC is wired correctly.

PRIO-212.cause: The robot controller and PLC is not wired when the robot controller is turned on. When the wire is disconnected after connection, PRIO-209 STOP FIPIO Connection Broken error occurs instead of this error.
PRIO-212.remedy: Check whether the robot controller and PLC is wired before the controller is turned on.

PRIO-213.cause: Logical connection between the robot controller and PLC is established.
PRIO-213.remedy: This is warning message for the operator. This message is displayed when $FIPIOVAR.$POST_WARN system variable is 1 (default:0).

PRIO-214.cause: Operation mode changes from IDLE or SECU to ACTIVE.
PRIO-214.remedy: This is warning message for the operator. This message is displayed when $FIPIOVAR.$POST_WARN system variable is 1 (default:0).

PRIO-220.cause: EGD Producer name/IP address is not initialized.
PRIO-220.remedy: On the EGD screen, type the robot IP address in the Producer Name/IP: field.

PRIO-221.cause: The amount of input consumed does not match the configured size.
PRIO-221.remedy: Check the EGD producer and make sure the configured producer size matches the configured consumer size.

PRIO-222.cause: The EGD Consumer task initilization failed. The consumer module is not loaded on the robot.
PRIO-222.remedy: The consumer module is not loaded on the robot. Re-load the EGD option.

PRIO-223.cause: The EGD Producer was unable to create a UDP network socket.
PRIO-223.remedy: This alarm generally implies that the Ethernet or TCP/IP interface is not set up correctly. For example, if no IP address is defined, then the Ethernet/IP cannot initialize. Verify network connectivity using the ping utility (on the robot and also on the local PC).

PRIO-224.cause: An EGD System Error has occurred.
PRIO-224.remedy: Turn off the controller, then turn it on again.

PRIO-225.cause: The EGD Consumer timed-out while waiting for an I/O message from an EGD Producer.
PRIO-225.remedy: Press RESET to clear the error. Check the EGD Producer device to verify that it is functioning properly. Check the EGD Consumer timeout value. Typically, the EGD timeout value should be three times the EGD Producer's interval. Refer to the Ethernet Global Data Setup and Operations Manual for more information.

PRIO-226.cause: The EGD Consumer was unable to create a UDP network socket.
PRIO-226.remedy: This alarm generally implies that the Ethernet or TCP/IP interface is not set up correctly. For example, if no IP address is defined, then the Ethernet/IP cannot initialize. Verify network connectivity using the ping utility (on the robot and also on the local PC).

PRIO-227.cause: The EGD Consumer was unable to bind to a UDP network socket.
PRIO-227.remedy: This alarm generally implies that the Ethernet or TCP/IP interface is not set up correctly. For example, if no IP address is defined, then the Ethernet/IP cannot initialize. Verify network connectivity using the ping utility (on the robot and also on the local PC).

PRIO-228.cause: EGD System Error. A general system failure has occurred.
PRIO-228.remedy: Turn off the controller, then turn it on again.

PRIO-230.cause: The robot EtherNet/IP Adapter Connection running on the robot is enabled and has an error. Refer to additional cause code text for further details.
PRIO-230.remedy: Alarm severity can be modified on the EtherNet/IP adapter configuration screen on a per connection basis, and last state behavior can be modified with $EIP_CFG.$KEEP_IO_ADP. Refer to the EtherNet/IP Setup and Operations Manual for more information.

PRIO-231.cause: The robot EtherNet/IP Adapter connection is enabled but no remote scanner has connected to it. Note that it is normal to see this message when the controller first is turned on since the remote scanner (eg. PLC) might not connect to the robot immediately after the robot has been turned on. The PLC will retry the connection again so normally the connection is made shortly after powerup.
PRIO-231.remedy: Configure the remote scanner (eg. PLC) to connect to the robot. Press RESET to clear alarm. An alarm will be reposted if the connection is still idle.

PRIO-232.cause: The robot EtherNet/IP Adapter was not able to initialize.
PRIO-232.remedy: This alarm generally implies that the Ethernet or TCP/IP interface is not set up correctly. For example, if no IP address is defined, then EtherNet/IP cannot initialize. Verify network connectivity using the ping utility (on the robot and also on the local PC). If the problem persists, document the events that led to the alarm, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

PRIO-233.message: EtherNet/IP Scn Not in Run Mode
PRIO-233.cause: A remote EtherNet/IP scanner is connected to the robot adapter in IDLE or program mode. No I/O data will be committed.
PRIO-233.remedy: Put the remote scanner in run mode, and retry the operation.

PRIO-268.cause: Fail to run Cell Finder Motn Cannot start the Cell Finder motion.
PRIO-268.remedy: Clear all the errors before executing Cell Finder.

PRIO-280.remedy: Write down the parenthesized number in the message and contact the FANUC service representative.

PRIO-281.cause: The FL-net board is not properly mounted on the control unit.
PRIO-281.remedy: If you want to use the FL-net function, insert the FL-net board properly.

PRIO-282.cause: The FL-net board does not function correctly.
PRIO-282.remedy: The FL-net board must be replaced. Write down the parenthesized number in the message and contact the FANUC service representative.

PRIO-283.cause: The IP address of my node is specified by the address that doesn't belong to the class C or host address (last number) is set to 0 or 255.
PRIO-283.remedy: Specify the IP address of my node by the address that belongs to the class C or set the host address to other than 0 and 255.

PRIO-284.cause: A time-out occurred in transmission from my node.
PRIO-284.remedy: Increase the value of the token monitoring time on the setting screen or decrease the amount of data to be transmitted from my node so that no time-out occurs in transmission from my node. Alternatively, a device may make a slow response to the network. Check whether my node is affected by such a device.

PRIO-285.cause: An error was detected in FL-net connection sequence.
PRIO-285.remedy: Check whether all settings are correct. If this error occurs though all settings are correct, save setting data in FLNET.SV and send the file to the FANUC service representative.

PRIO-286.cause: My node is in the frame reception wait state because there are no other nodes in the network or my node can recognize no other nodes.
PRIO-286.remedy: To start communication, make another node participate in the network. If my node does not recognize another node, check whether the robot and remote communication devices are connected to the network properly and are set correctly.

PRIO-287.cause: Some node has the same node number to my node.
PRIO-287.remedy: Change the node number of my node or the node which has the same node number. To change the node number of my node, change the least significant digit of the IP address on my node setting screen. After changing the node number, turn the power off, then on again.

PRIO-288.cause: My node was disconnected from the network. The cause may be disconnection of power or connection. My node may be disconnected from the network due to an error which has already occurred.
PRIO-288.remedy: Turn the power on and check whether my node can participate in the network and check whether the cables are connected properly. Also check whether another error message is issued. If another error message is issued, first remove the cause of the error.

PRIO-289.cause: My node participated in the network.
PRIO-289.remedy: This alarm message calls an operator's attention.

PRIO-290.cause: The setting of common memory of a node overlaps the common memory area setting of my node.
PRIO-290.remedy: Change the common memory area setting for my node or the node whose common memory area overlaps with that of my node to terminate the overlapping status.

PRIO-291.cause: The node with the node number displayed in the message was disconnected from the network.
PRIO-291.remedy: Check the node disconnected from the network by confirming the device settings and cable connection if the disconnected node isn't operated to disconnect. Also check whether another error message is issued. If another error message is issued, first remove the cause of the error. Please note that you can set WARN or STOP for each node as the severity of this error in the item for the error severity on the detailed participating node setting screen.

PRIO-292.cause: The node having the node number displayed in the message participated in the network.
PRIO-292.remedy: This alarm message calls an operator's attention.

PRIO-293.cause: The common memory area setting of a node overlaps that of the node with the node number displayed in the message.
PRIO-293.remedy: Change the setting of common memory area to terminate the overlapping status.

PRIO-294.cause: Multiple FL-net boards are inserted into the control unit.

PRIO-295.cause: FL-net sending register is too large or too small to change to integer.
PRIO-295.remedy: Change the register to smaller (less than 2147483584) or larger (equal or larger than -2147483776) value or send the register with float.

PRIO-296.cause: Setting is to use internal port for FL-net.
PRIO-296.remedy: Please use internal port or set to use board.

PRIO-297.message: FL-net rcv reg is too large
PRIO-297.cause: The number of FL-net receiving register is too large.
PRIO-297.remedy: Set the number of FL-net receiving register equal or under 50.

PRIO-298.cause: When total variety is 2, variety 1 is internal port only, variety 2 is board only. So using port in variety 1 is changed to internal port 2 if set to use board.
PRIO-298.remedy: This alarm message calls an operator's attention.

PRIO-320.remedy: Contact FANUC service representative The ID number in the brackets is required to track the problems.

PRIO-321.cause: No CC-Link Remote Device Station PCB is installed.
PRIO-321.remedy: Install CC-Link Remote Device Station PCB.

PRIO-322.cause: A station number out of the range (1 to 64) was used.
PRIO-322.remedy: Change Station No. or Number of Stations on CC-Link SETUP screen.

PRIO-323.remedy: Confirm the connection of CC-Link cable and terminal registers, and countermeasures to noise. Set Baud rate to match the Master station's baud rate.

PRIO-324.cause: This Remote Device station left the data link. The CC-Link cable were disconnected or the Master station was turned off.
PRIO-324.remedy: Confirm the connection of CC-Link cable and the status of the Master station. Please note that if you turn on the robot Remote Device station while the CC-Link cable is disconnected or the Master station is off, this alarm will NOT be posted.

PRIO-325.remedy: Confirm the status of the sequencer. Please note that this alarm is detected correctly only while the robot Remote Device station is exchanging data with the Master station.

PRIO-326.remedy: Confirm the status of the sequencer. Please note that this alarm is detected correctly only while the robot Remote Device station is exchanging data with the Master station.

PRIO-327.remedy: Change Number of Registers or Reg start index on CC-Link SETUP screen.

PRIO-328.cause: Too many AOs or Registers were assigned to RWr.
PRIO-328.remedy: Change Number of AOs and Number of Registers on CC-Link SETUP screen.

PRIO-329.cause: Too many AIs and Registers were assigned to RWw.
PRIO-329.remedy: Change Number of AIs and Number of Registers on CC-Link SETUP screen.

PRIO-330.cause: The number of points of RX/RY to be assigned to UOP is not enough.
PRIO-330.remedy: Change Number of Stations on CC-Link SETUP screen.

PRIO-331.cause: A outlying numerical value is set to a remote register.
PRIO-331.remedy: CC-Link function of robot supports only unsigned or signed 16bits word data. Do not enter another type of value to remote register. In R-30iB, you can send float value, which is larger than -32769 and smaller than 65536, if $CCLINKRD[board No.].$AUTO_REGCHG is set to not 0. The value is sent with integer by cutting off the floating part. In R-30iB, severity of this alarm can be changed to warning if $CCLINKRD[board No.].$REG_ER_WARN is set to not 0.

PRIO-332.remedy: Confirm the connection of CC-Link cable and terminal registers, and countermeasures to noise. Set Baud rate to match the Master station's baud rate.

PRIO-334.cause: A. Three or more CC-Link daughter boards are installed. B. Three or more CC-Link Remote Device Station PCB(B) are installed.
PRIO-334.remedy: Robot controller supports only two CC-Link communication boards. Please turn off the controller and remove excess board.

PRIO-335.cause: Two types of CC-Link Remote Device Station PCB are installed.
PRIO-335.remedy: The type of CC-Link Remote Device Station PCB must be the same. Please turn off the controller and remove all CC-Link board of another type.

PRIO-350.cause: The EtherNet/IP Scanner Connection running on the robot is enabled and has an error. Refer to additional cause code text for further details.
PRIO-350.remedy: Alarm severity can be modified using the EtherNet/IP advanced scanner configuration screen on a per connection basis, and last state behavior can be modified with $EIP_CFG.$KEEP_IO_SCN. Refer to the EtherNet/IP Setup and Operations Manual for more information. (Paint) %d is mapped to the following devices: 1-PLC 2-EQ1: SMC in arm process hardware 3-EQ2: SMC in arm process hardware 5-EQ1: Electrostatic process hardware 6-EQ2: Electrostatic process hardware EQ1 is typically on the left side of the booth and EQ2 on the right except for single arm, then EQ1 may be on the right. A communication error will occur if there is a problem with: 1. Power to the device 2. Communication to the device 3. A problem with the device itself. If the communication error occurs, reboot the robot controller. The power to the process hardware is also interlocked to reboot the devices. If the problem returns, inspect/replace the power and communication cables. "If the problem persists, replace the network process hardware itself. Additional considerations include Ethernet switches in the robot controller and power to those switches.

PRIO-351.cause: The robot EtherNet/IP scanner was not able to open a TCP or UDP network socket.
PRIO-351.remedy: This alarm generally implies that the Ethernet or TCP/IP interface is not set up correctly. For example, if no IP address is defined, then the EtherNet/IP cannot initialize. Verify network connectivity using the ping utility (on the robot and also on the local PC). If the problem persists, document the events that led to the alarm, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

PRIO-352.cause: The robot EtherNet/IP scanner was not able to bind a TCP or a UDP network socket.
PRIO-352.remedy: This alarm generally implies that the Ethernet or TCP/IP interface is not set up correctly. For example, if no IP address is defined, then the EtherNet/IP cannot initialize. Verify network connectivity using the ping utility (on the robot, and also on the local PC). If the problem persists, document the events that led to the alarm, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

PRIO-353.cause: The robot EtherNet/IP scanner was not able to send information on a TCP or UDP network socket.
PRIO-353.remedy: This alarm generally implies that the Ethernet or TCP/IP interface is not set up correctly. For example, if no IP address is defined, then the EtherNet/IP cannot initialize. Verify network connectivity using the ping utility (on the robot and also on the local PC). If the problem persists, document the events that led to the alarm, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

PRIO-354.cause: The robot EtherNet/IP scanner could not resolve the configured remote adapter hostname.
PRIO-354.remedy: Verify the Name/IP Address entered in the Scanner Configuration Screen is valid. Try to ping the address from the main EtherNet/IP screen. If using DNS, verify that DNS is properly configured. If using the robot Host Name tables (LOCAL and/or SHARED), verify the tables are properly configured. Press RESET to restart the robot scanner connection.

PRIO-355.cause: The robot EtherNet/IP scanner was not able to connect to the adapter device on a TCP network socket.
PRIO-355.remedy: Verify the robot controller and the remote adapter device are both connected to the same network. Check the remote adapter device and verify it is running properly. Ping the remote adapter device from the robot. Verify that EtherNet/IP is enabled on the adapter device. Press RESET to restart the robot scanner connection. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the alarm, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

PRIO-356.cause: The robot EtherNet/IP Scanner did not receive a List Services Reply message from the remote adapter.
PRIO-356.remedy: Verify the robot controller and the remote adapter device are both connected to the same network. Check the remote adapter device and verify it is running properly and verify that EtherNet/IP is enabled on the adapter. Ping the remote adapter device from the robot. Press RESET to restart the robot scanner connection.

PRIO-357.cause: The robot EtherNet/IP scanner did not receive a Register Session Reply message from the remote adapter.
PRIO-357.remedy: Check the remote adapter device and verify that EtherNet/IP is enabled. Press RESET to restart the robot scanner connection.

PRIO-358.cause: The robot EtherNet/IP scanner either did not receive a ForwardOpen Reply message from the remote adapter, or the robot scanner received a ForwardOpen Reply message from the remote adapter indicating a failure to establish an I/O connection.
PRIO-358.remedy: Verify the scanner settings in the robot's Scanner Configuration screen are correct–review the manual of the remote adapter device for the correct settings. Verify that the remote adapter does not currently have a duplicate explicit owner connection (another scanner device already connected to the same assembly instances). Check the remote adapter device and verify that EtherNet/IP is enabled, and that the device is accessible on the network. Take note of the hexadecimal code in the robot alarm text and lookup the error in the robot scanner manual. Press RESET to restart the robot scanner connection. Refer to the EtherNet/IP Setup and Operations Manual for more information.

PRIO-359.cause: The robot EtherNet/IP Scanner timed-out while waiting for an I/O update message from the remote adapter.
PRIO-359.remedy: Press RESET to restart the scanner connection. Check the remote adapter to verify it is functioning properly.

PRIO-360.message: EtherNet/IP Adp Not in Run Mode
PRIO-360.cause: The EtherNet/IP adapter to which the robot scanner is connected is in IDLE mode. No input data will be committed.
PRIO-360.remedy: Put the adapter in RUN mode.

PRIO-369.cause: An unexpected system level error has occurred.
PRIO-369.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

PRIO-370.cause: The specified board was not found in the system.
PRIO-370.remedy: Make sure the daughter board is properly configured and properly seated on the motherboard. Please be sure to check dip switch settings.

PRIO-371.remedy: Please check System LED on PMIO card. See Appendix A in PMIO Manual. Please restore pmcfg.zip and cycle power.

PRIO-372.remedy: Please check Channel LED on PMIO card. See Appendix A in PMIO Manual. Please restore pmcfg.zip and cycle power.

PRIO-373.remedy: Please restore pmcfg.zip and cycle power.

PRIO-374.remedy: Please restore pmcfg.zip and cycle power.

PRIO-375.remedy: This is expected when configuration is modified.

PRIO-376.remedy: Please check LEDs on PMIO card. See Appendix A in PMIO Manual. Please restore pmcfg.zip and cycle power. If problem persists please contact Fanuc.

PRIO-377.remedy: Please check LEDs on PMIO card. See Appendix A in PMIO Manual. Please restore pmcfg.zip and cycle power. If problem persists please contact Fanuc.

PRIO-378.remedy: Please check the diagnostic message screen for the connection for further details.

PRIO-379.cause: The IO-Device connection is not active
PRIO-379.remedy: Please check the diagnostic message screen for the connection for further details. Please check IO-Controller associated with this conenction for further details.

PRIO-380.remedy: Please check additional alarms and cause codes. Consult FANUC representative.

PRIO-381.remedy: Please check additional alarms and cause codes. Consult FANUC representative.

PRIO-382.remedy: Please check additional alarms and cause codes. Consult FANUC representative.

PRIO-396.remedy: Please check additional alarms and cause codes. Consult FANUC representative.

PRIO-397.remedy: Please follow appendix in PMIO Manual to update firmware.

PRIO-398.message: PMIO FW Upd, DO NOT POWER OFF
PRIO-398.remedy: This message is expected while updating firmware.

PRIO-399.remedy: This message is expected while updating firmware.

PRIO-490.cause: The Modbus TCP Server running on the robot is enabled and has an error. Refer to additional cause code text for further details.
PRIO-490.remedy: Alarm severity and last state behavior can be modified using the Modbus TCP Slave configuration screen. Refer to the Modbus Setup and Operations Manual for more information.

PRIO-493.cause: The Modbus TCP Server was not able to open and use a TCP network socket.
PRIO-493.remedy: This alarm generally implies that the Ethernet or TCP/IP interface is not set up correctly. For example, if no IP address is defined, then the TCP/IP stack cannot initialize. Verify network connectivity using the ping utility (on the robot, and also on the local PC).

PRIO-494.cause: A Modbus TCP master device is trying to establish a connection with the robot Modbus slave, but the server is already using all available connections. This is a warning alarm and will only be posted the first time this happens after each power-cycle. Per the Modbus TCP protocol, when a new connection request arrives and there are no unused connections, the oldest connection will be closed, and the new connection request will be accepted.
PRIO-494.remedy: Increase the number of connections using the Modbus TCP screen

PRIO-495.cause: The Modbus TCP server timed-out while waiting for an I/O message from a Modbus TCP client.
PRIO-495.remedy: Check the Modbus TCP client to verify it is functioning properly. Adjust the robot Modbus TCP timeout if necessary

PRIO-499.cause: Modbus TCP System Error. A general system failure has occurred.
PRIO-499.remedy: Turn off the controller, then turn it on again.

PRIO-520.cause: Setting of Override is invalid. Override can be set for only tree nummber of PMC.
PRIO-520.remedy: Reduce number of PMCs setting Ovreride.

PRIO-521.cause: Setting of Sequence number is invalid.

PRIO-522.cause: Setting of Memory Type is invalid.

PRIO-523.cause: Setting of Memory Type is invalid

PRIO-524.cause: Setting of Execution Rates is invalid.

PRIO-525.cause: PARAM*.PMC was not loaded. PMC adress values are not replaced.
PRIO-525.remedy: Please confirm setting of max PMC-path number.

PRIO-527.message: PMC:E relay data was not restored
PRIO-527.cause: E relay data was not restored

PRIO-528.cause: Step Sequence program cannnot be used. It can be used only PMC1.
PRIO-528.remedy: Please load this PMC program as PMC1.

PRIO-529.cause: PMC interface adress(M,N) setting is invalid
PRIO-529.remedy: Please change setting of PMC interface on PMC Setting screen.

PRIO-530.cause: Multi-Path PMC Option(J763) is not orderd. To use some function, J763 is needed.

PRIO-531.cause: Some function statements can not be used.
PRIO-531.remedy: Please delete invvalid functions from PMC progarms.

PRIO-532.message: PMC%d:Int.I/O[%d] setting is overlaped with other IO assignment
PRIO-532.cause: IO index setting is overlaped with other device. IO index of Int.I/O can not be used the same index.

PRIO-533.cause: IO index setting of Int.I/O is invalid.

PRIO-534.cause: PMC address setting of Int.I/O is invalid. PMC address must be set as 2 byte alignment.

PRIO-535.cause: PMC address setting of Int.I/O is invalid.

PRIO-536.cause: Number of System Int.I/O is limit.

PRIO-537.cause: Error of Int.I/O Copy Mode. Register is not integer.
PRIO-537.remedy: Please change setting or change register value.

PRIO-538.remedy: Please cycle power to change PMC setting

PRIO-539.cause: Temporary Memory to use PMC is lack.
PRIO-539.remedy: Please change PMC memory area size or use large memory.

PRIO-540.message: PMC%d:PMC programs are deleted at cycle power
PRIO-540.cause: Setting of max path PMC number is changed. PMC program will be deleted at next cycle time.
PRIO-540.remedy: Please set back mac path PMC number not to deleate PMC programs.

PRIO-541.cause: PMC program was deleted, because setting of max path PMC number is changed.

PRIO-542.message: PMC No ext. I/O rack:%d slot:%d
PRIO-542.cause: The device that set to External I/O of PMC is not found.
PRIO-542.remedy: Please check setting of PMC External I/O. Check the connections of I/O modules.

PRIO-543.message: PMC:Can not use Ext. I/O assignment
PRIO-543.cause: Internal I/O assignment X and Y address and External I/O assignment can not be used together
PRIO-543.remedy: Please delete setting of PMC External I/O. Or please delete Internal I/O setting of X and Y address.

PRIO-544.message: PMC:Can not use memory common mode
PRIO-544.cause: Internal I/O assignment X and Y address and setting of memory common mode can not be used together
PRIO-544.remedy: Please change setting of memory type. Or please delete Internal I/O setting of X and Y address.

PRIO-545.cause: PMC address assigned to Internal I/O cannot set as Override.
PRIO-545.remedy: Please use simulate value of I/O screen.

PRIO-546.cause: DCS PMC program has invalid address or function code.

PRIO-547.cause: Safety PMC execution state can not be changed.

PRIO-600.cause: PCI motherboard with CP1616 is not installed.
PRIO-600.remedy: Check PCI motherboard or CP1616 are inserted firmly.

PRIO-601.cause: PROFINET software on the robot controller is not working.
PRIO-601.remedy: Cycle power the robot controller. Consult FANUC representative if this error occurs repeatedly.

PRIO-602.remedy: Consult FANUC representative. Report the value in the error message to track the problem.

PRIO-603.remedy: Consult FANUC representative. Report the error message.

PRIO-604.remedy: Consult FANUC representative. There is another error message that shows the cause of this alarm. Open alarm history screen and select the alarm and press DETAIL to see all message displayed in two lines. Report all massage to track the problem.

PRIO-605.cause: Failed to start PROFINET I/O Device function.
PRIO-605.remedy: The value in the error message is error code from CP1616. The value might be one of the followings. 0x030D: Config in update Turn off the controller 0x030E: No communication to CP1616 Turn off the controller If value is not in the list or the error is not resolved by the remedy, consult FANUC representative. Report the value in the error message.

PRIO-606.cause: PROFINET I/O communication is aborted by I/O Controller.

PRIO-607.cause: PROFINET I/O communication is stopped by I/O Controller.

PRIO-608.cause: Reported module with slot number and subslot number does not match the configuration of project file downloaded to I/O Controller.
PRIO-608.remedy: Check the setting in setup module detail screen. Check the project file.

PRIO-609.cause: Remote stop of PROFINET CP1616 interface by remote configuration tool.
PRIO-609.remedy: Please press reset the controller after remote restart.

PRIO-610.cause: Failed to start PROFINET I/O Device function.
PRIO-610.remedy: The value in the error message is error code from CP1616. The value might be one of the followings. 0x030D: Config in update Turn off the controller 0x030E: No communication to CP1616 Turn off the controller If value is not in the list or the error is not resolved by the remedy, consult FANUC representative. Report the value in the error message.

PRIO-612.cause: Operating mode is changed to offline.

PRIO-613.cause: Operating mode is changed to clear.

PRIO-614.cause: Watchdog of CP1616 could not be started.
PRIO-614.remedy: Consult FANUC representative. Report the error message.

PRIO-615.cause: Specified station number is not found when switching TP instruction is executed.

PRIO-616.remedy: Check if the target station is connected well.

PRIO-617.cause: I/O Device function failed because the specified module is wrong.
PRIO-617.remedy: Check the module specified two numbers, the former is slot number, the latter is subslot number.

PRIO-618.cause: I/O Device function failed because the specified submodule is wrong.
PRIO-618.remedy: Check the module specified two numbers, the former is slot number, the latter is subslot number.

PRIO-619.cause: The stored configuration of the module that is specified by station number, slot number and subslot number does not match to the current configuration when the start mode is OPERATION.
PRIO-619.remedy: Check the parameters of the module that is specified by station number, slot number and subslot number.

PRIO-620.cause: The device whose Show error when deactivated setting is ON is deactivated.
PRIO-620.remedy: Check the station specified the station number, and activate it.

PRIO-621.cause: The start up of I/O Device has not completed or terminated by error.
PRIO-621.remedy: Disable I/O Device if I/O Device function is not used in setup general screen. If I/O Device function is used, check if any error related to I/O Device is present. Check if I/O Controller to communicate with the robot controller is running. This error can be released when the setting of I/O Device is correct and communication to the I/O Controller establishes.

PRIO-622.cause: The start up of I/O Controller has not completed or terminated by error.
PRIO-622.remedy: Disable I/O Controller if I/O Controller function is not used. If I/O Controller function is used, check if any error related to I/O Controller is present. This error can be released when the setting of I/O Controller is correct and communication to the I/O Devices establish.

PRIO-623.cause: The start up of I/O Controller has completed but the start up mode is not OPERATION.
PRIO-623.remedy: Change the start mode to OPERATION, and turn off/on the controller.

PRIO-624.cause: The stored configuration is different from the current configuration in the number of modules when the start mode is OPERATION.
PRIO-624.remedy: Check if the project downloaded to CP1616 matches the current configuration, and if the configuration was read in by the robot controller in READ IN mode.

PRIO-625.cause: PROFINET network configuration has been read in successfully when start mode is READ IN.
PRIO-625.remedy: This is just a notification of completion of read in. Check PROFINET I/O Controller communication and I/O data exchange before changing start mode to OPERATION.

PRIO-626.cause: PROFINET setting of the robot controller was changed and it is required to turn off/on the power to enable the change.
PRIO-626.remedy: Please turn off/on the power of the robot controller.

PRIO-627.cause: Start mode is changed to operation mode.

PRIO-628.cause: Group status could not be recovered.

PRIO-629.cause: Group status could not be recovered.

PRIO-630.message: PNIO(C) mod data out of area
PRIO-630.cause: Data of a module is out of the areas that are mapped to robot I/O. The address of the data is displayed by the following error message.
PRIO-630.remedy: Check the setting of area in I/O Controller Setup screen. Modify the address of data by configuration tool in PC.

PRIO-631.cause: Error related to input data of a module.
PRIO-631.remedy: This is an additional information of a previous error message.

PRIO-632.cause: Error related to output data of a module.
PRIO-632.remedy: This is an additional information of a previous error message.

PRIO-633.cause: Firmware update of PROFINET board has started.
PRIO-633.remedy: Wait until firmware update completed. Don't turn off the controller.

PRIO-635.remedy: Firmware update failed. If the firmware is lost, set $PNIO_DL.$NO_FIRM_ST = 1, and try updating firmware by vaild firmware file at controlled start mode.

PRIO-637.cause: The specified file can't be opened.
PRIO-637.remedy: Make sure the file name with device name is correct.

PRIO-638.cause: There is not enough memory in COMM processor for this operation.

PRIO-639.cause: Configuration of unsupported feature is found.
PRIO-639.remedy: Please show the cause code to know what is not supported. Change the configuration by remote configuration tool.

PRIO-640.cause: I/O producer status of the specified module of PROFINET I/O has turned to BAD.

PRIO-641.cause: I/O producer status of the specified module of PROFINET I/O has turned to GOOD.
PRIO-641.remedy: This is only a notification of recovery.

PRIO-642.cause: Alarm indication of PROFINET I/O has come.
PRIO-642.remedy: Check the alarm data of the specified module

PRIO-643.cause: The device specified by the alarm message is activated.

PRIO-644.cause: The length of a PROFINET message from I/F board exceeds the limit.
PRIO-644.remedy: Check if the limit parameter is adequate. Locate the event that causes this alarm.

PRIO-645.cause: The number of unread alarm indication gets too large. Probably there is no KAREL program that reads it out. Alarm indication should be read out because it uses memory while it is kept.
PRIO-645.remedy: Set $READ=2 of PNIO_ALM.VR to read out alarm indication.

PRIO-646.cause: I/O consumer status of the specified module of PROFINET I/O has turned to BAD.

PRIO-647.cause: I/O cosumer status of the specified module of PROFINET I/O has turned to GOOD.
PRIO-647.remedy: This is only a notification of recovery.

PRIO-648.cause: Too many devices exist in PROFINET project.
PRIO-648.remedy: Decrease the number of stations, I/O modules and interface modules.

PRIO-649.cause: Firmware version is too old to perform the operation.
PRIO-649.remedy: Update the firmware of PROFINET board to the the displayed version, or later.

PRIO-650.cause: Too many I/O comments were set.

PRIO-652.cause: The device with the specified station number is deactivated.

PRIO-653.cause: Alarm storm is detected. A device has been faulty and keeps on sending many alarms and diagnostics.
PRIO-653.remedy: Find out and fix the faulty device. Then release alarm storm status by TP screen or by system variable.

PRIO-655.cause: Backup of XDB file from PROFINET board has started.
PRIO-655.remedy: Wait until backup finishes. Don't turn off the controller during backup.

PRIO-656.cause: Backup of XDB file from PROFINET board has completed successfully.

PRIO-657.cause: Backup of XDB file from PROFINET board failed.

PRIO-658.cause: Backup of firmware from PROFINET board has started.
PRIO-658.remedy: Wait until backup finishes. Don't turn off the controller during backup.

PRIO-659.cause: Backup of firmware from PROFINET board completed successfully.

PRIO-660.cause: Backup of firmware from PROFINET board failed.

PRIO-661.cause: XDB backup failed because of a segment of data was dropped.

PRIO-662.cause: PROFINET communication is suspended because backup operation is running.

PRIO-663.cause: There is not enough memory in COMM processor for backup operation.
PRIO-663.remedy: Put underbar character before device path, for example, _UD1: in order to perform backup in memory saving mode, however, it will take much longer time to finish than normal mode.

PRIO-664.cause: There is a bad setting in I/O Device module setting. For example, slot number = 0 can't be used with V2.6 firmware.
PRIO-664.remedy: Check the cause code for what is bad setting. In the example case, Open I/O Device module list/detail screen. Renumber the slot number of the modules from slot 1. Then cycle power the controller.

PRIO-665.cause: The version of the firmware currently installed on the PROFINET board is not equal to that of tested firmware.
PRIO-665.remedy: This is an information of firmware version mismatch. It doesn't necessarily mean any problem is present. It is up to operator how to react this. For example, the operator may download the tested version, or keep using the version. On the other hand, when there is a problem, this error message shows that firmware version mismatch might cause the problem.

PRIO-666.message: PNIO(D): Wrong GSD in partner cfg
PRIO-666.cause: Error is found in I/O Device configuration from partner, the I/O Controller that tries to connect the robot. For example, the module of slot number 0 is present, which is not permissible when V2.6 firmware is used. This kind of error is caused probably because wrong GSD file is used when the partner is configured.
PRIO-666.remedy: Check the manual to see which GSD file should be used according to the software version of the robot controller and the firmware version of the firmware on PROFINET board. Install the proper GSD file to the configuration tool if needed. Correct the configuration of the partner. For example, replace robot I/O device by that from proper GSD file, compile the project and download it to the partner.

PRIO-667.cause: XDB backup file in the specified device path doesn't match the configuration on PROFINET board.
PRIO-667.remedy: Check if configuration is on PROFINET board. If there is no configuration, downloading XDB might be required. If there is configuration, the XDB backup file in the specified device path migth be old. It is up to the operator to download XDB backup file to PROFINET board, or to update XDB backup file.

PRIO-668.cause: The operaton of comparing XDB backup file in the specified device path fails.
PRIO-668.remedy: This is a system error. The cause code is the error status.

PRIO-669.cause: There is no XDB backup file in the specified device path.
PRIO-669.remedy: Confirm the device path. Create the backup file if required.

PRIO-670.cause: There is no configuration on PROFINET board.
PRIO-670.remedy: Download configuration to PROFINET board if I/O Controller function is used.

PRIO-671.cause: It isn't possible to check if configuration is present on PROFINET board. Possible causes: config in update, no communication with firmware.

PRIO-672.cause: The setting displayed in the cause code has the value with special meaning.
PRIO-672.remedy: Please see the cause code for which setting is special. In some cases, setting is changed for specific purpose. It is up to operator to decide the setting is correct or not. If the value is correct, just ignore the alarm.

PRIO-673.cause: PROFINET Safety is installed but can't be enabled for some reason. For example, the firmware version of PROFINET board doesn't meet the requirement. The slot number for safety module doesn't match that defined in GSD file.
PRIO-673.remedy: Check the firmware version on PROFINET board by looking $PNIO_DIAG.$FW_VERSION. Refer to PROFINET I/O function operation manual for the required firmware version and the GSD file for it. Download the required firmware to PROFINET board, and confirm the GSD is used in configuration tool. Check the slot number of safety module.

PRIO-674.cause: The firmware on PROFINET board can't be used with the current setting of robot. This may be because of replacement of PROFINET board.
PRIO-674.remedy: Download the firmware of the displayed version to PROFINET board.

PRIO-675.cause: Backup file of PROFINET I/O function is loaded. Old identification information and configuration are found.

PRIO-676.cause: Identification number of PROFINET I/O Device is set to the specified number.
PRIO-676.remedy: This is an information. The I/O Controller that connects to the robot I/O Device may need to be configured again by the GSD file with the device identification number.

PRIO-677.cause: SignOff function is enabled, but there is no assignment for SignOff signal.
PRIO-677.remedy: Assign SignOff signal, or disable SignOff function.

PRIO-678.cause: I/O Device starts with PROFIEnergy enabled.

PRIO-679.cause: I/O Device starts with PROFIEnergy disabled.

PRIO-680.cause: User application has acknowledged Start_Pause with the displayed PE_Mode.

PRIO-684.cause: Defective module setting is found around the displayed number in the module list of I/O Device. The module list should be filled with complete module setting. No intermediate empty or incomplete setting is permitted.
PRIO-684.remedy: Check module list of I/O Device, and remove all intermediate empty or incomplete setting.

PRIO-685.cause: PROFIsafe is stopped due to F_iPar_CRC check.
PRIO-685.remedy: If F_iPar_CRC check is enabled, F_iPar_CRC must be presend in F-Parameter sent from Safety PLC, and it must be equal to that calculated by robot based on current DCS parameters, otherwise PROFIsafe is stopped. If F_iPar_CRC check is disabled, F_iPar_CRC must not be present in F-Parameter sent from Safety PLC, otherwise PROFIsafe is stopped. F_iPar_CRC check enable/disable should be used by default setting because robot GSDML file determines if F_iPar_CRC is present in F-Parameter sent from PLC.

PRIO-686.cause: The number of I-device submodule exceeds the limit.
PRIO-686.remedy: Decrease the transfer area of I-Device in configuration tool.

PRIO-687.message: PNIO(D) mod data out of area
PRIO-687.cause: The number of I/O for I-Device is not enough for mapping the data of the submodule.
PRIO-687.remedy: Increase the number of I/O for I-Device, or decrease the length of I-Device data.

PRIO-688.cause: More than 1 submodules have the subslot ID of safety submodule.
PRIO-688.remedy: Only 1 safety submodule is permissible at the beginning of I-Device transfer area. Change the subslot ID of the specified submodule other than 0x1001 - 0x1008.

PRIO-689.cause: The mode of PROFINET has changed to STOP mode (former SUSPEND mode).

PRIO-690.cause: PROFINET interface is closing. It might be because of configuration error.
PRIO-690.remedy: Check alarm history to see if any error in I/O controller or I-Device.

PRIO-691.cause: Stop of PROFINET interface is requested, for example by manual operation.

PRIO-692.cause: Restart of PROFINET interface is requested, for example by manual operation.

PRIO-693.cause: Reset of the firmware on the PROFINET board started.

PRIO-694.cause: Reset of the firmware on the PROFINET board finished.

PRIO-695.cause: Requested Operation requires PROFINET to be stopped.

PRIO-696.message: PNIO: Too many number of I/O
PRIO-696.cause: More than DI2048/DO2048 are used in PFORINET, then Main board C (with High Speed COMM CPU) is required but it is not used.
PRIO-696.remedy: Reduce the number of DI/DO used in PROFINET, or replace the main board by Main Board C.

PRIO-700.cause: No CC-Link IE PCB is installed.

PRIO-701.remedy: When size is changed in master, this alarm may happen. Cycle power the controller. If this alarm happens even after cycle power, contact FANUC service representative. The ID number in the brackets is required to track the problems.

PRIO-702.remedy: Check CC-Link IE settings and cable. If you changed RX,RY,RWr,RWw size to larger in master, robot setting should be changed to the larger size and robot should be cycling power.

PRIO-703.cause: A outlying numerical value is set to a remote register.
PRIO-703.remedy: Reset, this alarm is only 1 shot. If register is changed, judgement for this alarm is done again. CC-Link IE function of robot supports unsigned or signed 16bits word data. Do not enter another type of value to remote register. You can send float value, which is larger than -32769 and smaller than 65536, if $CCIE.$AUTO_REGCHG is set to 1. The value is sent with integer by cutting off the floating part. Severity of this alarm can be changed to warning if $CCIE.$REG_ER_WARN is set to 1.

PRIO-704.message: CC-IE I/O data size is changed
PRIO-704.cause: Cyclic data size has been reduced by the master.

PRIO-711.message: AI/O value is out of range
PRIO-711.cause: Value of AI/O is out of range. This AI/O port is used conversion data. And range is defined in $AIO_CNV.
PRIO-711.remedy: Check AI/O value. Check and change $AIO_CNV setting.

PRIO-802.cause: EtherCAT input size is different from master.

PRIO-803.cause: EtherCAT output size is different from master.

PRIO-804.cause: Mode switch on EtherCAT board is communication soft update mode.
PRIO-804.remedy: Change mode switch on EtherCAT board to 0 to change normal mode and cycle power.

PRIO-805.cause: Mode switch on EtherCAT board is EEPROM update mode.
PRIO-805.remedy: Change mode switch on EtherCAT board to 0 to change normal mode and cycle power.

PRIO-806.cause: EtherCAT update file is not found.
PRIO-806.remedy: Check system variables $BOOT2 $BOOT3 $ECAT_SOFT $EEPROM_IMG under $ECAT and check the file.

PRIO-807.cause: Update for EtherCAT communication soft or EEPROM is finished.
PRIO-807.remedy: Change mode switch on EtherCAT board to 0 to change normal mode and cycle power.

PRIO-808.remedy: Tell FANUC with the number displayed.

PRIO-809.remedy: Tell FANUC with the number displayed.

PRIO-811.cause: EtherCAT Com Soft on EtherCAT Slave board is older or newer than the robot software.
PRIO-811.remedy: Update EtherCAT Com Soft and EEPROM image by the procedure written in EtherCAT operation manual.

PRIO-812.cause: This message shows up together with PRIO-811 to inform the required and the current version of EtherCAT Com Soft.
PRIO-812.remedy: Update EtherCAT Com Soft and EEPROM image by the procedure written in EtherCAT operation

PROC-001.cause: The memory size allocated in $PRCREP.$maxmem_siz has been filled.
PROC-001.remedy: Delete old programs not used anymore to clear old logged data, or clear all log data to start fresh logging.

PROC-002.cause: There is not enough FROM or DRAM to log any new process data.
PROC-002.remedy: Delete old programs not used anymore to clear old logged data, or clear all log data to start fresh logging.

PROC-003.cause: This is a notification that process data was remotely cleared.

PROC-004.cause: This is a notification that process data was cleared from the TP.

PROC-005.message: %s out of tol for PROG %s, PROCESS ID=%d
PROC-005.cause: Alarm monitoring for specified item is enabled, and logged value is not within upper and lower tolerances.
PROC-005.remedy: Check your process to verify it is within tolerance Adjust uppper and lower tolerances as needed.

PROF-000.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical service representative.

PROF-003.remedy: Please change configuration data on Master

PROF-004.remedy: Please change parameter data on Master

PROF-005.remedy: Please change Slave Parameter sets on the Master.

PROF-018.cause: A status message exists in the slave specific diagnostic area in the received diagnostic data.
PROF-018.remedy: Please invstigate the specific diagnostic data.

PROF-019.cause: Multiple Profibus boards are not supported.
PROF-019.remedy: Please set only one Profibus board.

PROF-020.cause: Argument for PR_ONLN or PR_OFFLN is invalid.
PROF-020.remedy: It should be integer and 1 to 32.

PROG-001.cause: This indicates an internal system error.
PROG-001.remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

PROG-002.cause: The task name specified is invalid.

PROG-003.cause: The program name specified is invalid.

PROG-005.cause: The specified program cannot be found.

PROG-006.cause: The specified line number cannot be found.

PROG-007.cause: The specified program is already being executed.

PROG-008.message: In a rtn when creating a task
PROG-008.cause: Execution cannot be started in sub-routine program.

PROG-009.message: Line not same rtn as paused at
PROG-009.cause: Resumption was attempted at a different line from the paused line.

PROG-010.cause: Resumption was attempted in a different program from the paused one.

PROG-011.remedy: Check the teach pendant enable switch and other running programs to determine who has motion control.

PROG-012.message: All groups not on the top
PROG-012.cause: There is paused motion later than motion that was attempted to resume.
PROG-012.remedy: Resume the motion paused the last time.

PROG-013.cause: This motion was paused by the MOTION PAUSE instruction. Only the RESUME MOTION program instruction can can resume the motion.
PROG-013.remedy: Use RESUME MOTION instruction in the program.

PROG-014.cause: The number of programs you attempted to start exceeded the maximum number.
PROG-014.remedy: Abort dispensable programs or perform a CTRL start and select PROGRAM INIT option to increase the number of tasks allowed.

PROG-015.remedy: Do not use backward execution at this point

PROG-016.cause: The specified task is not running or paused.
PROG-016.remedy: Check the task name. The task name is always the name of the program that was run. The task name will not change even if the running program calls a routine from a different program.

PROG-017.cause: The specified task is not running.

PROG-019.cause: The request to pause the program was ignored.
PROG-019.remedy: Change the NOPAUSE task attribute or use the KCL PAUSE command with the FORCE option.

PROG-020.cause: The specified program was already aborted.

PROG-021.cause: The request to abort the program was ignored.
PROG-021.remedy: Change the NOABORT task attribute or use the KCL ABORT command with the FORCE option.

PROG-023.cause: The specified program is not paused.

PROG-024.cause: The motion path record is lost.
PROG-024.remedy: Do not attempt backwards execution at this time.

PROG-025.remedy: Do not use backwards execution here.

PROG-026.cause: Backward execution cannot be used any more. The current line is on top of the memorized path.
PROG-026.remedy: Do not use backwards execution here.

PROG-027.cause: The task number specified is invalid.

PROG-029.cause: This indicates an internal system error.
PROG-029.remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

PROG-030.cause: The specified task attribute is not found.

PROG-031.cause: The specified task attribute is write protected.
PROG-031.remedy: Do not try to change the attribute.

PROG-032.cause: The value for the specified attribute is invalid.

PROG-034.cause: The specified routine cannot be found.
PROG-034.remedy: Check the routine name and verify it is loaded.

PROG-035.cause: Motion control for the specified group cannot be locked.
PROG-035.remedy: Check the teach pendant enable switch and other running programs to determine who has motion control.

PROG-036.message: The length of trace array is 0
PROG-036.cause: Not enough memory or the task attribute is not set correctly.
PROG-036.remedy: Set the trace buffer length using the KCL SET TASK TRACELEN command.

PROG-037.message: No data in the trace array
PROG-037.cause: There is no execution record in memory.
PROG-037.remedy: Turn on tracing using the KCL SET TRACE ON command.

PROG-039.cause: Motion control for the specified group was reserved, but it cannot be obtained.
PROG-039.remedy: Check the teach pendant enable switch and other running programs to determine who has motion control.

PROG-040.cause: Motion control for the specified group was already reserved by another program.
PROG-040.remedy: Check the other running programs to determine who has motion control.

PROG-041.cause: Motion control is released. The teach pendant currently has motion control. The robot cannot be started until motion control is obtained.

PROG-042.remedy: If you had expected that the task may have already released the group, this may not be an error. Otherwise, check UNLOCK_GROUP usage.

PROG-043.cause: Motion control was already released by request of this program.
PROG-043.remedy: If you had expected that the task may have already released the group, this may not be an error. Otherwise, check UNLOCK_GROUP usage.

PROG-044.message: Arm has not been released yet
PROG-044.cause: Motion control was not released yet.
PROG-044.remedy: If you had expected that the task may have already locked the group, this may not be an error. Otherwise, check LOCK_GROUP usage.

PROG-045.cause: Motion control was already released by the request of another program.
PROG-045.remedy: If you had expected that another task may have already released the group, this may not be an error. Otherwise, check UNLOCK_GROUP usage.

PROG-046.cause: The teach pendant was enabled while the program is executing.
PROG-046.remedy: Disable the teach pendant and resume the program.

PROG-047.cause: The teach pendant was disabled while the program is executing.
PROG-047.remedy: Enable the teach pendant and use shift-FWD to resume execution.

PROG-048.cause: The shift key was released while the program is executing.
PROG-048.remedy: Hold the shift key and press the FWD key to resume execution.

PROG-049.cause: Motion control cannot be released because the robot is moving.
PROG-049.remedy: Check the status of robot motion.

PROG-050.cause: The program is in the process of being aborted.
PROG-050.remedy: Wait a second. If this error continues to occur, perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

PROG-051.cause: The specified lines to which a move was attempted exceed the number of lines in the program.

PROG-052.cause: The user application task was forced to abort while the application is executing. The AMR may not have been completely processed.
PROG-052.remedy: This requires no special action for the user.

PROG-053.cause: The user application task was not executed.
PROG-053.remedy: Start the user application task before executing the application.

PROG-054.cause: FWD key was released while the program is executing.
PROG-054.remedy: Hold the FWD key with shift key to resume execution.

PROG-055.cause: BWD key was released while the program is executing.
PROG-055.remedy: Hold the BWD key with shift key to resume execution.

PROG-056.cause: Motion data output function is enable instead of machin lock id disable.
PROG-056.remedy: Please disable motion data output in test cycle menu.

PROG-057.message: Power Fail Recover memory is cleared
PROG-057.cause: The backup of the execution memory failed. Then, the system restarted automatically.

PROG-058.cause: Pausing when using M-TP. This error happens only when using the M-TP(J897) option.
PROG-058.remedy: Push the OK button, restart the program, or push servo-ON button on M-TP to reset this warning.

PROG-059.cause: Abnormal communication with the M-TP. This error happens only when using the M-TP(J897) option.
PROG-059.remedy: Power OFF and ON the controller.

PROG-060.cause: An attempt was made to set FANUC's uframe. This error happens only when using the M-TP(J897) option.
PROG-060.remedy: Don't set FANUC's uframe when using the M-TP.

PROG-061.cause: GD variable which is used by SHIFT-ON command is not set. This error happens only when using the M-TP(J897) option.

PROG-062.cause: This error happens only when using the M-TP(J897) option.

PROG-063.cause: This error happens only when using PROGRAM/JOG OVERRIDE function(J579). PROGRAM was executed during jog operation is executed.

PROG-064.cause: Execution is not allowed for TP Collection programs.
PROG-064.remedy: Do not try to execute TP Collection.

PTPG-000.cause: This error is caused when a internal problem has occurred within the Paint Plug In software. This fault is almost always caused by style paths which do things which were not anticipated when this software was written. The reasons for this could be: 1. The path is too fast 2. The instructions (PPS and PPE) are too close together 3. The delay and timing values specified in your Paint Plug In Setup are too large or do not make sense. 4. Your robot's CPU has failed.
PTPG-000.remedy: Write down the exact error number and message shown. Write down exactly what your robot was doing at the time of the failure. Make sure you include: Program name, line number, robot's location in the work cell, any cell I/O or other communciation activity, and exactly what the robot was doing right before the fault occured. This fault is usually fixed by doing a COLD start. If that does not work, contact your supervisor or call the FANUC America Corporation Hot Line.

PTPG-001.cause: This error is caused when a internal problem has occurred within the Paint Plug In software. This fault is almost always caused by style paths which do things which were not anticipated when this software was written. The reasons for this could be: 1. The path is too fast 2. The instructions (PPS and PPE) are too close together 3. The delay and timing values specified in your Paint Plug In Setup are too large or do not make sense. 4. Your robot's CPU has failed.
PTPG-001.remedy: Write down the exact error number and message shown. Write down exactly what your robot was doing at the time of the failure. Make sure you include: Program name, line number, robot's location in the work cell, any cell I/O or other communciation activity, and exactly what the robot was doing right before the fault occured. This fault is usually fixed by doing a COLD start. If that does not work, contact your supervisor or call the FANUC America Corporation Hot Line.

PTPG-002.cause: A citical task required to run the Paint Plug In software is missing or not running.
PTPG-002.remedy: Contact your FANUC America Corporation representative.

PTPG-003.cause: A TP Event Instruction was called (PPS[x] or PPE), but the corresponding TP program or sub-program was not loaded. This caused the Paint Plug-In to abort the job.
PTPG-003.remedy: Ensure the missing TP program is loaded.

PTPG-004.cause: This error is usually caused by a system failure.
PTPG-004.remedy: Check TPE instructions. Cycle power on controller.

PTPG-005.cause: The schedule index value of the current instruction execution is invalid.
PTPG-005.remedy: Check the index value of instruction.

PTPG-006.cause: The current Job has been aborted due to a fatal error.
PTPG-006.remedy: Correct the cause of this error, which is usually posted immediately before this error is posted.

PTPG-007.cause: The Group Mask attribute in the TP header of the specified program is set.
PTPG-007.remedy: Ensure that the Group mask is NOT set for the specified program.

PTPG-008.cause: The Paint Plug-In detected an unknown Paint Event, which caused the system to fault.
PTPG-008.remedy: Determine the cause for this unknown event to execute.

PTPG-009.cause: An Event TP program did not complete processing within the specified time.
PTPG-009.remedy: Ensure that the TP program instruction is correct.

PTPG-010.cause: The Paint Plug-In detected a Paint Start(PPS[]) TP instruction without a matching Paint End (PPE) instruction.
PTPG-010.remedy: Ensure that a PPE instruction is included at the end of the job.

PTPG-011.cause: The Paint Plug-In detected a Paint End (PPE) instruction without a Paint Start (PPS).
PTPG-011.remedy: Ensure that a PPS instruction is included before a PPE instruction.
