PWD-031.cause: The Operator password level does not have access to the FULL MENUS. Either a timeout occurred or a user logged out.
PWD-031.remedy: Press the TP MENUS hardkey and select SETUP PASSWORDS. Log in with either the Install, Setup, or Program password level. Press the TP FCTN hardkey and select QUICK/FULL MENUS to return to FULL MENUS.

PWD-032.cause: A user with Install level access logged in from SMON.
PWD-032.remedy: This is a status message you can use for tracking operations performed by the users.

PWD-033.cause: A user with Install level access logged in from KCL.
PWD-033.remedy: This is a status message you can use for tracking operations performed by the users.

PWD-034.cause: A user with Install level access logged in from Teach Pendant.
PWD-034.remedy: This is a status message you can use for tracking operations performed by the users.

PWD-035.cause: A user with Install level access logged in from CRT/Keyboard.
PWD-035.remedy: This is a status message you can use for tracking operations performed by the users.

PWD-036.cause: A user with Install level access logged out from SMON.
PWD-036.remedy: This is a status message you can use for tracking operations performed by the users.

PWD-037.cause: A user with Install level access logged out from SMON.
PWD-037.remedy: This is a status message you can use for tracking operations performed by the users.

PWD-038.cause: A user with Install level access logged out from SMON.
PWD-038.remedy: This is a status message you can use for tracking operations performed by the users.

PWD-039.cause: A user with Install level access logged out from SMON.
PWD-039.remedy: This is a status message you can use for tracking operations performed by the users.

PWD-050.cause: A user was logged out because of a password timeout from SMON.
PWD-050.remedy: Log in, if required. Adjust the timeout value if it is too short.

PWD-051.cause: A user was logged out because of a password timeout from KCL.
PWD-051.remedy: Log in, if required. Adjust the timeout value if it is too short.

PWD-052.cause: A user was logged out because of a password timeout from Teach Pendant.
PWD-052.remedy: Log in, if required. Adjust the timeout value if it is too short.

PWD-053.cause: A user was logged out because of a password timeout from CRT/Keyboard.
PWD-053.remedy: Log in, if required. Adjust the timeout value if it is too short.

PWD-054.cause: A user with Install level access logged in from the Internet.
PWD-054.remedy: This is a status message you can use to track operations performed by the users.

PWD-055.cause: A user with Install level access logged out from the Internet.
PWD-055.remedy: This is a status message you can use to track operations performed by the users.

PWD-060.cause: A user was logged out because of a password timeout from the Internet.
PWD-060.remedy: Log in if required. Lengthen the timeout value from the SETUP Passwords menu if it is too short.

PWD-061.cause: As a result of a user login, the pendant is using Full Menus instead of Quick Menus.
PWD-061.remedy: This is a status message you can use to track operations performed by the users.

PWD-062.message: Login from USB device is cancelled
PWD-062.cause: You cannot login to this device.

PWD-063.cause: Another user is already logged in to this device.

PWD-064.cause: The user password timeout has been extended.

PWD-065.cause: A password USB device has been inserted.
PWD-065.remedy: This is a status message you can use to track operations performed by the users.

PWD-066.cause: There are 2 causes for this alarm. The first is that the password USB device has incorrect username and password. This will be the cause code for PWD-062 Login from USB device is cancelled. The second is that a password configuration file, FRS:PASSWORD.DT, is invalid.
PWD-066.remedy: For the first cause, check the password USB device. Your INSTALL user may have to add your username and password using the SETUP Passwords menu. For the second cause, the INSTALL user should IMPORT a correct password configuration file using the SETUP Passwords menu. This file will replace FRS:PASSWORD.DT. It becomes a binary file for protection. It is possible that an invalid configuration file was restored because someone tried to break into the password system.

PWD-067.cause: You attempted to perform an operation that was password protected.
PWD-067.remedy: You must log in using the SETUP Passwords menu. If the operation is still not allowed, you might need to contact the user at your site with INSTALL level permissions to change your level.

PWD-068.cause: You attempted to display a menu that was password protected.
PWD-068.remedy: You must log in using the SETUP Passwords menu. If the operation is still not allowed, you might need to contact the user at your site with INSTALL level permissions to change your level.

PWD-069.cause: You attempted to perform an operation that was password protected.
PWD-069.remedy: You must log in using the SETUP Passwords menu. If the operation is still not allowed, you might need to contact the user at your site with INSTALL level permissions to change your level.

PWD-070.remedy: To enable passwords, go to the SETUP Passwords menu, press LOGIN and reenter the INSTALL user password.

PWD-071.cause: This operation is protected in TP disable by password autologin function.

PWD-072.cause: This operation is protected in AUTO mode by password autologin function.
PWD-072.remedy: Change to T1 or T2 mode.

PWD-075.cause: A teach pendant storage attribute was changed.
PWD-075.remedy: This is a status message you can use for tracking operations performed by the users.

QMGR-001.cause: An attempt was made to add entry to a queue when the queue was full.
QMGR-001.remedy: Use GET_QUEUE to remove entries or use a larger value for queue size in the INIT_QUEUE call.

QMGR-002.cause: An Attempt to use GET_QUEUE when there are no entries in the queue This is the normal result when no entries have been added or all have been removed by previous calls.

QMGR-003.cause: A bad sequence_no value is used in an INSERT_QUEUE or DELETE_QUEUE call. The value may be less than 1 or greater than the sequence number of the last entry in the queue.

QMGR-004.cause: n_skip parameter in COPY_QUEUE call is less than zero
QMGR-004.remedy: Use zero or a positive value

RIPE-001.cause: System network timing has been lost. The system has automatically been reestablished.
RIPE-001.remedy: If this continues to happen, the physical Network wiring configuration and setup should be checked for errors. Usually this is just a result of a re-power of one of the controllers.

RIPE-002.cause: System network timing has been lost but the system has automatically reestablished timing.
RIPE-002.remedy: If this continues to happen, the configuration and setup should be checked for errors.

RIPE-003.cause: The syntax of ROSIPCFG.XML is not correct.
RIPE-003.remedy: Consult TD:RIPINIT.TXT for detailed warnings and correct them.

RIPE-004.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

RIPE-005.cause: The rosipcfg.xml is different among the controllers in the RING
RIPE-005.remedy: Make sure that all controllers have identical rosipcfg.xml files

RIPE-006.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

RIPE-007.cause: This is a notification that a robot has gone offline. This is posted whenever a member robot is turned off or unplugged.

RIPE-008.cause: This is a notification that a robot has gone offline. This is posted whenever a member robot is turned on or plugged in.

RIPE-009.cause: Information about a member is updated. This is only posted in a system which is not automatically synchronized.

RIPE-010.cause: The indicated robot has had its protocol reset. This might be the cause of some other error.

RIPE-011.message: This robot is not in the ring
RIPE-011.cause: The IP address of this robot is not found anywhere in FRS:ROSIPCFG.XML.
RIPE-011.remedy: The configuration must include the correct IP addresses.

RIPE-012.cause: An initial tick time synchronization has occurred. This message is posted after all robots are powered up.

RIPE-013.message: Robot not found in ring data
RIPE-013.cause: A robot specified in a destination is not part of the ring defined in ROSIPCFG.XML.
RIPE-013.remedy: The configuration must include information on all robots in the ring.

RIPE-014.cause: The system has attempted to send a packet which is too large. The limit is 1472 bytes.
RIPE-014.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

RIPE-015.cause: A packet sent to all robots cannot be a round trip packet.
RIPE-015.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

RIPE-016.cause: A call was made to get network tick before the system ticks are synchronized.
RIPE-016.remedy: Wait for the synchronized message before requesting tick value.

RIPE-017.cause: A call was made to get network tick before the system ticks are synchronized.
RIPE-017.remedy: Wait for the synchronized message before requesting tick value.

RIPE-018.cause: This is a notification that a robot has gone offline. This is posted whenever a member robot is turned off or unplugged.

RIPE-019.cause: More than 48 requests are queued to RIPE have not been processed
RIPE-019.remedy: Check the network hardware. Structure the application to limit or throttle RIPE packet sends

RIPE-020.cause: The ROSIPCFG.XML file is not the same among the robots.
RIPE-020.remedy: Make the ROSIPCFG.XML file the same.

RIPE-021.cause: A robot has had its protocol reset similar to going online and offline.
RIPE-021.remedy: This is for information only but could be the result of a packet send on an unstable network.

RIPE-022.cause: Messages were received out of sequence. This could be due to bad network hardware.
RIPE-022.remedy: Power cycle may be required to reset depending on the number of robots involved.

RIPE-023.cause: Messages were received out of sequence. This could be due to bad network hardware.
RIPE-023.remedy: Power cycle may be required to reset depending on the number of robots involved. None

RIPE-024.cause: CPU is busy, RIPE may experience difficulties.

RMIT-001.cause: Remote Motion interface internal system error.
RMIT-001.remedy: Power off to recover. If problem persistes, please reload the controller.

RMIT-002.cause: The user tool number is not valid.
RMIT-002.remedy: Please make sure the tool number is within range.

RMIT-003.cause: The user frame number is not valid.
RMIT-003.remedy: Please make sure the user frame number is within range.

RMIT-004.cause: The position register number is not valid.
RMIT-004.remedy: Please make sure the position register number is within range.

RMIT-005.remedy: Please make sure the speed override set between 1 to 100

RMIT-006.cause: Robot Controller cannot start Teach Pendant program execution in AUTO mode
RMIT-006.remedy: Please make sure the Teach Pendant is disabled and the controller is in AUTO mode. Please clear/reset any error and the controller's servo is on before sending FRC_Initialize command.

RMIT-008.remedy: Please turn off the teach pendant and put controller in AUTO mode.

RMIT-009.cause: The RMI TP program is not running.
RMIT-009.remedy: Please use FRC_Initialize to start RMI Motion Interface again.

RMIT-010.cause: The RMI TP progam cannot be paused.
RMIT-010.remedy: Use FRC_Abort to abort the TP program and FRC_Initialize to restart the program.

RMIT-011.cause: The RMI TP progam can not be resumed.
RMIT-011.remedy: Use FRC_Initialize to restart Remote Motion Interface.

RMIT-012.cause: FRC_Reset command cannot clear all errors.
RMIT-012.remedy: Check robot controller for error that prevents the reset command.

RMIT-013.remedy: Check RMI manual to make sure correct RMI command is sent to robot controller.

RMIT-014.remedy: The RMI command has no effect on the robot controller due to current robot controller status.

RMIT-015.cause: The controller is in error state when receiving the RMI command.
RMIT-015.remedy: Make sure the robot controller is in valid state before sending RMI command

RMIT-016.cause: RMI Does not work when controller has HOT start enabled.
RMIT-016.remedy: Remote Motion Interface disable Hot start for next cycle start. Please cycle power.

RMIT-017.remedy: Make sure a valid payload schedule number is sent to the controller.

RMIT-018.cause: Invalid motion option in motion instruction, or the controller is not loaded with the required option.
RMIT-018.remedy: Make sure to send the correct motion option to controlller.

RMIT-019.cause: The input vision register number is not valid.
RMIT-019.remedy: Please make sure the vision register number is within range.

RMIT-020.cause: An invalid TP instruction is received by the controller.
RMIT-020.remedy: Check the instruction string to make sure correct RMI instruction is sent to robot controller. Make sure number of executing instruction is less or equal to eight.

RMIT-021.cause: The input value is out of acceptable range.
RMIT-021.remedy: Please check the value specified in the text string to make sure they are in the acceptable range.

RMIT-022.cause: The controller cannot parse the input text string.
RMIT-022.remedy: Please check the text string to make sure it comply with format specified in the manual

RMIT-023.remedy: Please make sure the position data text comply with the specification defined in the manual.

RMIT-024.cause: RMI is in HOLD state due to error in previous instruction packet.
RMIT-024.remedy: Please send FRC_Reset to reset the controller before sending new RMI instruction.

RMIT-025.cause: Remote device is not connected to the controller.
RMIT-025.remedy: Please send FRC_Connect packet to controller to establish the connection.

RMIT-026.cause: Robot is already connected to an external device
RMIT-026.remedy: Make sure there is no other remote device is connected to the robot controller. Or use FRC_Disconnect to disconnect previous connection.

RMIT-027.cause: Controller is still executing previous command.
RMIT-027.remedy: Please wait for controller to complete current command before sending next command packet.

RMIT-028.cause: Controller is still executing previous instructions.
RMIT-028.remedy: Please wait for controller to complete previous instruction before sending next instruction packet.

RMIT-029.cause: The new instruction has an invalid sequence ID number.
RMIT-029.remedy: Make sure the sequence ID is consecutive and monotonic increasing before sending next instruction packet.

RMIT-030.cause: The motion instruction has an invalid speed type.
RMIT-030.remedy: Make sure the motion string includes correct string for speed type.

RMIT-031.cause: The motion instruction has an invalid speed value.
RMIT-031.remedy: Make sure the motion string includes correct string for speed value.

RMIT-032.cause: The motion instruction has an invalid termination type.
RMIT-032.remedy: Make sure the motion string includes correct termination type.

RMIT-033.cause: The motion instruction has an invalid termination value.
RMIT-033.remedy: Make sure the motion string includes correct termination value.

RMIT-034.cause: The motion instruction has an invalid local condition port. type.
RMIT-034.remedy: Make sure the motion string includes correct local condition port type.

RMIT-035.cause: The motion instruction has an invalid ACC value.
RMIT-035.remedy: Make sure the motion string includes correct ACC value.

RMIT-036.cause: The motion instruction has an invalid destination position.
RMIT-036.remedy: Make sure the motion string includes correct destination position data.

RMIT-037.cause: The motion instruction has an invalid via position.
RMIT-037.remedy: Make sure the motion string includes correct via position data.

RMIT-038.cause: The instruction has an invalid port number.
RMIT-038.remedy: Make sure instruction string includes correct port number.

ROOP-001.cause: Internal CP Resume Offset on Path error.
ROOP-001.remedy: Contact FANUC Support with error and information on events leading up to the error.

ROOP-002.message: Resume offset on path not enabled
ROOP-002.cause: Resume Offset on Path feature has not been enabled.
ROOP-002.remedy: Enable feature at CTRL start in ROOP MENU.

ROOP-004.cause: Either an invalid motion group or mask has been specified. ROOP only supports group G1 for dispensing.
ROOP-004.remedy: Make sure TP Program only uses Group G1.

ROOP-005.cause: Internal ROOP path variable size is not initialized.
ROOP-005.remedy: Go to ROOP CTRL start menu and set ROOP max number of nodes > 0 and press F3 APPLY.

ROOP-006.cause: During ROOP playback, robot current position conversion from Joint to Cartesian failed.
ROOP-006.remedy: Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

ROOP-007.cause: During ROOP playback, recorded position conversion from Joint to Cartesian failed.
ROOP-007.remedy: Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

ROOP-008.cause: Internal setup for or edit of TP program failed.
ROOP-008.remedy: Contact FANUC Support with information on events leading up to the error. If present, refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

ROOP-009.cause: Distance between current robot position and recorded motion being issued is too large.
ROOP-009.remedy: Try one or more of the following: Go to ROOP CTRL start menu, increase ROOP speed and press F3 APPLY. Go to ROOP CTRL start menu, increase ROOP node exec delay and press F3 APPLY. Go to ROOP CTRL start menu, increase ROOP distance tol and press F3 APPLY.

ROOP-010.cause: ROOP attempted to use Auto Error Recovery but was unsuccessful.
ROOP-010.remedy: Review Auto Error Recovery setup for proper settings.

ROOP-011.cause: Internal ROOP path node append or delete failed.
ROOP-011.remedy: Contact FANUC Support with information on events leading up to the error. Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

ROOP-012.cause: No motion has been recorded for ROOP playback.
ROOP-012.remedy: Review circumstances when the original program paused. This is when data is recorded. Refer to the alarm history for more possible information.

ROOP-013.cause: Capacity is at 90% for recorded ROOP path.
ROOP-013.remedy: This is just a warning. If capacity reaches 100%, the program will ABORT. To reduce amount of recorded data, decrease the Resume Offset value on the ROOP setup menu. Doing this will require re-tuning of the Resume Offset setup menu Gun Delay for this dispense equipment however. To increase capacity, Go to ROOP CTRL start menu, increase ROOP max number of nodes and press F3 APPLY.

ROOP-014.cause: Capacity is FULL for recorded ROOP path.
ROOP-014.remedy: To reduce amount of recorded data, decrease the Resume Offset value on the ROOP setup menu. Doing this will require re-tuning of the Resume Offset setup menu Gun Delay for this dispense equipment however. To increase capacity, Go to ROOP CTRL start menu, increase ROOP max number of nodes and press F3 APPLY.

ROOP-015.cause: ROOP attempt to lock group G1 failed.
ROOP-015.remedy: Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

ROOP-016.cause: Either an invalid motion group or mask has been specified.
ROOP-016.remedy: Make sure TP Program has at least one valid motion group in group mask. Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

ROOP-017.remedy: Note that TP program names TMPRPMVG1.TP and TMPRPMVG1X.TP are reserved for ROOP. Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

ROOP-018.remedy: Note that TP program names TMPRPMVG1.TP and TMPRPMVG1X.TP are reserved for ROOP. Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

ROOP-019.remedy: Note that TP program names TMPRPMVG1.TP and TMPRPMVG1X.TP are reserved for ROOP. Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

ROOP-020.remedy: Note that TP program names TMPRPMVG1.TP and TMPRPMVG1X.TP are reserved for ROOP. Refer to the alarm DETAIL cause for more information.

ROOP-021.cause: This is only a warning. This indicates that the timing where the gun is resumed may not be accurate. If posted by itself, the ROOP setup Gun delay or an internal timing calculation is out of limits.
ROOP-021.remedy: Review circumstances when the original program paused. Refer to the alarm history for more possible information.

ROOP-022.cause: This is only a warning. The ROOP setup menu Resume Offset is out of limits. This also indicates that the timing where the gun is resumed may not be accurate.
ROOP-022.remedy: Set the ROOP setup menu Resume Offset within limits. Doing this may require re-tuning of the Resume Offset setup menu Gun Delay for this dispense equipment however.

ROOP-023.cause: This is only a warning. The robot cannot move as far back as requested because not enough CP data exists. This also indicates that the timing where the gun is resumed may not be accurate.
ROOP-023.remedy: To reduce the backup distance, decrease the Resume Offset value on the ROOP setup menu. Doing this will require re-tuning of the Resume Offset setup menu Gun Delay for this dispense equipment however. To increase the data available for CP resume offset, do one or more of the following the Resume Offset setup menu: Increase the Max Offset Res Dist. Decrease the Nominal Process Speed. Press DONE and allow the robot to cycle power, then manually cycle power again. Doing any of this will require re-tuning of all Resume Offset setup menu Gun Delays for all dispense equipments however.

ROOP-024.message: Insufficient CP data for return to pause
ROOP-024.cause: This is only a warning. The robot cannot move back to the original fault position because not enough CP data exists. This also indicates that the timing where the gun is resumed may not be accurate.
ROOP-024.remedy: To increase the data available for CP resume offset, do one or more of the following the Resume Offset setup menu: Increase the Max Offset Res Dist. Decrease the Nominal Process Speed. Press DONE and allow the robot to cycle power, then manually cycle power again. Doing any of this will require re-tuning of all Resume Offset setup menu Gun Delays for all dispense equipments however.

ROOP-025.cause: This is only a warning. The ROOP setup menu Gun Delay is out of limits. This also indicates that the timing where the gun is resumed may not be accurate.
ROOP-025.remedy: Set the ROOP setup menu Gun Delay within limits. If a decreased Gun Delay does not allow the gun to resume at the proper timing then the backup distance must be decreased. To reduce the backup distance, decrease the Resume Offset value on the ROOP setup menu. Doing this will require re-tuning of the Resume Offset setup menu Gun Delay for this dispense equipment however.

ROOP-026.cause: Unable to perform CP Resume Offset on Path and therefore resuming is prohibited in order to prevent shortcut motion.
ROOP-026.remedy: Verify correct setup for Auto Error Recovery and Resume Offset menus.

ROUT-022.cause: Incorrect number is specified for ORD builtin routine.
ROUT-022.remedy: Specify a number less than the string length.

ROUT-023.cause: Incorrect number is specified for SUBSTR builtin routine.
ROUT-023.remedy: Specify a number less than the string length.

ROUT-024.cause: Negative number is specified for length argument for SUBSTR builtin routine.

ROUT-025.cause: Incorrect number is specified for semaphore id.

ROUT-027.cause: Specified string variable does not have enough room to hold the return data.

ROUT-028.cause: Incorrect file attribute id was specified.

ROUT-029.cause: Incorrect file attribute value was specified.

ROUT-030.cause: A non-existent register number is specified.

ROUT-031.remedy: Specify the correct register type for the attempted operation.

ROUT-032.cause: Position type is not correct for the operation.

ROUT-034.remedy: Specify a program name other than a Karel program.

ROUT-035.cause: The specified value is out of range.
ROUT-035.remedy: Specify a value within the range.

ROUT-037.cause: Value used in SET_HEAD_TPE for bfr_size is invalid.
ROUT-037.remedy: Use buffer size in the range 1-255.

ROUT-038.cause: Attempt to access position data or type from TPE program when the position has not been recorded.
ROUT-038.remedy: Record position data using the TPP TOUCHUP function

ROUT-039.cause: Cannot unlock group while motion is executing.
ROUT-039.remedy: Wait until executing motion has completed.

ROUT-040.cause: Cannot unlock group while stopped motion exists.
ROUT-040.remedy: Resume stopped motion and wait until motion has completed or cancel stopped motion.

ROUT-041.cause: Variable displayed for dynaoic display is not a static variable. Parameter may be a local or constant. Neither of these is permitted as the displayed variable in INI_DYN_DIS calls.
ROUT-041.remedy: Copy constant or local variable to static variable and use this inINI_DYN_DIS* call.

ROUT-042.cause: The parameter designated by param_no does not exist.
ROUT-042.remedy: Confirm the param_no and the parameter in CALL/MACRO command in main TPE program.

ROUT-043.cause: The parameter data type does not match the CALL/MACRO argument data type.
ROUT-043.remedy: Confirm the parameter data type in CALL/MACRO command in main TPE program.

ROUT-044.cause: Tag name supplied in MSG_CONNECT, MSG_DISCO, or MSG_PING call was too long.
ROUT-044.remedy: Use tag name not over 12 characters.

ROUT-045.cause: Dictionary name supplied in built-in call is too long.
ROUT-045.remedy: Use name of 4 or less characters.

ROUT-046.cause: Call to apnd_mtn_opt, write_xyzwpr, or write_joint with option array not initialized
ROUT-046.remedy: Initialize the array by calling INIT_MTN_OPT

ROUT-047.cause: Stream instruction program buffer is full.
ROUT-047.remedy: Wait for stream program execution to complete more instructions, then retry.

ROUT-048.cause: The streaming program is not currently running.
ROUT-048.remedy: Issue the function on an active stream program.

ROUT-049.cause: The motion option data supplied in the motion write routine call is not valid, or does not match the specified motion type.
ROUT-049.remedy: Initialize and fill the motion options correctly.

ROUT-050.message: SET comment builtin string too long
ROUT-050.cause: A string containing over 16 characters passed as comment argument in SET_TPE_CMT call. Argrument truncated to 16 characters.
ROUT-050.remedy: Use comment string of 16 or fewer characters.

RPC-001.cause: The client could not encode its arguments in a remote procedure call.

RPC-002.cause: The client could not decode the results of a remote procedure call.

RPC-003.cause: The client could not send the data for a remote procedure call.

RPC-004.cause: The client could not receive a reply from a remote procedure call.

RPC-005.cause: The client timed out while waiting for a reply from a remote procedure call.

RPC-006.cause: The server received an older version of the RPC protocol.
RPC-006.remedy: Update the client software to use the same version of the RPC protocol.

RPC-007.cause: The client or server received an unauthorized remote procedure call.

RPC-008.cause: The server received a remote procedure call for a program which it does not support.

RPC-009.cause: The server received a remote procedure call which uses the wrong version of a program.
RPC-009.remedy: Update the client or server software.

RPC-010.cause: The server received a remote procedure call for a procedure which it does not support.

RPC-011.cause: The server could not decode the arguments of a remote procedure call.

RPC-013.cause: The client could not determine the server for the remote procedure call.
RPC-013.remedy: Check the system variables which configure the offline RPC server.

RPC-018.cause: The server received a remote procedure call which uses the wrong version of a program. The versions supported are shown.
RPC-018.remedy: Update the client or server software.

RPC-019.cause: This operation requires the PC Interface option to be loaded on the controller.
RPC-019.remedy: Install the PC Interface software option on the controller. Refer to the FANUC America Corporation Software Installation Manual for more information.

RPM-005.cause: There is not enough cmos memory for this rpm segment
RPM-005.remedy: Increase the cmos memory by deleting unused TPE Or increase pitch value so that rpm do not need so much cmos space.

RPM-009.cause: Attempt to playback a segment that is not recorded in the specified buffer
RPM-009.remedy: Check that RECORD is active for this segment and using the correct buffer number.

RPM-013.remedy: Use a buffer number in the range 1-$RPM_CONFIG.$N_BUFFERS

RPM-020.cause: There is no rpm data is stored in this segment
RPM-020.remedy: Check the position number Or re-record again

RPM-026.remedy: Time pitch value have to equal or greater than 100

RPM-027.remedy: Use motion attached arc start instruction

RPM-028.cause: The segment for RPM is either zero length move or too short
RPM-028.remedy: Zero length RPM motion is not allow

RPM-039.cause: RPM data has coordinated motion but TPE doesn't have. Or RPM data has non-coordinated motion but TPE has.
RPM-039.remedy: Use same coordinated motion type (CD or non-CD) to both TAST and RPM program.

RPM-050.remedy: Check segment length and increase the segment length.

RRMC-001.cause: Internal PLAN error. This class of error should not be encountered during normal operation
RRMC-001.remedy: The system may have been corrupted. This may have been caused by any of a number of reasons including: Incorrect loading and setup loading incompatible options, mixing software version when adding options and other memory corruption problems. The following is a list of possible remedies: 1. Perform a cold start. 2. Perform an init start and setup the robot again 3. Confirm that any options or additional software not on the original software distribution media is the same version number. If the main system software was supplied on several disks or memory cards, make sure that you are using a matched set. Also make sure that the installation manual being used is for this version of software. If any of the software version are not matched, a complete re-load with the correct software will be necessary. 4. Confirm that no incompatible or mutually exclusive option have been loaded. 5. Full software reload. 6. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

SDTL-055.remedy: Check displayed line of CSV file. String at which X_DYNDAT detected error is displayed, too. Check data type and its data format. Input data in proper format.

SDTL-056.message: Converted to real of out of range(Line %s)
SDTL-056.cause: Execution of X_DYNDAT causes this error. Very large (or small) value is specified as real value of register. It was interpreted as value of out of range. Data should be larger than -1.0E16 and less than 1.0E16. Scientific notation cannot be used in CSV file.

SDTL-057.cause: Execution of X_DYNDAT without argument causes this error. In this case, path of CSV file is decided by string register. Index of string register is decided by KAREL variable, [X_DYNDAT]IDEFSRIDX (KAREL variable IDEFSRIDX of KAREL program X_DYNDAT). String register of specified index doesn’t exist.
SDTL-057.remedy: Check value of [X_DYNDAT]IDEFSRIDX. Change its value to valid index of string register.

SDTL-058.cause: Execution of X_DYNDAT causes this error. %s shows specified path of CSV file. If X_DYNDAT is used without argument, string register used to decide file path is displayed, too. Following table shows examples. In all cases, specified file could not be opened. Table 3–1. Examples Example of Error Comment SDTL-058 Cannot open specified file (MC:\CP_0100.CSV) X_DYNDAT was executed by CALL instruction. The 1st argument corresponded to ‘MC:\CP_0100.CSV’. SDTL-058 Cannot open specified file () X_DYNDAT was executed by CALL instruction. The 1st argument corresponded to ‘’(null string). If CALL X_DYNDAT(SR[3]) is executed and SR[3] is ‘’ (null string), this can happen. SDTL-058 Cannot open specified file (SR[1]:MC:\CP_0100.CSV) X_DYNDAT was directly RUN or called without argument. Because KAREL variable IDEFSRIDX of X_DYNDAT was 1, value of SR[1] was used as file path of CSV file. SR[1] was ‘MC:\CP_0100.CSV’. SDTL-058 Cannot open specified file (SR[1]:) This is similar to the case above, but SR[1] was ‘’ (null string). Please refer to cause code, too. For example, if error is posted like following, please check if specified file exists or not. SDTL-058 Cannot open specified file (MC:\CP_0100.CSV) FILE-014 File not found.
SDTL-058.remedy: Check displayed file path. Check if specified file exists.

SDTL-078.cause: This alarm is posted by execution of KAREL program, STPAYLOD. Inertia of payload is out of range. It is specified by register. Suppose the 3rd argument of STPAYLOD is 101. Inertia of payload around X axis is specified by R[105]. If its value is -20.5, (X, 105, -20.500) is displayed.
SDTL-078.remedy: Check index of register and its value. Set proper value

SDTL-081.cause: This alarm is posted by execution of KAREL program, STPAYLOD. Register for payload does not exist.
SDTL-081.remedy: The 3rd argument of STPAYLOD is index of register of payload Set proper value.

SDTL-082.message: Register for payload center(%s) does not exist.
SDTL-082.cause: This alarm is posted by execution of KAREL program, STPAYLOD. Register for payload center does not exist. coordinate (X or Y or Z) and index are displayed, too.
SDTL-082.remedy: Suppose the 3rd argument of STPAYLOD is n. STPAYLOD uses R[n], R[n+1],...... R[n+6] Modify the 3rd argument so that the 7 registers exist. Set proper value to the 3rd argument

SDTL-083.message: Register for payload inertia (%s) does not exist.
SDTL-083.cause: This alarm is posted by execution of KAREL program, STPAYLOD. Register for payload inertia does not exist. coordinate (X or Y or Z) and index are displayed, too.
SDTL-083.remedy: Suppose the 3rd argument of STPAYLOD is n. STPAYLOD uses R[n], R[n+1],...... R[n+6] Modify the 3rd argument so that the 7 registers exist.

SEAL-000.cause: This error is caused when Dispensetool encounters a problem it is unable to solve internally. This fault is almost always caused by style paths which do things which were not anticipated when this software was written. The reasons for this could be: 1. The sealing path is too fast 2. The sealing instructions (SS and SE) are too close together 3. The delay and timing values specified in your sealing schedules are too large or do not make sense. 4. Your robot's CPU has failed
SEAL-000.remedy: Write down the exact error number and message shown. Write down exactly what your robot was doing at the time of the failure. Make sure you include: Program name, line number, robot's location in the work cell, any cell I/O or other communication activity, and exactly what the robot was doing right before the fault occurred. This fault is usually fixed by doing a COLD start. If that does not work, contact your supervisor or call the FANUC America Corporation Hot Line.

SEAL-010.cause: When an line tracking program is processed, it is scanned for the extreme values within each sealing segment. If an error occurs during this scanning process, an error is posted. The error may occur for several reasons: A jump instruction during a sealing segment, or an unsupported instruction during a sealing segment.
SEAL-010.remedy: Verify that every instruction between the first SS and the SE instructions is supported by DispenseTool. Also verify that no JUMP instructions exist between the first SS and the SE instruction.

SEAL-021.cause: In the Schedule number listed, the Gun On signal has been set up to turn on or off too long after the node the SS[] or SE is attached to. Currently, if this signal is set up to turn on or off greater than 100ms after the node, this warning will be posted and the signal will fore 100ms after the node. These are the formulas used to determine when the gun will be turned on or off relative to the node for seal schedule 'n': For SS[n]: Time_Before = EQUIPMENT_DELAY - GUNON_DELAY For SE: Time_Before = EQUIPMENT_DELAY - GUNOFF_DELAY Note that a NEGATIVE Time_Before means AFTER the node.
SEAL-021.remedy: There is no real danger in this condition. You should be aware that if you try to turn the gun on or off after 100ms AFTER the node, the signal will always be fired 100ms after the node and this warning will be posted. To correct this problem, make the equipment_delay more positive or the gunon/gunoff delay more negative, to move the firing of the signal up earlier.

SEAL-022.cause: In the Schedule number listed, the Start Meter signal has been set up to turn on or off too long after the node the SS[] or SE is attached to. Currently, if this signal is set up to turn on or off greater than 100ms after the node, this warning will be posted and the signal will fire 100ms after the node. These are the formulas used to determine when this signal will be turned on or off relative to the node for seal schedule 'n': For SS[n]: Time_Before = PRE_PRESSURE_DELAY + EQUIPMENT_DELAY - GUNON_DELAY For SE[n]: Time_Before = DE_PRESSURE_DELAY + EQUIPMENT_DELAY - GUNOFF_DELAY Note that a NEGATIVE Time_Before means AFTER the node.
SEAL-022.remedy: There is no real danger in this condition. You should be aware that if you try to turn this signal on or off after 100ms AFTER the node, the signal will always be fired 100ms after the node and this warning will be posted. To correct this problem, make the pre/de_pressure_delay or equipment_delay more positive or the gunon/gunoff delay more negative, to move the firing of the signal up earlier.

SEAL-023.cause: In the Schedule number listed, the Atomizing Air signal has been set up to turn on or off too long after the node the SS[] or SE is attached to. Currently, if this signal is set up to turn on or off greater than 100ms after the node, this warning will be posted and the signal will fire 100ms after the node. These are the formulas used to determine when this signal will be turned on or off relative to the node for seal schedule 'n': For SS[n]: Time_Before = ATOMIZING_ON_DELAY + EQUIPMENT_DELAY - GUNON_DELAY For SE[n]: Time_Before = ATOMIZING_OFF_DELAY + EQUIPMENT_DELAY - GUNOFF_DELAY Note that a NEGATIVE Time_Before means AFTER the node.
SEAL-023.remedy: There is no real danger in this condition. You should be aware that if you try to turn this signal on or off after 100ms AFTER the node, the signal will always be fired 100ms after the node and this warning will be posted. To correct this problem, make the atomizing_on/off/_delay or equipment_delay more positive or the gunon/gunoff delay more negative, to move the firing of the signal up earlier.

SEAL-024.cause: The high performance I/O triggering system (Motion Trigger) has returned a bad status. When this occurs, the redundant triggering system will take over, but the quality of the SSs and SEs will be poor. This condition is usually caused by one or more of the following: 1. A Gun On output is assigned to a output point which is nonzero and does not exist. 2. A Start Meter output is assigned to a output point which is nonzero and does not exist. 3. A Atomizing Air output is assigned to a output point which is nonzero and does not exist. 4. There is a problem with the software setup of the I/O system. 5. There is a problem with the hardware setup of the I/O system.
SEAL-024.remedy: Go to the Equipment Output menu and verify that all the Gun on, Start Meter, and Atomizing Air outputs are correctly defined or their indexes are set to zero. If the VALUE of a output port is '****', then the index number must be set to zero and the robot must be cold started. You must cold start the robot after changing anything on this menu.

SEAL-129.cause: The index value of seal start instruction is invalid.
SEAL-129.remedy: Check the index value of this SS instruction.

SEAL-131.cause: This error is caused by timing problems with Sealing commands (SS or SE). Timing problems could occur if the robot does not have enough time to plan for a sealing instruction before the robot passes that point in the path. For example: If the user is using a sealing schedule with a gunon delay of 1000ms and a gunoff delay of -1000ms and the robot executes the seam in 1500ms, the Dispensetool will detect the logic problem and post this fault. A path which has many sealing instructions very close to each other (closer than 30mm at 500mm/sec) is likely to have this problem.
SEAL-131.remedy: Make sure there is adequate time for each SS and SE to execute. You may do this by making sure you have only the minimum number of points in your path that you require. Dispensetool works best with as few points as possible. Also, make sure none of your schedules have gunon, gunoff, or equipment delays beyond that which is needed (usually between -100ms and +100ms is adequate). NOTE: Whenever a SEAL-131 occurs, the robot MUST be cold started to recover.

SEAL-132.cause: There was not enough time between a SS and the next SS or SE for the flow rate computations to be done.
SEAL-132.remedy: Step through your sealing PROCess program, making sure there is at least a centimeter between the points attached to each sealing instruction. Increase the distance between sealing instructions, delete one of the sealing instructions, or slow the robot down.

SEAL-177.cause: The Four Position End of Arm tool was moved, but the FLIP sensor reports that the tool is not in the correct FLIP/UNFLIP position (could be ON or OFF) after the timeout period set on the tool setup menu expired.
SEAL-177.remedy: Check air supply to the four position tool. Check proximity sensors on the four position tool. If the tool is slow, increase the timeout delay on the tool setup screen to allow enough time for the tool to complete motion.

SEAL-178.cause: The Four Position End of Arm tool was moved, but the UNFLIP sensor reports that the tool is not in the correct UNFLIP/FLIP position (could be ON or OFF) after the timeout period set on the tool setup menu expired.
SEAL-178.remedy: Check air supply to the four position tool. Check proximity sensors on the four position tool. If the tool is slow, increase the timeout delay on the tool setup screen to allow enough time for the tool to complete motion.

SEAL-179.cause: The Four Position End of Arm tool was moved, but the EXTEND sensor reports that the tool is not in the correct EXTEND/RETRACT position (could be ON or OFF) after the timeout period set on the tool setup menu expired.
SEAL-179.remedy: Check air supply to the four position tool. Check proximity sensors on the four position tool. If the tool is slow, increase the timeout delay on the tool setup screen to allow enough time for the tool to complete motion.

SEAL-180.cause: The Four Position End of Arm tool was moved, but the RETRACT sensor reports that the tool is not in the correct RETRACT/EXTEND position (could be ON or OFF) after the timeout period set on the tool setup menu expired.
SEAL-180.remedy: Check air supply to the four position tool. Check proximity sensors on the four position tool. If the tool is slow, increase the timeout delay on the tool setup screen to allow enough time for the tool to complete motion.

SEAL-200.cause: The dispensing equipment controller has detected a fault in its hardware.
SEAL-200.remedy: Perform maintenance and debug procedures as described in the dispensing equipment manual.

SEAL-201.cause: A dispensing gun malfunction has been detected by the dispensing controller.
SEAL-201.remedy: Perform dispensing gun maintenance and debug procedures.

SEAL-202.cause: A low pressure condition has been detected by the dispensing controller
SEAL-202.remedy: Check the pressure sensors at all points in the system. Perform standard system debug and maintenance procedures.

SEAL-203.cause: A high pressure condition has been detected in the dispensing gun nozzle. In specific, nozzle pressure signal is greater than (NOZZLE SENSOR RATING/100) * 5 volts for over one second.
SEAL-203.remedy: Reduce system pressure if it is permissible. Select a nozzle pressure transducer with a wider operating range.

SEAL-204.cause: The volume of material dispensed on the previous job was above the preset limit.
SEAL-204.remedy: Verify that the volume limits are correct for the specified job.

SEAL-205.cause: The volume of material dispensed on the previous job was below the preset limit
SEAL-205.remedy: Verify that the volume limits are correct for the specified job.

SEAL-206.cause: A error was detected in the flow meter readings.
SEAL-206.remedy: Verify that the flowmeter is operating correctly.

SEAL-207.cause: An incorrect bead condition was detected.

SEAL-208.cause: Interim value for volume has exceeded maximum interim limit.
SEAL-208.remedy: Re-learn part or increase maximum limit.

SEAL-209.cause: The problem is either the nozzle pressure is greater than setpoint for more than time limit or the upstream hose is ruptured and is leaking material.
SEAL-209.remedy: Use on-board diagnostics on the dispensing controller to verify that the nozzle pressure sensor is in order, replace sensor as required. Check for clog in gun or nozzle tip. If the problem is ruptured hose, replace hose

SEAL-210.cause: Nozzle pressure has dropped below setpoint value for more than time limit.
SEAL-210.remedy: Use on-board diagnostics on the dispenser controller to verify that the nozzle pressure sensor is in order, replace sensor as required.

SEAL-211.cause: Upstream pressure is greater than setpoint for more than time limit.
SEAL-211.remedy: Use on-board diagnostics on the dispenser controller to verify that the upstream pressure sensor is in order, replace sensor as required. Check for clog in gun or nozzle tip

SEAL-212.cause: Upstream pressure has dropped below setpoint value for more than time limit.

SEAL-213.cause: An unknown error code was received from the dispensing controller.

SEAL-214.cause: The dispenser has detected a abnormally low or high material flow rate. This could be caused by a plugged gun.

SEAL-326.cause: Line Tracking is NOT allowed with Dispensing in SpotTool+.
SEAL-326.remedy: Use Select->Detail menu to disable tracking (schedule = 0) to disable Tracking for this program.

SEAL-327.cause: This is only a warning message to indicate that all of the triggers / part detects in the tracking queue have been cleared. There are 4 different causes: 1. The CLRQUE key has been used on the MANUAL FUNCTIONS Line Track menu. 2. The Clear Track Que input on the Cell Inputs menu has been set high. 3. The detect queue was full and another detect was received. In this case a SEAL-330 error will also be posted to indicate that the queue was full. The queue is cleared because an extra trigger was detected so the data in the queue cannot be trusted. 4. A Tracking queue read error was posted.
SEAL-327.remedy: The remedies for the 4 scenarios above are: 1. Do not use CLRQUE key. 2. Do not set Clear Track Que input high. 3. Also see remedy for SEAL-330 error. Since the detect queue was full, this shows one of 2 possibilities: A. The maximum queue size is not sufficient to handle the number of detects needed in the queue. To increase the queue size, set $SPTK_CFG[x].MAX_QUE_SIZE and cycle power on the robot. B. Extra part detects are being sent to the robot and are mistakenly added to the queue. In this case the Part Detect input signal must be debounced by the cell controller. Alternately - a system variable exists which defines the minimum distance that the part / conveyor must travel since the last detect in order to allow a new detect into the queue. This variable is $SPTK_CFG[x].MIN_PD_DIST which defines that distance in mm. The default value is 400.0mm. It can be set to 0 to prevent the minimum distance check from being made. Changes take effect immediately. 4. See remedy for SEAL-332 error.

SEAL-328.cause: If the GET_PART macro is called and there are no triggers in the part detect queue then the macro waits for a valid detect to be placed into the queue. If the time that the robot is waiting for a detect exceeds a specified value then this warning message is generated.
SEAL-328.remedy: The detect wait condition is satisfied once a valid part detect is placed into the queue. If desired, the amount of wait time before this message is posted can be changed by setting the system variable $SPTK_CFG[x].WAIT_MSG_TO in ms. The default value is 3000ms. It can be set to (-)1 to prevent the message from being posted. Changes take effect immediately.

SEAL-329.cause: This is a message to indicate that the distance the part / conveyor has travelled since the previous part detect has not met / exceeded a minimum defined distance. This debounce logic prevents unwanted detects from being added to the part detect queue.
SEAL-329.remedy: Since extra part detects are being sent to the robot, two remedies are: 1. The Part Detect input signal must be debounced by the cell controller. 2. A system variable exists which defines the minimum distance that the part / conveyor must travel since the last detect in order to allow a new detect into the queue. This variable is $SPTK_CFG[x].MIN_PD_DIST which defines that distance in mm. The default value is 400.0mm. It can be set to 0 to prevent the minimum distance check from being made. Changes take effect immediately.

SEAL-330.cause: This message indicates that the part detect queue was full and another detect was received. In this case a SEAL-337 error will also be posted to indicate that the queue was subsequently cleared because an extra trigger was detected - so the data in the queue cannot be trusted.
SEAL-330.remedy: All related programs cannot be resumed and must be aborted. Any jobs being tracked (jobs that have passed the part detect switch/sensor) should be aborted and not be processed. Since the detect queue was full, this shows one of 2 possibilities: 1. The maximum queue size is not sufficient to handle the number of detects needed in the queue. To increase the queue size, set $SPTK_CFG[x].MAX_QUE_SIZE and cycle power on the robot. 2. Extra part detects are being sent to the robot and are mistakenly added to the queue. In this case the Part Detect input signal must be debounced by the cell controller. Alternately - a system variable exists which defines the minimum distance that the part / conveyor must travel since the last detect in order to allow a new detect into the queue. This variable is $SPTK_CFG[x].MIN_PD_DIST which defines that distance in mm. The default value is 400.0mm. It can be set to 0 to prevent the minimum distance check from being made. Changes take effect immediately.

SEAL-331.cause: The Enc Scale Factor in the Tracking Setup menu is not set to a value greater than 0.
SEAL-331.remedy: The tracking encoder should be set up such that the encoder counts are increasing as the conveyor moves in the forward direction. Consequently, the Enc Scale Factor in the Tracking Setup menu should be set to a value that is greater than 0. Cycle power on the robot after setting this value. Note that only tracking schedule #1 is used. All related programs should not be resumed and must be aborted. Any jobs being tracked (jobs that have passed the part detect switch/sensor) should be aborted and not be processed.

SEAL-332.cause: An error was encountered while reading trigger data from the part detect queue. An error will also be posted to indicate the specific queue error encountered. A SEAL-337 error will also be posted to indicate that the queue was subsequently cleared because the data in the queue cannot be trusted.
SEAL-332.remedy: Document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative. All related programs cannot be resumed and must be aborted. Any jobs being tracked (jobs that have passed the part detect switch/sensor) should be aborted and not be processed.

SEAL-333.cause: The trigger that was read from the part detect queue is stale. This indicates that the conveyor has already travelled far beyond the limits where the trigger would be usable.
SEAL-333.remedy: All related programs cannot be resumed and must be aborted. Any jobs being tracked (jobs that have passed the part detect switch/sensor) should be aborted and not be processed. 1. Verify that triggers are being added to and read from the part detect queue correctly as the conveyor moves forward and the job program executes. 2. Verify that no extraneous part detect triggers are being sent to the robot. 3. A system variable exists to limit the distance travelled past robot zero (or rail 0 if equipped) where the part detect trigger is usable. This variable is $SPTK_CFG[x].MAX_PD_DIST which defines that distance in mm. The default value is 8000.0mm. It can be set to a large value to delay when this error is posted. Changes take effect immediately.

SEAL-334.cause: While the conveyor was moving the encoder value passed from the maximum positive integer value the minimum negative integer value (or vice-versa).
SEAL-334.remedy: This is only a warning message and no remedy is needed. All operation should remain as normal.

SEAL-335.cause: The Enc Scale Factor in the Tracking Setup menu is not set to a value of 0.0
SEAL-335.remedy: All related programs cannot be resumed and must be aborted. Any jobs being tracked (jobs that have passed the part detect switch/sensor) should be aborted and not be processed. The tracking encoder should be set up such that the encoder counts are increasing as the conveyor moves in the forward direction. Consequently, the Enc Scale Factor in the Tracking Setup menu should be set to a value that is greater than 0. Cycle power on the robot after setting this value. Note that only tracking schedule #1 is used.

SEAL-336.cause: A check has been made of the current detect value before adding it to the part detect queue. It is compared to the previous detect value in light of the Enc Scale Factor in the Tracking Setup menu to ensure it is sensible. When posted, an additional code is also posted to provide further detail. Causes for codes are as follows: Key: PD = Previous Detect CD = Current Detect +S = Positive Enc Scale Factor -S = Negative Enc Scale Factor ROL = Rollover Ps0 = Passed 0 count Er1: PD>0 CD>0 +S CD<PD Er2: PD>0 CD>0 -S CD>PD Er3: PD<0 CD<0 +S PD>CD Er4: PD<0 CD<0 -S CD<PD Er5: PD>0 CD=0 +S PD>CD Er6: PD=0 CD>0 -S CD>PD Er7: PD<0 CD=0 -S CD>PD Er8: PD=0 CD<0 +S PD>CD Er9: Ps0 PD>0 CD<0 +S PD>CD Er10: ROL PD>0 CD<0 -S PD>CD Er11: Ps0 PD<0 CD>0 -S PD<CD Er12: ROL PD<0 CD>0 +S PD<CD Er98: PD=0 CD=0 PD=CD Er99: unknown error
SEAL-336.remedy: See causes above to determine the specific problem and possible inferred solution. If the problem persists, then the minimum part detect distance check can be disabled as follows: A system variable exists which defines the minimum distance that the part / conveyor must travel since the last detect in order to allow a new detect into the queue. This variable is $SPTK_CFG[x].MIN_PD_DIST which defines that distance in mm. The default value is 400.0mm. It can be set to 0 to prevent the minimum distance check from being made. Changes take effect immediately. Otherwise document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative. All related programs cannot be resumed and must be aborted. Any jobs being tracked (jobs that have passed the part detect switch/sensor) should be aborted and not be processed.

SEAL-343.cause: For the Process logger option, some user configurable system variables have been set up to monitor I/O via $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_INT_ARY[n] or $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_REAL_ARY[n]. The DATA_TYPE or DATA_INDEX fields refer to an invalid I/O point.
SEAL-343.remedy: Set the DATA_TYPE or DATA_INDEX fields to refer to a valid I/O point. If you do not wish to monitor an I/O point then set the ITEM field to a different value or set it to 0 to disable logging that item. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

SEAL-344.cause: For the Process logger option, some user configurable system variables have been set up to monitor a data register via $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_INT_ARY[n] or $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_REAL_ARY[n]. The type of data in that register was found to be invalid.
SEAL-344.remedy: Document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

SEAL-345.cause: For the Process logger option, some user configurable system variables have been set up to monitor a data register via $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_INT_ARY[n] or $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_REAL_ARY[n]. The DATA_INDEX field refers to an invalid data register.
SEAL-345.remedy: Set the DATA_INDEX field to refer to a valid data register. If you do not wish to monitor a data register then set the ITEM field to a different value or set it to 0 to disable logging that item. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

SEAL-346.cause: For the Process logger option, some user configurable system variables have been set up to monitor other system variables via $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_INT_ARY[n] or $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_REAL_ARY[n]. The type of data in that system variable was found to be invalid.
SEAL-346.remedy: Only variables of type INTEGER, REAL, or BOOLEAN are supported. Change the VAR_STRING field to refer to a system variable of one of these types only. If you do not wish to monitor a system variable then set the ITEM field to a different value or set it to 0 to disable logging that item. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

SEAL-347.cause: For the Process logger option, some user configurable system variables have been set up to monitor other system variables via $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_INT_ARY[n] or $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_REAL_ARY[n]. The system variable referred to by the VAR_STRING field is invalid.
SEAL-347.remedy: Change the VAR_STRING field to refer to a valid system variable. If you do not wish to monitor a system variable then set the ITEM field to a different value or set it to 0 to disable logging that item. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

SEAL-348.cause: For the Process logger option, some user configurable system variables have been set up to monitor items via: $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_INT_ARY[n] or $SLSETUP[x].PLSETUP.REC_REAL_ARY[n]. The item type referred to by the ITEM field is invalid.
SEAL-348.remedy: Change the ITEM field to refer to a valid item type. Valid values for ITEM are: 0 for no use 1 for I/O (signed short) 2 for I/O (unsigned short) 3 for Data number register 4 for String for sysvar If you do not wish to monitor an item then set the ITEM field to 0 to disable logging that item. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

SEAL-349.cause: For the Process logger option, when a program is executed (planned) a process_id # is assigned to the TP program line containing a SE statement. This unique identifier will be set to the position number or, if it is a standalone SE statement without motion then it will be set equal to the program line number. When the SE statement is executed a matching process_id must be found. In this case, no matching process_id was found.
SEAL-349.remedy: Document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

SEAL-350.cause: This is an internal error for the Process logger option.
SEAL-350.remedy: Record the error string parameters. Document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual for further information.

SEAL-359.cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to an operator panel emergency stop.
SEAL-359.remedy: Clear the operator panel emergency stop and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

SEAL-360.cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to a teach pendant emergency stop.
SEAL-360.remedy: Clear the teach pendant emergency stop and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

SEAL-361.cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to a servo disconnect input.
SEAL-361.remedy: Reset the servo disconnect and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

SEAL-362.cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to a Non Teacher Enabling Device (NTED) input.
SEAL-362.remedy: Reset the Non Teacher Enabling Device (NTED) and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

SEAL-363.cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to the deadman switch being released while the teach pendant is enabled.
SEAL-363.remedy: Press the deadman switch and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

SEAL-364.cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to the fence input.
SEAL-364.remedy: Reset the fence input and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

SEAL-365.cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to the hand broken input.
SEAL-365.remedy: Reset the hand broken input and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

SEAL-366.cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to an external emergency stop.
SEAL-366.remedy: Clear the external emergency stop and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

SEAL-367.cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to the user operator panel (UOP) IMSTP signal.
SEAL-367.remedy: Reset the user operator panel (UOP) IMSTP input and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

SEAL-368.cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to the controller being faulted.
SEAL-368.remedy: Clear the cause of the fault and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

SEAL-369.cause: Outputs and / or parameters associated with the dispensing equipment number indicated have been shut off due to the controller being held.
SEAL-369.remedy: Clear the cause of the hold condition and reset the robot. Also refer to the alarm history for any other errors that may be present. Please refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual STOP SIGNAL STATUS section for further information.

SEAL-370.cause: Data Monitor subsystem has been disabled, by user choice or automatically because limit on data files set by the user has been reached
SEAL-370.remedy: Enable Data Monitor Operation from the Utilities- Data Monitor screen. On Setup-Diagnostics screen, consider increasing Max Data Files Stored or setting Disable After Max Files to NO, if these settings caused Data Monitor to to be disabled. See SpotTool+ Setup and Operations Manual Advanced Functions for more information.

SEAL-371.cause: The limit on data files that may be stored by the Data Monitor subsystem has been reached.
SEAL-371.remedy: On Setup-Diagnostics screen, consider increasing Max Data Files Stored or setting Disable After Max Files to NO. See SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual (Advanced Functions) for more information on these items.

SEAL-372.cause: Data Monitor session is in progress and user tried to change setup that could affect the current session.
SEAL-372.remedy: Wait till the end of Data Monitor session. If in Automatic Sampling mode, this happens at job end. If sampling in Asynchronous mode, set SAMPLE NOW, under Setup-Diagnostics to STOP, to stop current session.

SEAL-373.cause: Asynchronous Data Monitoring has been disabled
SEAL-373.remedy: To re-enable, ensure that Utilities-Data Monitor-Data Monitor Operation is enabled. Set Setup-Diagnostics-Auto Sample Each Job to NO.

SEAL-374.cause: Asynchronous Data Monitor has been enabled.

SEAL-375.cause: File management features have been disabled because user set Setup-Diagnostics-Max Data Files Stored to 0. Stored data will be over-written by subsequent sampling sessions.
SEAL-375.remedy: No action required. To re-enable, you may set Max Data Files to non-zero value Ensure that destination data storage device has adequate space. See SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual (Advanced Functions)

SEAL-376.cause: File management features have been enabled because user set Setup-Diagnostics-Max Data Files Stored value. Data Monitor will store as many old data files as indicated.
SEAL-376.remedy: No action required if destination data storage device has adequate space. To disable, set value to 0. See SpotTool+ Setup and Operations manual (Advanced Functions) for more information.

SEAL-377.cause: Karel builtin SAMPLE_START returned a bad status.

SEAL-378.cause: Karel builtin SAMPLE_END returned a bad status.

SEAL-379.remedy: Ensure that these items on the Dispense Diagnostics Setup menu are set correctly: Auto sample each job: Asynch. start enable:

SEAL-380.cause: Dispense Diagnostics encountered an error while processing the sldiagdb.dt to set up the option.
SEAL-380.remedy: If sldiagdb.dt has been modified, then verify that it has been created and loaded correctly. Refer to FR:DGERRORS.LS for a summary of any errors encountered during processing. Refer to FR:DIAGVARS.LS for a summary of the settings that have been successfully made.

SEAL-381.cause: Dispense Diagnostics encountered NO errors while processing the sldiagdb.dt to set up the option.

SEAL-382.cause: Dispense Diagnostics encountered an error while attempting to copy the output DT file to rd:diag.dt.
SEAL-382.remedy: Refer to cause code on this alarm for failure reason. If -File not found- is also posted then please set Max data files stored to zero on the Dispense Diagnostics menu and try again. If -Device is full- is also posted then the RAM Disk free area is too small to accommodate the file. You may also try to power down the controller to clear out memory in the RAM Disk and try again. If this does not work then $FILE_MAXSEC may need to be changed to increase the RAM disk size. Refer to the SpotTool+ Setup and Operations Manual for help. If you do not wish to have the diag.dt file copied to the RAM Disk following every monitoring session then set the following variable: [SLVRPADG]copy_dt = FALSE.

SENC-001.cause: Difference between joint command and secondary joint angle exceeded tolerance
SENC-001.remedy: Check that secondary encoder reading is correct. Reduce speed. If alarm persists, report this issue

SENC-004.cause: Fail to enter accuracy mode. Robot is moving, or difference between primary and secondary encoders angles exceed tolerance
SENC-004.remedy: Enter accuracy mode only when robot is not moving. If robot is already stationary, check secondary encoder calibration

SENC-007.cause: difference between primary and secondary encoders angles exceed tolerance
SENC-007.remedy: exit accuracy mode and check secondary encoder calibration

SENC-008.cause: Fail to exit accuracy mode. Robot is moving
SENC-008.remedy: Exit accuracy mode only when robot is not moving

SENS-001.cause: During data reception, parity, overrun and framing errors occurred.
SENS-001.remedy: Check that the communication setting between the robot and sensor sides is not wrong.

SENS-002.cause: An attempt was made for data transmission, but DSR signal at the sensor side is in OFF-state.
SENS-002.remedy: Check that the specification and desconnection of cable connecting the robot and sensor.

SENS-003.cause: The undefined TCC was received from the sensor.
SENS-003.remedy: Check the data sent from the sensor.

SENS-004.cause: BCC of thereceived data from the sensor is wrong.
SENS-004.remedy: Check the data sent from the sensor.

SENS-005.cause: The format of the received data is wrong.
SENS-005.remedy: Check the data sent from the sensor.

SENS-006.cause: The answer from the sensor is not received within the allowable time.
SENS-006.remedy: Check that the sensor side does not stop due to an error, for example.

SENS-007.cause: The interval of characters sent from the sensor exceeded the allowable time.
SENS-007.remedy: Check that the sensor side does not stop due to an error, for example.

SENS-008.remedy: Check the compensation data sent from the sensor.

SHAP-000.message: KW ovrd reg. is out of range.
SHAP-000.cause: The value of Kerf Width is not in a valid range.
SHAP-000.remedy: Set the kerf width in a range of 0 to 4.99. If a range > 4.99 is needed, use the KWMINMAX.TP program.

SHAP-001.message: Speed ovrd reg. out of range.
SHAP-001.cause: The value in the register for TRAVEL SPEED override is not in a valid range.
SHAP-001.remedy: Set the travel speed in the speed override register to a value less than 2000.

SHAP-002.cause: The registers for each shape function such as kerf width override, speed override, and so forth in the Shape Setup menu must be unique. If you try to use the same register twice, this error will occur.
SHAP-002.remedy: Insure that each register is not used more than one time.

SHAP-003.cause: The scheduled corner radius is larger than the computed working radius of the scheduled diameter.
SHAP-003.remedy: Reduce the scheduled corner radius or increase the scheduled diameter.

SHAP-004.message: Slot Len. must be > than wid.
SHAP-004.cause: The scheduled width for the slot is larger than the scheduled length for the slot.
SHAP-004.remedy: Make the slot width smaller than the length or make the slot length larger than the width

SHAP-005.cause: The Shape Template FOR A CUT MACRO (ex: CUT_CIR.TP) has been modified and is no longer valid for this operation.
SHAP-005.remedy: Undo the modifications if you can or if you have a back up copy of this shape macro, reload it.

SHAP-006.cause: The passed in schedule number for the shape in the teach pendant program is out of range.
SHAP-006.remedy: Set the value in the range of 1 to 100.

SHAP-007.cause: The shape program requested could not be opened or the shape cut program was modified and an expected line is missing.
SHAP-007.remedy: The shape program might have been deleted. If you have a back up copy of this shape macro, reload it.

SHAP-008.cause: Could not update the shape macro with values in the shape schedule.
SHAP-008.remedy: If you have a back up copy of this shape macro, reload it.

SHAP-009.cause: The blend-in distance is too large for the specified shape.

SHAP-010.cause: The length for the key shape must be larger than Major diameter of the key shape.
SHAP-010.remedy: Increase the length of the key shape or decrease the size of the major diameter.

SHAP-011.message: Maj dia must be > Min dia.
SHAP-011.cause: The key shape major diameter, must be larger than the key shape minor diameter.
SHAP-011.remedy: Increase the size of the key shape major diameter or decrease the size of the key shape minor diameter.

SHAP-012.message: Program name must be set first.
SHAP-012.cause: The shape shift utility was executed without the name of the program entered correctly.
SHAP-012.remedy: Select a valid program for the shift function.

SHAP-013.message: Position num must be set first.
SHAP-013.cause: The shape shift utility was executed without the position number entered correctly.
SHAP-013.remedy: Select a valid position for the shift function.

SHAP-014.cause: Program name column was modified or position num column was modified.

SHAP-016.cause: The selected position does not exist in the selected program.
SHAP-016.remedy: Verify that you have the correct program selected and verify the position number is correct.

SHAP-017.cause: The position type of the position register being used, has been changed to joint representation.
SHAP-017.remedy: Change the position type back to Cartesian.

SHAP-021.cause: The center position for the Custom shape, has not been taught in the 'Center Position' position register.
SHAP-021.remedy: Record the center position for the custom shape in the position register.

SHAP-022.cause: The Custom Shape cut program has joint motions which are not allowed.
SHAP-022.remedy: Change the joint move to a linear move.

SHAP-031.cause: The macro table was not set correctly.
SHAP-031.remedy: The controller will try to set up the macro table again at the next Controlled start. It is possible that the macro table needed to be expanded and that can only be done by restarting the controller in Controlled start mode.

SHAP-040.message: Program is not of circular type
SHAP-040.cause: The program is not of a circular type. The program is either a non-shape generated program or the program is of a shape other than circular.
SHAP-040.remedy: Select a program that was generated as a circular type.

SHAP-041.message: Program is not of slot type
SHAP-041.cause: The program is not of a slot type. The program is either a non-shape generated program or the program is of a shape other than slot.
SHAP-041.remedy: Select a program that was generated as a slot type.

SHAP-042.message: Program is not of hexagon type
SHAP-042.cause: Program is not of hexagon type. The program is either a non-shape generated program or the program is of a shape other than hexagon.
SHAP-042.remedy: Select a program that was generated as a hexagon type.

SHAP-043.message: Program is not of rectangle type
SHAP-043.cause: The program is not of a rectangle type. The program is either a non-shape generated program or the program is of a shape other than a rectangle.
SHAP-043.remedy: Select a program that was generated as a rectangle type.

SHAP-044.message: Program is not of key type
SHAP-044.cause: The program is not of a key type. The program is either a non-shape generated program or the program is of a shape other than a key.
SHAP-044.remedy: Select a program that was generated as a key type.

SHAP-045.message: Program is not of pommel type
SHAP-045.cause: the program is not of a pommel type. The program is either a non-shape generated program or the program is of a shape other than pommel.
SHAP-045.remedy: Select a program that was generated as a pommel type.

SHAP-046.message: Program is not of custom type
SHAP-046.cause: The program is not of a custom type. The program is either a non-shape generated program or the program is of a shape other than custom.
SHAP-046.remedy: Select a program that was generated as a custom type.

SHAP-047.cause: The diameter must be > 0. The value for the diameter is 0 and a shape can not be generated with this setting.

SHAP-048.cause: The diameter must be > kerf width (KW). The diameter is smaller than the current kerf width and this size of shape can not be done.
SHAP-048.remedy: Set the value larger than the kerf width.

SHAP-049.cause: The length must be > 0. The value for length is 0 and a shape can not be generated with this setting.

SHAP-050.cause: The width must be > 0. The value for width is 0 and a shape can not be generated with this setting.

SHAP-051.cause: The width must be > kerf width (KW) The width is smaller than the current kerf width and this size of shape can not be done.
SHAP-051.remedy: Set the value larger than the kerf width.

SHAP-052.cause: NumPts must be a multiple of 2. In order for the proper number of circular points to be generated, this value needs to be in multiples of 2.
SHAP-052.remedy: Set the numbers of points to be in multiples of 2.

SHAP-053.cause: Easy Normal is not loaded. The optional Easy Normal feature, is not loaded on this system.
SHAP-053.remedy: Load the optional Easy Normal feature.

SHAP-054.cause: The program is write protected. The program selected is write protected and can not be used.
SHAP-054.remedy: Turn off protection if you want to use this program.

SHAP-055.cause: Not supported for custom. Move to the center position is not supported for a custom shape.
SHAP-055.remedy: Go to the created program and use step mode to get to the first position.

SHAP-056.message: The motion system is not ready
SHAP-056.cause: The motion system is not ready. To test the program, the motion system must be reset and ready to run.
SHAP-056.remedy: Reset the motion system so that the program can be executed.

SHAP-057.message: Edge distance must be < diameter/2 + KW
SHAP-057.cause: Edge distance must be < diameter/2 + kerf width (KW). The edge distance is larger than the diameter of the circle divided by 2 plus the kerf width.
SHAP-057.remedy: Make sure the edge distance does not exceed the diameter/2 + kerf width (KW).

SHAP-058.cause: Single step is not support for test mode.
SHAP-058.remedy: Turn off single step or go to program SELECT and select your program for normal execution with single step on.

SHAP-059.cause: Multi-grp prog not supported Multi-group template programs are not supported
SHAP-059.remedy: Create a new template with only one group mask or perform a Group Mask Exchange on the existing program.

SHAP-060.cause: Robot does not have kinematics. ShapeGen cannot be used.
SHAP-060.remedy: A different robot must be used.

SHAP-061.cause: Motion lines in template exceed limit Max allowed: 64 lines
SHAP-061.remedy: Reduce the motion line in ShapeGen template.

SHAP-062.cause: Position Register does not support in custom shape.

SPOT-001.cause: BU=* was specified in the SPOT instruction for backup state before the weld, but the backup was opened at the time the instruction was executed.
SPOT-001.remedy: Make sure that the backup is closed when using the BU=* command. Edit the BU=* to BU=C, or insert a BACKUP=CLOSE statement prior to this statement.

SPOT-002.cause: The isolation contactor on the specified weld controller is in a fault condition.
