If no program is running, then this message is posted if either the Iso contactor output is high or the Iso contactor input is high. If a program is running, or a manual weld is being executed, then the output, if defined, must be high, and the input, if defined, must be high too.
SPOT-002.remedy: Make sure that the CLOSE CONTACTOR macro instruction has been programmed in the teach pendant program.

SPOT-003.cause: The water saver input is low.
SPOT-003.remedy: Check the input from the weld controller, and reset as necessary.

SPOT-004.cause: The water flow OK input is low.
SPOT-004.remedy: Check the input from the weld controller, and reset as necessary.

SPOT-005.cause: The transformer OK input is low.
SPOT-005.remedy: Check the input from the weld controller, and reset as necessary.

SPOT-006.cause: The weld enable status from the weld controller does not match the robot's weld enable status.
SPOT-006.remedy: Check the robot's weld enable status on the SOFT PANEL/Appli. menu and compare it to the weld controller's weld enable status. These must be the same.

SPOT-007.cause: The robot timed out waiting for the Weld in Process input from the weld controller.
SPOT-007.remedy: Check the Weld I/O menu, as well as all wiring. If the input is going high, try increasing the timeout by setting $spoteqsetup[].$wld_inpr_to to a bigger number. The default is 2000 ms, or 2 seconds.

SPOT-008.cause: The robot timed out waiting for the Weld Complete input from the weld controller.
SPOT-008.remedy: Check the Weld I/O menu, as well as all wiring. If the input is going high, try increasing the timeout by setting $spoteqsetup[].$wld_comp_to to a bigger number. The default is 2000 ms, or 2 seconds.

SPOT-009.cause: The Weld Complete input was detected before the Weld in Process input was received.
SPOT-009.remedy: Check the length of the weld controller's Weld Complete output. It may need to be decreased.

SPOT-010.remedy: Check the weld controller for the reason for this alarm. Reset the fault, then chose Skip/Retry option to continue the program.

SPOT-011.remedy: Check the weld controller for the reason for this alarm.

SPOT-012.cause: An inavlid weld schedule was programmed in the teach pendant program.
SPOT-012.remedy: Check the S= value of the current line of the teach pendant program. The smallest schedule number allowed is 0. For digital weld controllers, the the largest schedule number allowed depends on the width of the Weld Schedule group output. If this GOUT is 4 I/O points wide, then the maximum schedule is 15. If the GOUT is 5 I/O points wide, then the maximum scheudule is 31. For serial weld controllers, the maximum schedule is 32. Re-program the S= value in the teach pendant program.

SPOT-013.cause: A P=* was encountered in the teach pendant program, but no previous pressure value has been used.
SPOT-013.remedy: Be sure to include a direct pressure value instead of using the *.

SPOT-014.cause: The robot timed out waiting for the backup gun to close.
SPOT-014.remedy: Check the Equipment I/O menu, as well as all wiring. If the input is going high, try increasing the timeout by setting $spoteqsetup[].$bu_cl_to to to a bigger number. The default is 2000 ms, or 2 seconds.

SPOT-015.cause: The robot timed out waiting for the gun to close.
SPOT-015.remedy: Check the Equipment I/O menu, as well as all wiring. If the input is going high, try increasing the timeout by setting $spoteqsetup[].$gun_cl_to to to a bigger number. The default is 2000 ms, or 2 seconds.

SPOT-016.cause: The robot timed out waiting for the backup gun to open.
SPOT-016.remedy: Check the Equipment I/O menu, as well as all wiring. If the input is going high, try increasing the timeout by setting $spoteqsetup[].$bu_op_to to to a bigger number. The default is 2000 ms, or 2 seconds.

SPOT-017.cause: The robot timed out waiting for the gun to open.
SPOT-017.remedy: Check the Equipment I/O menu, as well as all wiring. If the input is going high, try increasing the timeout by setting $spoteqsetup[].$bu_cl_to (gun open = backup close) to to a bigger number. The default is 2000 ms, or 2 seconds.

SPOT-018.cause: A serial communications error was detected.
SPOT-018.remedy: Ensure that all cables to the serial port are properly connected, and that the weld controller is powered on. The error code that is appended to this error message is the status of attempted read/write operation.

SPOT-019.cause: A timeout occured while polling the serial weld controller for status information.
SPOT-019.remedy: Ensure that all cables to the serial port are properly connected, and that the weld controller is powered on. Retry the command.

SPOT-020.cause: The robot has been jogged away from the position where the teach pendant was enabled.
SPOT-020.remedy: Move the robot back to the position where the teach pendant was enabled, abort the program, or continue (in linear motion) from position where the robot is currently positioned.

SPOT-021.message: GUN CLOSE DETECT input is on %s
SPOT-021.cause: The GUN CLOSE DETECT input is high at the same time that the GUN OPEN DETECT input is to be checked.
SPOT-021.remedy: Check the sensors to verify that the inputs are being properly turned on and off.

SPOT-022.message: GUN OPEN DETECT input is on %s
SPOT-022.cause: The GUN OPEN DETECT input is high at the same time that the GUN CLOSE DETECT input is to be checked.
SPOT-022.remedy: Check the sensors to verify that the inputs are being properly turned on and off.

SPOT-023.cause: The BU CLOSE DETECT input is high at the same time that the BU OPEN DETECT input is to be checked.
SPOT-023.remedy: Check the sensors to verify that the inputs are being properly turned on and off.

SPOT-024.cause: The BU OPEN DETECT input is high at the same time that the BU CLOSE DETECT input is to be checked.
SPOT-024.remedy: Check the sensors to verify that the inputs are being properly turned on and off.

SPOT-025.cause: An invalid binary valve pressure was programmed in the teach pendant program.
SPOT-025.remedy: Check the P= value of the current line of the teach pendant program. The smallest valve pressure allowed is 0. For digital weld controllers, the largest pressure number allowed depends on the width of the Valve Pressure group output. If this GOUT is 4 I/O points wide, then the maximum pressure is 15. If the GOUT is 5 I/O points wide, then the maximum pressure is 31. For serial weld controllers, the maximum pressure is 15. Re-program the P= value in the teach pendant program.

SPOT-026.cause: The robot timed out waiting for the weld controller to reset a major fault.
SPOT-026.remedy: Check the weld controller for the reason for this alarm. Reset the fault, then chose Skip/Retry option to continue the program.

SPOT-027.cause: A system failure has caused internal synchronization problems.

SPOT-028.remedy: Make sure that the port exists

SPOT-029.cause: Incorrect options loaded for serial weld control
SPOT-029.remedy: Make sure serial options properly loaded.

SPOT-030.cause: The specified gun contactor is in a fault condition. If a program is running, or a manual weld is being executed, then the output, if defined, must be high, and the input, if defined, must be high too.
SPOT-030.remedy: Make sure that the correct macro instruction has been programmed in the teach pendant program.

SPOT-031.cause: This error is only posted for set/reset type guns. The shot pin was not set correctly, so the gun could not be opened.
SPOT-031.remedy: Check the setting of the shot pin. Make sure the shot pin has been made before attempting to close the gun.

SPOT-032.cause: The Gun Close Detect input was not received within the specified timeout period.
SPOT-032.remedy: Verify the input is assigned correctly; verify the input is being made when the gun is closed; or if needed, increase the timeout value (in $spoteqsetup.$gun_cl_to).

SPOT-033.cause: The BU Open Detect input was not received within the specified timeout period.
SPOT-033.remedy: Verify the input is assigned correctly; verify the input is being made when the backup gun is opened; or if needed, increase the timeout value (in $spoteqsetup.$bu_op_to).

SPOT-034.cause: The BU Close Detect input was not received within the specified timeout period.
SPOT-034.remedy: Verify the input is assigned correctly; verify the input is being made when the backup gun is closed; or if needed, increase the timeout value (in $spoteqsetup.$bu_cl_to).

SPOT-035.cause: An invalid equipment number was specified.
SPOT-035.remedy: The current number of equipments that the system is configured for is displayed in the error message. Only use the value one up to and including the number posted on the error line. If you need to increase the number of equipment, then perform an INIT start (backup all files first), and enter the new number of equipment when prompted during the SETUP APPLICATION menu.

SPOT-036.cause: An invalid weld controller number was specified.
SPOT-036.remedy: The current number of weld controllers that the system is configured for is displayed in the error message. Only use the value one up to and including the number posted on the error line. If you need to increase the number of weld controllers, then perform a controlled start, and define the new number of weld controllers when prompted during the SETUP APPLICATION menu.

SPOT-037.cause: The GUN CONTACTOR TPE instruction was programmed, but no gun contactors are defined.
SPOT-037.remedy: Gun contactors are defined at controlled start, from the SETUP APPLICATION option under the FCTN key. If extra gun contactors are defined at controlled start, then the Equipment I/O menu will allow you to define the I/O for the gun contactor.

SPOT-038.cause: The stud low detect prox switch in the feed hopper for the current Power unit has indicated that the hopper needs more studs.
SPOT-038.remedy: Refill the hopper, or, if it is not low, check the function of the prox.

SPOT-039.cause: The welder power unit air pressure detect switch has indicated that the system air has fallen below the minimum operating level of 85 psi.

SPOT-040.cause: The Ready Relay for the current stud welding power unit is off. This is caused by the unit having a fault that has not been reset.

SPOT-041.cause: A TPE instruction was programmed to use a tool change equipment, but that tool was not attached to the arm.
SPOT-041.remedy: Make sure that the proper tool is attached to the arm before attempting to use it. Tool changes are done with TPE macros. Make sure that a call to the correct macro is made before attempting the SPOT or BACKUP operation.

SPOT-042.cause: The robot detected a Stud Welder Time Out Fault from the current controller during a weld. This fault occurrs when the controller does not detect a completed weld or a bad weld after the timer times out. Usually means that the stud is welded to both the target and the gun.
SPOT-042.remedy: Once the robot is paused, carefully pry the gun and the stud apart, then reset fault on weld controller and resume the program.

SPOT-043.cause: The Stud Weld controller has signaled the robot that a weld fault has occured. This indicates that insuficient current was passed during the weld, genererally resulting in a poor quality weld.
SPOT-043.remedy: The stud checker will automaticly verify the quality of the weld. If bad, check the position of the gun at the weld spot. Also check the schedule settings.

SPOT-044.cause: This fault is signaled by the Stud Weld controller if the voltage sensor reports too little arc voltage during the weld process. May result in a poor quality weld.
SPOT-044.remedy: The stud checker will automaticly verify the quality of the weld. If bad, check the position of the gun at the weld spot to insure that the tip is the correct distance.

SPOT-045.cause: The robot did not see the current sensor input go high throughout the weld, indicating no current
SPOT-045.remedy: Check the weld controler to verify that the schedule does include a heat setting. If so, verify operation of sensor

SPOT-046.cause: The Auto Retry Weld feature encountered a weld fault and retried the weld the indicated number of times. This warning is posted for every. SPOT instruction encountered in which the weld was retried at least once.
SPOT-046.remedy: This is just a warning to let the operator know that a weld was retried, and to alert the operator that weld controller maintenance may be required.

SPOT-047.cause: A Collision Detection Alarm has been detected. The robot may have collided with an object, or a Tip Stick may have occurred.
SPOT-047.remedy: Carefully jog the robot away from interfering objects, or free the weld gun from the Tip Stick.

SPOT-048.cause: No register has been defined for use with the Collision Guard Update macro.
SPOT-048.remedy: Use the Collision Guard SETUP screen to define a register for use with the macro.

SPOT-049.cause: The data contained in the Collision Guard macro register is not an integer or is not in the range of 1 to 200.
SPOT-049.remedy: Enter the correct data into the Collision Guard macro register.

SPOT-050.cause: An inavlid binary equalization pressure was programmed in the teach pendant program.
SPOT-050.remedy: Check the EP= value of the current line of the teach pendant program. The smallest valve pressure allowed is 0. For digital weld controllers, the largest pressure number allowed depends on the width of the Equalization Pressure group output. If this GOUT is 4 I/O points wide, then the maximum pressure is 15. If the GOUT is 5 I/O points wide, then the maximum pressure is 31. For serial weld controllers, the maximum pressure is 15. Re-program the EP= value in the teach pendant program.

SPOT-051.cause: A EP=* was encountered in the teach pendant program, but no previous pressure value has been used.
SPOT-051.remedy: Be sure to include a direct equalization pressure value instead of using the *.

SPOT-052.cause: A faulty stud weld has occurred. A pressure value has been used.
SPOT-052.remedy: Select the appropriate type of recover by pressing F4 [CHOICE].

SPOT-053.cause: The stud feeder for gun 1 is low on studs.
SPOT-053.remedy: Add more studs to the feeder for gun 1 at an appropriate time.

SPOT-054.cause: The stud feeder for gun 2 is low on studs.
SPOT-054.remedy: Add more studs to the feeder for gun 2 at an appropriate time.

SPOT-055.cause: A weld controller fault has occured on gun 1.
SPOT-055.remedy: Check the stud welding controller for the reason for this fault. Reset the fault, then choose the appropiate type of fault recovery.

SPOT-056.cause: Studwelding gun 1 has not been retracted.
SPOT-056.remedy: Press SHIFT-GUN which will return the studwelding gun to its retracted position. Reset the fault, then choose the appropriate type of fault recovery.

SPOT-057.cause: Studwelding gun2 has not been retracted.
SPOT-057.remedy: Press SHIFT-GUN which will return the studwelding gun to its retracted position. Reset the fault, then choose the appropiate type of fault recovery.

SPOT-058.cause: The studwelding controller detected that the air pressure has fallen below the minimum operating level of 85 psi.

SPOT-059.cause: A weld controller fault has occurred on gun 2.
SPOT-059.remedy: Check the stud welding controller for the reason for this fault. Reset the fault, then choose the appropiate type of fault recovery.

SPOT-061.cause: The robot controller could not communicate to the timer card to obtain information from the weld controller.
SPOT-061.remedy: Please retry function again. If conditions persists, please cycle power and try again.

SPOT-063.cause: A weld fault has happened on the weld controller.
SPOT-063.remedy: Please refer to manual for weld controller for detailed info on the fault.

SPOT-064.cause: A weld alert has happened on the weld controller.
SPOT-064.remedy: Please refer to manual for weld controller for detailed info on the alert.

SPOT-065.cause: A weld event has happened on the weld controller.
SPOT-065.remedy: This is logging information only. No remedy is required.

SPOT-066.cause: Unable to perform operation due to IWC status.
SPOT-066.remedy: Please see specific IWC error status and follow that remedy.

SPOT-067.message: No Shunt Trip output for WC:%s
SPOT-067.cause: The Shunt Trip output has not been defined.
SPOT-067.remedy: Please define a DO[] for the Shunt Trip.

SPOT-068.cause: The weld done input has not been mapped.

SPOT-069.cause: The maintenance input from the studwelder is on.
SPOT-069.remedy: Please check the studwelder for the cause of this input.

SPOT-070.remedy: Document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC technical representative.

SPOT-071.cause: The number of bits required for the equalization pressure condition is larger than the width of the group output for equalization pressure.
SPOT-071.remedy: Reduce the equalization pressure condition or increase the dimension of the group output.

SPOT-072.cause: The I/O assignment (mapping) for the equalization pressure output is invalid OR the output is offline.
SPOT-072.remedy: Map the I/O properly or put the I/O back online.

SPOT-073.cause: The dresser did not achieve the requested dress speed in time.
SPOT-073.remedy: Check the dresser for mechanical issues.

SPOT-074.message: Tdress sched speed exceeds dresser speed.
SPOT-074.cause: The speed specified in the dresser schedule exceeds the speed limit of the dresser.
SPOT-074.remedy: Reduce the dresser speed in the dresser schedule.

SPOT-075.cause: The number of cuts the dresser has done has exceeded the cutter limit for the dresser.
SPOT-075.remedy: Change the cutter blade and reset the cutter count.

SPOT-076.message: Max tip dresses on Gun #%d exceeded.
SPOT-076.cause: The number of dresses on the tips has exceeded the dress limit for the tips.
SPOT-076.remedy: Change the caps and reset the dress count.

SPOT-077.cause: The minimum torque required for dress determination was not acheived.
SPOT-077.remedy: Verify teach position of gun, and force in TIPDRESS is correct.

SPOT-078.cause: The maximum torque required for valid dress determination was not exceeded.
SPOT-078.remedy: Verify teach position of gun, and force in TIPDRESS is correct.

SPOT-079.cause: The Tip Dress schedule specified in the TIPDRESS instruction was greater than the number of available tip dress schedules.
SPOT-079.remedy: Edit the TIPDRESS instruction and verify the schedule value does not exceed $SGTDCFG.$NUM_SCHED.

SPOT-080.cause: The process axis number for the dresser for the current gun is invalide.
SPOT-080.remedy: Verify that $sgtdset[dresser_number].$axis_num is greater than 0 and less than $sgtdcfg.$num_dresrs.

SPOT-081.cause: The free spinning torque of the dresser has exceeded the user specified maximum.
SPOT-081.remedy: Verify operation of the dresser. This alarm could mean that there is an issue with the dressers gearbox.

SPOT-082.cause: The Weld In process input was detected before the Weld was initiated.
SPOT-082.remedy: Check the weld controller to make sure the weld inprocess input is turning off from the previous weld.

SPOT-083.cause: 1. Gun tips may have hit dresser blade earlier than expected. 2. Gun or dresser may be out-of-position slightly. 3. Tips may be out of alignment.
SPOT-083.remedy: 1.Re-teach the tip dressing position or adjust dresser position 2.Confirm part thickness value and gun zero position are correct 3.Increase early detection position tolerance ($sgtdset[x].$cntct_tol, default=3)

SPOT-084.cause: The dresser number specified does not exist.
SPOT-084.remedy: Verify that the dresser number specified is greater than 0 and less than $sgtdcfg.$num_dresrs.

SPOT-085.message: Speed to low during dress. Check for motor stalling.
SPOT-085.cause: The dresser motor speed was too low during phase 1 of the dress.
SPOT-085.remedy: Verify that the dressing pressure schedule is correct and not too high. If the dressing pressure is too high, it can stall the dressing motor.

SPOT-086.cause: Line Tracking is NOT allowed with Spotwelding.
SPOT-086.remedy: Use Select->Detail menu to disable tracking (schedule = 0) to disable Tracking for this program.

SPOT-087.cause: Tip dress schedule is configured to use weld controller controlled end of dress and send schedule to weld controller is not enabled.
SPOT-087.remedy: Enable send schedule to weld controller for the dresser in use or use a different end of dress method (Time/Revs) for this schedule.

SPOT-091.cause: A weld alarm or warning has happened on the weld controller.
SPOT-091.remedy: Please refer to manual for weld controller for detailed info on the fault or warning.

SPOT-270.cause: Internal error: equipment number is invalid.
SPOT-270.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC technical service representative.

SPOT-271.cause: Internal error: gun index is invalid.
SPOT-271.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC technical service representative.

SPOT-272.cause: Internal error: PX index is invalid.
SPOT-272.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC technical service representative.

SPOT-273.cause: Internal error: Pressure profile state is invalid.
SPOT-273.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC technical service representative.

SPOT-274.cause: Internal error: application status is inconsistent with task status. Application detected an error, but task did not pause.
SPOT-274.remedy: Record number at end of alarm message, and call Fanuc service center.

SPOT-306.cause: At least two of the models contained the same Model ID.
SPOT-306.remedy: 1. Review the vision results using either the Runtime screen or Vision Setup screen. 2. Adjust the Vision Process as necessary.

SPOT-307.cause: The Gun Tip base or tip model was not found by vision.
SPOT-307.remedy: 1. Verify that the enclosure LED is operational 2. Verify that the correct caps are on the weld gun 3. Adjust the Vision Process as necessary

SPOT-308.cause: The Robot Tip base or tip model was not found by vision.
SPOT-308.remedy: 1. Verify that the enclosure LED is operational 2. Verify that the correct caps are on the weld gun 3. Adjust the Vision Process as necessary

SPOT-309.cause: One or more of the four models required to make an alignment check was missing.
SPOT-309.remedy: 1. Verify that the enclosure LED is operational 2. Verify that the correct caps are on the weld gun 3. Adjust the Vision Process as necessary

SPOT-310.cause: The Gun tip wear exceeded the user set threshold
SPOT-310.remedy: 1. Change Cap and reset nominal condition 2. Verify user set threshold

SPOT-311.cause: The Gun Tip tip model displacement exceeded the user set threshold
SPOT-311.remedy: 1. Review the vision results using either the Runtime screen or Vision Setup screen 2. Verify the user set threshold 3. Adjust the Vision Process or equipment as necessary

SPOT-312.cause: The Gun Tip base model displacement exceeded the user set threshold
SPOT-312.remedy: 1. Review the vision results using either the Runtime screen or Vision Setup screen 2. Verify the user set threshold 3. Adjust the Vision Process or equipment as necessary

SPOT-313.cause: Gun Cap Base Location has moved too far from nominal position.
SPOT-313.remedy: Gun Shank may have slipped or tool bent.

SPOT-314.cause: The Robot tip wear exceeded the user set threshold
SPOT-314.remedy: 1. Change Cap and reset nominal condition 2. Verify user set threshold

SPOT-315.cause: The Robot Tip tip model displacement exceeded the user set threshold
SPOT-315.remedy: 1. Review the vision results using either the Runtime screen or Vision Setup screen. 2. Verify the user set threshold 3. Adjust the Vision Process or equipment as necessary

SPOT-316.cause: The Robot Tip base model displacement exceeded the user set threshold
SPOT-316.remedy: 1. Review the vision results using either the Runtime screen or Vision Setup screen. 2. Verify the user set threshold 3. Adjust the Vision Process or equipment as necessary

SPOT-317.cause: Robot Cap Base Location has moved too far from nominal position.
SPOT-317.remedy: Robot Shank may have slipped or tool bent.

SPOT-318.cause: The tips were out of alignment
SPOT-318.remedy: 1. Adjust equipment to realign weld caps 2. Adjust the Vision Process as necessary

SPOT-319.cause: Gun tip did not match the tip dressed model
SPOT-319.remedy: 1. Re-dress the weld caps 2. Adjust the Vision Process as necessary

SPOT-320.cause: Robot tip did not match the tip dressed model
SPOT-320.remedy: 1. Re-dress the weld caps 2. Adjust the Vision Process as necessary

SPOT-321.cause: Gun Cap did not match the new cap model
SPOT-321.remedy: 1. Change Gun Cap 2. Verify that the correct cap type is on the weld gun 3. Adjust the Vision Process as necessary

SPOT-322.cause: Robot Cap did not match the new cap model
SPOT-322.remedy: 1. Change Robot Cap 2. Verify that the correct cap type is on the weld gun 3. Adjust the Vision Process as necessary

SPOT-323.cause: This is a message for testing purposes only.
SPOT-323.remedy: Document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC technical representative.

SPOT-324.cause: User chose to Continue from a tip inspection fault

SPOT-325.cause: User chose to Retry from a tip inspection fault

SPOT-326.cause: User chose to Abort from a tip inspection fault

SPOT-327.cause: User did NOT choose any recovery from a tip inspection fault

SPOT-328.cause: Gun Cap has slipped on shank

SPOT-329.cause: Robot Cap has slipped on shank

SPOT-330.cause: Gun Cap Tip to Shank Distance has changed too much (Relative cap wear)

SPOT-331.cause: Robot Cap Tip to Shank Distance has changed too much (Relative cap wear)

SPOT-335.cause: The Gun Tip Trend value has exceeded the Max Trend Thresh

SPOT-336.cause: The Robot Tip Trend value has exceeded the Max Trend Thresh

SPOT-337.message: Tip Aignment Off Axis Distance Exceeds Threshold
SPOT-337.cause: Center Lines of caps are too far apart

SPOT-338.cause: A parameter is missing and cannot continue without it

SPOT-339.cause: Measurement of Gun Cap Surface area is too much

SPOT-340.cause: Measurement of Robot Cap Surface area is too much

SPOT-341.cause: After Dress Operation the incremental change in Gun cap length (Tip-Base) is insufficient

SPOT-342.cause: After Dress Operation the incremental change in Robot cap length (Tip-Base) is insufficient

SPOT-343.cause: After Dress Operation the incremental change in Gun cap length (Tip-Base) is too much
SPOT-343.remedy: Adjust time or pressure for Redress

SPOT-344.cause: After Dress Operation the incremental change in Robot cap length (Tip-Base) is too much
SPOT-344.remedy: Adjust time or pressure for Redress

SPOT-345.cause: After Dress Operation the incremental change in total cap length (Tip-Tip) is too little

SPOT-346.cause: After Dress Operation the incremental change in total cap length (Tip-Tip) is too little

SPOT-350.cause: No IWC boards were found on the controller.
SPOT-350.remedy: If an IWC board was expected, this indicates that there is probably a serious hardware problem and the board should be replaced. If an IWC board is not expected, then the IWC driver should be removed from the configuration.

SPOT-351.cause: The IWC driver is waiting for the PC/104 motherboard to complete its reset cycle.
SPOT-351.remedy: This is a system programming error.

SPOT-352.cause: The specified IWC board is not installed.
SPOT-352.remedy: This is a system programming error.

SPOT-353.cause: A message cannot be sent to the IWC because a previous message transaction is still in progress.
SPOT-353.remedy: This is a system programming error.

SPOT-354.cause: The buffers sent for a message transaction are not valid in number and/or length.
SPOT-354.remedy: This is a system programming error.

SPOT-355.cause: The function request to the IWC driver is invalid.
SPOT-355.remedy: This is a system programming error.

SPOT-356.cause: The IWC reported a checksum error during a message send operation. This may indicate a problem with the board or driver software.
SPOT-356.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC technical representative.

SPOT-357.cause: The IWC reported an invalid buffer during a message send operation. This may indicate a problem with the board or driver software.
SPOT-357.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

SPOT-358.cause: An invalid checksum was computed on a message segment received from the IWC board. This may indicate a problem with the board or driver software.
SPOT-358.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

SPOT-359.cause: An invalid buffer tag was detected on a message segment received from the IWC board. This may indicate a problem with the board or driver software.
SPOT-359.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

SPOT-360.cause: The buffer passed to the IWC driver was too small to hold the message received from the IWC.
SPOT-360.remedy: This is a system programming error.

SPOT-361.cause: The IWC did not acknowledge a message segment that was sent to it.
SPOT-361.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

SPOT-362.cause: The IWC did not send a response message within the allowable time limit.
SPOT-362.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

SPOT-363.cause: The IWC driver was unable to communicate with the PC/104 motherboard driver.
SPOT-363.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

SPOT-364.cause: An IWC board was detected, but the contents of the dual-port RAM area is not what is expected.
SPOT-364.remedy: Make sure that the correct type of IWC board is installed. If the problem persists, swap in a new board.

SPOT-365.cause: An IWC board was detected, but the version and/or revision level of its dual-port RAM is not supported by the installed driver.
SPOT-365.remedy: Install an IWC with a compatible version level, or check to see if there is an updated version of the driver available.

SPOT-366.cause: The driver was unable to register an interrupt for the IWC board.
SPOT-366.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

SPOT-367.message: Only 29 functions allowed in a schedule
SPOT-367.cause: The user tried to insert more than 29 functions into the schedule.
SPOT-367.remedy: Do not insert more than 29 functions in a schedule.

SPOT-368.message: Imp. can only come before weld FCTN
SPOT-368.cause: The user tried to insert an impulse function(function 60) before a non-weld function.
SPOT-368.remedy: Insert the impulse function directly before a weld function.

SPOT-369.message: FCTN not supported by the timer
SPOT-369.cause: The user directly entered an invalid function number to be inserted.
SPOT-369.remedy: Choose another function from the choice list, or look up the function number of a valid function.

SPOT-370.cause: The schedule failed 2 download tries to the timer.

SPOT-371.cause: The stepper failed 2 download tries to the timer.

SPOT-372.cause: The sequence file could not be read from the FROM.
SPOT-372.remedy: Make sure the sequence exists on FROM.

SPOT-373.cause: The setup data failed 2 download tries to the timer.

SPOT-374.cause: The dynamic data failed 2 download tries to the timer.

SPOT-375.cause: The stepper file could not be read from the FROM.
SPOT-375.remedy: Make sure the stepper exists on FROM.

SPOT-376.cause: The setup file could not be read from the FROM.
SPOT-376.remedy: Make sure the setup file exists on FROM.

SPOT-377.cause: The named file could not be read from the Device.
SPOT-377.remedy: Make sure the file exists on the Device.

SPOT-378.cause: The ID jumpers on the IWC card(s) are not set so that the cards can be identified as card #1 and card #2.
SPOT-378.remedy: If there is one card in the system, its ID must be set to 1. If there are two cards, one must be set as card 1 and the other as card 2 according to the slots they are in.

SPOT-379.cause: The IWC slave busy bit is set in the status word.
SPOT-379.remedy: Retry the operation after a short delay.

SPOT-380.cause: The firmware versions on the timer card must be the same if there are 2 timers. Either the firmware version itself is different, or the revision level of the firmware is different.
SPOT-380.remedy: Make sure that the firmware version and revision level match for both cards. It could be viewed by plugging in one card at a time and viewing the revision level of each one.

SPOT-399.cause: The IWC firmware has been upgraded on the timer card.

SPOT-530.cause: SPOT-530 is merely the cause code for SPOT-531. It provides equipment number, style number and duration, when weldct is less than expected. Note: equipment number is a hex value because one task can execute multiple equipment.
SPOT-530.remedy: This alarm is provided for background info - no remedy required.

SPOT-531.cause: Weld count observed for current job is smaller than benchmark value. Weld(s) may have been skipped. This alarm is posted along with SPOT-530. Possible causes are: WeldEnable=FALSE, StrokeEnabl=False, or Line is forcibly skipped in editor.
SPOT-531.remedy: Refer to equipment number, and style number in SPOT-530. If spots were missed, re-execute this style again. However, if spotcount table is stale (tp program for this style was edited, after benchmark was recorded), go to WeldCtChk screen, and peform following procedure: 1.Move cursor to appropriate style number 2.Press F3:ClrCurCt to reset spotct and other benchmark info: 3.Execute this style again, to update benchmark info. Note: benchmark automatically updates if tp name associated with a style changes. However, benchmark does NOT automatically update, if tp program is edited. User should execute procedure above to update benchmark data, after modifying a tp program. Set $WLDCTCFG.$WLDCTCHKENB = FALSE to disable this alarm.

SPOT-532.cause: Spot instruction was programmed with S=0, which tells system not to weld this point. $SPOTS0ALARM = 1, so SPOT-532 is posted with WARN severity to notify user in case S=0 was entered accidentally. Note that system does not pause, because SPOT-532 has warn severity.
SPOT-532.remedy: Enter weld schedule number greater than 0, if S=0 was accidental. Note: in dual gun case S=(0,0), the schedule can be 0 for one gun, but not both. Alternatively, set $SPOTS0ALARM to one of the following values: 0: for no alarm 2: for alarm with PAUSE severity

SPOT-533.cause: Spot instruction was programmed with S=0, which tells system not to weld this point. $SPOTS0ALARM = 2, so SPOT-533 is posted with PAUSE severity to notify user in case S=0 was entered accidentally. Note that system pauses, because SPOT-533 has PAUSE severity.
SPOT-533.remedy: Enter weld schedule number greater than 0, if S=0 was accidental. Note: in dual gun case S=(0,0), the schedule can be 0 for one gun, but not both. if S=0 was intentional/deliberate, then set $SPOTS0ALARM to one of the following values: 0: for no alarm 1: for alarm with warn severity

SPOT-534.cause: Severity specified for S=0 alarm (in $SPOTS0ALARM) is invalid. Note that system pauses, because SPOT-534 has PAUSE severity.
SPOT-534.remedy: Set $SPOTS0ALARM to one of the following values: 0: for no alarm 1: for alarm with warn severity 2: for alarm with pause severity

SPOT-540.cause: Common notification header for weld assurance. Cause code (541-546) identifies reason for this message.
SPOT-540.remedy: Address issue specified in cause code.

SPOT-541.cause: Weld controller enable input is false, so joining/fusion will not occur.
SPOT-541.remedy: Set weld enable = true or disable weld assurance.

SPOT-542.cause: Stroke enable flag is false, so joining/fusion will not occur.
SPOT-542.remedy: Set weld enable = true or disable weld assurance.

SPOT-543.cause: Weld schedule = 0, so joining/fusion will not occur.
SPOT-543.remedy: Set weld enable = true or disable weld assurance.

SPOT-544.cause: Weld duration was too short. Weld duration must be greater than min weld duration for pass status.
SPOT-544.remedy: Correct weld schedule, increase min duration or disable weld assurance.

SPOT-545.cause: Thickness after weld was too large. Thickness after weld should smaller than thickness before weld.
SPOT-545.remedy: Repeat weld, increase min thickness decrease or disable weld assurance.

SPOT-546.cause: Weld count did not increment. This can occur if weld enable is false or if software misoperation occurred.
SPOT-546.remedy: Make sure production settings are active and repeat weld schedule or disable weld assurance.

SPOT-547.message: Equip%s does not support this instruction
SPOT-547.cause: An instruction related to spot welding (water saver, iso contactor, etc) was specified in the tp program, but the equipment is configured as a fastener.
SPOT-547.remedy: Delete the instruction from the tp program.

SPOT-548.cause: FINE termination type is required for the application instruction that is attached to this motion.note: Airgun spot and airgun backup instructions have this requirement.Servogun spot and other application instructions do NOT have this requirement.
SPOT-548.remedy: Change termtype in tp program to FINE.

SPRM-000.remedy: Change ths command speed and destination speed within the speed limit

SPRM-001.remedy: Power off to recover. If problem persistes, please reload the controller.

SPRM-002.cause: Ramp is disabled dor backward motion.
SPRM-002.remedy: Specification. Ramp does not support backward motion.

SPRM-003.cause: Ramp does not support deg/sec for its speed unit.
SPRM-003.remedy: Change speed unit to mm/sec cm/min or inch/min.

SPRM-004.cause: Ramp does not support time based speed unit(msec or sec)
SPRM-004.remedy: Change speed unit to mm/sec cm/min or inch/min.

SPRM-005.cause: The ramp software is loaded incorrectly.

SPRM-006.cause: Ramp is disabled for rotation dominated motion.
SPRM-006.remedy: Current position has large orientation change. Please re-record the position with less orientation change to run the speed ramp motion.

SPRM-007.cause: Ramp is disabled for short motion.
SPRM-007.remedy: The current motion travels in short distance, not enough for ramp motion to speed up. Please re-record the position with longer distance to order run the speed ramp motion.

SPRM-008.cause: Max Speed is not supported. Ramp does not support max speed for its speed unit.
SPRM-008.remedy: Change speed unit to mm/sec, cm/min, or inch/min.

SPRM-009.message: No Ramp resume in hot start.
SPRM-009.cause: Ramp resume is disabled when in hot start mode.
SPRM-009.remedy: Do not resume speed ramp in

SRIO-001.cause: Illegal function code was specified. System error.

SRIO-002.remedy: Open serial port before using it.

SRIO-003.cause: Serial port has already been opened, and it was tried to be opened again.
SRIO-003.remedy: Do not try to open the serial port which has already be opened.

SRIO-004.remedy: Initialize the serial port before using it.

SRIO-005.remedy: Check if serial port setup is correct. Check if cable is broken. Check if there exists a noise source near controller. Check target device status.

SRIO-006.remedy: Check if serial port setup is correct. Check if cable is broken. Check if there exists a noise source near controller.

SRIO-007.remedy: Check if serial port setup is correct. Check if cable is broken. Check if there exists a noise source near controller.

SRIO-008.remedy: Check if serial port setup is correct. Check if cable is broken. Check if there exists a noise source near controller.

SRIO-009.cause: Serial port parity error and overrun error occured.
SRIO-009.remedy: Check if serial port setup is correct. Check if cable is broken. Check if there exists a noise source near controller.

SRIO-010.cause: Serial port parity error and frame error occured
SRIO-010.remedy: Check if serial port setup is correct. Check if cable is broken. Check if there exists a noise source near controller.

SRIO-011.cause: Serial port overrun error and frame error occured.
SRIO-011.remedy: Check if serial port setup is correct. Check if cable is broken. Check if there exists a noise source near controller.

SRIO-012.cause: Serial port parity error, overrun error, and frame error occured.
SRIO-012.remedy: Check if serial port setup is correct. Check if cable is broken. Check if there exists a noise source near controller.

SRIO-013.message: S. PORT DSR OFF & HARDWARE ERR
SRIO-013.cause: Serial port DSR is off and harware error occured.
SRIO-013.remedy: Check if serial port setup is correct. Check if cable is broken. Check if there exists a noise source near controller. Check target device status. Check the hardware.

SRIO-014.cause: Serial port request count is illegal. System error.

SRIO-015.cause: Cancel current serial port setup. This code does not appear at normal time. System error.

SRIO-016.cause: Initialize serial port at power failure recovery. This code does not appear at normal time. System error.

SRVO-001.cause: The EMERGENCY STOP button on the operator panel or operation box was pressed.
SRVO-001.remedy: 1. Twist the operator panel EMERGENCY STOP button clockwise to release it, then press RESET. 2. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SRVO-002.cause: The EMERGENCY STOP button on the teach pendant was pressed.
SRVO-002.remedy: 1. Twist the teach pendant EMERGENCY STOP button clockwise to release it, then press RESET. 2. If this alarm cannot be reset, replace the teach pendant. (Paint) In addition to the above comments, replace teach pendant cable and, if applicable, the ISB.

SRVO-003.cause: The deadman switch was not pressed when the teach pendant was enabled.
SRVO-003.remedy: 1. Press the deadman switch to release it, then press RESET. If the deadman switch is three position switch type, press the deadman switch to middle position to release it, then press RESET. 2. If this alarm cannot be reset, replace the teach pendant.

SRVO-004.cause: The safety door or fence is open.
SRVO-004.remedy: 1. Close the safety fence after checking that a worker is not inside the safe fence, then press RESET. 2. If this alarm cannot be reset, Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SRVO-005.cause: A hardware limit switch on an axis was tripped. Usually, the movement of the robot is prevented from exceeding a limit beyond the maximum range of movement (software limits) for each axis. However, when the robot is shipped, the overtravel state is set for transit.
SRVO-005.remedy: 1. Hold down the SHIFT key, and press RESET to reset the alarm. 2. Continue holding the SHIFT key, and jog the robot to bring all axes into the movable range. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. NOTE: 1. The direction of jog of each axis is limited until the alarm is released. It cannot jog to the direction where the axis moved when the alarm is occurred. 2. In the robot calibration incomplete status, you can release the above note1 limitation with the overtravel release screen [SYSTEM/ OT release]. Note 1. The jog direction of each axis is limited until the alarm is released. It cannot jog to the direction where the axis moved when the alarm is occurred. 2. In the robot calibration incomplete status, you can release the above note1 limitation with the overtravel release screen [SYSTEM/ OT release]. 3. (Paint) In addition to Action 3 above, verify the jumper on the EIM: OT to 24VF. Replace the EIM and cable between the 6 axis servo amplifier and EIM. Verify the Fiber Optic cables are in the correct FSSB ports.

SRVO-006.cause: A safety hand has broken. If no broken hand can be found, however, the most likely cause is the HBK signal of a robot connection cable being at the 0 V level.
SRVO-006.remedy: 1. Hold down the SHIFT key, and press RESET to reset the alarm. 2. While holding down the SHIFT key, jog the tool to the workplace. Replace the safety hand or check the safety joint cable. If the Hand broken signal is not in use, it can be disabled in the system config screen / Hand broken setting. After these measures, hold down the SHIFT key, and press RESET. 3. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SRVO-007.cause: The external EMERGENCY STOP button was pressed.
SRVO-007.remedy: 1. If you are using the external emergency stop, clear the source of the fault, and press RESET. 2. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. (Paint) In addition to the above comments, this may be the interlock to the paint system. See applicable system drawings.

SRVO-008.cause: The brake fuse is blown on the EMG Control PCB.
SRVO-008.remedy: Replace the fuse. Check the LED (FALM) on the printed circuit board for emergency stop control to determine whether the fuse has blown.

SRVO-009.cause: The pneumatic pressure alarm indicates the presence of a defect. If the pneumatic pressure alarm is not detected, however, the most likely cause is the PPABN signal of a robot connection cable being at the 0 V level.
SRVO-009.remedy: 1. Repair the pneumatic pressure or check the cable. 2. If the pneumatic pressure signal is not in use, it can be disabled in the system config screen. 3. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SRVO-010.cause: The belt broken robot digital input is asserted.
SRVO-010.remedy: 1. If the belt is found to be defective in any way, repair it and then press RESET. 2. When the belt is found to be normal, signal RDI [7] in the robot connection cable might be abnormal. Check the cable. Note: In the robot series whose system variable $PARAM_GROUP.$BELT_ENABLE is TRUE, this alarm is detected. Note In the robot series whose system variable $PARAM_GROUP.$BELT_ENABLE is TRUE, this alarm is detected.

SRVO-011.cause: The teach pendant attachment switch on the operator panel was operated while the teach pendant was enabled.
SRVO-011.remedy: Reconnect the teach pendant cable to continue operation with the teach pendant disabled.

SRVO-012.remedy: This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

SRVO-013.cause: Upon power-up with power restoration enabled (hot start), the configuration of the DSP modules on the axis control printed circuit board and the multi-function printed circuit board has been changed.
SRVO-013.remedy: Turn on the power in cold start mode.

SRVO-014.cause: When a fan motor stops on backplane unit, TP shows the following message. In one minutes from occurring of alarm, robot stops and cannot be operated from TP. The robot can be recovered by replacing a fan motor. Number in the bracket indicates which fan is abnormal. (1): fan above the slot1 (2): fan above the slot2 (3): both fans
SRVO-014.remedy: 1. Check the fan motor and its cables. Replace them if necessary. 2. Replace the backplane unit. Before executing the remedy 3, perform a complete controller back up as image to save all your programs and settings. 3. Replace the main board, and restore the image backup. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SRVO-015.cause: The temperature of the control unit is higher than the specified value. In one minute from occurring of alarm, robot stops and cannot be operated from TP.
SRVO-015.remedy: 1. If the ambient temperature is higher than specified (45°C), cool down the ambient temperature. 2. If the fan motor is not running, check it and its cables. Replace them if necessary. Before executing the remedy 3, perform a complete controller back up as image to save all your programs and settings. 3. Replace the main board, and restore the image backup. (The thermostat on the main board may be faulty.) Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SRVO-016.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-017.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-018.cause: The brake current exceeded the specification.
SRVO-018.remedy: There is possibility that the robot connection cable might short. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. "(Paint) In addition to the above comments, check/replace the Brake Board in systems with Manual Brake Release. See drawings in the Robot— Specific Controller Maintenance Addendum for the brake circuit connections.

SRVO-019.cause: On the terminal block on the printed circuit board of the operator panel, no connection is established between signals *SVON1 and *SVON2. When an external switch is connected, it should be checked.

SRVO-020.cause: The teach pendant cable is disconnected or a momentary break occurred in any one of the TP emergency stop circuits: TP emergency stop, DEADMAN, or fence.
SRVO-020.remedy: Check the teach pendant cable and connections.

SRVO-021.cause: The ready signal of the servo amplifier corresponding to the displayed group and axis was turned off.
SRVO-021.remedy: 1. Refer to those cause/measures when the alarm history is confirmed and other alarms have occurred at the same time. 2. If this alarm occurred after add axis or modification of axis' setup, confirm whether a set content is correct. If the mistake is found, modify it. Especially, confirm whether to find the mistake in the FSSB line number, the amplifier axis number, and the amplifier type. 3. Confirm the setting of the machine lock for the multi group. • Advance to measures 4 when all motion groups machine lock are released. • Release the machine lock of the robot when the robot (six axis amplifier) is a machine lock. Note: When six axis amplifier is made a machine lock, the amplifier subordinate to this turns off and SRDY is turned off. 4. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note 1. When six axis amplifier is made a machine lock, the amplifier subordinate to this turns off and SRDY is turned off. 2. There is a possibility when the specification of the teach pendant is not correct compared with the controller. For instance, when the teach pendant of the RIA/CE specification is used in the controller of non-RIA/CE specification, this alarm might occur. Connect the correct teach pendant corresponding to the controller.

SRVO-022.cause: SRDY was already on when an attempt was made to turn on the MCC with HRDY. (HRDY is the signal sent from the host to the servo system to specify whether to turn the servo amplifier's MCC on or off. SRDY is the signal sent from the servo system to the host to indicate whether a servo amplifier's MCC is on or off.)
SRVO-022.remedy: 1. Replace the servo amplifier applicable to the alarm message. 2. Replace the servo card module or the auxiliary axis board applicable to the alarm message.

SRVO-023.cause: When the robot stopped, the servo positional error exceeded a specified value ($PARAM_GROUP.$STOPERLIM). This alarm means that the robot cannot reach a taught point or cannot keep a taught posture. Probable causes: 1. Overload 2. External force to the robot 3. Disconnection or misconnection of the motor power cable or brake cable 4. Incorrect setup for the robot which has 2 axis brake option 5. Insufficient torque by low voltage of power supply 6. Brake failure (includes mis-setting of brake number for auxiliary axis) 7. Aux. brake unit failure for aux. axis 8. Amplifier failure 9. Motor failure 10. Motor power cable or brake cable failure
SRVO-023.remedy: 1. Check whether the duty and applied load exceed the rating. If so, reduce the duty or applied load. 2. Check whether the robot is pushed or pulled by an external force. If so, remove the external force to the robot or modify the taught point. 3. Check whether the power line of the robot connection cable or the cable in the mechanical unit are down. 4. Check whether the motor power cable/connector and brake cable/connector are connected correctly. Especially, check whether the power cable/connectors are not connected to other motors. 5. Check whether the robot setup (setting of 2BK or 6BK) is correct, if the used robot has 2BK option. 6. Measure the supplied voltage. Then, check whether the voltage is matched to the controller specification. 7. Check whether the motor brake is released properly when RESET is pressed or the robot moves. First of all, check whether the setting of brake number is correct when this alarm occurs on an auxiliary axis. 8. When this alarm occurs on the auxiliary axis whose brake is controlled by the aux. brake unit, check the fuse on the aux. brake unit. 9. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. About auxiliary axis, refer to the Auxiliary Axis Option Maintenance Manual. (Paint) Verify the brakes are releasing and there is no mechanical binding of the joint with manual brake release if available. If joint moves freely, change the Motor, RVV, or servo amp.

SRVO-024.cause: When the robot moved, the servo positional error exceeded a specified value ($PARAM_GROUP.$MOVER_OFFST). This alarm means that the excessive path deviation occurs. Probable cause: Same as described above (SRVO-023).
SRVO-024.remedy: Perform the same action as that described for the previous item (SRVO-023). However, it does not relate to the brake option setting in this case. (Paint) See SRVO-023.

SRVO-025.cause: The motion command is too large.
SRVO-025.remedy: 1. Perform a Cold start • Turn off the robot. • On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. • While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. 2. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-026.cause: An attempt was made to exceed the maximum rated motor speed ($PARAM_GROUP.$MOT_SPD_LIM). The motor speed is clamped to its maximum rated value.
SRVO-026.remedy: This is just a notification. However, you should attempt to eliminate this error and not repeat the circumstances that led up to it.

SRVO-027.cause: An attempt was made to perform calibration, but mastering has not yet been completed.
SRVO-027.remedy: Perform mastering from the calibration screen [6 SYSTEM Master/Cal]. (Paint) Mastering also applies to process axis such as gear pump or canister motors.

SRVO-030.cause: When the Brake On Hold function is enabled, this alarm is issued whenever a hold signal is input.
SRVO-030.remedy: 1. This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this message. 2. If you do not use this function, disable [Brake On Hold] on the general item setting screen [6 SETUP General] and perform a power cycle.

SRVO-031.cause: A user servo alarm was issued. This alarm is occurred when system variable $MCR_GRP[i].$SOFT_ALARM is set to TRUE.
SRVO-031.remedy: Confirm why $MCR_GRP[i].$SOFT_ALARM is set to to TRUE.

SRVO-033.cause: An attempt was made to set a reference point for quick mastering, but calibration has not yet been completed.
SRVO-033.remedy: Perform calibration by following the procedure below. 1. Turn on the power. 2. Execute [CALIBRATION] from the calibration screen [6 SYSTEM Master/Cal]. (Paint) Loss of calibration for no reason may also happen if the fiber optic cable length between devices exceeds 42 meters on the FSSB.

SRVO-034.cause: An attempt was made to perform quick mastering, but a required reference point has not yet been set.
SRVO-034.remedy: Set a reference point for simple mastering from the calibration screen.

SRVO-035.cause: A value higher than the maximum axis speed ($PARAM_GROUP.$JNTVELLIM) was specified. Each actual axis speed is tied to the maximum speed.
SRVO-035.remedy: Decrease the axis speed value to be within limit specified in ($PARAM_GROUP.$JNTVELLIM).

SRVO-036.cause: The in-position monitor time ($PARAM_GROUP.$IMPOS_TIME) has elapsed, but the robot cannot reach a taught point within the specified in-position ($PARAM_GROUP.$STOPTOL).
SRVO-036.remedy: Perform the same action as that described for SRVO-023 (Stop error excess).

SRVO-037.cause: The *IMSTP signal, which is a peripheral device I/O signal, is OFF.
SRVO-037.remedy: Turn on the *IMSTP signal. (Paint) This is typically the software interlock to the paint system.

SRVO-038.cause: A pulse count detected at power-on differs from one detected at power-off. This could be due to the following: 1. File (SYSMAST.SV) that saved in the state at an axis position different from a present axis position was loaded. 2. The software brake setting is incorrect. 3. A incorrect brake type was set to the robot with two-axis brake option. 4. File (SYSMAST.SV) that saved with other robots was loaded. 5. The axis position was changed with a brake release unit while the controller power is off. 6. The axis fell while the controller power is off due to the brake trouble. (Paint) This alarm may occur when the robot is powered off, the brakes are released, and an axis is moved quickly. It may also be due to a bad pulsecoder. Remaster or replace the pulsecoder.
SRVO-038.remedy: 1. Refer SRVO-222 when this error occurs with SRVO-222. 2. For the above cause 2 and 3, confirm the setup or brake type setting and correct setting. For the above cause 4, re-load SYSMAST.SV of the robot. Afterwards, PULSE RESET operation should be done. There are the following two methods. • Method 1: Move the cursor to $MCR.$SPC_RESET on the system variable screen, and select F4 TRUE. It becomes TRUE momentarily, it writes in FALSE at once. Then push the reset button. • Method 2: F3 RES_PCA is pushed on the MASTER/CAL screen, and select F4 YES. Then push the alarm release button. Note The MASTER/CAL screen is not usually displayed. The worker who has the operation qualification does. Check whether the robot position on Teach Pendant is correct. If incorrect, re-mastering is required.

SRVO-039.cause: CMC cannot work because the calculated motor speed exceeded the specification.
SRVO-039.remedy: Reduce the motion speed or disable CMC.

SRVO-040.cause: Zero position master is done with mark position (not with zero position).
SRVO-040.remedy: This message is only for S-420iR. S-420iR has the mark at non-zero position for J2 and J3. So Zero position master is not done with zero pos for S-420iS. Confirm the position of each axis to be at mark position. If the robot is not S-420iR, $scr_grp.$robot_model may be wrong. Set correct $scr_grp.$robot_model.

SRVO-041.cause: A value of the internal motion command is too big.
SRVO-041.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-042.cause: This alarm means that the contacts of the magnetic contactor have stuck together. The alarm condition occurs if the magnetic contactor is already on when an attempt is made to turn it on. The alarm condition is detected between the time the contact sticking occurs, and the time an attempt is made to turn it on.
SRVO-042.remedy: 1. Check the magnetic contactor, and replace it if necessary. 2. If the contacts of the magnetic contactor have stuck to each other, turn off the circuit breaker. If the power is switched off without turning off the circuit breaker, the servo amplifier might get damaged, because the stuck contacts keep 3-phase 200 VAC applied to the servo amplifier. 3. Replace the E-Stop unit. 4. Replace the servo amplifier.

SRVO-043.cause: The energy produced by regenerative discharge is excessive. As a result, all the generated energy cannot be dissipated as heat.
SRVO-043.remedy: 1. This alarm may occur if the axis is subjected to frequent acceleration/deceleration or if the axis is vertical and generates a large amount of regenerative energy. If this alarm has occurred, relax the conditions. 2. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. (Paint) This typically indicates an issue with the supply voltage such as a missing phase or low voltage. It may also be due to the wrong transformer tap setting.

SRVO-044.cause: The DC voltage (DC link voltage) of the main circuit power supply is abnormally high.
SRVO-044.remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual.

SRVO-045.cause: An excessively high current flowed through the main circuit of the servo amplifier.
SRVO-045.remedy: Turn off the controller power, and disconnect the power cable from the servo amplifier indicated by the alarm message. Also disconnect the brake cable to avoid the axis falling unexpectedly. 1. In the above condition, supply controller power again and check if this alarm occurs again. If this alarm occurs again, replace the servo amplifier. 2. About the power cable, check the insulation of their U, V, W and the GND lines each other. If there is a short-circuit, replace the power cable. 3. About the power cable, measure the resistance between their U and V,V and W and W and U with an ohmmeter that has a very low resistance range. If the resistances at the three places are different from each other, the motor, the power cable is defective. Check each item in detail and replace it if necessary. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SRVO-046.cause: The root-mean-square current value which is calculated internally by the servo system exceeds the maximum permissible value. This alarm is issued to protect the motor and amplifier from damage of thermal destruction. Probable cause: 1. Overload 2. External force to the robot 3. Disconnection of the brake cable 4. Insufficient torque by low voltage of power supply 5. Brake failure (includes mis-setting of brake number for auxiliary axis) 6. Aux. brake unit failure for aux. axis 7. Amplifier failure 8. Motor failure 9. Motor power cable or brake cable failure
SRVO-046.remedy: 1. Check whether the duty and applied load exceed the rating. If so, reduce the duty or applied load. 2. Check whether the robot is pushed or pulled by external force. If so, remove the external force to the robot or modify the taught point. 3. Check whether the brake cable/connector are connected correctly. 4. Measure the supplied voltage. Then, check whether the voltage is matched to the controller specification. 5. Check whether the motor brake is released properly when Reset or the robot moves. First of all, check whether the setting of brake number is correct when this alarm occurs on auxiliary axis. 6. When this alarm occurs on the auxiliary axis which brake is controlled by the aux. brake unit, check the fuse on the aux. brake unit. 7. If this alarm cannot be reset, the troubles of related parts are thought. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. About auxiliary axis, refer to the Auxiliary Axis Option Maintenance Manual.

SRVO-047.cause: The control power supply voltage to servo amplifier is excessively low.
SRVO-047.remedy: There is possibly trouble with the servo amplifier and/or the power supply unit. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SRVO-049.cause: The thermostat in the transfer worked. Alternatively, the fuse in the servo amplifier has blown.
SRVO-049.remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual. (Paint) Some paint systems use two transformers. This is indicates by having two A cabinets with separate disconnects stacked on each other. The alarm does not indicate which transformer is overheated.

SRVO-050.cause: A collision was detected. (An excessively large disturbance torque was estimated by the servo software.) Probable causes are: 1. Collision (Tip stick) / External force to the robot 2. Overload / Heavy acceleration 3. Increasing of the friction by low temperature 4. Insufficient torque by low voltage of power supply 5. Brake failure (includes mis-setting of brake number for auxiliary axis) 6. Aux. brake unit failure for aux. axis 7. Amplifier failure 8. The E-Stop unit failure 9. Motor failure 10. Motor power cable or brake cable failure 11. Reducer failure
SRVO-050.remedy: 1. Check whether the robot has collided with an object. To release this alarm, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. Release only RESET key. Still pressing the SHIFT key, and press any jog key to the axis away from the collision. 2. Check whether the payload (mass, center of gravity, and inertia) are set correctly. 3. Check whether the applied load exceed the rating. If so, reduce the applied load. If you use the ACC override more than 100, please reduce the value of ACC override. Allowable disturbance threshold level can be changed from STATUS/Axis/Disturb screen. 4. If this alarm occurs when the robot is used after long time interval or when the temperature is very low, run the robot with low speed for a while before running with normal speed. 5. Check whether the motor power cable/connector and brake cable/connector are connected correctly. Especially, check whether the power cable/connector are not connected to other motors. 6. Measure the supplied voltage. Then, check whether the voltage is matched to the controller specification. 7. Check whether the motor brake is released properly when RESET is pressed or the robot moves. First of all, check whether the setting of brake number is correct when this alarm occurs on auxiliary axis. 8. When this alarm occurs on the auxiliary axis which brake is controlled by the aux. brake unit, check the fuse on the aux. brake unit. 9. There might be a failure with the following parts. Replace it or contact your FANUC technical representative. • Aux. brake unit (if it is used.) • Servo amplifier • Servo motor • Robot connection cable (power/brake line) • Cable in the mechanical unit (power/brake line) • Reducer (Paint) Identify the correct axis and investigate if there was a collision or other mechanical interference with the joint."

SRVO-051.cause: The offset of the current feedback value is excessively large. Current detection circuit failure is in the amplifier.

SRVO-053.cause: Disturbance estimated in the software exceeds the threshold value. There is a possibility that SRVO-050 occurs when the robot runs leaving this warning.
SRVO-053.remedy: 1. Check whether the payload (mass, center of gravity, and inertia) are set correctly. 2. Check whether the applied load exceed the rating. If so, reduce the applied load. 3. If this alarm occurs when the robot is used after long time interval or when the temperature is very low, run the robot with low speed for a while before running with normal speed.

SRVO-054.cause: An access to the servo module memory failed. Note: Before you continue to the next step, perform a complete controller backup to save all of your programs and settings from memory for this robot. After you complete the next step, restore the saved data to the new main board if the memory has been lost. Otherwise, you could injure personnel, damage equipment, or lose data. Refer to the application-specific Setup and Operations Manual for information on how to back up controller memory.
SRVO-054.remedy: Replace the axis control card on the main board.

SRVO-055.cause: A communication error has occurred between the main board and the servo amplifier. (from main board to servo amplifier.)
SRVO-055.remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual. About auxiliary axis, refer to the Auxiliary Axis Option Maintenance Manual. (Paint) Possible issue with fiber optic cable or DC power to the communication circuit of the servo amplifier. On dual arm systems with two transformers it is important to power up the remote controller at or before the same time the main controller is powered up. This fault may also occur if the Fiber Optic cable length is over 42 meters between any two FSSB devices. Additionally a short on the 5V in the pulsecoder/cable will crowbar the supply needed to communicate on the FSSB. Having the software configured for a line tracking module but not having the module present on the network may also cause FSSB faults.

SRVO-056.cause: A communication error has occurred between the main board and servo amplifier. (from servo amplifier to main board.)
SRVO-056.remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual. About auxiliary axis, refer to the Auxiliary Axis Option Maintenance Manual. (Paint) See SRVO-055.

SRVO-057.cause: Communication was interrupted between the main board and the servo amplifier.
SRVO-057.remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual. About auxiliary axis, refer to the Auxiliary Axis Option Maintenance Manual. (Paint) See SRVO-055.

SRVO-058.remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual. Note: Need power cycle to release this alarm. (Paint) See SRVO-055.

SRVO-059.remedy: Check the servo amplifier and its wiring. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note: Perform a power cycle to release this alarm.

SRVO-060.cause: Communication between the auxiliary axis board and servo amplifier was interrupted.
SRVO-060.remedy: 1. Check whether the optical cable between the auxiliary axis board and servo amplifier is connected securely. 2. Replace the auxiliary axis board. 3. Replace the servo amplifier. Before executing the following, perform a complete controller back-up to save all your programs and settings. 4. Replace the main board. 5. Replace the backplane. Note: Perform a power cycle to release this alarm.

SRVO-061.cause: The clock for the rotation counter in the Pulsecoder is abnormal.
SRVO-061.remedy: Replace the Pulsecoder. After replacing, perform mastering. Note If this alarm occurs along with a SRVO-068 DTERR, SRVO-069 CRCERR, or SRVO-070 STBERR, disregard this alarm and refer to the other three alarm remedies.

SRVO-062.cause: This alarm is issued when the battery for backing up the absolute position data of the Pulsecoder is not connected or is empty. The battery cable inside the robot might have become disconnected.
SRVO-062.remedy: Replace the battery in the battery box of the robot base or the Pulsecoder. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Correct the cause of the alarm, then turn on the power again after doing PULSE RESET operation. Mastering is required. There are the following two methods for PULSE RESET. • Method 1: Move the cursor to $MCR.$SPC_RESET on the system variable screen, and select F4 TRUE. It becomes TRUE momentarily, it writes in FALSE at once. Then push the reset button. • Method 2: F3 RES_PCA is pushed on the MASTER/CAL screen, and select F4 YES. Then press the alarm release button. Note The MASTER/CAL screen is not usually displayed. (Paint) There are 5 D batteries and a fuse in this circuit located on the ACP door. Verify all connections at the BIM are secure. Replace the Fuse, batteries, or BIM.

SRVO-063.cause: The built-in rotation counter on the Pulsecoder is abnormal.
SRVO-063.remedy: 1. Replace the Pulsecoder. 2. After replacing, set the system variable $MCR.$SPC_RESET to TRUE, and turn the power off and then on again. Master the robot. Note If this alarm occurs along with a SRVO-068 DTERR, SRVO-069 CRCERR, or SRVO-070 STBERR, disregard this alarm and refer to the other three alarm remedies.

SRVO-064.cause: This alarm is issued when the phase of a pulse signal generated by the Pulsecoder is abnormal.
SRVO-064.remedy: Replace the Pulsecoder. After replacing, perform mastering. Note If this alarm occurs along with a SRVO-068 DTERR, SRVO-069 CRCERR, or SRVO-070 STBERR, disregard this alarm and refer to the other three alarm remedies. (Paint) Identify the proper axis and replace the pulsecoder.

SRVO-065.cause: The battery voltage for the Pulsecoder has dropped below the allowable minimum.
SRVO-065.remedy: Replace the battery. Note: When this alarm is issued, immediately replace the battery while the system power is turned on. If the BZAL alarm is issued because the battery is not replaced in time, position data will be lost, thus necessitating robot mastering. (Paint) There are 5 D batteries in this circuit located on the ACP door. Replace the Batteries.

SRVO-066.cause: The Pulsecoder ROM checksum data is abnormal.
SRVO-066.remedy: Replace the Pulsecoder. After replacing, perform mastering. Note If this alarm occurs along with a SRVO-068 DTERR, SRVO-069 CRCERR, or SRVO-070 STBERR, disregard this alarm and refer to the other three alarm remedies.

SRVO-067.cause: The temperature inside the Pulsecoder has become too high, causing the built-in thermostat to actuate.
SRVO-067.remedy: 1. Check the operating conditions of the robot. If any of the rating specified for the robot, such as its rated duty cycle or load, are exceeded, modify the use of the robot such that the ratings are not exceeded. 2. If this alarm is issued, even when the power is turned on and the motor has not overheated, replace the motor. (Paint) Verify the Purge Air is on since that also cools the motors. Verify the axis is not overloaded.

SRVO-068.cause: A request signal was sent to the serial Pulsecoder, but no serial data was returned.
SRVO-068.remedy: 1. Check the connection of the cable between the Pulsecoder and servo amplifier. (If the alarm is occurred at robot axes, check the connection of the robot interconnection cable (for the Pulsecoder)). 2. Check the shielding of the above cable is connected securely to the grounding plate. 3. Replace the Pulsecoder. 4. Replace the servo amplifier. 5. Replace the robot interconnection cable (for the Pulsecoder). Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. (Paint) This alarm occurs when the CPU cannot communicate with the pulsecoder(s). Possible causes include damaged Pulsecoder, damaged cable, damaged EIM.

SRVO-069.remedy: Refer to the SRVO-068 Remedy. (Paint) See SRVO-068 and also consider this fault may occur because noise is getting to the pulsecoder communication, power, or battery conductors.

SRVO-070.cause: A serial data start bit or stop bit error occurred.
SRVO-070.remedy: Refer to the SRVO-068 Remedy. (Paint) See SRVO-068 and also consider this fault may occur because noise is getting to the pulsecoder communication, power, or battery conductors.

SRVO-071.cause: The excessively large feedback speed was detected.
SRVO-071.remedy: 1. This alarm does not indicate the main cause of the problem if issued together with the PHAL alarm (SRVO-064). 2. It might be mis-detection by the noise. Check whether the ground/shield is connected correctly. If possible, enhance the ground/shield. 3. Replace the Pulsecoder of the motor. Mastering is required. 4. Replace the servo amplifier 5. Replace the robot connection cable 6. Replace the cable in the mechanical unit (Paint) See SRVO-068 and also consider this fault may occur because noise is getting to the pulsecoder communication, power, or battery conductors.

SRVO-072.remedy: Replace the Pulsecoder, then perform mastering.

SRVO-073.cause: The Pulsecoder may be faulty, or noise may be causing the Pulsecoder to malfunction.
SRVO-073.remedy: 1. Improve the shielding. 2. Replace the Pulsecoder, then perform mastering. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. (Paint) See SRVO-068 and also consider this fault may occur because noise is getting to the pulsecoder communication, power, or battery conductors.

SRVO-074.cause: The LED on the Pulsecoder has become disconnected.
SRVO-074.remedy: Replace the Pulsecoder, then perform mastering.

SRVO-075.cause: The absolute position of the Pulsecoder has not yet been established. This alarm appears normally after BZAL or CMAL.
SRVO-075.remedy: Reset the alarm, and jog the axis on which the alarm has occurred until the same alarm does not occur again. (Jog one motor revolution). This alarm must be cleared before mastering.

SRVO-076.cause: An excessive disturbance was calculated in the servo software at the beginning of motion. (An abnormal load was detected. The cause might be welding.)
SRVO-076.remedy: Perform the same action as that described for SRVO-050 (CALM alarm). Note: The threshold level for the tip stick detection cannot be changed from STATUS/Axis/Disturb screen.

SRVO-077.cause: The line tracking pulse count overflowed.
SRVO-077.remedy: Contact your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

SRVO-078.cause: The servo parameter has been updated.

SRVO-079.cause: The gun tip position during the pressuring operation (SPOT or PRESS_MOTN) exceeded the stroke limit for the gun. The squeezing operation stopped because the gun axis had over-extended.
SRVO-079.remedy: Check the master position and close stroke limit for the gun. If these values are incorrect, then update them. If these values are correct, then install new tips so that the gun can operate within the stroke limits, during pressuring.

SRVO-080.cause: The root-mean-square current value which is calculated internally by the servo system exceeds the maximum permissible value. This alarm is issued to protect the motor and amplifier from a damage of thermal destruction. Probable cause: 1. Overload 2. External force to the robot 3. Disconnection of the brake cable 4. Insufficient torque by low voltage of power supply 5. Brake failure (includes mis-setting of brake number for auxiliary axis) 6. Aux. brake unit failure for aux. axis 7. Amplifier failure 8. Motor failure 9. Motor power cable or brake cable failure
SRVO-080.remedy: 1. Check whether the duty and applied load exceed the rating. If so, reduce the duty or applied load. 2. Check whether the robot is pushed or pulled by external force. If so, remove the external force to the robot or modify the taught point. 3. Check whether the brake cable/connector are connected correctly. 4. Measure the supplied voltage. Then, check whether the voltage is matched to the controller specification. 5. Check whether the motor brake is released properly when Reset or the robot moves. First of all, check whether the setting of brake number is correct when this alarm occurs on auxiliary axis. 6. When this alarm occurs on the auxiliary axis which brake is controlled by the aux. brake unit, check the fuse on the aux. brake unit. 7. If this alarm cannot be reset, the troubles of related parts are thought. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. About auxiliary axis, refer to the Auxiliary Axis Option Maintenance Manual.

SRVO-081.cause: The pulse count for the line tracking encoder (incremental Pulsecoder) has overflowed.
SRVO-081.remedy: 1. Reduce the encoder speed (conveyor speed). 2. Replace the incremental Pulsecoder for the line tracking. 3. Replace the line tracking cable. 4. Replace the line tracking interface board.

SRVO-082.cause: The line tracking Pulsecoder has not been connected.
SRVO-082.remedy: 1. Check the connection cable at each end (the line tracking I/F board and the Pulsecoder) 2. Check whether the shielding of the connection cable is connected securely to the grounding plate. 3. Replace the line tracking cable. 4. Replace the Pulsecoder. 5. Replace the line tracking interface board. (Paint) See the system drawings for conveyor encoder connections.

SRVO-083.cause: The clock for the rotation counter in the line tracking Pulsecoder is abnormal.
SRVO-083.remedy: See the description for the SRVO-061 CKAL alarm.

SRVO-084.cause: This alarm is issued when the battery for backing up the absolute position data for the Pulsecoder is not connected.
SRVO-084.remedy: See the description for the SRVO-062 BZAL alarm.

SRVO-085.cause: The built-in rotation counter on the line tracking Pulsecoder is abnormal.
