SRVO-085.remedy: See the description for the SRVO-063 RCAL alarm.

SRVO-086.cause: This alarm is issued when the phase of a pulse signal generated by the Pulsecoder is abnormal.
SRVO-086.remedy: See the description for SRVO-064 PHAL alarm.

SRVO-087.cause: This alarm is issued when the battery voltage for backing up the absolute position data of the Pulsecoder has dropped below the allowable minimum.
SRVO-087.remedy: See the description for SRVO-065 BLAL alarm.

SRVO-088.cause: The line tracking Pulsecoder ROM checksum data is abnormal.
SRVO-088.remedy: See the description for the SRVO-066 CSAL alarm.

SRVO-089.remedy: See the description for SRVO-067 OHAL2 alarm.

SRVO-090.cause: An error occurred during communication between the Pulsecoder and the line tracking interface board.
SRVO-090.remedy: 1. Check the connection cable at each end (the line tracking I/F board and the Pulsecoder) 2. Check whether the shielding of the connection cable is connected securely to the grounding plate. 3. Replace the line tracking cable. 4. Replace the Pulsecoder. 5. Replace the line tracking interface board.

SRVO-091.cause: An error occurred during communication between the Pulsecoder and the line tracking interface board.

SRVO-092.cause: An error occurred during communication between the Pulsecoder and the line tracking interface board.

SRVO-093.cause: An excessive speed was detected with the line tracking encoder.
SRVO-093.remedy: 1. This alarm does not indicate the main cause of the problem if issued together with the PHAL alarm(SRVO-086). Refer to SRVO-086. 2. Reduce the encoder speed (conveyor speed). 3. Check whether the shield of the line tracking cable is connected to earth bar in the controller. 4. Replace the absolute Pulsecoder for the line tracking. 5. Replace the line tracking cable. 6. Replace the line tracking interface board.

SRVO-094.remedy: See the description for SRVO-072 PMAL alarm.

SRVO-095.cause: It is likely that the Pulsecoder is abnormal or the Pulsecoder has malfunctioned due to noise.
SRVO-095.remedy: 1. Reinforce the earth of the flange of the motor. 2. Replace the Pulsecoder.

SRVO-096.cause: The LED on the Pulsecoder has become disconnected.
SRVO-096.remedy: See the description for SRVO-074 LDAL alarm.

SRVO-097.cause: The absolute position of the Pulsecoder has not yet been established.
SRVO-097.remedy: See the description for SRVO-075 Pulse not established. (Paint) Jog all applicable axes at least one motor revolution and master/calibrate. One motor revolution may be up to 15 degrees on a rotational axis and up to 150mm on a linear application.

SRVO-098.cause: The acceleration sensor has not been connected. Otherwise, an error occurred during communication between the acceleration sensor and the main board.
SRVO-098.remedy: 1. Check connection of the connector of the connecting cable. 2. Check the shielding of the above cable is connected securely to the grounding plate. 3. Replace the above cable. 4. Replace the acceleration sensor. Before executing the remedy 5, perform a complete controller back up as image to save all your programs and settings. 5. Replace the main board, and restore the image backup.

SRVO-099.cause: Data changed during transfer from the acceleration sensor.

SRVO-100.cause: A stop bit error of the data from the acceleration sensor occurred.

SRVO-101.cause: A Robot overtravel limit switch has been pressed.

SRVO-102.cause: The hand broken (*HBK) robot input is asserted.

SRVO-103.cause: The pneumatic pressure (PPABN) robot input is asserted.

SRVO-104.cause: No longer occurs. Welding electrode of controller. This might occur only for the R-J Dual arm controller.
SRVO-104.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-105.cause: 1. The controller door is opened or E.stop signals are detected for a short time. 2. The specification of the teach pendant is not correct compared with the controller.
SRVO-105.remedy: 1. Close the controller door, and press RESET. 2. Check the specification of the teach pendant is not correct compared with the controller. For instance, the teach pendant of the RIA/CE specification is used in the controller of non-RIA/CE specification, this alarm might occur. Connect the teach pendant corresponding to the controller. 3. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. (Paint) This is a general fault indicating the run chain is open for unknown reasons. Troubleshoot other error codes first.

SRVO-106.cause: 1. The controller door is opened or E.stop signals are detected for a short time. 2. The specification of the teach pendant is not correct compared with the controller.
SRVO-106.remedy: See the description for the SRVO-105 Door open or E.Stop.

SRVO-107.cause: The FET current for brake of an extended axis (brake number 2 or greater) exceeded the specification.
SRVO-107.remedy: Check the brake for zero or abnormally low impedance. Then check the brake cable. Then check 200VAC. Then check the servo amplifier or emergency stop control PCB if brake ports are used.

SRVO-108.cause: The error may have occurred in communication of the force sensor.
SRVO-108.remedy: See the error message about the force sensor.

SRVO-109.cause: 1. The acceleration sensor has not been connected. 2. A sensor other than acceleration sensor is detected.
SRVO-109.remedy: 1. Check connection of the connector of the connecting cable. 2. Check the shielding of the above cable is connected securely to the grounding plate. 3. Replace the above cable. 4. Replace the acceleration sensor. Before executing the remedy 5, perform a complete controller back up as image to save all your programs and settings. 5. Replace the main board, and restore the image backup.

SRVO-110.cause: 1. Pulse module channel setting is wrong on the axis. 2. GS3D-ACC sensor is disabled on the axis. 3. The axis assignment is already used on Line-tracking or Full-closed control. 4. Setting for GS3D-ACC sensor is wrong on the axis.
SRVO-110.remedy: 1. Please set servo parameter No.290 of the axis GS3D-ACC sensor is assigned with correct channel number on your pulse module(1-8), and cycle power. 2. Please set servo parameter No.10/Bit7=ON of the axis GS3D-ACC sensor is assigned, and cycle power. 3. You cannot assign GS3D-ACC sensor to the axis. Please assign GS3D-ACC sensor to another axis, and cycle power. 4. Please set following parameters, and cycle power. - $ENC_STAT[ch].$ENC_EXISTS = TRUE - $SCR.$ENC_AXIS[ch] = hardware axis number(1-56) (ch indicates channel number(1-8) of GS3D-ACC sensor on your pulse module).

SRVO-111.cause: Follow-up time is over when softfloat is OFF. (When $SFLT_ERRTYP=0)
SRVO-111.remedy: 1. Check whether external force is not applied to the robot before the softfloat is turned on. 2. Check whether the robot does not move as posture greatly changes during softfloat. 3. If needed, make $SFLT_FUPTIM larger.

SRVO-112.cause: Follow-up time is over when softfloat is OFF. (When $SFLT_ERRTYP=1)
SRVO-112.remedy: See the description for the SRVO-111 Softfloat time out.

SRVO-113.cause: While Cartesian Softfloat is being executed, the position error on the rectangular coordinates becomes greater than the tolerance that is set by the user.
SRVO-113.remedy: Find and remove the cause of the position error becoming greater. Or, make the tolerance larger, turn off and then turn on the controller. The tolerance is the value of the following system variables. X direction [mm]: $PARAM_GROUP[].$CB_IX Y direction [mm]: $PARAM_GROUP[].$CB_IY Z direction [mm]: $PARAM_GROUP[].$CB_IZ

SRVO-114.cause: A singularity was detected during robot motion.
SRVO-114.remedy: Re-teach the program points, use WJNT, or use JOINT MOTYPE.

SRVO-115.cause: The linear path passes outside of the axis limit.
SRVO-115.remedy: Re-teach program points, or use JOINT MOTYPE

SRVO-116.cause: One or more of the robot axes have exceeded an axis soft limit while executing SOFFLOAT.
SRVO-116.remedy: Jog the robot within the limits to resume. Adjust the program or process to keep robot axes within limits, or increase the axis limits.

SRVO-117.cause: Machinelock has been set on a group that is using the same brake number as a different group that is not machinelocked.
SRVO-117.remedy: 1. Set machinelock for all groups using the common brake. 2. Change brake connections so the same brake number is not used by different groups.

SRVO-118.cause: This error indicates that an error occurs during SFIGET execution.
SRVO-118.remedy: Perform an action according to the number that is displayed in the alarm message. 5: The schedule number is not specified or abnormal schedule number other than 1~10 integral value is specified. Specify the correct softfloat schedule number with SFIGET. 1,2,3,4: This error indicates that the software internal error occurs during SFIGET execution. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-119.cause: Override is not 100 % when execute SFIGET program.
SRVO-119.remedy: Set override 100% and re-execute SFIGET program again.

SRVO-120.cause: The difference between the integrator torque just before soft float execution starts and $SFLT_GRP. $SFLT_IVAL exceeded a specified value ($SFLT_GRP. $SFIVALLIM).
SRVO-120.remedy: Execute SFIGET program again, or set $SFLT_GRP. $SFIVALLIM more larger.

SRVO-121.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-122.cause: The last angle update request does not match the current angle.
SRVO-122.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-123.cause: The rotation speed of fan motor on backplane unit has slowed down. Number in the bracket indicates which fan is abnormal. (1): fan above the slot1 (2): fan above the slot2 (3): both fans
SRVO-123.remedy: 1. Check the fan motor and its cables. Replace them if necessary. 2. Replace the backplane unit. Before executing the remedy 3, perform a complete controller back up as image to save all your programs and settings. 3. Replace the main board, and restore the image backup. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note If SRVO-014 appears after SRVO-123, refer SRVO-014.

SRVO-124.cause: If 'SRVO-024 Move Error excess' Alarm occurs and the group is not calibrated, this alarm is posted too.
SRVO-124.remedy: Refer to the Remedy of SRVO-024

SRVO-125.cause: The quick stop speed is too high.
SRVO-125.remedy: Reduce the speed when a quick stop is executed.

SRVO-126.cause: The program was over during the process of quick stop.

SRVO-127.cause: Unsupported power supply software is loaded.

SRVO-130.cause: Heat sink temperature of the main circuit of the Power Supply (αiPS) has risen abnormally.
SRVO-130.remedy: 1. Check the rotation of the cooling fan of the Power Supply (αiPS). 2. Decrease the duty cycle of operation. 3. Replace the Power Supply (αiPS).

SRVO-131.cause: The control power supply voltage on the Power Supply (αiPS) is abnormally low.
SRVO-131.remedy: 1. Check the input power supply. 2. Replace the Power Supply (αiPS).

SRVO-132.cause: The current in the main power circuit of the servo amplifier exceeded specification.

SRVO-133.cause: The cooling fan for the Control circuit of the Power Supply (αiPS) stopped.
SRVO-133.remedy: 1. Check the status of the cooling fan. And replace it if it was abnormal. 2. Replace the Power Supply (αiPS).

SRVO-134.cause: The DC voltage (DC link voltage) of the main circuit power supply on the Power Supply (αiPS) is abnormally low.
SRVO-134.remedy: 1. It is possible that an instant disconnection of power source causes this alarm. Check whether an instant disconnection occurred. 2. Verify that the input voltage to the controller is within the rated voltage. Verify that the transformer setting is correct. 3. Modify the program in order that robot and the auxiliary axis do not accelerate simultaneously in the system with the auxiliary axis. 4. After confirming steps 1-3, cycle power on the controller. SRVO-134 requires the power to be cycled in order to clear the servo alarm. If alarm remains, proceed to step 5. 5. Replace the E-stop unit. 6. Replace the 6-axis amplifier. 7. Replace the Power Supply (aiPS). Note: You need to cycle power to release this alarm Note: You need to cycle power to release this alarm. (Paint) Troubleshoot other faults first if any are posted. Possible causes include: low supply voltage, missing supply phase, incorrect transformer tap setting, bad transformer, bad estop unit.

SRVO-135.cause: The cooling fan for the Control circuit stopped.
SRVO-135.remedy: 1. Replace the internal fan motor of the auxiliary servo amplifier that is indicated by the alarm message. 2. Replace the servo amplifier that is indicated by the alarm message.

SRVO-136.cause: The servo amplifier DC current (DC link voltage) is abnormally low.
SRVO-136.remedy: • This alarm occurred when robot is moving. 1. Check the input voltage to the controller is within the rated voltage and no phase is lack. And check the setting of the transformer is correct. 2. It is possible that an instant disconnection of power source causes this alarm. Check whether an instant disconnection occurred. 3. Replace the E-stop unit. 4. Replace the servo amplifier. • If this alarm occurred before the magnetic contactor is turned on: 1. Check whether the circuit breaker in the E-stop unit is OFF. If it is OFF, check the servo amplifier and the wiring between the servo amplifier and the E-stop unit. If anything is abnormal, replace it. Else turn on the breaker. 2. Check the input voltage to the controller is within the rated voltage and no phase is lack. And check the setting of the transformer is correct. 3. Replace the E-stop unit. 4. Replace the servo amplifier. • In an auxiliary axis system and if this alarm occurred right after the EMERGENCY STOP button was pressed, check whether the auxiliary axis unit is installed correctly. (Paint) See SRVO-134.

SRVO-138.cause: A Pulsecoder signal error was detected by the software. The probable cause is noise or a failure (disconnection) in the Pulsecoder internal circuit.
SRVO-138.remedy: 1. If a normal operation can be resumed by turning the controller power off and on again, it is likely that the cause is noise. Enhance the shielding of the Pulsecoder cable. 2. If a normal operation cannot be resumed by cycle power, the Pulsecoder is defective. Replace it, and perform mastering.

SRVO-141.cause: A servomotor's built-in thermostat was actuated.

SRVO-142.remedy: If the robot is overloaded or the duty cycle exceeds specification, this alarm occurs. Check the regenerative discharge transistor. Check the thermostat on the servo amplifier after the servo amplifier has cooled. It should not be open. If the problem persists, replace the servo amplifier. Check the controller cabinet fans for blocked filters; clean them if necessary.

SRVO-143.cause: Input power applied to the amplifier has been lost.
SRVO-143.remedy: Check the connections and cables of the input power.

SRVO-144.cause: The DC voltage of the main circuit power supply is excessively low.

SRVO-145.cause: This alarm indicates a problem with the back-up charge circuit for the amplifier.

SRVO-146.cause: The DC voltage of the main circuit power supply is too low.
SRVO-146.remedy: Check each interphase voltage of the three-phase voltage (200 VAC) applied to the servo amplifier. If the applied voltage is found to be 170 VAC or less, check the input power supply voltage. Replace the servo amplifier.

SRVO-147.cause: This alarm indicates a problem with the back-up charge circuit for the amplifier.
SRVO-147.remedy: 1. Check the cable between the servo amplifier (CN1) and the MCC. Replace it if necessary. 2. For a model using the B cabinet, check whether the transformer fuses (F1 and F3) have blown. 3. Replace the printed circuit board for emergency stop control. 4. Replace the servo amplifier.

SRVO-148.cause: The current in the main power circuit of the servo amplifier exceeded specification.
SRVO-148.remedy: Disconnect the motor power wires from the servo amplifier and turn on power. If an HCAL occurs, replace the transistor module or servo amplifier. Measure the resistance between GND and U, V, W individually on the cable terminals. If shorted, determine if the cable or motor is bad. Check the resistance between U-V, V-W, and W-U using a measuring instrument sensitive enough to detect small resistances at the cable terminations. If the resistances are the same, replace the servo amplifier. If the resistances are different, determine if the cable or motor is bad. If the problem persists, replace the SIF module on the axis control for the defective axis.

SRVO-149.cause: An excessively high current flowed through the main circuit of a servo amplifier.

SRVO-150.cause: The cooling fan for the control circuit stopped.
SRVO-150.remedy: Check the fan. Replace it if necessary.

SRVO-151.cause: The cooling fan for the control circuit stopped.

SRVO-152.remedy: 1. The IPM might be overheated. Reset the emergency stop after approximately ten minutes. Disconnect the power lines from the terminals on the amplifier, and check the insulation of PE from U, V, and W. 2. If there are short circuits, disconnect the motor connector power lines and check the insulation of PE from U, V, and W. 1) Replace the motor if U, V, and W short-circuit with PE. 2) Replace the power lines if U, V, and W do not short-circuit with PE. 3. Noise on the actual current (IR, IS) running in the amplifier module might cause this alarm. Remove this noise such as with taking ground of sealed earth. 4. Replace the amplifier.

SRVO-153.cause: The main circuit could not be charged within the specified time.
SRVO-153.remedy: 1. A short circuit might have occurred in the DC link. Check the connection. 2. The charging current control resistor might be faulty. Replace the E-Stop unit. 3. Replace the servo amplifier.

SRVO-154.cause: The DC voltage of the main circuit power supply is abnormally high.

SRVO-155.cause: The energy produced by regenerative discharge is excessive.

SRVO-156.cause: Abnormally high current flowed through the main circuit of the servo amplifier.
SRVO-156.remedy: Refer to the remedy of SRVO-045.

SRVO-157.cause: The charge of the capacitor of DC link voltage on the servo amplifier could not finish within specified time.
SRVO-157.remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. (Paint) Troubleshoot other faults first if any are posted. Possible causes include: low supply voltage, missing supply phase, incorrect transformer tap setting, bad transformer, bad estop unit.

SRVO-160.cause: The emergency stop button on the operator panel was pressed, or the external emergency stop function was activated. EMGIN1 and EMGINC are not strapped to each other. Or, EMGIN2 and EMGINC are not strapped to each other.
SRVO-160.remedy: Release the emergency stop button. If the external emergency stop function has been activated, remove the cause. If no cause can be found, and no jumper is installed between EMGIN1 and EMGINC or between EMGIN2 and EMGINC on the terminal block of the emergency stop control printed circuit board, but cables are connected to the terminals, check the cables.

SRVO-161.cause: The teach pendant deadman switch is released or the fence circuit is open.
SRVO-161.remedy: Press teach pendant deadman switch or determine the cause of the fence and then press RESET.

SRVO-162.cause: The deadman switch is released, the fence circuit is open, the operator panel ESTOP button is pressed, or the external ESTOP signal is received.
SRVO-162.remedy: Remove the cause then press RESET.

SRVO-163.cause: Different DSM (Digital Servo Module) are mounted on the controller
SRVO-163.remedy: Change the DSM hardware to be same.

SRVO-164.cause: The DSM (Digital Servo Module) type is mismatched to the servo parameter version.
SRVO-164.remedy: Change the current DSP-IV module to DSP_V or initialize the robot library again to load the correct servo parameter file.

SRVO-165.cause: The operator panel emergency stop push button is pressed and miswiring on SVON2 or EMG2 is detected.
SRVO-165.remedy: Power off. Correct the wiring on SVON2 or EMG2. Power on. Twist the operator panel emergency stop push button clockwise to release. Press RESET.

SRVO-166.cause: The teach pendant emergency stop push button is pressed and miswiring on SVON2 or EMG2 is detected.
SRVO-166.remedy: Power off. Correct the wiring on SVON2 or EMG2. Power on. Twist the teach pendant emergency stop push button clockwise to release. Press RESET.

SRVO-167.cause: The teach pendant deadman switch is released while the teach pendant is enabled. And miswiring on SVON2 or EMG2 is detected.
SRVO-167.remedy: Power off. Correct the wiring on SVON2 or EMG2. Power on. Press teach pendant deadman switch. Press RESET.

SRVO-168.cause: Refer to SRVO-007 or SRVO-019. And miswiring on SVON2 or EMG2 is detected.
SRVO-168.remedy: Power off. Correct the wiring on SVON2 or EMG2. Power on. And Refer to SRVO-007 or SRVO-019.

SRVO-169.cause: The external emergency stop signal or the servo disconnect signal or SVOFF signal is asserted.
SRVO-169.remedy: 1. Release the external emergency stop signal and press RESET. 2. If the servo disconnect signal or SVOFF signal is used, release it and press RESET.

SRVO-170.cause: The number of DSPs on the axis card is lacking.
SRVO-170.remedy: 1. Check the software axis config (FSSB line number). 2. Replace the axis card with a card has enough DSPs for your system. 3. Add an auxiliary axis board.

SRVO-171.cause: The motor can not rotate as fast as the calculated speed required for the current motion.

SRVO-172.cause: The motor cannot rotate as fast as the calculated speed required for the current motion.
SRVO-172.remedy: This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

SRVO-173.cause: The motor cannot rotate as fast as the calculated speed required for the current motion.
SRVO-173.remedy: This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

SRVO-174.cause: The motor cannot accelerate as much as the calculated acceleration required for the current motion.
SRVO-174.remedy: This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

SRVO-176.cause: An incorrect CJ mode was used.
SRVO-176.remedy: This is an internal motion error. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-179.cause: The torque of the axis has exceeded the limit.

SRVO-180.cause: Controllable axis does not exist on any group.
SRVO-180.remedy: Please execute aux axis setting at controlled start. Note: Perform a power cycle to release this alarm.

SRVO-181.cause: The robot was going to move while identifying the payload.
SRVO-181.remedy: Press RESET. Be careful not to move the robot while identifying the payload.

SRVO-182.message: Needed init. has not been done
SRVO-182.cause: This is an error internal to the system. A system variable or internal work memory has not been initialized normally.
SRVO-182.remedy: 1. Turn the power off and on again. 2. If the alarm is still issued, document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-183.remedy: Remove the factor that turned servo off, and press the RESET button.

SRVO-184.cause: The data area that this instruction tried to use had been locked by another task.
SRVO-184.remedy: 1. If this alarm is occurred when the Payload Estimation is restarted, execute the Payload Estimation after it waits for a while. 2. Execute the Payload Estimation after power cycle. 3. If the alarm is still issued, document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-185.cause: This is an error internal to the system.
SRVO-185.remedy: 1. Execute the Payload Estimation after power cycle. 2. If the alarm is still issued, document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-186.message: Needed Data has not been got
SRVO-186.cause: This is an error internal to the system.
SRVO-186.remedy: 1. Execute the Payload Estimation after power cycle. 2. If the alarm is still issued document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-187.cause: Estimating the load information of this type requires specifying the mass of the load.
SRVO-187.remedy: Specify the mass of the load before Payload Estimation.

SRVO-188.cause: The system could not allocate the enough memory area on the DRAM for Payload Estimation.
SRVO-188.remedy: 1. Execute the Payload Estimation after power cycle. 2. If the alarm is still issued, you need to update the memory size of DRAM. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-189.cause: The error may have occurred in communication of the force sensor.
SRVO-189.remedy: See the error message about the force sensor.

SRVO-190.cause: A sensor other than Serial Pulsecoder is detected.
SRVO-190.remedy: 1. Check connection of the connector of the connecting cable. 2. Check the shielding of the above cable is connected securely to the grounding plate. 3. Replace the above cable. 4. Replace the Serial Pulsecoder. Before executing the remedy 5, perform a complete controller back up as image to save all your programs and settings. 5. Replace the main board, and restore the image backup.

SRVO-191.cause: The motion command exceeded the specification.
SRVO-191.remedy: This is an internal motion error. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative. Note You need to cycle power to release this alarm.

SRVO-192.cause: The fence circuit is open or the SVON input circuit is open.
SRVO-192.remedy: Close the fence circuit or SVON input circuit, and then press RESET.

SRVO-193.cause: The SVON input circuit is open.
SRVO-193.remedy: Close SVON input circuit, and then press RESET. Refer to the maintenance manual for details.

SRVO-194.cause: A servo disconnect input signal is turned off.
SRVO-194.remedy: 1. If a servo disconnect switch is connected, release the switch, and then press RESET. 2. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SRVO-195.cause: The Non Teacher Enabling Device is released or servo is disconnected.
SRVO-195.remedy: Press the Non Teacher Enabling Device or connect servo, and then press RESET. Refer to the maintenance manual for details.

SRVO-196.cause: The fence circuit is open or the SVON input circuit is open and mis-wiring on the SVON is detected.
SRVO-196.remedy: Power off. Correct the wiring on SVON. Close the fence circuit or SVON input circuit, and then press RESET.

SRVO-197.cause: The SVON input circuit is open and mis-wiring on SVON is detected.
SRVO-197.remedy: Power off. Correct the wiring on SVON. Close the SVON input circuit, and then press RESET.

SRVO-198.cause: The external emergency stop push button is pressed and mis-wiring on SVON is detected.
SRVO-198.remedy: Power off. Correct the wiring on SVON. If using external emergency stop, clear the source of the fault, and press RESET. If not, the check wiring at EMGIN1, EMGIN2, and EMGINC on the EMG control PCB. Check for 100 VAC input to the EMG control PCB.

SRVO-199.cause: A Controlled Stop has been done.
SRVO-199.remedy: After this alarm, a Fence open or SVOFF input alarm is detected. See the remedy of those alarms for more information.

SRVO-200.cause: The control box fan motor has failed.
SRVO-200.remedy: Check and/or replace the fan. Refer to the maintenance manual for details.

SRVO-201.cause: The EMERGENCY STOP button on the operator's panel/operation box was pressed, but the EMERGENCY STOP line was not disconnected.
SRVO-201.remedy: 1. Release the operator panel EMERGENCY STOP button, then press RESET. 2. When the operator panel EMERGENCY STOP button is pushed again, and this alarm occurs again, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note: This alarm might occur when the emergency stop button is pushed slowly. In this case, the above remedy 2 is unnecessary.

SRVO-202.cause: The EMERGENCY STOP button on the Teach Pendant was pressed, but the EMERGENCY STOP line was not disconnected.
SRVO-202.remedy: 1. Release the teach pendant EMERGENCY STOP button, then press RESET. 2. When the teach pendant EMERGENCY STOP button is pushed again, and this alarm occurs again, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note: This alarm might occur when the emergency stop button is pushed slowly. In this case, the above remedy 2 is unnecessary.

SRVO-203.cause: The SVON signal line was opened while the SVEMG wiring is incorrect.
SRVO-203.remedy: Correct any SVEMG wiring errors. Input an SVON signal, and turn the power off and then on again. Refer to the maintenance manual for details.

SRVO-204.cause: The external emergency stop push button was pressed, but the EMERGENCY STOP line was not disconnected.
SRVO-204.remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note: Need power cycle to release this alarm. (Paint) In addition to the above comments, this may be the interlock to the paint system. See applicable system drawings.

SRVO-205.cause: The fence circuit was opened, but the EMERGENCY STOP line was not disconnected.
SRVO-205.remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note Need power cycle to release this alarm.

SRVO-206.cause: The teach pendant deadman switch was released while the teach pendant was enabled, but the EMERGENCY STOP line was not disconnected.
SRVO-206.remedy: Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note: Need power cycle to release this alarm.

SRVO-207.message: TP switch abnormal or Door open
SRVO-207.cause: The EMERGENCY STOP line has been disconnected although there is no e-stop factor.
SRVO-207.remedy: 1. Replace the teach pendant. 2. Replace the teach pendant cable. 3. Replace the operator's panel/operation box. 4. Replace the E-stop unit. 5. Replace the servo amplifier.

SRVO-208.cause: The FET current for the brake of an extended axis (brake number 2 or greater) exceeded the specification.
SRVO-208.remedy: Check the brake for zero or abnormally low impedance. Then check the brake cable. Then check 200VAC. Then check servo amplifier or emergency stop control PCB if brake ports are used. Refer to the maintenance manual for details.

SRVO-209.cause: An abnormality of the emergency stop line of robot 2 or later was detected.
SRVO-209.remedy: 1. Replace the E-Stop unit of robot 2 or later. 2. Replace the servo amplifier of robot 2 or later. 3. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-210.cause: Mis-wiring of SVEMG signal on Extended robot is detected.
SRVO-210.remedy: Power off. Correct the wiring on SVEMG on controller of Extended robot. Close fence circuit and then press reset.

SRVO-211.cause: The teach pendant was disabled while the mode switch was set in the T1 or T2 position and robot 1 and 2 were disconnected. Alternatively, there is a failure in the hardware.
SRVO-211.remedy: 1. Set the teach pendant enable/disable switch to on, and press RESET. 2. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-212.cause: The fuse on Panel PCB is blown

SRVO-213.cause: A fuse (FUSE) on the emergency stop board has blown.
SRVO-213.remedy: Replace the fuse (FUSE2) on the emergency stop board or the emergency stop board. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. (Paint) Make sure the EXT24 and EXT0 are either supplied or jumped to INT signals on the ESTOP Unit.

SRVO-214.cause: The fuse on the servo amplifier has blown. Number in the bracket indicates which 6ch amplifier is abnormal.
SRVO-214.remedy: Replace the fuse on the servo amplifier. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SRVO-215.cause: The fuse FUSE1 on the brake unit has blown. Number in the bracket indicates which 6ch amplifier the brake unit is connected.
SRVO-215.remedy: Replace this fuse after replacing the brake cable because it might be defective. (If this fuse has blown, it may be caused by some defect of the brake cable.) (Paint) The 6-ch AMP sees that the brake fuse signal is active via the connection on CRM97. Check the process axis brake control PCB/fuse.

SRVO-216.cause: The current flowing through the robot cable has exceeded its limit. Number in the bracket indicates which amplifier number is abnormal.
SRVO-216.remedy: 1. Slow the motion of the robot where possible. Check the robot operation conditions. If the robot is used with a condition exceeding the duty or load weight robot rating, reduce the load condition value to the specification range. 2. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SRVO-217.cause: The emergency stop board is not found when the controller power is turned on.
SRVO-217.remedy: 1. Check whether fuse FUSE1 on the emergency stop board has blown. If the fuse has blown, check and correct the cause then replace the fuse. 2. Check the cable between emergency stop board and main board. Replace them if necessary. 3. Replace the E-Stop unit. Before executing the remedy 4, perform a complete controller back up as image to save all your programs and settings. 4. Replace the main board, and restore the image backup. (Paint) This alarm is posted when either the estop board or Safety I/O card is missing from the Safety buss. Check/replace the cable and Estop Board/Safety I/O board.

SRVO-218.cause: The external emergency stop signal or the servo disconnect signal is asserted.
SRVO-218.remedy: 1. Release the external emergency stop signal and press RESET. 2. If the servo disconnect signal is used, release it and press RESET.

SRVO-220.cause: The fuse for SDI has blown.
SRVO-220.remedy: Replace the fuse on the main board or main board itself. Refer to the Mate Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SRVO-221.cause: A controlled axis card corresponding to the set number of axes ($SCR_GRP.$AXISORDER) is not mounted.
SRVO-221.remedy: 1. Check whether the set number of axes is valid. If the number is invalid, set the correct number. 2. Replace the axis control card with a card corresponding to the set number of axes.

SRVO-222.cause: The servo amplifiers were not found at the power up sequence. Numbers in parentheses show the group number and the axis number in the group. (In software version V9.10P/14 or earlier, there is only one number in parentheses, and it means the amplifier number.)
SRVO-222.remedy: 1. When any LED on the servo amplifier does not light with the power supply of the controller turned on, the power is not supplied to the servo amplifier. Confirm whether there is neither disconnecting nor loosening in each connector on the servo amplifier and the E-Stop unit. 2. Turn off the power of the controller, disconnect the Pulsecoder cable JF1,JF2 from the servo amplifier and turn on the power of the controller again. If this alarm does not occur, the Pulsecoder cable may have a ground fault. (The LED of the servo amplifier may display blinking ‘ —’ in this case.) 3. Check whether the servo amplifier for auxiliary axis for the R-30iA controller is connected to the R-30iB controller. 4. Check the software axis config (FSSB line number, hardware start axis number). 5. Replace the servo amplifier for auxiliary axis. 6. Replace the 6-axis servo amplifier. 7. Replace the optical fiber cable. 8. Replace the servo card or the auxiliary axis servo card.

SRVO-223.cause: A servo DSP initialization failure occurred due to hardware failure or wrong software setting. Then, the software entered DSP dry run mode. The first number indicates the cause of the failure. The second number is extra information.
SRVO-223.remedy: Perform an action according to the first number that is displayed in the alarm message. 1: This is a warning due to $scr.$startup_cnd=12. 2,3,4,7: Replace a servo card. 5: Invalid ATR setting. Software axis config (FSSB line number, amplifier axis number) might be wrong. 6: SRVO-180 occurs simultaneously. Controllable axis does not exist on any group. Execute aux axis setting to add axis at controlled start. 8,10: SRVO-058 (FSSB init error) occurs simultaneously. Follow the remedy of SRVO-058. 9: There is no amplifier that is connected to the servo card. • Check the hardware connection. • Check the optical fiber cable. • Check whether the servo amplifier power is supplied. • Check whether the fuse on the servo amplifier has blown. • Replace the optical fiber cable. • Replace the servo amplifier. 11: Invalid axisorder setting. Non-existing axis number is specified. Software axis config (FSSB line number) might be wrong or auxiliary axis board is necessary. 12: SRVO-059 (Servo amp init error) occurs simultaneously. Follow the remedy of SRVO-059. 13,14,15: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC representative. 16: SRVO-181 (Up to 4 aux axes allowed in a group) occurs simultaneously. Follow the remedy of SRVO-181. 17: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your local FANUC representative. (In software version 7DF1/14 or earlier, this alarm can occur also when software axis config is wrong. Check the software axis config (FSSB line number).) Note You need to cycle power to release this alarm.

SRVO-224.cause: Hardware slot of the auxiliary axis board has been changed.
SRVO-224.remedy: Please verify this change is valid. If this change is due to a simple mistake, please restore the hardware configuration to its original condition.

SRVO-225.cause: This servo card is not supported.
SRVO-225.remedy: Replace the servo card according to the number that is displayed in the alarm message. 1: Servo card, 2: Auxiliary axis board 1, 3: Auxiliary axis board 2

SRVO-226.cause: Mismatch between the motor current setting and the amplifier current is detected.
SRVO-226.remedy: Please change the motor current limit to a proper value.

SRVO-230.cause: 1. A failure occurred in chain 1 (+24V)/chain2(0V) of emergency stop circuit. 2. There is a possibility that the specification of the teach pendant is incorrect when occurring immediately after turning on of the power supply. For instance, this might occur if the teach pendant of non-RIA/CE specification is connected with the controller of the RIA/CE specification.
SRVO-230.remedy: 1. In the above case 2, connect a correct teach pendant. 2. Confirm the history of the alarm on the Alarm Log screen. If occurring with either 'Operator panel E-stop', 'Teach pendant E-stop' or 'Deadman switch released', the emergency stop button is released, and it presses again. For deadman switch, the deadman switch is gripped once and it released again. Chain abnormal state was released if occurring SRVO-236 'Chain failure is repaired'. Release e-stop button, deadman and press reset button. 3. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After these measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary. a. Press the emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel once and release it. b. Press F4 'RES_1CH' on the Alarm Active screen. c. Press RESET. (Paint) This alarm occurs when only one of the two contacts on the safety circuit close. Verify that the EA, EG, and EE signal inputs are all closed at the Estop Board.

SRVO-231.cause: 1. A failure occurred in chain 1 (+24V)/chain2(0V) of emergency stop circuit. 2. There is a possibility that the specification of the teach pendant is incorrect when occurring immediately after turning on of the power supply. For instance, this might occur if the teach pendant of non-RIA/CE specification is connected with the controller of the RIA/CE specification.
SRVO-231.remedy: See the description for the SRVO-230 Chain 1 abnormal. (Paint) This alarm occurs when only one of the two contacts on the safety circuit close. Verify that the EA, EG, and EE signal inputs are all closed at the Estop Board.

SRVO-232.cause: The NTED (non-teacher enabling device) was detected.
SRVO-232.remedy: 1. Press the NTED (non-teacher enabling device), and then press the reset key. 2. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SRVO-233.cause: The mode switch is set in the T1 or T2 position, and the teach pendant is disabled. Alternatively, the controller door is open. There is also a failure in the hardware.
SRVO-233.remedy: 1. After setting the teach pendant enable/disable switch to on, close the controller door, and press the reset key. 2. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. (Paint) If you should be in Auto mode, look at the Mode selector inputs. If you should be in Teach mode, verify the pendant is enabled then replace the teach pendant.

SRVO-234.cause: The deadman switch on the teach pendant was released.

SRVO-235.cause: A temporary chain failure was detected.
SRVO-235.remedy: 1. Press the e-stop button on the teach pendant or the operator panel again. If occurring SRVO-236 'Chain failure is repaired'. Release e-stop button and Press RESET. 2. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After these measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary. a. The emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel is pressed once, and released. b. F4 'RES_1CH' is pressed on the Alarm Active screen. c. The reset button is pressed.

SRVO-236.remedy: When the system checked for the chain failure again, the chain failure had been removed. Press RESET.

SRVO-237.cause: An attempt to reset the chain failure failed.
SRVO-237.remedy: Refer to the remedy of SRVO-230.

SRVO-238.cause: A single chain 1 (+24V) failure occurred when the SVON (Servo ON/OFF switch) input was asserted.
SRVO-238.remedy: Repair the circuit of chain 1 (+24V) on the SVON hardware. Set CHAIN FAILURE detection to TRUE on the SYSTEM/CONFIG screen. Press RESET on the teach pendant.

SRVO-239.cause: A single chain 2 (0V) failure occurred when a SVON (Servo ON/OFF switch) input was asserted.
SRVO-239.remedy: Repair the circuit of the chain 2 (0V) on SVON the hardware. Set CHAIN FAILURE detection to TRUE on the SYSTEM/CONFIG screen. Press RESET on the teach pendant.

SRVO-240.cause: Although the fence circuit was disconnected, the emergency stop line was not disconnected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.
SRVO-240.remedy: A problem exists with either the panel board, the e-stop unit or other related parts. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After these measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary. 1. Press the emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel once and then release it. 2. Press F4 'RES_1CH' on the Alarm Active screen. 3. Press the RESET button.

SRVO-241.cause: Although the fence circuit was disconnected, the emergency stop line was not disconnected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.
SRVO-241.remedy: A problem exists with either the panel board, the e-stop unit or other related parts are thought. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After these measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary. 1. Press the emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel once and release it. 2. Press F4 'RES_1CH' on the Alarm Active screen. 3. Press the RESET button.

SRVO-242.cause: Although the external emergency stop circuit was disconnected, the emergency stop line was not disconnected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.
SRVO-242.remedy: The panel board, the e-stop unit or other related parts might be faulty. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary. 1) The emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel is pressed once, and released. 2) F4 'RES_1CH' is pressed on the Alarm Active screen. 3) The reset button is pressed.

SRVO-243.cause: Although the external emergency stop circuit was disconnected, the emergency stop line was not disconnected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.
SRVO-243.remedy: The panel board, the e-stop unit or other related parts might be faulty. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After these measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary. 1. The emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel is pressed once, and released. 2. F4 'RES_1CH' is pressed on the Alarm Active screen. 3. The reset button is pressed.

SRVO-244.cause: An abnormal chain occurred with the robot displayed in ().
SRVO-244.remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-230.

SRVO-245.cause: An abnormal chain occurred with the robot displayed in ().
SRVO-245.remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-230.

SRVO-246.cause: An abnormal chain occurred with the robot displayed in ().
SRVO-246.remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-230.

SRVO-247.cause: An abnormal chain occurred with the robot displayed in ().
SRVO-247.remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-230.

SRVO-248.cause: The status of two DIs of DEADMAN switch do not match.
SRVO-248.remedy: 1. Release both deadman switches at once. If SRVO-236 Chain failure is repaired occurred, there is no hardware problem. This alarm could occur when deadman switch is pressed halfway. 2. When SRVO-236 does not occur, please replace hardware in following order. - Teach pendant - Cable between teach pendant and the emergency stop board - the emergency stop board - Cable between the emergency stop board and main board. 3. After measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary. • The emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel is pressed once, and released. • F4 'RES_1CH' is pressed on the Alarm Active screen. • The reset button is pressed.

SRVO-250.cause: Status of MAINON1 signal is still OFF even if SVEMG is ON It is abnormal of E.STOP circuit
SRVO-250.remedy: Repair the circuit of E.Stop hardware Power off/on again

SRVO-251.cause: An abnormality was detected in the internal relay (DB relay) of the servo amplifier.

SRVO-252.cause: An abnormality was detected in the current detection circuit inside the servo amplifier.

SRVO-253.cause: An overheat was detected inside the servo amplifier.
SRVO-253.remedy: Check that the cooling fan is working properly, or replace the servo amplifier.

SRVO-254.cause: Welding occurs at a relay in E-STOP circuit.

SRVO-255.cause: Welding occurs at relay in E-STOP circuit.

SRVO-256.cause: MCC control output is abnormal in the 6ch. amplifier.

SRVO-260.cause: Although the NTED circuit was disconnected, the emergency stop line was not disconnected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.
SRVO-260.remedy: Refer to the remedy of SRVO-240.

SRVO-261.cause: Although the NTED circuit was disconnected, the emergency stop line was not disconnected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.
SRVO-261.remedy: Refer to the remedy of SRVO-240.

SRVO-262.cause: Although the SVDISC circuit was disconnected, the emergency stop line was not disconnected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.
SRVO-262.remedy: Refer to the remedy of SRVO-240.

SRVO-263.cause: Although the SVDISC circuit was disconnected, the emergency stop line was not disconnected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.
SRVO-263.remedy: Refer to the remedy of SRVO-240.

SRVO-264.cause: The emergency stop unit is abnormal.
SRVO-264.remedy: There is a possibility of the connector loosening or the circuit faults in the emergency stop unit. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note: You need to cycle power to release this alarm.

SRVO-265.cause: The emergency stop unit is abnormal.
SRVO-265.remedy: The emergency stop unit circuitry is faulty. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SRVO-266.remedy: There is miswiring of the FENCE signal. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After these measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary. 1. The emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel is pressed once, and released. 2. F4 'RES_1CH' is pressed on the Alarm Active screen. 3. The reset button is pressed.

SRVO-267.remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-266.

SRVO-268.remedy: There is miswiring of the SVOFF signal. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After these measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary. 1. The emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel is pressed once, and released. 2. F4 'RES_1CH' is pressed on the Alarm Active screen. 3. The reset button is pressed. (Paint) The optional manual brake release function uses this input before releasing the brakes. The multi-arm robot isolate function uses this input to isolate a robot. See circuitry in the robot-specific Maintenance Addendums for cables, brake board, and isolate board replacement.

SRVO-269.remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-268. (Paint) The optional manual brake release function uses this input before releasing the brakes. The multi-arm robot isolate function uses this input to isolate a robot. See circuitry in the Robot-Specific Maintenance Addendum for cables, brake board, and isolate board replacement.

SRVO-270.remedy: The EXEMG signal is miswired. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After these measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary. 1. The emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel is pressed once, and released. 2. F4 'RES_1CH' is pressed on the Alarm Active screen. 3. The reset button is pressed. (Paint) This alarm occurs when only one of the two contacts on the external emergency stop safety circuit close. Verify that the EE signal inputs are all closed at the Estop Board.

SRVO-271.remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-270. (Paint) This alarm occurs when only one of the two contacts on the external emergency stop safety circuit close. Verify that the EE signal inputs are all closed at the Estop Board.

SRVO-272.remedy: The SVDISC signal is miswired. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After these measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary. 1. The emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel is pressed once, and released. 2. F4 'RES_1CH' is pressed on the Alarm Active screen. 3. The reset button is pressed.

SRVO-273.remedy: The SVDISC signal is miswired. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After these measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary. 1. The emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel is pressed once, and released. 2. F4 'RES_1CH' is pressed on the Alarm Active screen. 3. The reset button is pressed.

SRVO-274.remedy: The NTED signal is miswired. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. After these measures, the release operation of chain abnormal state is necessary. 1. The emergency stop button on the teach pendant or operator panel is pressed once, and released. 2. F4 'RES_1CH' is pressed on the Alarm Active screen. 3. The reset button is pressed.

SRVO-275.remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-274.

SRVO-276.cause: The robot cannot operate in T2 mode.
SRVO-276.remedy: Set the mode switch to the T1 or AUTO position.

SRVO-277.cause: The emergency stop line was not disconnected although the emergency stop button on the operator's panel was pressed.
SRVO-277.remedy: 1. Release the operator panel EMERGENCY STOP button, then cycle controller power again. 2. When the operator panel EMERGENCY STOP button is pushed again, and this alarm occurs again, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note 1. Need power cycle to release this alarm. 2. This alarm might occur when the emergency stop button is pushed too slowly. In this case, the above remedy 2 is unnecessary. (Paint) This alarm occurs when only one of the two contacts from the ACP mounted estop pushbutton circuit close. Also check the pendant estop button because they are in series.

SRVO-278.cause: The EMERGENCY STOP button on the Teach Pendant was pressed, but the EMERGENCY STOP line was not disconnected.
SRVO-278.remedy: 1. Release the TP EMERGENCY STOP button, then the controller power cycle again. 2. When the TP EMERGENCY STOP button is pushed again, and this alarm occurs again, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. Note 1. Need power cycle to release this alarm. 2. This alarm might occur when the emergency stop button is pushed too slowly. In this case, the above remedy 2 is unnecessary. (Paint) This alarm occurs when only one of the two contacts from the teach pendant estop pushbutton circuit close. Also check the ACP estop button because they are in series.

SRVO-279.cause: The Emergency stop circuit is abnormal.
SRVO-279.remedy: 1. Replace the Emergency Stop Unit. 2. Replace the Servo Amplifier. Note: Cycle controller power to release this alarm.

SRVO-280.cause: The SVOFF (servo off signal) was input. Note The paint controller is placed in this alarm state when using the manual brake release function. When the BRAKE ENABLE switch is placed in the ON position, this alarm is generated. If your controller is a paint controller with manual brake release functionality, make sure that the BRAKE ENABLE switch is in the OFF position before trying to reset this alarm.
SRVO-280.remedy: 1. Find out what caused the SVOFF to be input, and remove the cause. Press the RESET button. 2. If this alarm cannot be reset, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. (Paint) The optional manual brake release function uses this input before releasing the brakes. The multi-arm robot isolate function uses this input to isolate a robot. See circuitry in the Robot-Specific Maintenance Addendums for cables, brake board, and isolate board replacement.

SRVO-281.cause: When the SVOFF signal was asserted, an SVEMG error was detected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.
SRVO-281.remedy: If the RDY LED (green) is lit: 1. Check the switch and cable connected to 9 (EGS1) - 10 (EGS11) and 11 (EGS2) - 12 (EGS21) on operator panel terminal TBOP4. 2. Replace the panel board. 3. Replace the EStop unit. 4. Replace the servo amplifier. 5. Replace the connection cable between the EStop unit and the panel board. If the RDY LED (green) is not lit: 1. Replace the cable connecting between the main board (JRS11) and the panel board (JRS11). 2. Replace the panel board. Note: Before executing the next step, perform a complete controller back-up to save all of your programs and settings. Failure to perform this task could result in damage to the equipment or lost data. 3. Replace the main board. (Paint) The optional manual brake release function uses this input before releasing the brakes. The multi-arm robot isolate function uses this input to isolate a robot. See circuitry in the robot specific maintenance addendums for cables, brake board, and isolate board replacement. Note: If the SYST-067 Panel HSSB disconnect alarm occurs simultaneously or the RDY LED is turned off, the following alarms are also generated: • SRVO-001 Operator panel E-Stop • SRVO-004 Fence open • SRVO-007 External emergency stop • SRVO-204 External (SVEMG abnormal) E-Stop • SRVO-280 SVOFF input Check the alarm history display on the teach pendant.

SRVO-282.cause: Although the SVOFF (servo off signal) circuit was disconnected, the emergency stop line was not disconnected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.
SRVO-282.remedy: Refer to the remedy of SRVO-240.

SRVO-283.cause: Although the SVOFF (servo off signal) circuit was disconnected, the emergency stop line was not disconnected. The emergency stop circuit is faulty.
SRVO-283.remedy: Refer to the remedy of SRVO-240.

SRVO-286.cause: The emergency stop unit is abnormal.
SRVO-286.remedy: Refer to the remedy of SRVO-264. Note: Cycle controller power to release this alarm.

SRVO-287.cause: The emergency stop unit is abnormal.
SRVO-287.remedy: Refer to the remedy of SRVO-265.

SRVO-289.cause: A Smooth Stop has been done.
SRVO-289.remedy: After this alarm, such as operator panel E-stop alarm is detected. See the remedy of those alarms for more information.

SRVO-290.cause: The DC link current of the servo amplifier is abnormally high.
SRVO-290.remedy: Refer to the remedy of SRVO-045.

SRVO-291.cause: It was detected that the IPM element in the amplifier had overheated.
SRVO-291.remedy: 1. Check whether the amplifier fan rotates normally. 2. Decrease the duty cycle of operation. 3. If this symptom occurs frequently, replace the amplifier. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SRVO-292.cause: The external fan for the servo amplifier module (SVM, alpha iSV) is faulty.

SRVO-293.cause: The three-phase input power supply is abnormal or the Power Supply (αiPS) module is faulty.
SRVO-293.remedy: 1. Check the three-phase input power supply. 2. Replace the Power Supply (αiPS).

SRVO-294.cause: The external fan for the Power Supply (αiPS) is faulty.

SRVO-295.cause: A communication error occurred between the Power Supply (αiPS) and the servo amplifier.
SRVO-295.remedy: 1. Replace the 6–axis amplifier. 2. Replace the cable for communication the Power Supply (αiPS) and servo amplifier. 3. Replace the Power Supply (αiPS). 4. Replace the servo amplifier (αiSV).

SRVO-296.cause: 1. The cooling fan for the regenerative resistance of the Power Supply (αiPS) stops. 2. The use condition is too hard for the regenerative resistance of the Power Supply (αiPS).
SRVO-296.remedy: 1. Check the fan for the regenerative resistor is working. If it stops, replace the fan. 2. Lower the teaching speed in the program. 3. Replace the Power Supply (αiPS).

SRVO-297.cause: Three-phase input power supply voltage is low.
SRVO-297.remedy: 1. Check the voltage of the three-phase input power. 2. Replace the Power Supply (αiPS). 3. Replace the 6–axis amplifier. 4. Replace the E-stop unit. Refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information. (Paint) Troubleshoot other faults first if any are posted. Possible causes include: low supply voltage, missing supply phase, incorrect transformer tap setting, bad transformer, bad estop unit.

SRVO-298.cause: The speed calculated in the servo software is abnormal.
SRVO-298.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative. To reset the alarm condition requires turning the controller power off and on again. Note Need power cycle to release this alarm.

SRVO-299.remedy: The power has been automatically recovered. Press RESET to remove the alarm condition.

SRVO-300.cause: When the HBK setting is disabled, a hand-broken signal was detected.
SRVO-300.remedy: To remove the alarm condition, press RESET. Check whether the hand-broken signal circuit is connected to the robot. If the circuit is connected to the robot, enable the hand-broken setting.

SRVO-301.cause: When the HBK setting is disabled, a hand-broken signal was detected.
SRVO-301.remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-300.

SRVO-302.cause: When the HBK setting is disabled, a hand-broken signal was detected.
SRVO-302.remedy: To remove the alarm condition, press RESET. Check whether the hand-broken signal circuit is connected to the robot. If the circuit is connected to the robot, enable the hand-broken setting.

SRVO-303.cause: When the HBK setting is disabled, a hand-broken signal was detected.
SRVO-303.remedy: Refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-302.

SRVO-304.cause: The brake release signal of the C-flex robot was input.

SRVO-305.remedy: Turn off and on the controller power supply.

SRVO-306.cause: Displayed robot arm did not start up within a fixed time.
SRVO-306.remedy: Please confirm the robot arm is displayed with warning message.

SRVO-307.cause: The HBK setting has been enabled because HBK signal is closed.
SRVO-307.remedy: HBK signal has been closed when HBK setting is disabled. Therefore HBK setting has been enabled.

SRVO-310.cause: A current robot position that software calculates is abnormal.
SRVO-310.remedy: 1. Mastering data could be incorrect. Confirm whether incorrect backup data is restored or mastering has been executed at the wrong position. In that case, execute mastering. 2. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-311.cause: A communication error has occurred between the main board and Laser I/F Unit. (from main board to Laser I/F Unit.)

SRVO-312.cause: A communication error has occurred between the main board and Laser I/F Unit. (from Laser I/F Unit to main board.)

SRVO-313.cause: Communication was interrupted between the main board and Laser I/F Unit.

SRVO-314.cause: The servo amplifiers were not found at the power up sequence.

SRVO-315.cause: Magnetic Phase Detection (MPDT) for 3rd party motor failed. Probable causes are: 1. The motor power cable is disconnected. 2. The axis falls down by the gravity during performing of MPDT. 3. Other alarm occurs during performing of MPDT. 4. The motor cannot move due to large load or friction.
SRVO-315.remedy: 1. Check whether the motor power cable is connected correctly. 2. MPDT cannot be applied for gravity axis. If possible, change the posture. 3. Remove the reason of other alarms which occurred at same time. 4. Check whether the axis which requires to perform MPDT does not contact with any object. 5. Confirm that brake is not engaged.

SRVO-316.cause: Magnetic Phase Detection (MPDT) process time is up. Probable cause: 1. The axis fell down because of gravity during performing of MPDT. 2. Other alarms occurred during performing of MPDT.
SRVO-316.remedy: 1. MPDT cannot be applied for gravity axis. If possible, change the posture. 2. Remove the reason of other alarm which occurred at the same time.

SRVO-317.cause: Magnetic Phase Detection (MPDT) process cannot start because machine lock is enabled for that group.
SRVO-317.remedy: Disable machine lock for that group.

SRVO-318.cause: Magnetic Phase Detection (MPDT) process cannot start because servo ready (SRDY) is off.
SRVO-318.remedy: Remove the reason of servo ready (SRDY) off.

SRVO-322.cause: The SVOFF (Servo off signal) is input.
SRVO-322.remedy: 1. Release the SVOFF signal and press RESET. 2. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-323.cause: Torque limit reached. The third number indicates the line number of the TP program.
SRVO-323.remedy: Modify TP program to be less aggressive.

SRVO-324.cause: Disturbance estimated in the software exceeds the threshold value. There is possibility that SRVO-050 occurs when the robot runs leaving this warning.
SRVO-324.remedy: 1. Check whether the payload (mass, center of gravity, and inertia) are set correctly. 2. Check whether the applied load exceed the rating. If so, reduce the applied load. 3. If this alarm occurs when the robot is used after long time interval or when the temperature is very low, run the robot with low speed for a while before running with normal speed.

SRVO-325.cause: Varies by alarm number: Alarm 101: fail to send command to MPC Alarm 102: fail to send command to DSP (buffer full) Alarm 103: fail to send command to FLTR Alarm 105: illegal axis number Alarm 106: CPMCWT was OFF when first command Alarm 107: NOCPMC is detected Alarm 108: ANACC is detected Alarm 109: limit error is detected

SRVO-326.cause: The different between motion command and machine pulse exceeded specified threshold.
SRVO-326.remedy: Internal motion error. Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-327.cause: The servo positional error on the cartesian coordinates exceeds a specified value ($PARAM2_GRP.$CARTERRLIM). The first argument that is shown in the alarm message indicates the group number. The second argument indicates which cartesian direction (X/Y/Z/Euclidean distance) the servo positional error exceeds the threshold.
SRVO-327.remedy: Perform the same action as that described for SRVO-023.

SRVO-328.cause: The retry count of the Pulsecoder exceeded a limit value of $PLS_ER_LIM when $PLS_ER_CHK=1.
SRVO-328.remedy: It is likely that the Pulsecoder has malfunctioned due to noise or the Pulsecoder is abnormal. 1. Check if there exists a noise source near the Pulsecoder. 2. Replace the Pulsecoder. 3. Replace the Pulsecoder cable. 4. Replace the Line tracking I/F board. 5. If the error is not cleared with the above remedies, refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-090(DTERR).

SRVO-329.message: FB comp cnt err(G:%d A:%d Enc:%d)
SRVO-329.cause: The position feedback compensation count of the Pulsecoder exceeded a limit value of $PLS_CMP_LIM when $PLS_ER_CHK=1.
SRVO-329.remedy: It is likely that the Pulsecoder has malfunctioned due to noise or the Pulsecoder is abnormal. 1. Check if there exists a noise source near the Pulsecoder. 2. Replace the Pulsecoder. 3. Replace the Pulsecoder cable. 4. Replace the Line tracking I/F board. 5. If the error is not cleared with the above remedies, refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-090(DTERR).

SRVO-330.cause: The retry count of the Pulsecoder exceeded a limit value of $PLS_ER_LIM when $PLS_ER_CHK=1.
SRVO-330.remedy: It is likely that the Pulsecoder has malfunctioned due to noise or the Pulsecoder is abnormal. 1. Check if there exists a noise source near the Pulsecoder. 2. Replace the Pulsecoder. 3. Replace the Pulsecoder cable. 4. Replace the servo amplifier. 5. If the error is not cleared with the above remedies, refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-068(DTERR).

SRVO-331.cause: The position feedback compensation count of the Pulsecoder exceeded a limit value of $PLS_CMP_LIM when $PLS_ER_CHK=1.
SRVO-331.remedy: It is likely that the Pulsecoder has malfunctioned due to noise or the Pulsecoder is abnormal. 1. Check if there exists a noise source near the Pulsecoder. 2. Replace the Pulsecoder. 3. Replace the Pulsecoder cable. 4. Replace the servo amplifier. 5. If the error is not cleared with the above remedies, refer to the Cause and Remedy of SRVO-068(DTERR).

SRVO-332.cause: Power off is required to reset the CMAL alarm.
SRVO-332.remedy: Turn off/on the controller, and then, perform the mastering.

SRVO-334.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative. Note: You need to cycle power to release this alarm.

SRVO-335.cause: A failure was detected in the safety signal input circuit.
SRVO-335.remedy: Replace the emergency stop board. In case of B-cabinet, replace the optional safety I/O board.

SRVO-336.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information. Replace the CPU card. Replace the main board.

SRVO-337.cause: When an image restore is done and "No" is selected for initialize DCS parameter, if the previous DCS parameters are different from what is in the image file, this alarm occurs.
SRVO-337.remedy: 1. Do an APPLY of the DCS parameters if an image restore was done. 2. If power down occurred while DCS parameters were being changed, set the DCS parameters again. 3. Load backup files. 4. Replace main board, CPU card, FROM/SRAM module.

SRVO-338.cause: A DCS process error is detected.
SRVO-338.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-339.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-340.cause: The TCP speed exceeds 250mm/sec in T1 mode.

SRVO-341.cause: The flange speed exceeds 250mm/sec in T1 mode.

SRVO-342.cause: An error occurred in the DCS Cartesian position check.

SRVO-343.cause: An error occurred in the DCS Cartesian speed check.

SRVO-344.cause: A software internal error has occurred.
SRVO-344.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-345.cause: A error occurred in the DCS Joint position check.

SRVO-346.cause: An error occurred in DCS Joint speed check.

SRVO-347.cause: A software internal error has occurred.
SRVO-347.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-348.cause: A command was issued to turn off the magnetic contactor, but the magnetic contactor was not turned off.
SRVO-348.remedy: 1. Replace the E-stop unit. 2. If a signal is connected to the E-Stop unit CRMA74, check whether there is a problem in the connection destination. (Paint) This alarm occurs when only one of the auxiliary contacts on a contactor on the E-Stop board does not toggle properly. The issue may be with a contactor in the E-Stop unit in the main or remote A-cabinet. Replace the E-Stop unit.

SRVO-349.cause: A command was issued to turn on the magnetic contactor, but the magnetic contactor was not turned on.
SRVO-349.remedy: 1. Replace the E-stop unit. 2. Replace the servo amplifier. (Paint) This alarm occurs when only one of the auxiliary contacts on a contactor on the E-Stop board does not toggle properly. The issue may be with a contactor in the E-Stop unit in the main or remote A-cabinet. Replace the E-Stop unit.

SRVO-350.cause: An error occurred in the RAM self test.
SRVO-350.remedy: Replace the CPU card or main board.

SRVO-351.cause: An error occurred in the safety software CRC test.
SRVO-351.remedy: Load the system software or replace the FROM/SRAM module.

SRVO-352.cause: The safety software does not run with the proper timing.
SRVO-352.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-353.cause: The safety software does not run with the proper timing.
SRVO-353.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-354.cause: The safety software does not run with the proper timing.
SRVO-354.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-355.cause: The safety software does not run with the proper timing.
SRVO-355.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-356.cause: The safety software does not run with the proper timing.
SRVO-356.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-357.cause: 1. Cartesian Position Check, Cartesian Speed Check or T1 Mode Speed Check is enabled for a motion group that does not exist. 2. Joint Position Check or Joint Speed Check is enabled for an axis that does not exist. 3. Joint Position Check or Joint Speed Check is enabled for an axis that is excluded. 4. Cartesian Position Check, Cartesian Speed Check or T1 Mode Speed Check is enabled for a motion group that has an excluded axis that is not an auxiliary extended axis.
SRVO-357.remedy: Disable Joint Position Check, Joint Speed Check, Cartesian Position Check, Cartesian Speed Check or T1 Mode Speed Check.

SRVO-358.cause: Invalid data is set in the DCS parameters.
SRVO-358.remedy: Check DCS setting. Load backup files that were saved when the parameters were correct.

SRVO-359.cause: 1. When config Signature Date/Time is ACTUAL in DCS CIP Safety menu, System clock setting is invalid. (Valid year is 2004-2150.) 2. Invalid data is set in the DCS parameters.
SRVO-359.remedy: 1. Config Signature Date/Time to FIXED, or set correct date/time to system clock. 2. Check DCS setting. Load backup files that were saved when the parameters were correct.

SRVO-360.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-361.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-362.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-363.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-364.cause: This robot model is not supported.
SRVO-364.remedy: Delete "DCS Position/Speed Check function" option. This alarm can be cleared by setting $DCS_CFG.$SYS_PARAM to 1, but in this case, Position/Speed Check function can not be used.

SRVO-365.cause: Difference between position command and position feedback exceeds position tolerance. The same cause as "SRVO-023 Stop error excess" or "SRVO-024 Move error excess" is expected.
SRVO-365.remedy: Please refer the Remedy of SRVO-023. Check the setting data displayed in the DCS robot setup menu.

SRVO-366.cause: Invalid data is set in DCS parameter for axis number
SRVO-366.remedy: Check the setting data displayed in the DCS robot setup menu.

SRVO-367.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-368.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-370.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the emergency stop board internal signal (SVON).

SRVO-371.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the emergency stop board internal signal (SVON).

SRVO-372.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the emergency stop switch on the operator's panel.
SRVO-372.remedy: 1. Replace the emergency stop board. 2. Replace the teach pendant cable. 3. Replace the teach pendant. 4. Replace the emergency stop button on the operator's panel. (Paint) This alarm occurs when only one of the two contacts from the ACP mounted estop pushbutton circuit close. Also check the pendant estop button because they are in series.

SRVO-373.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the emergency stop switch on the operator's panel.
SRVO-373.remedy: 1. Replace the emergency stop board. 2. Replace the teach pendant cable. 3. Replace the teach pendant. 4. Replace the emergency stop button on the operator's panel. (Paint) This alarm occurs when only one of the two contacts from the ACP mounted estop pushbutton circuit close. Also check the pendant estop button because they are in series.

SRVO-374.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the mode switch signal.
SRVO-374.remedy: 1. Check the mode switch and its cable. Replace them if a defect is found. 2. Replace the emergency stop board. (Paint) The Mode Switch may be located on the ACP or interlocked to the system. This alarm indicates there is an issue with one of the Mode switch circuits.

SRVO-375.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the mode switch signal.
SRVO-375.remedy: 1. Check the mode switch and its cable. Replace them if a defect is found. 2. Replace the emergency stop board. 3. (Paint) The Mode Switch may be located on the ACP or interlocked to the system. This alarm indicates there is an issue with one of the Mode switch circuits.

SRVO-376.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the mode switch signal.
SRVO-376.remedy: 1. Check the mode switch and its cable. Replace them if a defect is found. 2. Replace the emergency stop board. (Paint) The Mode Switch may be located on the ACP or interlocked to the system. This alarm indicates there is an issue with one of the Mode switch circuits.

SRVO-377.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the mode switch signal.
SRVO-377.remedy: 1. Check the mode switch and its cable. Replace them if a defect is found. 2. Replace the emergency stop board. (Paint) The Mode Switch may be located on the ACP or interlocked to the system. This alarm indicates there is an issue with one of the Mode switch circuits.

SRVO-378.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the SFDI signal. xx shows signal name.
SRVO-378.remedy: 1. Check whether the circuitry connected to the dual input signal (SFDI) is faulty. 2. Check whether the timing of the dual input signal (SFDI) satisfies the timing specification. 3. In case of B-cabinet, replace the optional safety I/O board. 4. Replace the emergency stop board. Note In order to clear this fault, the chain fault will need to be reset. To reset the chain fault press F4 RES_1CH on the active alarm menu and press F4 YES to reset the single channel fault. (Paint) SFDI signals exist on the Estop Board(s) and optional Safety I/O Board(s). This alarm will be posted if there is an issue with the Estop Board, Safety I/O Board or cable.

SRVO-379.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the OPSFTY signal.
SRVO-379.remedy: 1. Check whether the circuitry connected to the dual input signal (OPSFTY) is faulty. 2. Check whether the timing of the dual input signal (OPSFTY) satisfies the timing specification. 3. Replace the panel board.

SRVO-380.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the OPSFTY signal.
SRVO-380.remedy: 1. Check whether the circuitry connected to the dual input signal (OPSFTY) is faulty. 2. Check whether the timing of the dual input signal (OPSFTY) satisfies the timing specification. 3. Replace the panel board.

SRVO-381.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the OPSFTY signal.
SRVO-381.remedy: 1. Check whether the circuitry connected to the dual input signal (OPSFTY) is faulty. 2. Check whether the timing of the dual input signal (OPSFTY) satisfies the timing specification. 3. Replace the panel board.

SRVO-382.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the OPSFTY signal.
SRVO-382.remedy: 1. Check whether the circuitry connected to the dual input signal (OPSFTY) is faulty. 2. Check whether the timing of the dual input signal (OPSFTY) satisfies the timing specification. 3. Replace the panel board.

SRVO-383.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the OPSFTY signal.
SRVO-383.remedy: 1. Check whether the circuitry connected to the dual input signal (OPSFTY) is faulty. 2. Check whether the timing of the dual input signal (OPSFTY) satisfies the timing specification. 3. Replace the panel board.

SRVO-384.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the OPSFTY signal.
SRVO-384.remedy: 1. Check whether the circuitry connected to the dual input signal (OPSFTY) is faulty. 2. Check whether the timing of the dual input signal (OPSFTY) satisfies the timing specification. 3. Replace the panel board.

SRVO-385.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the OPSFTY signal.
SRVO-385.remedy: 1. Check whether the circuitry connected to the dual input signal (OPSFTY) is faulty. 2. Check whether the timing of the dual input signal (OPSFTY) satisfies the timing specification. 3. Replace the panel board.

SRVO-386.remedy: Use soft float with a wide margin.

SRVO-387.cause: The position or schedule is not proper.
SRVO-387.remedy: Use soft float in the proper position and schedule

SRVO-388.remedy: Use soft float with a wide margin.

SRVO-393.message: Other diagnosis data is being recorded.
SRVO-393.cause: Other diagnosis data is being recorded.
SRVO-393.remedy: Wait until the recording is finished.

SRVO-394.cause: iRDiagnostics- Robot Condition Detection Function has detected abnormality. Reducer may be degraded.
SRVO-394.remedy: Check the mechanical part of the corresponding axis.

SRVO-397.cause: J2 motion is too aggressive. This warning means J2 motion has been slowed down.

SRVO-399.cause: This is a notification that Torsion Compensation failed to execute. This message is shown by Tool Torsion Compensation option etc. When ID is 0: robot is not mastered or not calibrated yet. When ID is 1: an invalid schedule number is specified. When ID is 2: an invalid tool number is specified in current schedule. When ID is 3 or 4: direction is not defined.(in schedule to compensate along the direction defined by TCP velocity vector)
SRVO-399.remedy: When ID is 0: master and calibrate the robot. When ID is 1: specify valid schedule number. When ID is 2: specify valid tool number in current schedule. When ID is 3 or 4: in these schedules, start compensation while TCP is moving.

SRVO-402.cause: Cartesian Position Check function detected that a model is out of a safe zone. The first value: Cartesian Position Check No. G: Group number M: User model number (0: Robot model)
SRVO-402.remedy: If the robot is actually out of the safe zone, press SHIFT key and RESET key, and jog the robot to the safe zone.
