SRVO-403.cause: Cartesian Speed Check function detected over speed. The first value: Cartesian Speed Check No. G: Group number

SRVO-404.cause: Joint Position Check function detected that an axis is out of a safe zone. The first value: Joint Position Check No. G: Group number A: Axis number
SRVO-404.remedy: If the robot is actually out of the safe zone, press SHIFT key and RESET key, and jog the robot to the safe zone.

SRVO-405.cause: Joint Speed Check function detected over speed. The first value: Joint Speed Check No. G: Group number A: Axis number

SRVO-412.cause: DCS servo on process is stopped.
SRVO-412.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-413.cause: Results of Safe I/O process by 2 CPU are different. This alarm sometimes occurs when the safety input signals on the emergency stop board and Safe I/O board such as External E-STOP or SFDI are changed repeatedly in a very short time.
SRVO-413.remedy: Check the connection of the safety input signals on the emergency stop board and Safe I/O board. Check the other alarms for more information.

SRVO-414.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information. Replace CPU card. Replace main board.

SRVO-415.cause: 1. Selected DCS tool frame number is not defined. 2. Verify I/O of DCS tool frame is not set in the selected DCS tool frame

SRVO-416.cause: All Verify I/O of DCS tool frame are OFF or two or more Verify I/O are ON for more than 1sec.

SRVO-417.cause: Invalid DCS approach speed check parameter for Cartesian position check.
SRVO-417.remedy: Check DCS approach speed check parameter

SRVO-418.cause: Invalid DCS approach speed check parameter for Joint position check.
SRVO-418.remedy: Check DCS approach speed check parameter

SRVO-420.cause: Safety function by FL-net communication error occurs.
SRVO-420.remedy: Check Safety function by FL-net connection

SRVO-421.cause: $DMR_GRP.$MASTER_DONE is not ready to be set to TRUE because Universal Joint phase calibration data is not set.
SRVO-421.remedy: When you enter the mastering data via direct entry, enter Universal Joint phase calibration data and set $DMR_M3_GRP.$MASTER2_ENB = TRUE first. After that, set $DMR_GRP.$MASTER_DONE = TRUE

SRVO-422.cause: Emergency stop occurs on other controllers in Shared Teach Pendant group.
SRVO-422.remedy: Clear the source of the fault, and press RESET on ther controller.

SRVO-423.message: Shared TP: T1/T2 on other robot
SRVO-423.cause: Any other controllers in Shared Teach Pendant gropu is not AUTO.
SRVO-423.remedy: To start production running in Auto mode, change modes of all controllers in the Shared Teach Pendant group Auto.

SRVO-424.cause: Robot in T1 mode cannot move if there is T2 mode controller in the group. Robot in T2 mode cannot move if there is T1 mode controller in the group.
SRVO-424.remedy: To move a robot in T1/T2 mode, set the modes of all other controllers in Shared Teach Pendant group to the same or AUTO.

SRVO-425.cause: Configuration for Shared Teach Pendant group is mismatched with other controllers in the group.
SRVO-425.remedy: Check configuration for Shared Teach Pendan group.

SRVO-426.cause: A robot tries to perform Touch Detection.
SRVO-426.remedy: There is no need to take any measures.

SRVO-427.message: EQZ No sensitivity at this Pos (G:%d)
SRVO-427.cause: There is no sensitive axis at this posture.
SRVO-427.remedy: Change the robot posture and try Equalization again.

SRVO-428.cause: Length of EQ motion (distance between taught positions) was too short.
SRVO-428.remedy: Modify your TP program to enhance the distance to the destination position of EQ motion. Typically you only need to increase the argument value to EQTCHPOS.

SRVO-429.cause: Equalization was infeasible at this robot posture. This message tells you the last EQ was done with Ghost Run mode.
SRVO-429.remedy: If possible, try to change the configuration (U/D, T/B) of the robot

SRVO-430.cause: Cannot start equalization because this robot does not. support equalization.
SRVO-430.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-431.cause: Cannot start equalization for some reason.
SRVO-431.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-432.cause: Equalization was aborted for some reason, HOLD, E-STOP etc.
SRVO-432.remedy: Equalization is no longer effective in this motion. If you need to try the Equalization motion again, jog the robot away from the part, then restart from the line before equalization motion.

SRVO-433.cause: Equalization Soft Direction is not selected
SRVO-433.remedy: Select Soft Direction via the setup screen.

SRVO-434.cause: Equalization is infeasible at this robot posture. Equalization requires that at least one axis among J1, J2 or J3 is sensitive to the reaction force from the part. This alarm means there is no sensitive axis.
SRVO-434.remedy: If possible, try to change the configuration (U/D, T/B) of the robot.

SRVO-435.cause: Motion with equalization exceeded the Robot Move Limit.
SRVO-435.remedy: This alarm indicates an overrun of the robot motion. 1. Check if the workpiece exists. 2. If this alarm is posted without an obvious overrun, increase Robot Move Limit via the setup menu.

SRVO-436.cause: Robot reached to its stroke range limit during Equalization motion.
SRVO-436.remedy: If possible, try to change the configuration (F/N, U/D, T/B) and turn number of the robot.

SRVO-437.cause: Robot wrist axis is near the singular point. In other words, J5 is near 0.
SRVO-437.remedy: If possible, try to change the configuration (U/D, T/B) of the robot.

SRVO-438.cause: An instantaneous high speed motion was detected. One possible cause is that robot posture is bad (near SRVO-434 condition)
SRVO-438.remedy: If possible, try to change the configuration (U/D, T/B) of the robot.

SRVO-439.cause: Ending process of EQ motion was not normally done.
SRVO-439.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative. Note Need power cycle to release this alarm.

SRVO-440.cause: Some arguments in KAREL are invalid.
SRVO-440.remedy: Correct the arguments in the KAREL program

SRVO-441.cause: Gun Mount Type is not selected.
SRVO-441.remedy: Select Gun Mount Type via the setup screen.

SRVO-442.cause: Robot kept moving when Equlization is about to end.
SRVO-442.remedy: Check if the part is firmly fixed.

SRVO-443.cause: Because EQTCHPOS was not called or not successfully processed, destination position of EQ motion is not calculated.
SRVO-443.remedy: 1. Check if EQTCHPOS is called before EQ start. If not called, add call EQTCHPOS before EQ start. 2. If EQTCHPOS causes SRVO-440 or other alarm, modify arguments of EQTCHPOS to eliminate the alarm.

SRVO-444.cause: (1): Failed to get destination angle of last motion segment before EQ. (2): Failed to calculate EQ position by forward kinematics, probably because of stroke limit.
SRVO-444.remedy: (1): Document the events that led to the error, and contact your FANUC technical representative. (2): Check joint position when EQTCHPOS was called.

SRVO-445.cause: Both Equalization and Softfloat become enabled.
SRVO-445.remedy: Don't use Equalization and Softfloat at the same time.

SRVO-446.cause: In Auxiliary axis servo off (Local stop) function, the safe I/O assigned to the fence input is OFF when the auxiliary axis is not servo off condition. The value displayed in the message shows the No. of local stop that the alarm occurs. The value is hexadecimal, and each bit is corresponded to each item in DCS local stop menu (1:No.1, 2:No.2, 4:No.3, 8:No.4, 10:No.5, 20:No.6, 40:No.7, 80:No.8).
SRVO-446.remedy: Set the safe I/O assigned to the fence input to ON, or set the auxiliary axis servo to off.

SRVO-447.cause: In Auxiliary axis servo off (Local stop) function, mismatch of STO-OUT and STO-FB is detected. The value displayed in the message shows the No. of local stop that the alarm occurs. The value is hexadecimal, and each bit is corresponded to each item in DCS local stop menu (1:No.1, 2:No.2, 4:No.3, 8:No.4, 10:No.5, 20:No.6, 40:No.7, 80:No.8).
SRVO-447.remedy: 1: Check the setting of DCS local stop menu. 2: Check the connection between emergency stop board and auxiliary axis servo amplifier. 3: Replace the cable between emergency stop board and auxiliary axis servo amplifier. 4: Replace the emergency stop board. 5: Replace the auxiliary axis servo amplifier.

SRVO-448.cause: The monitored signal of safety output is not OFF even though OFF pulse is output. The signal name that the trouble is detected is displayed after the alarm message.
SRVO-448.remedy: 1. Check the cabling of safety output circuit. 2. In case of B-cabinet, replace the optional safety I/O board. 3. Replace the emergency stop board.

SRVO-449.cause: The monitored signal of safety ouput is different from the output command. The signal name that the trouble is detected is displayed after the alarm message.
SRVO-449.remedy: 1. Check the cabling of safety output circuit. 2. In case of B-cabinet, replace the optional safety I/O board. 3. Replace the emergency stop board.

SRVO-450.cause: The two drive off inputs are not in the same status.
SRVO-450.remedy: 1. Check the line of the two drive off inputs. 2. Replace the servo amplifier.

SRVO-451.cause: An error is found in the serial bus communication in the servo amplifier.

SRVO-452.cause: An error is found in the ROM data in the servo amplifier.

SRVO-453.cause: Driver supply voltage in the servo amplifier is low.

SRVO-454.cause: An error was found in CPU bus data in the amplifier.

SRVO-455.cause: An error occurred in CPU operation in the amplifier.

SRVO-456.cause: An error is found in the motor current detection data in the servo amplifier.

SRVO-457.cause: Ground fault occurs in the motor power line.
SRVO-457.remedy: 1. Check the ground fault of the motor and the motor power cable. 2. Replace the Power Supply (alpha iPS). 3. Replace the servo amplifier.

SRVO-458.cause: The root-mean-square current value which is calculated internally by the Power Supply (alpha iPS) exceeds the maximum permissible value. This alarm is issued to protect the Power Supply (alpha iPS) from damage of thermal destruction. Probable cause: 1. Overload 2. External force to the robot 3. Disconnection of the brake cable 4. Insufficient torque by low voltage of power supply 5. Brake failure (includes mis-setting of brake number for auxiliary axis) 6. Auxiliary brake unit failure for auxiliary axis 7. The Power Supply (alpha iPS) failure 8. The servo amplifier failure
SRVO-458.remedy: 1. Check whether the duty and applied load exceed the rating. If so, reduce the duty or applied load. 2. Check whether the robot is pushed or pulled by external force. If so, remove the external force to the robot or modify the taught point. 3. Check whether the brake cable/connector are connected correctly. 4. Measure the supplied voltage. Then, check whether the voltage is matched to the controller specification. 5. Check whether the motor brake is released properly when reset or the robot moves. First of all, check whether the setting of brake number is correct when this alarm occurs on auxiliary axis. 6. When this alarm occurs on the auxiliary axis which brake is controlled by the auxiliary brake unit, check the fuse on the auxiliary brake unit. 7. Replace the Power Supply (alpha iPS). 8. Replace the servo amplifier.

SRVO-459.cause: An error is found in the discharge circuit in the 6-axis amplifier.

SRVO-460.cause: An error is found in the setting of the parameters in the Power Supply (alpha iPS) or servo amplifier.
SRVO-460.remedy: 1. Replace the Power Supply (alpha iPS). 2. Replace the servo amplifier.

SRVO-461.cause: An error is found in the circuit in the Power Supply (alpha iPS) or servo amplifier.

SRVO-468.cause: Temporary detached node exists in Safety function by FL-net.
SRVO-468.remedy: This alarm occurs at start-up and for user to pay attention, so this alarm is defeasible by reset. Change the detached node to ENTRY not to occur this alarm at start-up.

SRVO-470.cause: Wireless data sequence number is wrong.

SRVO-471.message: I/O Link i slave(%d-%d) status abnormal
SRVO-471.cause: A chain alarm was detected with the I/O Link i slave signal. (x-x) shows signal number.
SRVO-471.remedy: 1. Check whether I/O Link cable is connected correctly. 2. Check whether the timing of the dual input signal for I/O Link i slave satisfies the timing specification. 3. Replace CPU card. Replace main board.

SRVO-472.message: A%d is moved in stop check
SRVO-472.cause: The suspended axis is moved when the contact stop status of Collaborative Robot is ESCP.
SRVO-472.remedy: Clear the external force to the collaborative robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your local FANUC representative.

SRVO-473.cause: The result is different in 2 CPU for Collaborative Robot.
SRVO-473.remedy: Check the other alarms for more information. Note: You need to cycle power to release this alarm.

SRVO-474.cause: The speed of movement by Push to Escape of Collaborative Robot exceeds the limit.
SRVO-474.remedy: Clear the external force to the collaborative robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your local FANUC representative.

SRVO-475.cause: The direction of movement by Push to Escape of Collaborative Robot exceeds is invalid.
SRVO-475.remedy: Clear the external force to the collaborative robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your local FANUC representative.

SRVO-476.cause: Internal error of the collaborative robot function.
SRVO-476.remedy: Restart the controller. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your local FANUC representative.

SRVO-477.cause: The sensor calibration data of the collaborative robot are wrong.
SRVO-477.remedy: Copy "CLLB.CM" file from the CD-R which is appendix of the collaborative robot to a memory card or USB memory. Perform the same file with a teach pendant, set the sensor calibration parameter. After this change, perform “APPLY TO DCS PARAMETER”. Refer to “1.3 Apply to DCS parameter” in ”Dual Check Safety Function Operator’s manual” for detail. As this file is unique to each collaborative robot, do not use other robot’s file. Check that the serial number which is printed on CD-R is same as the number which is written on collaborative robot sensor.

SRVO-478.cause: The force sensor temperature difference is too large.
SRVO-478.remedy: Please make sure that the environment temperature does not change greatly, and then restart the controller. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your local FANUC representative.

SRVO-479.cause: The force sensor temperature changes too fast.
SRVO-479.remedy: Please make sure that the environment temperature does not change greatly, and then restart the controller. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your local FANUC representative.

SRVO-480.remedy: 1. Restart the controller. 2. Replace the force sensor cable. 3. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-481.cause: Current payload number of Collaborative Robot is invalid. By default, the payload number is 0 (invalid setting).
SRVO-481.remedy: Set the payload number between 1 and 10.

SRVO-482.message: Robot is moved in stop check
SRVO-482.cause: Collaborative Robot moved when the contact stop status is STOP.
SRVO-482.remedy: Clear the external force to the collaborative robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your local FANUC representative.

SRVO-483.cause: Mode was chnaged to AUTO by mode switch on TP screen.
SRVO-483.remedy: Input AUTO confirmation singal by the switch outside of safeguard.

SRVO-484.cause: In Safe I/O consistency check function, mismatch of Safe I/O is detected.
SRVO-484.remedy: 1. Check the setting of Safety I/O consistency check function. 2. Check the cabling of safety I/O circuit. 3. Check failure of the device that cabled to safety I/O. Note You need to cycle power to release this alarm.

SRVO-485.cause: Operation speed by Hand Guidance exceeds limit.
SRVO-485.remedy: Check limit speed setting of Hand Guidance.

SRVO-486.cause: The EMERGENCY STOP button on the Hand Guidance device was pressed.
SRVO-486.remedy: 1. Release EMERGENCY STOP on the Hand Guidance device, then press RESET. 2. Check setting and connection to Safety I/O board. 3. If this alarm cannot be reset, replace the Hand Guidance device.

SRVO-487.cause: The DEADMAN switch of Hand Guidance device was not pressed.
SRVO-487.remedy: 1. Press the DEADMAN switch to release it, then press RESET. 2. If you want to use with Collaborative robot, enable Contact stop. 3. Set Hand Guidance disable I/O to ON if you do not use Hand Guidance function then. 4. If this alarm cannot be reset, replace the Hand Guidance device.

SRVO-488.cause: Cartesian Position Check function detected that robot speed exceeds limit. The first value: Cartesian Position Check No. G: Group number N: Speed limit Number
SRVO-488.remedy: Decrease speed if the CPC is UNSF

SRVO-489.remedy: Please take the following actions. 1 Restart the controller. 2. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your local FANUC representative.

SRVO-490.remedy: 1. Restart the controller. 2. Replace the sensor cable. 3. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-491.remedy: SHIFT+RESET and jog to a safe position

SRVO-493.cause: The stop distance of Contact stop of Collaborative Robot exceeds the limit.
SRVO-493.remedy: SHIFT+RESET and jog to safe position.

SRVO-494.cause: An error occurred in the DMA self test.

SRVO-495.message: Mastering is invalid just after power up(G:%d id:%d)
SRVO-495.cause: Mastering is invalid just after power up.
SRVO-495.remedy: RESET. If mastering is needed, try again.

SRVO-497.remedy: Please check initial force data and its CRC code.

SRVO-498.cause: The EMERGENCY STOP button on the Manual Pulse Generator was pressed.
SRVO-498.remedy: 1. Release EMERGENCY STOP on the Manual Pulse Generator, then press RESET. 2. If this alarm cannot be reset, replace the Manual Pulse Generator.

SRVO-499.cause: The deadman switch of Manual Pulse Generator was not pressed.
SRVO-499.remedy: 1. Press the Manual Pulse Generator to release it, then press RESET. 2. Set disable Manual Pulse Generator in the setting screen, if you do not use Manual Pulse Generator then. 1. If this alarm cannot be reset, replace the Manual Pulse Generato.

SRVO-500.cause: CC-Link IE Safety communication error occurs.
SRVO-500.remedy: Check CC-Link IE Safety connection. Please check initial force data and its CRC code.

SRVO-501.cause: Cartesian Position Check function detected that a model is out of a safe zone in Validation CPC. The first value: Cartesian Position Check No. G: Group number M: User model number (0: Robot model)
SRVO-501.remedy: If the robot is actually out of thesafe zone, press SHIFT key and RESET key, and jog the robot to the safe zone.

SRVO-502.message: Manual Guided Teaching FUP time out (G:%d)
SRVO-502.cause: A follow-up after manual guided teaching did not finish in a certain period of time. This could happen when the robot keeps moving after manual guided teaching ends. The number in the parentheses shows the group number.
SRVO-502.remedy: 1. Do not keep applying large external force to the robot after manual guided teaching. 2. Check for other alarms that occurred at the same time.

SRVO-503.remedy: 1. Restart the controller. 2. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-504.remedy: 1. Restart the controller. 2. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative.

SRVO-505.cause: Sensor Temperature change rate too large
SRVO-505.remedy: Please check the temperature change rate of ambient temperature or robot.

SRVO-506.message: Speed Limit for manual guided teaching
SRVO-506.cause: Robot speed exceeds limit during manual guided teaching

SRVO-507.cause: Robot speed exceeds limit during manual guided teaching

SRVO-601.cause: The EMERGENCY STOP button on the Teach Pendant was pressed. Or, the EMERGENCY STOP button on the operator panel was pressed.
SRVO-601.remedy: Twist the EMERGENCY STOP button clockwise to release it, then press RESET.

SRVO-602.cause: The EMERGENCY STOP button on the Teach Pendant was pressed. Or, the external EMERGENCY STOP button was pressed.
SRVO-602.remedy: Twist the teach pendant EMERGENCY STOP button clockwise to release it, then press RESET. If you are using the external emergency stop, clear the source of the fault, and press RESET.

SRVO-603.remedy: 1. Press the deadman switch to release it, then press RESET. If the deadman switch is three position switch type, press the deadman switch to middle position to release it, then press RESET. 2. Press the NTED (non-teacher enabling device), and then press RESET. 3. If this alarm cannot be reset, replace the teach pendant. Or, refer to the Controller Maintenance Manual for more information.

SSPC-228.remedy: Enter a valid Central Plane Schedule id.

SSPC-230.cause: Too few total number of combination pairs or fixtures. Central Plane Check starts at certain combination pairs and fixtures.

SSPC-240.cause: No IIC DSP is available. Dedicated DSP is required for IIC.

SVGN-001.remedy: Record error and report to hotline.

SVGN-002.cause: This is an internal system error.
SVGN-002.remedy: Record error and report to hotline.

SVGN-004.cause: A failure occurred while allocating memory.
SVGN-004.remedy: Check amount of memory being used by the system. Perform a cold start on the controller. Record error and report to hotline.

SVGN-005.remedy: Repower, go to control start, and then back to cold start. This action re-generates the internal servogun program and may correct the problem. Record the error and report to hotline, if the problem persists.

SVGN-008.cause: Instruction syntax error. This instruction is for air gun spot.
SVGN-008.remedy: Reteach the instruction. Reteach servo gun SPOT instruction.

SVGN-009.cause: The robot group and/or gun group are not enabled, in the group mask of this teach pendant program.
SVGN-009.remedy: Determine the robot group number and gun group number for this equipment, then re-create the program, with these groups enabled.

SVGN-010.cause: Invalid servo gun group number (greater than total number of groups).
SVGN-010.remedy: Check the group number assigned to this servogun (equipment).

SVGN-011.cause: Incremental, offset or tool offset instructions can not execute with servo gun SPOT instruction at the same program line.

SVGN-012.cause: The register index specified in the instruction is invalid.

SVGN-013.cause: The Pressure specified in the pressure schedule, or pressure instruction, exceeds the Max Pressure for the gun.
SVGN-013.remedy: Reduce the Pressure in the pressure schedule or program, or increase the Max Pressure item on the Servo Gun General SETUP screen. Confirm that the new pressure value does not exceed the mechanical limitation of the gun.

SVGN-015.cause: Pointer to gun, schedule, backup or distance data is invalid.
SVGN-015.remedy: Check servo gun configuration data. Record error and report to hotline.

SVGN-016.cause: The pressure specified in the pressure schedule or pressure instruction is lower than the lowest reachable pressure on the calibration curve.
SVGN-016.remedy: Increase the Weld Pressure, set weld pressure = 0, or recalibrate pressure. Note 1: when weld pressure = 0, the minimum possible pressure (actual tip force may not be 0) is used. SVGN-016 will not be posted even if the calibration curve does not contain a point where weld pressure = 0. Note 2: add a calibration point at or below the specified pressure to ensure the gun can achieve the low pressure. Note 3: reducing the contact speed might make it possible to achieve lower pressures.

SVGN-017.cause: Single-segment calibration method is enabled and prm_a1 is invalid (less than 0.0001 OR greater than 100.0).
SVGN-017.remedy: Change the calibration method to the multi-linear segment method if possible. Do this by setting the sysvars $sgsyscfg.$cal_model = 12 and $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv = 3, then perform the pressure calibration again.

SVGN-018.cause: The torque value is illegal (less than $sgsyscfg.$minimum_trq OR greater than max rated torque). This alarm can occur at the following times: SPOT[], PRESS_MOTN[], or PRESS[]kgf execution.
SVGN-018.remedy: Confirm that the pressure calibration data is valid.

SVGN-019.cause: Same as SVGN-020, but severity is WARN. Note: SVGN-019 can occur during autotuning or if $sgsyscfg.$pst_ertype = 1; SVGN-020 occurs otherwise.

SVGN-020.cause: The SPOT, PRESS_MOTN or TIPDRESS, instruction failed because gun closure was not detected(1) or gun pressure was unstable(2). The number after pressure shortage (1 or 2) identifies the failure type. Scan the list below for the cause that most nearly matches the condition at hand, then refer to the remedy for that cause. Shortage 1) The instruction completed - gun tip moved to the pushing depth position - without torque increasing to the gun close detection value (1/2 Std Overtorque Value). • 1A) If gun moved to current close axis limit (ClosLim from SVGN-177) without achieving pressure, then axis limit is too small. • 1B) Pushing depth parameter in pressure schedule is not large enough to overcome gun bending at target pressure plus tip wear amount since last measurement. • 1C) Part thickness parameter (Thk from SVGN-177) is much larger than actual part thickness • 1D) Gun zero master position is incorrect (if tips are worn and user chooses to not use tip wear comp, then start with 1B) • 1E) Gun close detection torque may be excessive (or larger than Max Motor torque) due to a large restriction in gun mechanism. Shortage 2) The torque for pressuring varied from the target value. There are (2) likely causes: • 2A) Target pressure is at very low or high end of gun operating range (tips are likely touching part) • 2B) Friction in gun mechanism has increased considerably since gun was autotuned (tips are likely NOT touching part)
SVGN-020.remedy: Shortage 1) • 1A) When tip wear compensation is used, close axis limit is adjusted to avoid over-stroking gun (ClosLim becomes smaller than StdLim when caps are worn). To extend axis limit, change tips, then run tip wear comp update program when using tip wear comp. Next, check the original close limit (StdLim) setting on servo gun setup screen and adjust if not correct. • 1B) Increase pushing depth in pressure schedule (set $sgsyscfg.$sho_pshdpth=TRUE to see pushing depth parameter) • 1C) Reduce part thickness in the pressure schedule so it is closer to actual part thickness. • 1D) If using tip wear compensation, re-master the gun by running the tip wear compensation update program. Otherwise, refer to 1B or re-master the gun with new tips from the gun master screen. • 1E) Adjust the gun mechanism to relieve the restriction. Re-tune the gun (autotune) and calibrate pressure after adjustment. Shortage 2) • 2A) Re-tune the gun (autotune) then confirm pressure calibration. If problem persists, or if the alarm occurs during tip wear measurement, autotune with Initial Filter set to a value between 10-30. To see Initial Filter item, set $sgsyscfg.$sho_atn_cfg=TRUE then press enter on Auto Tune item from Gun Setup Utility before tuning. • 2B) Re-tune the gun (autotune) to adjust the gun close detection limit, then confirm pressure calibration. If required, adjust the gun mechanism to relieve the cause of friction increase.

SVGN-021.cause: The BU schedule number (condition) is not initialized or is invalid.
SVGN-021.remedy: Set a valid backup schedule number (greater than or equal to 0, AND less than or equal to $sgsyscfg.$back_elm) into the instruction in the teach pendant program.

SVGN-022.cause: The pressure schedule number (condition) is not initialized or is invalid.
SVGN-022.remedy: Set a valid Pressure schedule number (greater than or equal to 1, AND less than or equal to $sgsyscfg.$sch_elm) into the instruction in the teach pendant program.

SVGN-023.remedy: Go to the Servo Gun General SETUP screen, select Pressure calibration, and perform pressure calibration procedure.

SVGN-024.cause: Tip Wear Compensation setup (calibration) is not complete.
SVGN-024.remedy: Perform the Tip Wear Setup procedure. Consult the Servo Gun Manual for details on this procedure.

SVGN-025.cause: Invalid BU schedule (condition) number (greater than $sgsyscfg.$back_elm, or less than 0).
SVGN-025.remedy: Specify a backup condition number within the range above.

SVGN-026.cause: Invalid P schedule (condition) number (greater than $sgsyscfg.$sch_elm, or less than 1).
SVGN-026.remedy: Specify a pressure condition number within the range above.

SVGN-027.cause: Some program elements (like positional data for example) have not been recorded.
SVGN-027.remedy: Enter data for the missing program elements.

SVGN-029.cause: The motor torque required to achieve the pressure specified in the pressure schedule or pressure instruction exceeds the Max Torque value specified on the Servogun SETUP screen.
SVGN-029.remedy: 1. Reduce the Pressure value. 2. Check Pressure Calibration data. 3. Calibrate Pressure again if the data is incorrect. 4. Increase the Max Motor Torque value on the Servo Gun General SETUP screen, if possible. Note: motor torque value on the General SETUP screen can be regarded as a fractional percentage of the maximum allowable torque. The screen will not allow this value to be set larger than amp + motor rating.

SVGN-030.cause: Tip stick detection DI is ON.
SVGN-030.remedy: Jog the gun open or use a tool to separate the tip from the part, if the tip is stuck. If the tip is not stuck, then determine why the tip stick input is on.

SVGN-031.cause: When tear off function is executing, program cannot be started.
SVGN-031.remedy: Restart program after tear off function finished.

SVGN-032.cause: The measured tip wear on the gun side (moving tip) indicates that the tip has grown by an amount greater than the Gun Increased Error(mm) setting.
SVGN-032.remedy: First confirm the condition of the tip. If the tip is not ok, then replace it, and perform tip wear measurement again. If a chip from tip dressing remains on the tip, remove this chip then re-measure the tip wear. If new tips were installed after the previous tip wear measurement, be sure the tip wear update program was run with the New Tips Parameter set to (1) in the Call instruction for the tip wear macro. If this parameter was not set correctly, then press fault reset and run the tip wear update program again with the New Tips Parameter set to (1). If the tip is OK and the new tip parameter was set correctly, then perform the tip wear measurement again. Observe the gun closely during this operation. Be sure the tips touch during the 1st step of the tip wear measurement and be sure the gun tip touches the fixture during the 2nd step (if used). If the gun tip does not close fully during either step, then the gun friction has probably increased. To compensate, run Autotuning then Pressure Calibration and perform the tip wear setup procedure again with new tips. Inspect the gun to find the reason for the increase in friction. If both steps of the measurement perform correctly then it might be necessary to increase the value of the Increase Error(mm) setting for the robot side tip. Do this on the Tip Wear Detection screen (SETUP-SERVO GUN-GENERAL SETUP).

SVGN-033.cause: The measured tip wear on the robot side (stationary tip) indicates that the tip has grown by an amount greater than the Robot Increased Error(mm) setting
SVGN-033.remedy: First confirm the condition of the tip. If the tip is not ok, then replace it, and perform tip wear measurement again. If a chip from tip dressing remains on the tip, remove this chip then re-measure the tip wear. If new tips were installed after the previous tip wear measurement, be sure the tip wear update program was run with the New Tips Parameter set to (1) in the Call instruction for the tip wear macro. If this parameter was not set correctly, then press fault reset and run the tip wear update program again with the New Tips Parameter set to (1). If the tip is OK and the new tip parameter was set correctly, then perform the tip wear measurement again. Observe the gun closely during this operation. Be sure the tips touch during the 1st step of the tip wear measurement and be sure the gun tip touches the fixture during the 2nd step (if used). If the gun tip does not close fully during either step, then the gun friction has probably increased. To compensate, run Autotuning then Pressure Calibration and perform the tip wear setup procedure again with new tips. Inspect the gun to find the reason for the increase in friction. If both steps of the measurement perform correctly then it may be necessary to increase the value of the Increase Error(mm) setting for the robot side tip. Do this on the Tip Wear Detection screen (SETUP-SERVO GUN-GENERAL SETUP).

SVGN-034.cause: The Tip Wear difference between the robot tips on the dual gun exceeds the specified tolerance.
SVGN-034.remedy: Replace or dress the tips (and tip holder if necessary) and run the tip wear update program for each gun. Alternatively, increase the difference tolerance in the Tip Wear Detection screen (Press MENUS. Select SETUP. Select SERVO GUN. Select GENERAL SETUP.)

SVGN-035.cause: The pressure enable signal (input) did not turn on before the wait time expired.
SVGN-035.remedy: Determine why the pressure enable signal did not turn on. Or, increase the value of time out($SPOTEQSETUP[].$PEN_TMOUT) if it is too short.

SVGN-036.cause: The comp confirmation signal (input) did not turn on before the wait time expired.
SVGN-036.remedy: Check the reason that the comp confirmation signal is off. Or, increase the value of time out($SPOTEQSETUP[].$NSE_TMOUT), if it is too short.

SVGN-037.cause: The pressure enable signal number is illegal.
SVGN-037.remedy: Map the pressure enable input to a valid input index via ($SPOTEQIO[].$DI_PEN_I).

SVGN-038.cause: The comp confirmation signal number is illegal.
SVGN-038.remedy: Map the comp confirmation input to a valid input index via ($SPOTEQIO[].$DI_NSE_I).

SVGN-039.cause: Same as SVGN-040, but with a WARN severity.

SVGN-040.cause: The Measured part thickness deviates from the specified value more than the Under or Over thickness limit(mm). The part may be out-of-tolerance. Note: the alarm message indicates the detected(measured) thickness. This value is also displayed on the servogun status screen. Please refer to the secondary alarm code for more specific diagnostic information.
SVGN-040.remedy: Check the master position for the gun axis and make sure the tips touch at the zero position (+/- 0.1mm). Confirm that tip wear and gun sag compensation are enabled and that the compensation values are correct. Check the part or re-enter the part thickness in the pressure schedule. Alternatively, increase the Under and Over thickness limits in the Part Thickness check screen found on the Servo Gun General Setup screen. Resume the program, to retry the measurement. Perform thickness check calibration again, if the problem persists.

SVGN-041.cause: There is not enough permanent memory. It is impossible to allocate the system variable.
SVGN-041.remedy: Please increase the size of S-RAM module. Or, decrease the value of $SGSYSCFG.$M_GUN_NUM.

SVGN-042.cause: The number of $SGGUN is less than total number of axes in the servo gun group(s).
SVGN-042.remedy: Increase $SGSYSCFG.$M_GUN_NUM to the minimum value required to accommodate all servo gun axes. After changing this sysvar, go to control start, and then perform a Cold start, to make the change effective.

SVGN-043.cause: User has started Servo Gun autotuning.
SVGN-043.remedy: No remedy required. This is a warning message to log the event.

SVGN-044.cause: User has successfully completed auto tuning.
SVGN-044.remedy: User should cycle power to use servo gun.

SVGN-045.cause: Auto Tuning Could not be completed.
SVGN-045.remedy: Restart Auto tuning on the tuning menu, and try the operation again.

SVGN-046.cause: The user executed autotuning while the system was faulted.
SVGN-046.remedy: Clear ALL FAULTS and start tuning again.

SVGN-047.remedy: Disable STEP mode, and start tuning again.

SVGN-048.cause: Machine Lock is enabled for the servo gun group.
SVGN-048.remedy: Disable Machine lock from the TEST CYCLE Menu, and start tuning again.

SVGN-049.remedy: Clear the HOLD, and start tuning again.

SVGN-050.cause: Re-power is required to make some parameter changes effective.

SVGN-051.cause: SHIFT + backup (hardkey) was pressed but no Backup Schedule (stroke) was selected.
SVGN-051.remedy: Select a backup schedule by pressing the backup hardkey (without the SHIFT key).

SVGN-052.cause: The motion group number of the user program for manual pressure or manual backup is not matched to the Servo Gun group.
SVGN-052.remedy: Change the motion group number of the program to match the Servo Gun.

SVGN-053.cause: The specified backup schedule (stroke) index is not valid.
SVGN-053.remedy: Set a valid backup schedule number.

SVGN-054.cause: $EQNUM is not use in the system.
SVGN-054.remedy: Set the valid equipment number to $EQNUM.

SVGN-055.cause: The equipment specified by $EQNUM is not assigned to the Servo Gun
SVGN-055.remedy: Set the equipment number which is assigned to Servo Gun to $EQNUM.

SVGN-056.cause: Specified number is not valid for $GUNNUM.
SVGN-056.remedy: $GUNNUM can be set only 1 or 2 which is corresponding to GUN1 or GUN2

SVGN-057.message: Tip Wear Down Cal. is INCOMP.
SVGN-057.cause: Tip Wear Compensation setup is not complete.
SVGN-057.remedy: Perform the Tip Wear Setup procedure. Consult the Servo Gun Manual for details on this procedure.

SVGN-058.cause: The tool frame number or user frame number is different from the standard position.
SVGN-058.remedy: Change the frame number to same number of standard position.

SVGN-059.cause: System cannot read the position register which is specified by $PRINDEX.

SVGN-060.cause: The pressure program name is not set correctly.
SVGN-060.remedy: Set correct program name in manual operation setup screen.

SVGN-061.cause: The backup program name is not set correctly.
SVGN-061.remedy: Set correct program name in manual operation setup screen.

SVGN-062.cause: Shift + GUN hardkey was pressed, but no Pressure Schedule was selected.
SVGN-062.remedy: Select a pressure schedule, by pressing GUN hardkey, without shift key.

SVGN-063.cause: The GUN hardkey was pressed (to select pressure), but no Pressure Schedule was enabled.
SVGN-063.remedy: Enable Pressure Schedule(s) for Manual Operation by setting the Manual item to TRUE in the Pressure Schedule data table.

SVGN-064.cause: Manual Weld Verification feature was enabled.
SVGN-064.remedy: Just a notification, no action necessary.

SVGN-065.cause: Manual Weld Verification feature was disabled.
SVGN-065.remedy: Just a notification, no action necessary.

SVGN-066.cause: Manual Weld Verification feature was activated.
SVGN-066.remedy: Just a notification, to let user know he is in this mode and that groups may be disabled automatically for him

SVGN-067.cause: Manual Weld Verification feature was activated.
SVGN-067.remedy: Just a notification, to let user know he is in this mode and that groups may be enabled automatically for him

SVGN-068.cause: Could not load tp program for tip wear measurement. See cause code for reason.
SVGN-068.remedy: Resume the program, to re-attempt the load. If the load is successful, then the tip wear measurement will continue.

SVGN-069.message: Pressure position is near close limit.
SVGN-069.cause: The actual position of the gun during pressuring (SPOT or PRESS_MOTN) is approaching the gun's close limit: the distance between the gun tip (position) and the close limit < $SGSYSCFG.$CLSLMWRNTOL.
SVGN-069.remedy: Check the master position and close stroke limit for the gun. If these values are incorrect, then update them. If these values are correct, then install new tips OR, reduce the value in $SGSYSCFG.$CLSLMWRNTOL (mm) to withhold this alarm until the gun tip is closer to the close stroke limit. Set $SGSYSCFG.$CLSLMWRNTOL (mm) = 0, to disable this alarm.

SVGN-070.cause: The gun change function is disabled.

SVGN-071.cause: Machine lock for robot axes is enabled at gun attach instruction.

SVGN-073.cause: Gun is not detached. Some AXISORDER are not 0.
SVGN-073.remedy: GUN ATTACH instruction can be executed only when no gun is attached.

SVGN-074.cause: Gun is not detached. Gun attach input signal is OFF.
SVGN-074.remedy: GUN ATTACH instruction can be executed only when no gun is attached.

SVGN-075.cause: Gun is not attached. Gun attach input signal is ON.
SVGN-075.remedy: GUN DETACH instruction can be executed only when a gun is attached.

SVGN-076.cause: Another program is executing GUN ATTACH or GUN DETACH instruction. $CHG_PHASE is not 0 at executing the instruction.
SVGN-076.remedy: Wait until another program end GUN ATTACH/DETACH instruction.

SVGN-077.remedy: Confirm the setting for Gun identify signal.

SVGN-078.remedy: Confirm the setting for Gun set signal.

SVGN-079.cause: GUN ATTACH or GUN DETACH instruction is canceled while executing the instruction.

SVGN-080.cause: GUN ATTACH or GUN DETACH instruction become timeout while executing the instruction.

SVGN-081.cause: Mastering data of the gun is lost by a pause while mastering.
SVGN-081.remedy: Do COLD START the system. Then master the gun by manual operation.

SVGN-082.cause: Gun mastering is failed by a pause while mastering.

SVGN-083.cause: GUN ATTACH instruction failed. Please see cause code.

SVGN-084.cause: GUN DETACH instruction failed. Please see cause code.

SVGN-085.cause: The mastering of servo gun axis has not been performed yet. System variable $master_done set FALSE.
SVGN-085.remedy: Please perform the mastering of the servo gun axis.

SVGN-086.cause: The calibration of servo gun axis has not been performed yet. System variable $calibrate set FALSE.
SVGN-086.remedy: Please calibrate the servo gun axis.

SVGN-087.cause: Reference position has not been set when quick mastering.
SVGN-087.remedy: Quick mastering may not be possible. Fixture or zero master.

SVGN-088.cause: The gun number specified by the GUN DETACH instruction is different than the currently attached gun.
SVGN-088.remedy: Verify the gun number of GUN DETACH instruction.

SVGN-089.cause: While the calibrate motion, the detect condition was not triggered.
SVGN-089.remedy: Verify the detect condition in the gun change setup screen.

SVGN-090.cause: The PR[] index for the calibrate motion is not set.
SVGN-090.remedy: Please set PR[] index for the calibrate motion in the gun change setup screen.

SVGN-091.cause: The Touch torque for the calibrate motion is not set.
SVGN-091.remedy: Please set Touch torque for the calibrate motion in the gun change setup screen.

SVGN-092.cause: The Detect signal for the calibrate motion is not set.
SVGN-092.remedy: Please set Detect signal for the calibrate motion in the gun change setup screen.

SVGN-093.cause: At the Gun Zero Master[] instruction, Servo gun axis does not stop.
SVGN-093.remedy: After servo gun axis stops, execute the Gun Zero Master[] instruction.

SVGN-094.cause: At the Gun exhange[] instruction, the new gun could not be activated.
SVGN-094.remedy: Make sure that the each servogun has valid axisorder

SVGN-095.cause: Opposable gun type is required for target gun.
SVGN-095.remedy: Set gun type as opposable, if appropriate.

SVGN-096.cause: This operation cannot be performed while Gun Close (stroke enable) is disabled.
SVGN-096.remedy: Set the Gun operation to stroke (stroke enable) on the SoftPanel screen. Note: The SoftPanel screen can be accessed from the TEST CYCLE menu.

SVGN-097.cause: The tips did not touch during the 1st step of tip wear measurement due to an increase in gun friction or the tips touched but they are now longer than the reference tips by an amount greater than the Mis-Detect Toler.(mm)
SVGN-097.remedy: If the tips are not fully closed when the alarm occurs, then the re-master operation failed during tip wear measurement. This usually happens because the gun friction has increased since the gun was last Autotuned. Autotune the gun again and/or inspect the cause of the friction increase. After this is complete, put new tips on the gun and perform the tip wear setup procedure again. If the tips are closed when the alarm occurs, then the tips are longer than allowed. The tips measured during tip wear setup are the reference tips. New tips can only be longer than the reference tips by an amount equal to the Mis-Detect Toler.(mm) specified in the Tip Wear Detection screen (within the Servo Gun SETUP screen). Either increase the Mis-Detect Toler.(mm) or replace the tips with shorter tips. If the tips seem to be the correct length, then perform the tip wear setup procedure again to establish new reference tips.

SVGN-098.cause: The Digital Output assigned for notification of excessive Gun Tip Wear (amount) is invalid.
SVGN-098.remedy: Check the present setting of the Inform Signal for the Maximum Wear Check (gun) found on the Tip Wear Detection screen (within the Servo Gun SETUP screen). Change the DO number to one that is configured and unused. Check the Digital Output list (I/O-Type-DIGITAL-OUTPUTS) to find an available DO point to use.

SVGN-099.cause: The Digital Output assigned for the notification of excessive Robot Tip Wear (amount) is invalid.
SVGN-099.remedy: Check the present setting of the Inform Signal for the Maximum Wear Check (robot) found on the Tip Wear Detection screen (within the Servo Gun SETUP screen). Change the DO number to one that is configured and unused. Check the Digital Output list (I/O-Type-DIGITAL-OUTPUTS) to find an available DO point to use.

SVGN-100.cause: Specified register number is out of range.

SVGN-101.cause: The specified position register number is out of range.
SVGN-101.remedy: Set a valid position register number.

SVGN-102.cause: The increased error limit for Gun(movable) tip is set to 0.0mm
SVGN-102.remedy: Set the Increased error to a value greater than 0.0mm if Increased Error checking is needed. This item is set on the Tip Wear Detection screen (within the Servo Gun SETUP screen).

SVGN-103.cause: Increased error limit for Robot(stationary) tip is set to 0.0mm
SVGN-103.remedy: Set the Increased error to a value greater than 0.0mm if the Increased Error checking is needed. This item is set on the Tip Wear Detection screen (within the Servo Gun SETUP screen).

SVGN-104.cause: An excessive load is detected, during tip wear setup or tip wear update. The gun zero position might be incorrect.
SVGN-104.remedy: Remove any foreign object between the tips, and/or re-master the gun. Resume the tip wear setup or update operation. If the alarm still occurs, then the gun friction has increased since it was last Autotuned. Autotune the gun again and/or inspect the gun to determine the cause of the friction increase.

SVGN-105.cause: The pulse coder alarm was not reset.
SVGN-105.remedy: Reset the pulse coder alarm again.

SVGN-106.remedy: Perform the Tip Wear Setup procedure. Consult the Servo Gun Manual for details on this procedure.

SVGN-107.cause: The load threshold used to detect contact with the fixture for the second step of tip wear measurement has not been set.
SVGN-107.remedy: Perform the Tip Wear Setup procedure. Consult the Servo Gun Manual for details on this procedure.

SVGN-108.cause: The reference zero position (i.e. standard pulse) used for tip wear measurement has not been set.
SVGN-108.remedy: Perform the Tip Wear Setup procedure. Consult the Servo Gun Manual for details on this procedure.

SVGN-109.cause: The reference open position (i.e. standard opening) used for the second step of tip wear measurement has not been set.
SVGN-109.remedy: Perform the Tip Wear Setup procedure. Consult the Servo Gun Manual for details on this procedure.

SVGN-110.message: Tip wear no detect DI index.
SVGN-110.cause: The Tip wear Detection Type is set to DI, but no DI index is specified.
SVGN-110.remedy: Confirm that DI detection is the desired type (LOAD detection is the default type). If so, then assign an available DI point to the tip wear detection sensor and set that index value into the Detect Signal item on the Tip Wear Detection Screen.

SVGN-111.cause: The gun tip reached the master position without detecting the fixture (i.e. tip wear plate) during the second step of tip wear measurement.
SVGN-111.remedy: Confirm that the zero position is correct, then confirm that a rigid fixture is between the tips during the second step of tip wear measurement.

SVGN-112.cause: Tip wear measurement or thickness check calibration started, but Servo tuning is incomplete.
SVGN-112.remedy: Complete servo auto-tuning. Go to the Gun Setup Utility (UTILITIES-GUN SETUP) and select the Auto Tune item. The Auto Tune program can be started after completing the previous steps in the utility.

SVGN-113.cause: The tip wear setup or update program started with the gun closed.
SVGN-113.remedy: Open the tips, then execute the tip wear measurement program again. If the problem persists, master the gun, then execute the tip wear measurement program again.

SVGN-114.cause: The moving tip did not touch the fixture during the second step of tip wear measurement due to an increase in gun friction, or the fixture and/or robot master position has changed since tip wear was initialized.
SVGN-114.remedy: If the moving tip is not pressing into the fixture when the alarm occurs, the fixture touch load (i.e. pressing force) was reached without actually touching the fixture. This usually happens because the gun friction has increased since the tip wear setup program was run. Increase the Margin of Load item in the Tip Wear Detection Screen to overcome the increase in friction. Doing this can affect the tip wear measurement, so the tip wear setup procedure should be performed again. Autotune the gun again and/or inspect the gun for the cause of the friction increase. If the moving tip is pressing into the fixture when the alarm occurs then the fixture position has moved relative to the robot master position, the robot master data has changed, or the points in the program TW_MV2PT.tp have changed. Perform the tip wear setup procedure again.

SVGN-115.remedy: Retry the operation. Make sure that there is some separation (at least a few mm), between the guntip/fixedtip and drive mechanism/open_hardstop.

SVGN-116.cause: Magnet Phase detection is unavailable with the current calibration motion type.
SVGN-116.remedy: Change the calibration motion type(to 7or8) in the Gun change screen.

SVGN-117.cause: The Gun closing motion to set the reference position failed.
SVGN-117.remedy: Confirm that the Touch torque(%) on the Gun SETUP screen is set appropriately.

SVGN-118.cause: The maximum tip wear amount has been exceeded on the gun tip.
SVGN-118.remedy: Replace the gun tip or re-run tip wear setup.

SVGN-119.cause: The maximum tip wear amount has been exceeded on the robot tip.
SVGN-119.remedy: Replace the robot tip or re-run tip wear setup.

SVGN-120.message: Skipped max gun torque update: Gun%d.
SVGN-120.cause: Max gun torque was not updated due to an invalid parameter.
SVGN-120.remedy: See the cause code to identify the reason for the update failure. Correct the problem as described by the remedy for the alarm specified in the cause code.

SVGN-122.cause: The specified pressure cannot be used, it does not lie on the calibration curve (2nd order).
SVGN-122.remedy: Change the calibration method to the multi-linear segment method if possible. Do this by setting the system variables $sgsyscfg.$cal_model = 12 and $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv = 3, then perform the pressure calibration again. Alternatively, perform pressure calibration again, or reduce max pressure.

SVGN-123.cause: Overtorque protection has been disabled. This is merely a warning to notify the operator.

SVGN-124.message: Max gun torque must be > floor.
SVGN-124.cause: The Max Gun Torque parameter in OverTorque Protection is less than the Standard OverTorque Value. The Max Gun Torque is the torque required to achieve the Max Pressure of the gun (according to the Pressure Calibration data). The Standard OverTorque Value is the lowest torque (i.e. floor) where an abnormal torque condition can be accurately observed due to gun friction.
SVGN-124.remedy: To eliminate this alarm either the Max Gun Torque must be increased or the Standard OverTorque Value needs to be lower. If OverTorque Protection is still enabled, there might be no action necessary. View the Parameter Summary in OverTorque Protection to judge whether the values are acceptable. The Max Gun Torque can be increased by increasing the Max Pressure on the Servo Gun General Setup Screen. If OverTorque Protection is presently disabled, be sure to enable it after this. If the Pressure Calibration is not complete or the data is old, perform the Pressure Calibration again.

SVGN-125.message: Max gun torque must be < ceil.
SVGN-125.cause: The Max Gun Torque parameter in OverTorque Protection is set higher than the maximum torque of the servo motor.
SVGN-125.remedy: Make sure Pressure Calibration of the gun is complete and the data is entered correctly. Perform Pressure Calibration again if possible. Decrease The Max Gun Torque by decreasing the Max Pressure of the gun via the Servogun General SETUP Screen.

SVGN-126.message: Servo parameters exceed max gun torque.
SVGN-126.cause: Overtorque protection is enabled, but one or more of the parameters responsible for limiting torque exceeded the max gun torque.
SVGN-126.remedy: Disable, then re-enable overtorque protection, in order to re-write servo parameters. Alternatively, disable overtorque protection OR enable machine lock on the servogun group to disable this alarm.

SVGN-127.message: DSP max gun torque update timeout.
SVGN-127.cause: Timeout, waiting for acknowledgement of new overtorque parameters.
SVGN-127.remedy: Cycle power or toggle overtorque protect enable to write parameters again.

SVGN-128.cause: A string parameter or a value less than 0.0 was passed into the THK_VAL macro.
SVGN-128.remedy: Re-enter a parameter value greater than or equal to 0.0 into the thickness value macro.

SVGN-129.cause: A string parameter or a value less than 0.0 was specified for the THK_TOL macro.
SVGN-129.remedy: Re-enter a parameter value greater than or equal to 0.0 into the thickness tolerance macro.

SVGN-130.cause: A string parameter or a value other than 1 or 2 was specified for the THK_SEV macro.
SVGN-130.remedy: Re-enter a parameter value of 1 or 2 into the thickness severity macro.

SVGN-131.cause: A string parameter or a value other than 1, 2, or 3 was specified for gun index in a THK_ macro.
SVGN-131.remedy: This parameter is optional but if it is specified, set it as follows: 1: Gun.A only 2: Gun.B only (dual gun case) 3: Gun.A+B (dual gun case)

SVGN-132.message: Invalid inform signal (dualgun max wear diff).
SVGN-132.cause: An invalid output index is assigned for notification of excessive difference between fixed tip wear amounts (on gunA and gunB).
SVGN-132.remedy: Confirm that the setting of rack, slot and start point is valid. Cycle power if necessary, to make the io assignment effective. Set index=0 to disable this signal.

SVGN-133.cause: An encoder scale value of 0.0 was detected.
SVGN-133.remedy: Re-enter the gear ratio on the NOBOT Maintenance menu.

SVGN-134.cause: Thickness Check Calibration was never performed or did not complete successfully.
SVGN-134.remedy: Go to Gun Setup Utility screen (UTILITIES-GUN SETUP) and re-execute the Thickness Check Calibration.

SVGN-135.message: Thickness check cal err: bad torque
SVGN-135.cause: A thickness check calibration point has a torque value that is not greater than 0.0, or is not in ascending order.
SVGN-135.remedy: Go to the Gun Setup Utility Screen (UTILITIES-GUN SETUP) and re-execute the Thickness Check Calibration.

SVGN-136.message: Thickness check cal err: bad deflection
SVGN-136.cause: A thickness check calibration point has a deflection value that is not greater than 0.0, or is not in ascending order.
SVGN-136.remedy: Go to the Gun Setup Utility Screen (UTILITIES-GUN SETUP) and re-execute Thickness Check Calibration. If the error still occurs, re-master and re-execute Thickness Check Calibration.

SVGN-137.message: Invalid Number of Thickness Cal pts.
SVGN-137.cause: The number of Thickness Check calibration points is less than 2 or greater than 4.
SVGN-137.remedy: Display the system variable screen and enter a value of 2, 3, or 4 into $sgthkset#.$num_cal_pts, where # = gun number.

SVGN-138.cause: The tip wear ratio for one step wear measurement is invalid (less than 0.0 or greater than 1.0).
SVGN-138.remedy: Set the wear ratio in the Tip Wear measurement macro program to a value between 0 and 1. The macro program WR_UPDAT is used to perform the Tip Wear measurement with the 1-Step Method. Set the wear-ratio which is found as a parameter in a CALL instruction to the program TWKCALC2, or a similar name. Follow the program comments to find the proper parameter to adjust: CALL TWKCALC2(wear-ratio,AR[2]).

SVGN-139.message: Could not read tip stick detect input.
SVGN-139.cause: Tip stick detect input could not be read, due to an I/O error.
SVGN-139.remedy: Check the I/O mapping/configuration and I/O device status.

SVGN-140.cause: The specified start distance number is not valid.
SVGN-140.remedy: Specify a start distance number greater than or equal to 1 and less than or equal to $sgsyscfg.$dst_elm.

SVGN-141.cause: The specified end distance number is not valid.
SVGN-141.remedy: Specify an end distance number greater than or equal to 1 and less than or equal to $sgsyscfg.$dst_elm.

SVGN-142.cause: The decel rate option setting is incompatible with the speed calibration specification.
SVGN-142.remedy: Set $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv=3 OR contact FANUC America Corporation for assistance. Note: $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv==3 is the default setting for this variable, so absolute speed calibration is a non-standard setting.

SVGN-143.cause: Automaster operation is executing and position error due to push depth exceeds stoperlim. Stop error excess alarm may occur.

SVGN-144.cause: Gun deflection at torque = 0 exceeds $SGTHKSET#.$MAX_D0BIAS. Gun deflection should be ~0 at torque=0, so gun master position may be incorrect.
SVGN-144.remedy: 1. Remaster gun – if system is setup to do tip wear measurements, run the tip wear measurement program (typ. wr_updat or tw_updat). If not doing tip wear measurements, go to gun master screen and execute mastering with new tips. 2. Execute Thickness Check Calibration (UTILITIES-GUN SETUP). 3. If problem persists, increase $SGTHKSET#.$MAX_D0BIAS (default = 1.0mm).

SVGN-146.cause: Joint velocity limit must be greater than zero, for mm/sec pressure calibration speed specification.
SVGN-146.remedy: Update joint velocity limit using one of the following methods: 1. Re-enter the gear ratio via the Servo Gun Axes item on the Maintenance menu, at Control start. 2. Directly enter the Max Joint Speed on the Axis Data screen of the Servo Gun Setup menu, at control start.

SVGN-147.cause: The minimum gun opening distance required to achieve the specified contact speed for this Pressure Schedule is larger than the opening specified by the Start Distance schedule used in the SPOT or Press_Motion instruction. The correct contact speed might not have been achieved during execution of this instruction.
SVGN-147.remedy: Increase the Start Distances assigned to the Distance Schedule that is used when this alarm occurs. Go to the Distance Schedule data table (DATA-DISTANCE) and increase the gun and/or robot distances.

SVGN-148.cause: Can't identify routine name corresponding to the standalone instruction. Refer to cause code for root cause.

SVGN-149.cause: CP mode is not enabled, but synchronize move to pressure position is enabled AND/OR linear distance is enabled.
SVGN-149.remedy: Enable CP mode (set $cpcfg.$cp_enable=TRUE) or contact FANUC America Corporation for assistance.

SVGN-150.cause: The linear distance function is enabled, but synchronize move to pressure is not enabled.
SVGN-150.remedy: Enable synchronize move to pressure position (set $sgsyscfg.$sync_mv2prs=TRUE) OR disable linear distance (set $sgsyscfg.$lin_dst_enb=FALSE).

SVGN-151.message: Cannot add file to backup/restore list.
SVGN-151.cause: Servogun sysvar file(s) could not be added to backup/restore list.
SVGN-151.remedy: Report problem to FANUC America Corporation.

SVGN-152.cause: The Digital Output assigned to notify of increased error on the Gun Tip is invalid.
SVGN-152.remedy: Check the present value of $sggun#.$setup.$tipincioidx (on the system variable screen). Change this value to the number of a DO that is configured and unused. Check the Digital Output list (I/O-Type-DIGITAL-OUTPUTS) to find an available DO point to use.

SVGN-153.cause: The Digital Output assigned to notify of increased error on the Robot Tip is invalid.
SVGN-153.remedy: Check the present value of $sggun#.$setup.$rbtincioidx (on the system variable screen). Change this value to the number of a DO that is configured and unused. Check the Digital Output list (I/O-Type-DIGITAL-OUTPUTS) to find an available DO point to use.

SVGN-154.cause: Tip wear update did not complete, due to cancel or gun close error. Refer to cause code for specific reason.
SVGN-154.remedy: Correct the condition identified in the cause code, then run tip wear update again.

SVGN-155.cause: Pressure shortage occurred during zero calibration and “Cancel tip wear update and exit” or “Initiate fast fault recovery” was chosen on the alarm recovery screen.
SVGN-155.remedy: Correct the issue that caused the pressure shortage, then run tip wear update again.

SVGN-156.cause: Gun close reference position was NOT recorded (for tip wear gun close check). PRESS_MOTN[] instruction did not complete or was skipped, during zero calibration.

SVGN-157.message: Gun not closed at zero cal process end.
SVGN-157.cause: Zero calibration was not performed because gun is not closed (gun is too far from close position). Note1: the condition for SVGN-157 detection is: |a-b| > c, where: a = Gun position after PRESS_MOTN[] instruction executes in zero calibration program (TWZRCLB2). b = Gun position when Gun Zero Master[] instruction executes in zero calibration program(TWZRCLB2). c = Gun close error tolerance (default: 2.0mm). Note2: Items a-b and c are karel variables in program: TWKINIT. a-b: Posdiff is stored in [TWKINIT]gcls_posdif[ eq# ] c: Close error tol is stored in [TWKINIT]gcls_err_tol Note3: Posdiff can be thought of as position b, with position a as Zero master position. For example, if a is more closed than b, and gun open direction is negative, then posdif polarity is negative (magnitude equals distance between a and b).
SVGN-157.remedy: 1. If gun position is changing after PRESS_MOTN[] (inverted gun that drops/drifts for example) then correct this condition so zero calibration is accurate. 2. Increase gcls_err_tol, if gcls_err_tol is too small. 3. Perform tip wear update again. 4. Disable gun close error check by setting [TWKINIT]gcls_err_enb = FALSE.

SVGN-158.cause: This alarm provides information to identify the root cause of the pressure shortage alarm. Parameters meanings are: Thk: Thickness expected (value specified in pressure schedule) Push.Exp: Pushing depth expected (larger of pushing depth in pressure schedule and speed depth) Push.Aval: Pushing depth available (thk + current close stroke limit) Push.Max: Pushing depth maximum (thk + standard close stroke limit)
SVGN-158.remedy: If thickness and/or pushing depth are incorrect, then adjust them. If stroke limit has become too small, install new tips.

SVGN-159.cause: Pressure margin conversion for touchup process failed. See cause code for reason.

SVGN-160.cause: A pressure calibration point has a torque value that is not greater than 0.0, or is not in ascending order.
SVGN-160.remedy: Perform Pressure Calibration again. Make sure that both torque and pressure increase at each successive calibration point.

SVGN-161.cause: A Speed value in the Pressure Calibration table is less than the min speed or greater than the max speed.
SVGN-161.remedy: Perform Pressure Calibration again. Make sure that the Speed for each point in the Pressure Calibration table is within the operating range of the gun.

SVGN-162.cause: A pressure calibration point has a pressure (force) value that is not greater than 0.0, or is not in ascending order.
SVGN-162.remedy: Perform Pressure Calibration again. Make sure that both torque and pressure increase, at each successive calibration point.

SVGN-163.cause: The calibration model setting ($sgsyscfg.$cal_model) is not supported. The following settings are supported: 3: Single linear segment pressure and speed model 12: Multiple linear segment pressure and speed model piece-wise pressure calibration.
SVGN-163.remedy: Change setting to one of the settings above, and reperform calibration if necessary.

SVGN-164.cause: Pressure to speed conversion specification ($sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv) is not supported. The following setting combinations are supported: $sgsyscfg.$cal_model = 3 and $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv = 0: Single linear segment, JNT%. $sgsyscfg.$cal_model = 3 and $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv = 3, Single linear segment, mm/sec converted at spot. $sgsyscfg.$cal_model = 12 and $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv = 3, Multiple linear segments, mm/sec converted at spot.
SVGN-164.remedy: Change setting to one of the settings above, and re-perform calibration if necessary. Note: $sgsyscfg.$frc2spd_cnv==3 is the default setting for this variable.

SVGN-165.cause: The open distance condition for equalization pressure trigger, was not met before the start of motion to pressure position, for the next spot. The equalization trigger state for the next spot might have been delayed, in this case.
SVGN-165.remedy: Increase the end and/or start distance value on the distance schedule screen, or decrease the open distance for the equalization pressure trigger AFTER the SPOT.

SVGN-166.cause: The specified equalization pressure trigger type is not supported.
SVGN-166.remedy: Select a valid trigger on the Spot equipment SETUP screen.

SVGN-167.cause: The specified equalization pressure trigger event is undefined.
SVGN-167.remedy: Go to the spot equipment setup screen, and select a valid trigger event.

SVGN-168.cause: The pushing depth specified in the pressure schedule or the minimum pushing depth, exceed the strokelimit. The contact speed might be slightly lower than specified as a result of this alarm.
SVGN-168.remedy: Update one or more of the parameters used to specify pushing depth: $sgsch#[].$push_depth and $sggun.$setup.$push_margin. If these parameters cannot be reduced, then increase the strokelimit, if possible. Note that this is only a warning.

SVGN-169.cause: The minimum push depth (internally calculated distance) required to decelerate from the contact speed exceeds the maximum possible pushing depth: part thickness + close stroke limit. The value of the minimum pushing depth (specified in the alarm message) was clamped to the maximum possible pushing depth.
SVGN-169.remedy: Decrease $sggun#.$setup.$push_margin, or increase the close stroke limit. Although this alarm has a warn severity, this condition should be corrected since the minimum push depth has been clamped to a value that is small enough to affect contact speed and/or contact speed persistence. Note 1: SVGN-169, basically indicates that the close limit value is abnormal, since minimum push depth is typically less than 5mm. Note 2: part thickness is automatically added to the pushing depth value during tryout mode to compensate for the missing part.

SVGN-170.cause: The instruction format PRESS_MOTN[SD=,P=,SEL=(,)] cannot be used with the setting $SGSYSDG.$UGA_IDX4GB=FALSE. GunB must use GunA data, for this instruction.
SVGN-170.remedy: If you want to use the instruction format PRESS_MOTN[SD=,P=,SEL=(,)] then set $SGSYSDG.$UGA_IDX4GB=TRUE. If you do not want to use the instruction format PRESS_MOTN[SD=,P=,SEL=(,)] then change the instruction to PRESS_MOTN[SD=(,),P=(,)] (the setting of $SGSYSDG.$UGA_IDX4GB is ignored for the format PRESS_MOTN[SD=(,),P=(,)]).

SVGN-171.cause: The Pressure[]kgf or Pressure level Gun instruction was executed, and the requested torque > max gun torque (OTP torque limit mode).
SVGN-171.remedy: Perform autotuning or disable overtorque protection.

SVGN-172.message: Can not move gun during interrupt
SVGN-172.cause: A SPOT[] or PRESS_MOTN[] instruction was performed during an interrupt routine (Ex. TB,TA,DB,program monitor etc).
SVGN-172.remedy: Adjust the trigger timing of interrupt routine. Also, wait until the interrupt routine completes then run the servo gun instruction

SVGN-173.cause: A timeout occurred during power-up Gun-attach sequence. Possible causes are: 1. A servo problem interrupted the servo startup sequence, and caused the attach sequence to fail. For example, fuse FS1 on servo amp is blown. 2. The servo gun is NOT connected correctly. For example pulsecoder cable is disconnected.
SVGN-173.remedy: Check alarm log for servo errors and and correct the issue if one is found. For example: SRVO-058 FSSB %d init error (%d) If no servo problem is found, then check cable connections for servogun. Also, check motor and gun change board. If this problem persists contact your FANUC technical representative.

SVGN-174.cause: The Servo Gun softpart could not be notified of the event. Refer to the function code(fcod) and status(stat).
SVGN-174.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical service representative.

SVGN-175.cause: GunTouchup(F3) or AutoTouchup(F4) was requested but touchup did not occur. This alarm (SVGN-175) only indicates that touchup failure has occurred, SVGN-176 identifies cause of SVGN-175. Note: SVGN-175 is not posted during program touchup.
SVGN-175.remedy: See SVGN-176. NOTE: SVGN-175 is an optional alarm (enabled by default). Set $SGSYSTCH.$PTNOTRECALM = FALSE to disable SVGN-275.

SVGN-176.remedy: Refer to remedy for message in string.

SVGN-177.cause: This is information at pressure shortage.
SVGN-177.remedy: Incorrect thickness or/and gun close limit would cause a pressure shortage If thikness or/and gun close limit is incorrect, gun tip can not go correct push depth for setpoint pressure The Thk is value which is specifiied in pressure schedule. Check if thikness value in pressure schedule is correct for actual thickness. This CloseLim is present gun close limit,and the StdLim is gun close limit of no-wear down. If CloseLim is too shorter than StdLim, replace gun tip then perform wear down update program. If StdLim is already too short, set the correct standard limit in servo gun setup screen.

SVGN-178.cause: This is information of standard stroke limit.
SVGN-178.remedy: Gun storke limit is compensated by tip wear down. The standard value is stroke limit when TW_SETUP or WR_SETUP is performed an original value. This shorter standard storke limit may cause pressure shortage. If the standard storke limit is shorter than original value,set correct standard limit in servo gun setup screen.

SVGN-179.cause: The program attempted the servogun command with more than 2 groups.
SVGN-179.remedy: The servogun option supports a maximum of 2 groups due to complex synchronization. Use a program with less than 3 groups in the group mask, or remove servogun command (SPOT or PRESS_MOTN) from the program.

SVGN-180.cause: Persisted pressure after HOLD is canceled
SVGN-180.remedy: Pressure could not be persisted during BWD or ABORT So Persisted pressure is canceled This is warning massage for blowing out. Please check panel status if you are welding.

SVGN-181.cause: The Measured part thickness is less than the under-thickness limit(mm). The part may be out-of-tolerance. NOTE: This message displays the nominal (expected/programmed) thickness and the under-thickness (MinAllowable) limit.

SVGN-182.cause: The Measured part thickness is greater than the over-thickness limit(mm). The part may be out-of-tolerance. NOTE: This message displays the nominal (expected/programmed) thickness and the over-thickness (MaxAllowable) limit.

SVGN-183.cause: Gun touchup function has modified position of spot point. This message is provided for informational purposes only, it is not a fault/problem. Note: SVGN-183 is not posted during program touchup.
SVGN-183.remedy: The 4 parameters in SVGN-183 p1/p2/p3/ p4 provide details about the modified point. p3: Corrected value is the difference between new recorded position and old recorded position. Note: robot close direction is positive polarity, so if new position is shifted in robot open direction (relative to old position) corrected value will be negative. p4: Thickness value is actual thickness measured during thickness check. Note: If thickness check is disabled, nominal thickness (value in pressure schedule) is reported.

SVGN-184.cause: Spot point touchup was cancelled, because shift key was released and program edit screen was de-selected (new screen was selected).
SVGN-184.remedy: Execute point touchup again, and don't exit editor screen.

SVGN-185.cause: Data collected during search process exceeded storage buffer. Note: SVGN-185 only occurs during unpress (a process that is no longer used), so it is basically obsolete.
SVGN-185.remedy: Reduce unpress time by increasing speed ($SGGUN#.$TEACH.$LWDT_CLOSPD) or decreasing observation time ($SGGUN#.$TEACH.$LWDT_OBSLEN).

SVGN-186.cause: This indicates information for tip increased error. The left value indicates the last wear down. The right value indicates current measured wear down. Since the current measured wear down is incorrect, so increased alarm is posted. Difference of the right value from the left value becomes increased error amount.
SVGN-186.remedy: Please see remedy for SVGN-32 and/or SVGN-33. Note: If current measured wear down is nearly 0, update program might be performed without new tip flag.

SVGN-187.message: Do gun zero mastering with new tip
SVGN-187.cause: Tip wear setup was performed, without performing gun zero mastering first. This condition can lead to incorrect mastering for tip wear reference position and cause gun stroke limit to become incorrect.
SVGN-187.remedy: Perform gun zero mastering in gun zero mastering screen with new tip.

SVGN-188.cause: An internal error has occurred. Execution restart information is incomplete.
SVGN-188.remedy: Document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

SVGN-189.cause: Tipwear had been setup, but a BZAL alarm occurred and tipwear zero reference (pls0) is not up to date. Pls0 must be updated after BZAL to maintain proper stroke limit (Overstroke protection is turned of after BZAL to avoid invalid strokelimit values).
SVGN-189.remedy: Go to gun master screen and execute recalibrate or master. Either action updates pls0, and turns overstroke protection on.

SVGN-190.cause: Open (search start) distance for upper panel detection exceeded gun stroke limit, so open distance was clamped to gun open limit. Note: Gun open distance for upper panel search depends on touchup type: if point touchup: open distance = initial pos + search prep dist if prog touchup: open distance = thk.nom+thk.err.max+pos.err.max+searchprep dist SVGN-190 does not cause any problem if panel contact occurs AFTER search start. However, if panel contact occurs BEFORE search start, excessive push and/or touchup failure may result. Note: backup pos = org pos + search_backup_dist + rbt_bkup_dist. Search backup distance is distance required in order to detect panel at org_pos. Search backup distance + robot backup distance is distance required to detect panel at org_pos AFTER robot moves fixed tip away from panel. I.E. robot backup distance does not affect guntip to panel distance and is considered optional. Therefore, in case where gun open distance is sufficient to accomodate panel detection after moving fixed tip from panel (by robot backup distance), SVGN-386 (and not SVGN-190) is posted. However, if open limit is too small to even accomodate backup distance for search then both SVGN-386 and SVGN-190 are posted.
SVGN-190.remedy: If point touchup is being performed, close gun (jog) to reduce open distance. If program touchup is being performed, reduce one or more of the following parameters: upper panel detect distance, max thickness error, max pos error.

SVGN-191.cause: Thickness Check Calibration was successful - parameters were updated. Note: This alarm is merely status information, it is not a fault/problem.

SVGN-192.cause: Thickness Check Calibration parameter is not updated Thickness Check Calibration could not finished correctly Note: If thickness Check Calibration had done before, the last parameter is restored.
SVGN-192.remedy: Please see cause code or other relative alarm on alarm screen Remove cause that makes pausing stopping sequence Then retry Thickness Check Calib sequence to updated parameter.

SVGN-193.cause: Automaster operation was successful, and mm distance between old and new master position is provided for reference.
SVGN-193.remedy: No remedy needed - this alarm is for information purposes only.

SVGN-194.cause: Automaster operation failed. Refer to cause code for reason.
SVGN-194.remedy: Formulate remedy based on cause code.

SVGN-195.cause: Automaster operation was successful, and master count values - old and new - are provided for reference.
SVGN-195.remedy: No remedy needed - this alarm is for information purposes only.

SVGN-196.cause: Auto wear calibrate operation was successful, and mm distance between old and new pulse0 value is provided for reference.
SVGN-196.remedy: No remedy needed - this alarm is for information purposes only.

SVGN-197.cause: Auto wear calibrate operation failed. Refer to cause code for reason.
SVGN-197.remedy: No remedy needed - this alarm is for information purposes only.

SVGN-198.cause: Auto wear calibrate operation was successful, and master count values - old and new - are provided for reference.
SVGN-198.remedy: Refer to cause code for specific information.

SVGN-199.cause: Status information about automaster operation is being posted.
SVGN-199.remedy: Refer to cause code for specific information.

SVGN-200.message: FCTRL must be off for automaster.
SVGN-200.cause: Automaster was requested while gun was still in force control. Automaster cannot start until fctrl is cleared.
SVGN-200.remedy: Press fault reset and execute automaster again. (SVGN-200 alarm automatically resets force control).

SVGN-201.cause: The posted error occurred on GunA (gun index 1) of the dual gun.
SVGN-201.remedy: Correct the error on the gun number corresponding to GunA (gun index 1).

SVGN-202.cause: The posted error occurred on GunB (gun index 2) of the dual gun.
