SVGN-612.cause: Dither compensation enable/disable state has changed, and repower is necessary to activate change.
SVGN-612.remedy: Cycle power. This alarm is merely a notification, it is not an abnormal condition.

SVTL-001.remedy: Make sure axis number is right.

SVTL-002.cause: Time out while Updating servo parameters.
SVTL-002.remedy: This should only happen in desktop unit or virtual robot. Otherwise, please check alarm log for other errors.

SVTL-003.cause: Servo Tool is active when TP program is executed.
SVTL-003.remedy: Abort the original TP program which activates Servo Tool or execute SERVOTOOL END inst.

SVTL-004.cause: Torque limit used in Servo Tool schedule ID is less than 0.1%.
SVTL-004.remedy: Set torque limit in Servo Tool schedule ID to more than 0.1%.

SVTL-005.cause: Group number in Servo Tool schedule ID does not match with current TP program's group mask.
SVTL-005.remedy: Use group number 0 in Servo Tool schedule or change TP program's group mask.

SVTL-006.cause: The destination position has been reached before contact detected.
SVTL-006.remedy: Make sure part is present or increase torque limit.

SVTL-007.cause: Program is paused while detecting part.
SVTL-007.remedy: Not pause program while part detecting.

SVTL-008.cause: Program continues after pause while detecting.
SVTL-008.remedy: Not pause program while part detecting.

SVTL-009.cause: Zero group mask program is running when Servo Tool is active.

SVTL-010.cause: Time out occured while detecting part and coasting to the destination position.
SVTL-010.remedy: Make sure part present, increase torque limit, or increase time out value.

SVTL-011.cause: Software axis limit occurred while axis is under low torque for G: group, A: axis, and U: upper or lower limit.
SVTL-011.remedy: This is a warning to remind the axis may be pushed out of

SVTL-012.cause: forward kinemtics failed or unknown position type of taught points

SVTL-013.cause: the axis ServoTool endabled was not moving before motion line finished.

SYST-001.cause: You attempted an operation while the hold button (input) is pressed.
SYST-001.remedy: Clear the hold button (input), and try the same operation.

SYST-002.cause: Meaning The condition that the robot is being held is locked by the program, and it could not be cleared. If a HOLD statement is executed in a KAREL program, the held condition can only be cleared by the same program using the UNHOLD statement/action, or by aborting the program. If a motion is attempted in such condition, this error message is displayed.
SYST-002.remedy: Wait until the UNHOLD statement is executed by the KAREL program, or abort the KAREL program.

SYST-003.cause: The attempted operation could not be done because the teach pendant is enabled.
SYST-003.remedy: Disable the teach pendant, and try the same operation again.

SYST-004.cause: The attempted operation could not be done because the System Operator Panel is enabled.
SYST-004.remedy: Turn the REMOTE switch on the SOP to REMOTE side, and try the same operation again.

SYST-005.cause: The attempted operation could not be done because the User Operator Panel is enabled.
SYST-005.remedy: Set the remote/local operation mode to Local in the system configuration screen (if the operation is attempted from the SOP), or set the $RMT_MASTER system variable correctly. Refer to the Software Reference Manual, Chapter 2 System Variables, for more information on system variables. Set the variable to one of the following values: 0:User Operator, 1:CRT/KB, 2:Host computer, 3:Remote device none, 4:RobotLink master

SYST-006.cause: The attempted operation could not be done because KCL is the master device.
SYST-006.remedy: Set the remote/local operation mode to Local in the system configuration screen (if the operation is attempted from the SOP), or set the $RMT_MASTER system variable correctly. Refer to the Software Reference Manual, Chapter 2 System Variables, for more information on system variables. Set the variable to one of the following values: 0:User Operator Panel, 1:CRT/KB, 2:Host computer, 3:Remote device none, 4:RobotLink master

SYST-007.cause: The attempted operation could not be done because the NETWORK command processor is the master device.
SYST-007.remedy: Set the remote/local operation mode to Local in the system configuration screen (if the operation is attempted from the SOP), or set the $RMT_MASTER system variable correctly. Refer to the Software Reference Manual, Chapter 2 System Variables, for more information on system variables. Set the variable to one of the following values: 0:User Operator Panel, 1:CRT/KB, 2:Host computer, 3:Remote device none, 4:RobotLink master

SYST-008.cause: The system variable $RMT_MASTER is set to disable all devices. Therefore, no remote device can issue motion.
SYST-008.remedy: Set the remote/local operation mode to Local in the system configuration screen (if the operation is attempted from the SOP), or set the $RMT_MASTER system variable correctly. Refer to the Software Reference Manual, Chapter 2 System Variables, for more information on system variables. Set the variable to one of the following values: 0:User Operator Panel, 1:CRT/KB, 2:Host computer, 3:Remote device none, 4:RobotLink master

SYST-009.cause: The attempted operation could not be done because the safety fence is open.
SYST-009.remedy: Close the safety fence, and try the same operation again.

SYST-010.cause: The number of task has reached the maximum.
SYST-010.remedy: Abort one of the running task.

SYST-011.cause: The system has failed to run the program.
SYST-011.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

SYST-013.cause: The specified PNS number is not in the range of 1 to 9999.

SYST-014.cause: PNS operation has failed by some reason.
SYST-014.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

SYST-015.cause: RSR operation has failed by some reason.
SYST-015.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use MENU to display the Alarm Log screen.

SYST-016.cause: ENBL signal in UOP is off

SYST-018.cause: Attempt to continue program from different line from paused line
SYST-018.remedy: Respond YES or NO in the prompt box on at the teach pendant

SYST-019.remedy: Select a program from the program select menu on the teach pendant, or using PNS

SYST-020.cause: The program specified by PNS is different from the currently selected program. This error occurs in Mate controllers only.
SYST-020.remedy: Select a correct program from the program select menu on the teach pendant.

SYST-021.cause: An error has been detected by the system
SYST-021.remedy: Press RESET to clear error condition

SYST-022.cause: The paused program cannot be continued if the PNS input ports are not zero. This error occurs in Mate controllers only.
SYST-022.remedy: Set all PNS input ports to OFF.

SYST-023.remedy: Check the teach pendant cable. Replace the cable if necessary.

SYST-024.message: PNSTROBE is OFF. Cannot start exec
SYST-024.cause: Because PNSTROBE is off, prod_start could not be processed

SYST-025.cause: The type of teach pendant being connected, is different from the one that was disconnected.
SYST-025.remedy: Connect the same type of teach pendant as disconnected.

SYST-026.cause: System has executed normal power startup
SYST-026.remedy: This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

SYST-027.cause: HOT start has failed for one of the following reasons: 1. Power failed during system start up. 2. Flash ROM module was changed. 3. A run-time error occurred. 4. System internal error 1. 5. System internal error 2.

SYST-028.cause: $PWR_HOT,$PWR_SEMI program has been aborted by the system due to time out (40sec)
SYST-028.remedy: Decrease program size so that it can be executed within the time out limit

SYST-029.cause: The connect/isolate key was turn to the connect side
SYST-029.remedy: This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

SYST-030.cause: The connect/isolate key was turn to the isolate side
SYST-030.remedy: This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

SYST-031.cause: An error has occurred accessing F-ROM
SYST-031.remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

SYST-032.message: ENBL signal from UOP is lost
SYST-032.cause: ENBL input signal from UOP is lost
SYST-032.remedy: Determine and correct the cause of loss of this signal.

SYST-033.message: SFSPD signal from UOP is lost

SYST-033.remedy: Determine and correct the cause of loss of this signal.

SYST-034.message: HOLD signal from SOP/UOP is lost
SYST-034.cause: HOLD input signal from SOP/UOP is lost
SYST-034.remedy: Determine and correct the cause of loss of this signal.

SYST-035.message: Low or No Battery Power on MAIN
SYST-035.cause: Battery in PSU board is low in power.
SYST-035.remedy: Replace the Old Battery with a new battery of same kind.

SYST-036.remedy: This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

SYST-037.remedy: Please fix the CE Sign key switch

SYST-038.remedy: This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

SYST-039.remedy: This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

SYST-040.remedy: This is just a notification. You do not have to do anything for this warning message.

SYST-042.cause: The mode switch was changed from T1 or T2 mode to AUTO mode and the DEADMAN was already pressed. The DEADMAN must be released when switching to AUTO mode
SYST-042.remedy: Release the DEADMAN and press RESET.

SYST-043.cause: The mode selector is in T1 or T2 and the TP ON/OFF switch is in the OFF position
SYST-043.remedy: Turn the TP ON/OFF switch to ON. Press RESET.

SYST-044.cause: The mode selector is in T1 or T2 and the TP ON/OFF switch is in the OFF position and SVON is ON. This is an abnormal condition.
SYST-044.remedy: Call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

SYST-045.cause: The mode selector is in AUTO and the TP ON/OFF switch is in the ON position
SYST-045.remedy: Turn the TP ON/OFF switch to OFF. Press RESET.

SYST-046.cause: Either 1.Control Reliable or CE Mark hardware exists but the CR or CE Mark option has not been loaded,or 2.The Control Reliable/CE Mark option has been loaded but the hardware is not available.
SYST-046.remedy: If the Control Reliable/CE Mark option has not been loaded, load the Control Reliable/ CE Mark option. If it has been loaded then this is a system without the Control Reliable/ CE Mark hardware and the system must be totally reloaded WITHOUT the Control Reliable/CE Mark option.

SYST-047.cause: Attempt to continue program from distant position from stopped position.
SYST-047.remedy: Respond ABORT or CONTINUE in the prompt box on at the teach pendant

SYST-048.cause: OS couldn't give NECALC soft part enough memory

SYST-049.cause: OS couldn't give SFCALC soft part enough memory

SYST-050.cause: Invalid time used in TG request
SYST-050.remedy: Time must be less than 6,000,000 us

SYST-051.cause: Excessive time iin trigger routines First number indicates event routine (1) or scan routine (2). Second number indicates individual overrrun (1) or excessive cumative CPU use (2). Third number: event number(hexadecimal) or scan routine address Fourth number: limit (microseconds or 100ths of one pct) Fifth number: time used (microseconds or 100ths of one pct)
SYST-051.remedy: Event or scan routine need to be made more efficient, scan rate reduced, or system variable values increased to permit more CPU usage.

SYST-052.remedy: Use cancel request to delete old entry

SYST-054.cause: Specified event ID already in use
SYST-054.remedy: Use unique event ID or cancel previous request

SYST-055.cause: Specified event ID is not presently in use

SYST-056.cause: A call to syscnrtn was made when the scan list was full. A maximum of 10 scan routines, including the standard table scanning routine, may be active at one time.
SYST-056.remedy: Either cancel scan routines that are no longer needed or combine scan routines

SYST-057.cause: The interval parameter in a call to syscnrtn was greater than 1000000 (1 second).
SYST-057.remedy: Use a value in the range 1-1000000

SYST-058.cause: syscnrtn was called specifying a routine and data_p that is already being scanned
SYST-058.remedy: Don't request the same rtn/data_p twice

SYST-059.cause: syclclsc was called with a routine and data_p that that does not match any active scans

SYST-060.cause: syaddtbl called with pointer to table that is already in the scan list

SYST-061.cause: syaddtbl called when all 10 condition/action table slots are already in use
SYST-061.remedy: Cancel tables that are no longer needed or combine tables.

SYST-062.cause: sycncltb called with cond/act table that is not active.
SYST-062.remedy: Check for duplicate sycncltb call or wrong table pointer

SYST-063.cause: System error: consecutive time interval start calls
SYST-063.remedy: Contact FANUC America Corporation with information on events leading up to error

SYST-064.cause: System error: Invalid data in scan table The following can result in this error: Too many cond/action sets (max = 10) Invalid condition code Invalid action code Too many actions (max = 3)
SYST-064.remedy: Contact FANUC America Corporation with information on events leading up to error

SYST-065.cause: SFCALC task can't get enough MPU power.
SYST-065.remedy: Please reduce some software options or disable some motion groups which had been enabled.

SYST-066.cause: Communication with the advanced Teach Pendant was interrupted.
SYST-066.remedy: Too much communication may have caused the interrupt. Check the teach pendant cable. Replace the cable if necessary.

SYST-069.cause: The selected style number is zero or greater than the size of the style table.
SYST-069.remedy: Select a valid style number, or adjust the size of the table.

SYST-070.cause: There is no program name in the style table.
SYST-070.remedy: Put a valid program name in the proper place in the style table.

SYST-071.cause: The selected style program does not exist on the controller.
SYST-071.remedy: Create a program for the style, or put a valid program name in the style table.

SYST-072.cause: The selected style program is not enabled.
SYST-072.remedy: Set the VALID field to YES in the style table.

SYST-073.cause: The style input does not match the manually selected style.
SYST-073.remedy: The PLC must send a style code that matches the manual selection.

SYST-074.cause: Communications with the Karel shell extension failed.

SYST-075.cause: The shell was unable to start due to resource allocation failures.

SYST-076.cause: The shell could not set up its required condition handlers.

SYST-077.cause: The controller is interlocked with the PLC
SYST-077.remedy: This is an informational message. There is no error.

SYST-078.cause: The controller is isolated from PLC control.
SYST-078.remedy: This is an informational message. There is no error

SYST-079.cause: One or more of the pre-startup system checks failed.
SYST-079.remedy: Look for a previous message that indicates exactly which check failed and take corrective action.

SYST-080.cause: The system is in a faulted state.
SYST-080.remedy: Reset the fault before trying the operation again.

SYST-081.cause: The program can not start because the robot is not at the defined home position.
SYST-081.remedy: Move the robot to the home position.

SYST-082.cause: The program can not be resumed because the robot has been moved from the position on the path where it stopped.

SYST-083.cause: One or more I/O points are simulated.

SYST-085.cause: The general speed override is not 100%

SYST-086.cause: The system has forced the general speed override to 100%

SYST-088.cause: The system has forced the program speed override to 100%.

SYST-091.remedy: Take the system out of single-step mode.

SYST-092.cause: The system has forced single-stepping to be off.

SYST-093.cause: The program can not start because the process is not ready.
SYST-093.remedy: Make the process equipment ready for running a program.

SYST-094.cause: The system has forced the process equipment to the ready state.

SYST-095.cause: An internal error occurred with the remote diagnosis function.

SYST-096.cause: A task specified by the PC is not correct.
SYST-096.remedy: Check the remote diagnosis software on the PC.

SYST-097.remedy: Check if a modem is installed. Check the modem type setting.

SYST-098.cause: The modem card is removed during communication.
SYST-098.remedy: Reinsert the modem card, then restart the remote diagnosis function. Check if the modem card is inserted into the PCMCIA slot correctly.

SYST-099.cause: There is no response from the modem card.
SYST-099.remedy: Check if a modem card is inserted correctly. Check the mode card.

SYST-100.cause: DSR was turned off during communication.
SYST-100.remedy: Check the connection between Robot and the modem. If a modem card is used, check if the modem card is not destroyed and if the modem card is inserted correctly.

SYST-102.cause: Internal Error in Remote Diagnose function.

SYST-103.cause: User bypassed not-home condition at program startup.

SYST-104.cause: User bypassed TCP position tolerance at program resume.

SYST-105.cause: User bypassed I/O simulated at program startup.

SYST-106.cause: User bypassed general override < 100% at program startup.

SYST-107.cause: User bypassed program override < 100% at program startup.

SYST-109.cause: User bypassed single-step condition at program startup.

SYST-110.cause: User bypassed process not ready at program startup.

SYST-111.cause: No home position defined for motion group 1.
SYST-111.remedy: Enable at least one reference position for group 1 as a home position, or disable the home position startup check.

SYST-112.cause: The production start input, which is required with the current program selection options, has not been defined.
SYST-112.remedy: Set up a production start input in the Cell Input I/O menu and restart the robot.

SYST-113.cause: The style number input group, which is required with the current program selection options, has not been defined.
SYST-113.remedy: Set up a style number input group in the Cell Input I/O and Group I/O menus and restart the robot.

SYST-114.cause: One or more RSR inputs, which are required with the current program selection options, have not been defined.
SYST-114.remedy: Set up the RSR inputs in the Cell Input I/O menu and restart the robot.

SYST-115.cause: One or more PNS selection inputs, which are required with the current program selection options, have not been defined.
SYST-115.remedy: Set up the PNS selection inputs in the Cell Input I/O and Group I/O menus and restart the robot.

SYST-116.cause: One or more RSR echo outputs, which are required with the current program selection options, have not been defined.
SYST-116.remedy: Set up the RSR echo outputs in the Cell Output I/O menu and restart the robot.

SYST-117.cause: The PNS echo outputs, which are required with the current program selection options, have not been defined.
SYST-117.remedy: Set up the PNS echo outputs in the Cell Output I/O and Group I/O menus and restart the robot.

SYST-118.cause: The PNS strobe input, which is required with the current program selection options, has not been defined.

SYST-119.remedy: Set up an acknowledgement strobe output in the Cell Output I/O menu and restart the robot.

SYST-120.cause: One or more style option inputs, which are required with the current program selection options, have not been defined.
SYST-120.remedy: Set up the style option inputs in the Cell Input I/O menu and restart the robot.

SYST-121.cause: The decision code input group, which is required with the current program selection options, has not been defined.
SYST-121.remedy: Set up a decision code input group in the Cell Input I/O and Group I/O menus and restart the robot.

SYST-122.cause: The echo/manual style output group, which is required with the current program selection options, has not been defined.
SYST-122.remedy: Set up a style output group in the Cell Output I/O and Group I/O menus and restart the robot.

SYST-123.cause: One or more style option outputs, which are required with the current program selection options, have not been defined.
SYST-123.remedy: Set up the style option outputs in the Cell Output I/O menu and restart the robot.

SYST-124.cause: The decision code output group, which is required with the current program selection options, has not been defined.
SYST-124.remedy: Set up a decision code output group in the Cell Output I/O and Group I/O menus and restart the robot.

SYST-125.cause: The in-cycle output, which is required with the current program selection options, has not been defined.
SYST-125.remedy: Set up an in-cycle output in the Cell Output I/O menu and restart the robot.

SYST-126.cause: The task_OK output, which is required with the current program selection options, has not been defined.
SYST-126.remedy: Set up a task-OK output in the Cell Output I/O menu and restart the robot.

SYST-127.cause: The isolate mode output, which is required with the current program selection options, has not been defined.
SYST-127.remedy: Set up an isolate mode output in the Cell Output I/O menu and restart the robot.

SYST-128.cause: The interlock mode output, which is required with the current program selection options, has not been defined.
SYST-128.remedy: Set up an interlock mode output in the Cell Output I/O menu and restart the robot.

SYST-129.cause: The manual style request output, which is required with the current program selection options, has not been defined.
SYST-129.remedy: Set up a manual style request output in the Cell Output I/O menu and restart the robot.

SYST-130.cause: The shell is already running an active program.
SYST-130.remedy: Finish or abort the current program before requesting a new program selection.

SYST-131.cause: The manual style request cannot be done. There is also a secondary error posted that gives the reason.

SYST-132.cause: The specified manual style was not requested by the PLC within the allowable time period.
SYST-132.remedy: Determine why the PLC did not respond to the request, or increase the timeout value.

SYST-133.cause: A request for a system trigger function (scan routine, etc) was made before the tables for these are initialized.
SYST-133.remedy: Defer any of these requests until late in the cold-start process

SYST-134.cause: A frequency input connected to one of the HDI inputs momentarily or for an extended time had a frequency exceeding the setting for the maximum. The channel or input number is indicated in the alarm text.
SYST-134.remedy: Reduce or eliminate the noise on the signal with additional grounding or shielding. If the frequency dip switch setting on the HDI Pulse Module is for the low range (640 Hz) and normal input frequencies will be above this, change the settings. Change the dip switch setting to the high range (1000 Hz) and the system variable $FQINT_SETUP[n].$FREQ_MAX_AL to 1020. If the frequency dip switch setting on the HDI Pulse Module is for the high range (1000 Hz) and normal input frequencies will always be below the low range change the setting to the low range. If the device providing the frequency (a flow meter for example) is providing frequencies above 1000 Hz, either change settings on the meter or change the type of meter so that the frequency provided is reduced. To disable this alarm, change the setting of the system variable $FQINT_SETUP[n].$FREQ_MAX_AL to 1200 if using the HDI Pulse Module or to 0 otherwise.

SYST-135.cause: The system clock has an invalid time. The clock may not have been set.
SYST-135.remedy: Reset the system Clock using the SYSTEM Clock TP page

SYST-136.cause: The system clock was reset by either an Operator or by the SNTP protocol, if SNTP is enabled.
SYST-136.remedy: Check the system Clock using the SYSTEM Clock teach pendant screen.

SYST-137.cause: The requested device is not installed on the motherboard.

SYST-138.cause: The specified motherboard is not installed.

SYST-139.cause: The specified motherboard index is not a valid value.
SYST-139.remedy: This is a programming error. Specify only index 0 or 1

SYST-140.cause: An invalid interrupt number was specified by the device driver.
SYST-140.remedy: Specify an IRQ from 3 through 7 only.

SYST-141.cause: BMON was automatically updated because of a newer version.

SYST-142.message: ABS time in sytmrev in past
SYST-142.cause: The time specified for a timed event has already passed The event will trigger immediately
SYST-142.remedy: Specify a later time for the event

SYST-143.cause: pkt_data_size parameter in syinpev_gen call is too big.

SYST-144.cause: Invalid or unassigned DOUT number specified in the indicated system variable.
SYST-144.remedy: Set the sysem variable to zero (no port used) or to a valid port number and ensure that the indicated DOUT is assigned.

SYST-145.cause: DOUT specified in the indicated system variable is Off-line.
SYST-145.remedy: Set the device to which the DOUT is assigned On-line.

SYST-146.cause: n_pkts_parameter in syinpev_gen call is invalid.
SYST-146.remedy: Use value in the range of 1 to 20, or zero if evnt_rtn_2 not used

SYST-148.cause: Dynamic Brake is disabled by dynamic brake release request signal (DI[$DYN_BRK.$DI_IDX]).
SYST-148.remedy: If you would like to turn on servo, please turn off dynamic brake release request signal.

SYST-149.cause: Dynamic Brake is enabled because dynamic brake release request is turned off.

SYST-150.cause: The program is started except from the 1st line.
SYST-150.remedy: Respond YES or NO in the prompt box on at the teach pendant

SYST-151.cause: After the program is started except from the 1st line, respond YES in the prompt box on at the teach pendant.

SYST-152.message: Cannot force DO's in AUTO mode
SYST-152.cause: Attempt to force output signal while controller is in AUTO mode
SYST-152.remedy: Exit AUTO mode before doing this operation

SYST-153.message: Cannot SIM/UNSIM DO's in AUTO mode
SYST-153.cause: Attempt to force output signal while controller is in AUTO mode
SYST-153.remedy: Exit AUTO mode before doing this operation

SYST-154.cause: Production start received when controller is in ISOLATE or BYPASS mode
SYST-154.remedy: Put controller into AUTO or INTERLOCK mode before doing this operation

SYST-156.cause: This PCB is not used on this controller.

SYST-157.cause: CE/RIA software does not exist in this controller.
SYST-157.remedy: Install CE/RIA option to this controller.

SYST-158.message: Robot cannot move in T2 mode
SYST-158.cause: The mode selector is in T2. Robot cannot move in T2 mode.
SYST-158.remedy: Change the mode switch to T1 or AUTO mode.

SYST-160.message: Value output to GO %d out of limit
SYST-160.cause: Value to be outputted to GO with Error Output feature is out of limit for this group output.
SYST-160.remedy: Configure GO using more digital outputs.

SYST-161.cause: Remote diagnostics are not started because the servo status is on.
SYST-161.remedy: Turn off the servo then retry the remote diagnostics.

SYST-162.cause: The servo is turned on during remote diagnostics.
SYST-162.remedy: Turn off the servo before attempting remote diagnostics.

SYST-163.message: Cannot operate IO during Remote diagnostic
SYST-163.cause: An attempt was made to operate I/O during remote diagnostics.
SYST-163.remedy: Do not operate I/O during remote diagnostics.

SYST-164.cause: Communication with the teach pendant was interrupted.
SYST-164.remedy: Too much communication may have caused the interrupt. Check that the teach pendant cable is working properly. Replace the cable if necessary.

SYST-165.cause: Intermittent errors occurred during communication with the teach pendant.
SYST-165.remedy: Check the teach pendant cable, and replace the cable if necessary. Check the teach pendant and replace the teach pendant if necessary.

SYST-166.cause: Intermittent errors occurred during communication with the teach pendant.
SYST-166.remedy: Check the teach pendant cable, and replace the cable if necessary. Check the teach pendant and replace the teach pendant if necessary.

SYST-168.cause: An attempt was made to operate an isolated Robot.
SYST-168.remedy: Do not operate an isolated Robot.

SYST-169.cause: S/W Registration is in effect. This alarm is posted when there are more than 28 days until registration expires.
SYST-169.remedy: Contact FANUC to obtain an authorization key.

SYST-170.cause: S/W Registration is in effect. This alarm is posted when there are between 14 and 28 days until registration expires.
SYST-170.remedy: Contact FANUC to obtain an authorization key.

SYST-171.cause: S/W Registration is in effect. This alarm is posted when there are between 1 and 14 days until registration expires.
SYST-171.remedy: Contact FANUC to obtain an authorization key.

SYST-172.cause: S/W Registration is in effect. This alarm is posted when registration has expired. The robot cannot be operated in any automatic mode until registration is extended.
SYST-172.remedy: Contact FANUC to obtain an authorization key.

SYST-173.cause: S/W Registration is in effect. Display to the S/W Registration screen for more details.
SYST-173.remedy: Contact FANUC to obtain an authorization key.

SYST-174.cause: Software Registration is in effect but the Software Registration option is not loaded.

SYST-175.cause: S/W Registration is in effect. The System was updated. This message is for reference only. No action is required.
SYST-175.remedy: The System was updated. This message is for reference only. No action is required.

SYST-176.cause: The system software is updated by the Auto Software update function.
SYST-176.remedy: This message is for reference only. No action is required.

SYST-177.cause: The attempted operation could not be done because the robot is under control of the RobotLink Master robot.
SYST-177.remedy: Set the remote/local operation mode to Local in the system configuration screen (if the operation is attempted from the SOP), or set the $RMT_MASTER system variable correctly.

SYST-188.cause: The book of operation logbook was not created.
SYST-188.remedy: Reduce the number of books or $LOG_BUFF[ ].$SIZE to allocate book.

SYST-189.cause: There is no book of operation logbook.

SYST-195.message: TP (on Rob#%d) enabled in T2 mode
SYST-195.cause: More than one teach pendant is enabled while in T2 mode within the multi-arm ring.
SYST-195.remedy: Disable the teach pendant which is not being used for the desired operation.

SYST-196.cause: The desired operation could not be performed because teach pendants were enabled within the multi-arm ring.
SYST-196.remedy: Disable the teach pendants which are not being used for the desired operation.

SYST-197.cause: The master robot did not receive a heartbeat message from the slave robots within the time specified by the $rkmashconf.$heartbt_tmo system variable.
SYST-197.remedy: Check and repair any broken network connections.

SYST-198.cause: Some slave robots are not ready to run a program.
SYST-198.remedy: All slave robots have Auto/T1/T2 switch to be AUTO. $RMT_MASTER system variable must be 4 (Robot Link). Verify the system variable $RMT_MASTER is set to 4 on all slave robots.

SYST-199.cause: The selected robot program could not be changed because the robot has been defined as a slave to a master robot, and the teach pendant is disabled.
SYST-199.remedy: If you are selecting the program using a teach pendant, enable the teach pendant to select a different program name.

SYST-200.cause: Only the teach pendant on the master robot can perform the SHIFT-FWD/BWD operation for multi-arm programs.
SYST-200.remedy: Use the teach pendant on the master robot to perform the SHIFT-FWD/BWD operation.

SYST-201.cause: The master robot number does not match with the one specified in the slave header.
SYST-201.remedy: Verify the master robot number in the slave program header.

SYST-202.cause: One or more of the specified slave robots does not accept the command from the master robot because of $rmt_master system variable value.
SYST-202.remedy: Verify that the system variable $RMT_MASTER is set to 4 on all slave robots.

SYST-203.cause: This is a notification that a robot has been successfully added to the robot link network as a slave robot.

SYST-204.cause: The program run sequence is still in progress.
SYST-204.remedy: Wait until the previous request is taken care of before you continue.

SYST-205.cause: The teach pendant FWD or BWD key was pressed without also pressing the SHIFT key.
SYST-205.remedy: Press the SHIFT key in addition to pressing the FWD or BWD key.

SYST-206.cause: The operation was canceled by pressing the RESET key.

SYST-207.cause: An error message has been posted on another robot.
SYST-207.remedy: Display the error history screen of the robot where the error was posted, and perform the remedy stated in the error message.

SYST-208.cause: The attempted operation is not supported. For example, you tried to run separate programs for dual-arm robots.
SYST-208.remedy: Be sure to perform only the supported operations.

SYST-210.message: Only one Family program on Slave Controller
SYST-210.cause: The attempted operation is not supported. No more than one family program is allowed on a slave controller.
SYST-210.remedy: Create a new set of programs with one family program on each a controller.

SYST-211.cause: The communications processor did not respond within the specified time-out limit.
SYST-211.remedy: Turn off the controller and then turn it on again. If the alarm persists document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC technical representative.

SYST-212.message: Need to apply to DCS param
SYST-212.cause: Mastering data or robot parameters are changed, but they are not applied to the DCS parameter.
SYST-212.remedy: Press F3(APPLY) in the DCS menu.

SYST-213.cause: A user cycled power from the function menu.

SYST-214.cause: A DCS ESTOP occurred. This occurs only when $DCS_CFG.$TEST_PARAM1 bit 0 is 1.

SYST-215.cause: A DCS ESTOP occurred. This occurs only when $DCS_CFG.$TEST_PARAM1 bit 0 is 1.

SYST-216.cause: A DCS DCSALM occurred. This occurs only when $DCS_CFG.$TEST_PARAM1 bit 0 is 1.

SYST-217.cause: The DCS position/speed process setting is set to ENABLE, when the hardware is not DCS type or the DCS option is not loaded.
SYST-217.remedy: Set the DCS position/speed process to DISABLE, or load the DCS option, or change the hardware to DCS type.

SYST-218.message: DCS Unavailable robot model G:%x Hex
SYST-218.cause: The Dual Check Safety Position/Speed Check Function option is loaded, but this robot model is not supported.
SYST-218.remedy: Delete the Dual Check Safety Position/Speed check function option. This alarm can be cleared by setting $DCS_CFG.$SYS_PARAM to 1, but in this case, Position/Speed check function can not be used.

SYST-219.cause: When 'Position/Speed process' is enabled, backup files are loaded and DCS parameter is changed. The meaning of 'i' is the following. • 1: Image backup is loaded. • 2: SYSVARS.SV is loaded and DCS parameter is changed. • 4: SYSVARS.SV is loaded and DCS parameter for robot setting is changed. • 8: SYSMAST.SV is loaded and DCS parameter in mastering parameter for DCS is changed. • 16: SYSPASS.SV is loaded and code number for DCS parameter is changed.
SYST-219.remedy: Check the setting in DCS menu, and do the VERIFY operation in the DCS top menu.

SYST-220.cause: The process synchronization condition was not satisfied within the specified time-out limit.
SYST-220.remedy: 1. Check the program logic (seq_id inconsistency, etc.) 2. Use a longer time-out limit (in the sync schedule).

SYST-221.cause: The sync schedule does not match between robots.
SYST-221.remedy: 1. Make sure same schedule number is used in the program between robots. 2. Make sure the schedule content (robot mask, etc.) is the same between robots.

SYST-223.remedy: 0x%x shows the cause of the failure. Find the definition in the list below. Remove the cause of the failure and try the backup again. • 0x%x Cause and remedy • 0x1 This isn't used. • 0x2 Memory allocation failed. Call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative. • 0x3 Information in FROM cannot be acquired. Call your FANUC technical representatiCve. • 0x4 Make sure there is enough free space on the MC. Make sure a FLASH ATA card is inserted in the MC card slot. • 0x5 Controller could not open FROM***.IMG. Destination device might be broken. • 0x6 Controller could not read FROM. FROM module or main board FROM might be broken. • 0x7 Controller could not write data to FROM***.IMG. Destination device might be broken. • 0x8 Controller could not close FROM***.IMG. The following are possible causes: — There are already backup files on the destination device and they are write-protected. — MC was removed during backup. — Communication was disconnected during backup to TFTP server. — TFTP server is not running. • 0x9 Make sure there is enough free space on MC. Make sure FLASH ATA card is inserted to MC card slot. • 0xa Controller cannot open SRAM***.IMG. Destination device might be broken. • 0xb Controller could not write data to SRAM***.IMG. Destination device might be broken. • 0xc Controller could not close SRAM***.IMG. The following are possible causes: — There are already backup files on the destination device and they are write-protected. — MC was removed during backup. — Communication was disconnected during backup to TFTP server. — TFTP server is not running. • 0xd File for internal use may be broken. Try the backup again. • 0xe File for internal use may be broken. Try the backup again. • 0xf After power was cycled by image backup function, a backup file was found on the MC. This happens if power is turned off during automatic image backup. Retry backup from file screen again. • 0x20 Initialization of network failed. Confirm wiring and BOOTP server is running.

TCPP-011.cause: The first motion segment time (time between first two taught points) is shorter than the prediction equipment delay time as specified by $TCPPIR.$TCDELAY.
TCPP-011.remedy: Extend time of first motion segment (increase distance or decrease speed) to allow TCP Speed Prediction to begin during the first motion segment.

TCPP-015.remedy: Check the value for the current position data.

TCPP-016.remedy: Check to make sure that the Cartesian Filter option has been properly loaded and initialized.

TCPP-017.remedy: No action is necessary, but the TCP Speed value will not be valid for several motions.

TCPP-018.cause: The program positions beginning with this line have caused an error condition which makes further speed prediction invalid. The speed prediction task has therefore entered an error handling mode within which it discontinues speed prediction but provides the actual robot speed as an output reference with an affective equipment delay time of 0. (That is, with $TCPPIR.$TCDELAY = 0.)
TCPP-018.remedy: Check the error log to find speed limit errors which may be causing this TCPP error to occur. Check the program beginning with this line to determine if the robot can not function as programmed. Modify the program to avoid all such speed limit errors. In cases which list speed limit errors for the wrist axes, the error can often be eliminated by changing the motion command from using mm/sec speed commands to using deg/sec speed commands which better control motion with large wrist orientation changes.

TCPP-019.cause: A speed override occured beginning with this line causing an error condition which makes further speed prediction invalid. The speed prediction task has therefore entered an error handling mode within which it discontinues speed prediction but provides the actual robot speed as an output reference.
TCPP-019.remedy: Normal prediction will resume automatically once the speed override has propagated through the system. No further action is required. The user should avoid this during production program execution and should be aware that it may invalidate live application testing since neither the robot nor the speed prediction task are performing as programmed.

TG-006.remedy: Time before must be greater than -0.1 seconds

TG-008.cause: An I/O port was not triggered when it was supposed to. This is usually caused by too many I/O events being set up to fire within too short a time frame.
TG-008.remedy: You must adjust your path so that it does not try to fire so many I/O events within a such a short time. Start by moving the last few motions before this error occured further apart and/or slowing them down.

TG-009.cause: This is a warning to indicate that the trigger time for the specified TG event was miscalculated, so the event was fired immediately. No user action is required.

TG-010.message: Pts Too Close %s^4 L:%d^5 Sch:%d^2 Ev:%d^3
TG-010.cause: This is a warning indicating that two taught points containing triggering events were too close to each other, such that the second point trigger time had to be adjust to prevent firing before the first point trigger.
TG-010.remedy: Modify the position of the node (line number and program number) indicated so that it is further away from the preceding position in the program.

TG-011.cause: An internal error occurred while attempting to allocate memory.
TG-011.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, including an All File Backup from the time of the error if possible, and contact your FANUC America Corporation Technical Representative.

TG-012.message: Bad Num ISDT in Sch %d^2 Ev%d^3
TG-012.cause: A trigger schedule (system variable $TGSCHED[num], where “num”is the schedule indicated in the alarm text) has an event defined with an invalid process axis number.
TG-012.remedy: Generally this alarm occurs when a process axis related option is loaded, but the process axes have not been properly setup. Go to controlled start and run the process axis setup from the MAINTENANCE menu.

TG-013.message: Invalid IO Port in Sch%d^2 Ev%d^3
TG-013.cause: In the trigger schedule number $TGSCHED[num] indicated by the alarm text, the indicated event number has an invalid port type specified.
TG-013.remedy: Change $TGSCHED[Sch].$PORT_TYPE[Ev] to a valid port type. Note that Robot Digital Input and Group Input are not allowed. If you have not modified these variables since loading, then obtain a file backup and contact your FANUC America Corporation Technical Representative.

TG-014.cause: The number of outstanding trigger events exceeds the maximum. This indicates either an excessive number of very short segments in a TP program with trigger instructions, or an internal error.
TG-014.remedy: Examine the TP programs running at the time of the error for a very large number of motion lines that have instructions with trigger events and that are very close together or the same point. If this condition is not found, obtain as much information as possible about the events leading up to the error as well as a file backup and easy debug (if available) and contact FANUC America Corporation Technical Support.

TG-015.remedy: If this alarm appears, obtain a controller backup (image at least) and contact your FANUC America Corporation Technical Representative.

TG-016.message: Bad Time Before in Sch%d^2 Ev%d^3
TG-016.cause: The indicate trigger schedule event in $TGSCHED[Sch] has an invalid value for time before.
TG-016.remedy: The time before (or anticipator) value cannot be less than (i.e. more negative than) -100 msec. Check all anticipator values defined in the application to be sure none indicate a time after (i.e. negative time before) greater in magnitude than 100 msec.

TG-017.cause: An internal error occurred during processing of a TP instruction.
TG-017.remedy: Obtain a controller backup and easy debug (if available) and contact your FANUC America Corporation Technical Representative.

TG-018.cause: There are too many outstanding trigger events that have not yet been fired. This indicates either an excessive number of short motion segments with trigger instructions, or else an internal error.
TG-018.remedy: Examine the TP programs executing at the time of the error to confirm that there are not a large number of short or zero length motion segments back-to-back with application instructions. If this condition does not exist, then obtain a controller backup (and easy debug if available) from the time of the error and contact your FANUC America Corporation Technical Representative.

TG-019.cause: This alarm is currently not used.
TG-019.remedy: If this alarm appears, obtain an image backup and contact your FANUC America Corporation Technical Representative.

TG-020.cause: This indicates an error occurred in the planning of an application TP instruction and is always accompanied by another TG-XXX alarm.
TG-020.remedy: Examine the alarm log for the other TG-XXX alarm that was posted at the same time and proceed according to the cause/remedy for that alarm.

THSR-001.cause: Trying to execute a touch sensing instruction out of sequence. For example, a Search Start instruction follows a Offset start instruction without Offset end in between.
THSR-001.remedy: Please check the touch sensing instruction sequence, or abort the current program and start again.

THSR-002.cause: The input schedule number is beyond the allowable range.
THSR-002.remedy: Choose a schedule number from 1 to 32.

THSR-003.cause: The input work frame number is beyond the allowable range
THSR-003.remedy: Choose a work frame number from 1 to 32.

THSR-004.cause: The input position register number is beyond the allowable range.
THSR-004.remedy: Choose an approperiate position register number.

THSR-005.cause: The specified position register for search result is beyond the allowable range.
THSR-005.remedy: Choose an approperiate position register number.

THSR-007.cause: The touch I/O assignment is incorrect.
THSR-007.remedy: Please check touch I/O setup screen under the setup menu.

THSR-008.cause: The arc weld circuitry is enable.
THSR-008.remedy: Please disable arc welding circuitry before enabling touch sensing.

THSR-010.cause: The motion system is in error state.
THSR-010.remedy: Hit the reset button to reset the controller.

THSR-011.cause: The specified search port is beyond the allowable range.
THSR-011.remedy: Change the port type and port number in the touch I/O sub-menu.

THSR-012.cause: The specified search pattern is not recognizable.
THSR-012.remedy: Change the search pattern in the touch sensor schedule.

THSR-013.cause: Number of searches is not coincident with the search. pattern.
THSR-013.remedy: Change the search pattern or add/delete search instructions.

THSR-014.cause: This is a warning message. The specified search distance is beyond the allowable range. A default speed is used.
THSR-014.remedy: Change the search speed in the touch sensor schedule.

THSR-015.cause: The specified search speed is beyond the allowable range.
THSR-015.remedy: Change the search speed in the touch sensor schedule.

THSR-016.cause: The specified return speed is beyond the allowable range. A default speed is used.
THSR-016.remedy: Change the retunr speed in the touch sensor schedule.

THSR-017.cause: The search produces no contact with the part
THSR-017.remedy: Use touchup to teach a new search start position.

THSR-018.cause: Too many searches for the specified search pattern.

THSR-019.cause: NONE search type can not be mixed with directional search within one search pattern.
THSR-019.remedy: Delete all searches with NONE type or delete coordinated searches.

THSR-020.cause: The searches do not generate a satisfactory offset.
THSR-020.remedy: Check the search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. Or, use touchup to teach a new search start position.

THSR-021.cause: The touched positions are too close to each other.

THSR-022.cause: Search instructions have no master data.

THSR-023.cause: The search instruction does not have a search start.

THSR-024.cause: The offset end instruction does not have an associated offset start instruction.

THSR-025.cause: The search start instruction is nested inside another search start instruction.
THSR-025.remedy: Add a search_end instruction in appropriate place or delete extra search start

THSR-026.cause: The offset start instruction is nested inside another offset start instruction.
THSR-026.remedy: Add a offset_end instruction in appropriate place or delete extra offset start

THSR-027.cause: No preplan motion inside search start.
THSR-027.remedy: It is normal to issue an stop error when preplan is on within search start

THSR-028.cause: The search motion has to be in group 1. motion.
THSR-028.remedy: Use group 1 to record search motions.

THSR-029.cause: The search produces no contact with the part
THSR-029.remedy: Use touchup to teach a new search start position.

THSR-030.cause: Wire makes contact with part before search motion starts
THSR-030.remedy: Check part and wire, or teach a new search start position.

THSR-031.cause: The input register number is illegal, and it is reset by the software to the maximum available number.

THSR-032.cause: The position type in the position register should be XYZWPR type. Joint representation is not allowed.
THSR-032.remedy: Change the position representation to XYZWPR type.

THSR-033.cause: Touch sensing system does not have enough points to compute the geometry

THSR-034.cause: Touch sensing does not allow backward execution on search motion

THSR-035.remedy: Remove unneeded loaded variables and programs

THSR-036.cause: Coord motion is not installed or not calibrated
THSR-036.remedy: Install coord motion and calibrate cd pair

THSR-038.cause: Touch frame or schedule reference grp mismatches leader grp

THSR-039.cause: None simple search requires frame Reference grp equal to schedule reference grp

THSR-040.cause: Search distance in touch schedule is too short
THSR-040.remedy: Increase search distance in touch schedule

THSR-041.cause: An invalid touch sensing group mask in the program detail, or the Search routine was not performed prior to Touch Offset.
THSR-041.remedy: Check that the Touch Schedule and Robot Group Mask together with Reference Group should be equal to the group mask in the teach pendant program header. Also, the Search routine should be performed directly before the Touch Offset.

THSR-042.cause: Touch Sensing does not support a Maintenance Program.
THSR-042.remedy: Disable the Maintenance Program in the Error Recovery menu, or use Resume Program in teach pendant program for error recovery. To display the Error Recovery menu: 1. Press MENUS. 2. Select SETUP. 3. Press F1, [TYPE]. 4. Select Err recovery.

THSR-043.cause: The touch sensing analog input calibration file was not found.
THSR-043.remedy: Create an analog input calibration file called th_calib.dt. The calibration file needs to be stored in frs: via the SMON command SMON(ppc)> rep th_calib.dt then turn off and then turn on the controller for the calibration file to take effect.

THSR-044.cause: The analog input calibration file has an invalid data format.
THSR-044.remedy: Correct the data format in the analog input calibration file, including configuration data and lookup table. Refer to the Analog Input Calibration Data section in the Touch Sensing chapter of the ArcTool Setup and Operations Manual for the correct data format.

THSR-045.cause: Analog input support has not been calibrated.
THSR-045.remedy: Create an analog input calibration file with the correct data format. Refer to the Laser Analog Input Calibration Data section in the Touch Sensing chapter of the ArcTool Setup and Operations Manual for more information.

THSR-046.cause: The analog input data is not valid.
THSR-046.remedy: Analog input data needs to be within a valid range. The valid range of analog input value is defined by MaxAnalogInput and MinAnalogInput specified in the same calibration file th_calib.dt.

THSR-047.cause: The searches do not generate a satisfactory circle.
THSR-047.remedy: Check the OD/ID search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. Or, use touchup to teach a new search start position.

THSR-048.cause: An illegal number of 1D/1D+R search directions exists.
THSR-048.remedy: Check the 1D/1D+R search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. The number of 1D/1D+R search directions should be exactly 1.

THSR-049.cause: An illegal number of 2D/2D+R search directions exist.
THSR-049.remedy: Check the 2D/2D+R search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. The number of 2D/2D+R search directions should be exactly 2.

THSR-050.cause: An illegal number of 3D/3D+R search directions exists.
THSR-050.remedy: Check the 3D/3D+R search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. The number of 3D/3D+R search directions should be exactly 3.

THSR-051.cause: An error occurred computing the offset along the first search direction.
THSR-051.remedy: Check search instructions with the first search direction. The first search direction is specified in the first search instruction in the corresponding Search Start section. Check the search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. Or, use touchup to teach a new search start position.

THSR-052.cause: Error computing the offset along the 2nd search direction.
THSR-052.remedy: Check the search instructions with the 2nd search direction. The 2nd search direction is the first new search direction other than the 1st search direction in the corresponding Search Start section. Check the search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. Or, use touchup to teach a new search start position.

THSR-053.cause: An error occurred computing the offset along the 3rd search direction.
THSR-053.remedy: Check search instructions with the 3rd search direction. The 3rd search direction is the first new search direction other than the 1st and the 2nd search directions in the corresponding Search Start section. Check the search pattern and search instructions in the pattern. Or, use touchup to teach a new search start position.

THSR-054.cause: The master flag in the schedule is ON during simple search.
THSR-054.remedy: Set the master flag in the schedule to OFF during simple search.

THSR-055.cause: The search speed is outside the default search speed limit configured by the system variable th_default.
THSR-055.remedy: Set the search speed within the default search speed limit.

TJOG-001.cause: An attempt was made to jog multiple arms at an invalid jog mode.

TJOG-002.cause: An attempt was made to start the tracking jog feature on a single arm controller.
TJOG-002.remedy: Start the tracking jog feature on a controller with multiple arm hardware.

TJOG-003.cause: An attempt was made to start the tracking jog feature when TJOG is disabled in $track_jog.$enable.
TJOG-003.remedy: Enable $track_jog.$enable before starting the tracking jog feature.

TJOG-004.message: G%d is not a robot arm group
TJOG-004.cause: Trying to start the tracking jog feature on a non-robot motion group.
TJOG-004.remedy: Change to a robot motion group before starting the tracking jog feature.

TMAT-000.cause: TorchMate has found that the offset of the torch from the original TCP is beyond the offset limits in the SETUP screen.
TMAT-000.remedy: Determine if the Torch needs to be replaced at this time. Replace it if necessary, or increase the offset limits in the TorchMate SETUP screen.

TMAT-001.cause: The wire is in contact with the touch plate or is grounded prior to executing the touch move; CAUSE 1: The wire stickout is too long; CAUSE 2: The starting position for the touch move is to close to the touch plate; CAUSE 3: The weld equipment touch circuit or user provided external touch circuit has shorted.
TMAT-001.remedy: REMEDY1: Shorten the wire stickout before TorchMate execution by retracting the wire or clipping the wire; REMEDY 2: Increase the value of the Start Search position in the TorchMate SETUP menu; REMEDY 3: Contact the manufacturer for proper use of their touch sense circuit (ie. the welder may require a blocking diode) and inspect any touch circuit hardware for correct installation or for damaged components.

TMAT-002.cause: Cause1:The TorchMate sensor circuit indicates the wire is in contact with the touch plate before the search move (too much stickout-the search start distance is too small.) Cause 2: An electrical short exists in the touch circuit (for example, some circuits require a blocking diode on the power supply.)
TMAT-002.remedy: Remedy1: Decrease the stickout, increase the search start distance, or replace the bent torch. Remedy 2: Contact the supplier of your weld equipment regarding the touch circuit requirements and auxilliary wiring (if needed.)

TMAT-003.cause: This error indicates that Z compensation was disabled while mastering and enabled during TorchMate adjustment. TorchMate cannot compensate for Z offset if it is not mastered.
TMAT-003.remedy: Disable Z compensation in the TorchMate SETUP screen.

TMAT-004.cause: Mastering was stopped by releasing the SHIFT key.
TMAT-004.remedy: Select the MASTER softkey to execute mastering. Press and hold the SHIFT key until mastering is complete.

TMAT-005.message: WO[1] is not available for output
TMAT-005.cause: The TorchMate output signal has been assigned to the Weld Start output.
TMAT-005.remedy: Reassign the TorchMate output signal to the welder's touch sense circuit, or to an external circuit designed to provide the touch input when the wire contacts the touch plate.

TMAT-006.cause: The speed override must be 100% during both mastering and TorchMate Adjustment.
TMAT-006.remedy: Set the override to 100%, and execute mastering or TorchMate Adjust again.

TMAT-007.cause: TorchMate does not function if DRY RUN is turned on.
TMAT-007.remedy: Display the Test Cycle menu, and turn DRY RUN off.

TMAT-008.cause: CAUSE1: TorchMate Adjustment was attempted before mastering. CAUSE 2: TorchMate Ajustment has Z offset enabled, but the mastering was done with Z offset disabled. CAUSE 3: TorchMate Ajustment has Z offset disabled, but the mastering was done with Z offset enabled.
TMAT-008.remedy: Calibrate the TCP correctly before using TorchMate Adjustment.

TMAT-009.cause: The automatic setup of macros during installation cannot find an unused Macro number. No macro table entry will be automatically assigned to TM_ADJST, TM_ADJ2, TM_ADJ3.
TMAT-009.remedy: The Macro teach pendant program will be loaded on the controller. Remove an unused Macro from the Macro table, and assign TM_ADJST to that number if you require the TorchMate macro assignment in the Macro table.

TMAT-010.message: Cannot run TorchMate in T1 Mode
TMAT-010.cause: An attempt was made to run TorchMate adjust or mastering in T1 mode on a CE or Control reliable controller. This error applies to TorchMate and TorchMateII on R-J, R-J2, and early software releases on R-J3 controllers. This restriction does not apply to software releases on R-J3 and later controllers.
TMAT-010.remedy: On the affected controllers, change the Teach mode to T2 and rerun mastering or TorchMate adjustment.

TMAT-011.cause: TorchMate mastering or TorchMate adjustment has been attempted on an undefined equipment.
TMAT-011.remedy: Set up multiple equipment prior to mastering or using TorchMate adjustment on this equipment.

TMAT-012.cause: The UTOOL that you are trying to adjust or master is not defined.
TMAT-012.remedy: Set up your UTOOL using the six-point method.

TMAT-013.message: %s is corrupt or does not exist
TMAT-013.cause: The UTOOL that you are trying to adjust or master is not defined.
TMAT-013.remedy: On the ATFLASH release media for your robot, locate the the programs PRODUCT\TORCHMAT\TMTMPLT.TP and PRODUCT\TORCHMAT\TMTPSET1.TP. Copy these to the root level of the media. Insert the media into the port on the controller SOP. From the MENU/FILE screen, perform a [DIR] on the memory card (MC:) for *.TP. Load these files selecting to OVERWRITE when prompted.

TMAT-014.cause: During TorchMate mastering, the MOVETO operation in the TorchMate SETUP screen, or TorchMate adjustment was attempted on a motion group currently held by a PAUSED or RUNNING program.
TMAT-014.remedy: Abort the PAUSED or RUNNING program prior to executing any of these functions.

TMAT-015.cause: TorchMate mastering or TorchMate adjustment was used on a motion group that is not associated with the robot(s) in your system. CAUSE 1: At mastering, the group is determined by the currently selected jog motion group as shown in the TP status line. You have selected for jogging a motion group associated to a positioner, nobot, or index device. CAUSE 2: TorchMate adjustment has macros for each robot group installed on your system. The currently executing program includes a TorchMate macro and does not include that correct robot motion group, or it does not contain a robot motion group at all.
TMAT-015.remedy: REMEDY1: Select for jogging a motion group that is associated with the robot(s) in your system. REMEDY 2: Correct the programming error.

TMAT-016.cause: This indicates that the TorchMate Touchup Monitor has been turned on (Touchup monitor value is > 0.0 Hrs.), that the program contains a robot motion group(s), and that a TorchMate adjustment has not been done within the alloted time.
TMAT-016.remedy: This is cleared by pressing the ENTER key. It is recommended that you execute TorchMate adjust for the motion group(s) in this program prior to touching up any points.

TMAT-017.cause: This indicates that the TorchMate collision monitor has been turned on and that it has detected that a collision detect alarm, a disturbance excess alarm, or a move/stop error excess alarm has occurred.
TMAT-017.remedy: This alarm causes a prompt box to be displayed. Press the ENTER key to clear the prompt box. Inspect the torch for collision damage. Run TorchMate adjust if necessary.

TMAT-018.message: DCS tool frame is not allowed
TMAT-018.cause: TorchMate cannot use for DCS tool frame.
TMAT-018.remedy: Do not peform TorchMate for DCS tool frame. If you want to use TorchMate for the current tool number, remove the setup

TMSN-000.remedy: Check the GIN port or use a valid GIN port number.

TMSN-001.remedy: Power off to recover. If problem persistes, please reload the controller.

TMSN-002.remedy: Please use an integer or a real in calling END_MTN_TIM KAREL program.

TMSN-003.cause: The Time Synchronization software is not properly. installed.

TMSN-004.cause: No RECD_MTN_TIM call before calling END_MTN_TIM program.
TMSN-004.remedy: Check TP program logic and add RECD_MTN_TIM call before calling END_MTN_TIM.

TMSN-005.cause: The TP program does not have motion control.
TMSN-005.remedy: Check TP program group mask use DETAIL function key in select menu.

TMSN-006.cause: Motion Time recording aborted due to program pause/abort
TMSN-006.remedy: Re-run the TP program without pause or abort to record correct motion time.

TMSN-007.cause: Time Synchronization is not enabled for this motion.

TMSN-008.cause: Time synchronization is disabled for backward program execution.

TMSN-009.cause: Motion is too short.Time synchronization is not enable for this motion.
TMSN-009.remedy: Use SyncTime on long motion or change previous motion termation type to FINE.

TMSN-010.cause: Please use 100% speed override for time recording.

TMSN-011.cause: Time synchronization requires Constant Path option.
TMSN-011.remedy: Please enable constant path if Constant Path option is is installed.

TMSN-012.cause: Circular Motion Type. Time synchronization is not enable for this motion.
TMSN-012.remedy: Please use JOINT or LINEAR motion type when using the time synchronization.

TMSN-013.cause: ARC Motion Type. Time synchronization is not enable for this motion.
TMSN-013.remedy: Please use JOINT or LINEAR motion type when using the time synchronization.

TMSN-014.cause: Time synchronization does support SEC or MSEC speed
TMSN-014.remedy: Please change the speed unit to other type.

TOOL-001.cause: When tool change was disabled on the servo tool initial setup screen, an attempt was made to execute a tool change instruction (TOOL ATTACH or TOOL DETACH).
TOOL-001.remedy: Perform a Controlled start, open the servo tool initial setup screen, then set the tool change function to ENABLE.

TOOL-002.cause: 1) A machine lock is applied to the robot axis when the TOOL ATTACH instruction or the TOOL DETATCH instruction is executed. 2) A machine lock is applied to the servo tool axis when the TOOL DETACH instruction is executed.
TOOL-002.remedy: Release the machine lock applied to the robot axis or the servo tool axis.

TOOL-003.cause: The tool number assignments are wrong.

TOOL-004.cause: An attempt was made to execute the TOOL ATTACH instruction when a servo tool was not detached. System variable $AXISORDER should have been changed to 0.
TOOL-004.remedy: If any tool is attached, the TOOL ATTACH instruction cannot be executed.

TOOL-005.cause: An attempt was made to execute the TOOL ATTACH instruction when a servo tool was not detached. The servo tool attach confirmation signal is ON.
TOOL-005.remedy: If any tool is attached, the TOOL ATTACH instruction cannot be executed.

TOOL-006.cause: While no servo tool was attached, an attempt was made to execute the TOOL DETACH instruction. The servo tool attach confirmation signal is OFF.
TOOL-006.remedy: Unless a tool is attached, the TOOL DETACH instruction cannot be executed.

TOOL-007.cause: Another program is executing a TOOL ATTACH or TOOL DETACH instruction.
TOOL-007.remedy: After the TOOL ATTACH or TOOL DETACH instruction being executed by the other program is completed, rerun the program.

TOOL-008.cause: The servo tool identification signal is OFF.
TOOL-008.remedy: Check whether the tool number taught in the instruction and the actual tool match. Check whether the servo tool identification signal is set correctly.

TOOL-009.cause: The servo tool mount signal is OFF.
TOOL-009.remedy: Check whether the tool is mounted correctly. Check whether the servo tool mount signal is set correctly.

TOOL-010.cause: The TOOL ATTACH or TOOL DETACH instruction is canceled while executing the instruction.
TOOL-010.remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

TOOL-011.cause: The TOOL ATTACH or TOOL DETACH instruction times out while executing the instruction.
TOOL-011.remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

TOOL-012.cause: Mastering data of a servo tool was lost because of an unexpected stop during mastering of the tool.
TOOL-012.remedy: 1. The tool pulse values and mastering data are lost. So, first move the tool by manual feed to cancel the “SRVO-075 Pulse not established” alarm. This alarm may not be occurring. If so, skip this step and proceed to the next step. 2. Next, carry out tool 0 position mastering and calibration manually.

TOOL-014.cause: The TOOL ATTACH instruction failed. Refer to the cause code for details.
TOOL-014.remedy: Refer to the cause code for details.

TOOL-015.remedy: See the cause code for more information.

TOOL-016.cause: Mastering of the servo tool axis has not been performed.
TOOL-016.remedy: Perform mastering of the servo tool axis.

TOOL-017.cause: The servo tool axis has not been calibrated.

TOOL-018.cause: A reference position required for quick mastering is not set.

TOOL-019.cause: The attached tool is not the tool specified in the TOOL ATTACH instruction.
TOOL-019.remedy: Check the tool number specified in the TOOL ATTACH instruction.

TOOL-020.cause: The detection condition (touch torque or the detection signal) was not satisfied during calibration.
TOOL-020.remedy: Check the detection condition on the Tool Change SETUP screen. REMEDY 1 1. The tool pulse values and mastering data are lost. So, move the tool by manual feed to cancel the “SRVO-075 Pulse not established” alarm. 2. Carry out tool 0 position mastering and calibration manually. The tool 0 position may be an approximate position. 3. Execute the detach instruction to temporarily detach the tool. Also, physically detach the tool from the robot. Otherwise, the tool will not be calibrated at the next attach operation. 4. Execute the attach instruction again to attach the tool. Calibration this time is carried out at the reference position to restore the position. REMEDY 2 1. Directly change the system variable to detach the tool. To do this, set the following system variable to 0: $SCR_GRP[servo tool operation group No. (normally, 2)].$AXISORDER[all 1 to 9] 2. Turn the controller power OFF then back ON. 3. The robot starts up with the tool in a detached state. Move the robot by manual feed to physically attach the robot and tool. 4. Execute the attach instruction to attach the tool.

TOOL-021.cause: For the calibration motion type 3 to 6, no position register number is set.
TOOL-021.remedy: Set the position register number on the Tool Change SETUP screen.

TOOL-022.cause: For the calibration motion type 3 or 4, no touch torque is set.
TOOL-022.remedy: Set touch torque on the Tool Change SETUP screen.

TOOL-023.cause: For the calibration motion type 5 or 6, no detection signal is set.
TOOL-023.remedy: Set the detection signal on the Tool Change SETUP screen.

TOOL-024.cause: At the calibration motion, Servo tool axis does not stop.
TOOL-024.remedy: After servo tool axis stops, execute calibration motion

TOOL-025.cause: $SCR_GRP[].$AXISORDER[] of the tool was set to an illegal value.
TOOL-025.remedy: Set $SCR_GRP[].$AXISORDER[] of the tool to zero, and turn off and on the controller.

TOOL-026.cause: The battery type of the multi-axis tool was set to OFF.
TOOL-026.remedy: Set the battery type of the multi-axis tool to ON.

TOOL-027.cause: A timeout occurred during Tool-attach or -detach at the start.
TOOL-027.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical service representative.

TOOL-028.remedy: Document the events that led to the error, and call your FANUC America Corporation technical service representative.

TPIF-001.remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

TPIF-053.cause: The program has not been selected by BACKGROUND editing

TPIF-054.cause: 1. There is not enough memory. 2. The background program is invalid.

TPIF-055.cause: Failed recovering original program which has been selected by the BACKGROUND

TPIF-060.remedy: You can record this position on joint type only by selecting the function key.

TPIF-061.cause: This position data has not been changed to displayed groups because you selected the function key which did not record the position, when checking in singularity
TPIF-061.remedy: Check this recorded position again before excution

TPIF-062.message: AND operator was replaced to OR
TPIF-062.cause: All AND operators on this line were replaced with OR operators.
TPIF-062.remedy: You cannot mix AND and OR operator on a the same line. Verify that all logical operators on this line are the same before execution.

TPIF-063.message: OR operator was replaced to AND
TPIF-063.cause: All OR operator on this line were replaced by AND operators. You cannot mix AND OR operaotr on a the same line
TPIF-063.remedy: Verify all logical operators on this line before execution

TPIF-064.cause: Too many AND/OR operators (Max.4 on a single line)
TPIF-064.remedy: Teach the logical operation on another line

TPIF-065.message: Arithmetic operator was unified to +- or */
TPIF-065.cause: Arithmetic operator on this line was changed to +- or */. Cannot mix arithmatic + and - operators with * and / operators on the same line.
TPIF-065.remedy: Verify all arithmetic operators on this line before execution

TPIF-066.cause: Too many arithmetic operators (Max.5 on a single line)
TPIF-066.remedy: Teach the arithmetic operation on another line

TPIF-067.cause: Too many arguments (Max.30 for a program or a macro)

TPIF-068.cause: This instruction contains too many items. You can add only a limited number of items to a line. It is limited by the fact that a single line can be only 255 bytes long. The number of items depends on how much memory each item takes.
TPIF-068.remedy: Split this long complex line into several simpler lines.

TPIF-069.cause: You cannot foreground edit a program from the CRT or from the Internet. You can only edit using a background program.
TPIF-069.remedy: Select the BACKGROUND program in the SELECT screen.

TPIF-070.remedy: Check the sub type of the program.

TPIF-071.remedy: Check sub type of the program

TPIF-072.remedy: Check sub type of the program

TPIF-090.cause: The program specified in $PWR_HOT, $PWR_SEMI and $PWR_NORMAL must not have motion group.
TPIF-090.remedy: Set * to all motion group in program detail screen on TP.

TPIF-091.cause: An error occurred when accessing a position register.
TPIF-091.remedy: Refer to the error cause code on the ALARM log screen.

TPIF-092.cause: The value_array that was passed to a built-in was incorrectly specified. The error line shows the index into value_array where the error occurred and the type expected by the built-in.
TPIF-092.remedy: Make sure the value_array specifies the correct names for the variables and that the types expected are correct.

TPIF-093.cause: A KAREL program called a user interface built-in which required the USER menu to be displayed on the teach pendant or CRT.
TPIF-093.remedy: Use FORCE_SPMENU(tp_panel, SPI_TPUSER, 1) before calling the user interface built-in on the teach pendant. Use FORCE_SPMENU(crt_panel, SPI_TPUSER, 1) before calling the user interface built-in on the CRT.

TPIF-094.cause: A KAREL program called a user interface built-in which required the USER2 menu to be displayed on the teach pendant or CRT.
TPIF-094.remedy: Use FORCE_SPMENU(tp_panel, SPI_TPUSER2, 1) before calling the user interface built-in on the teach pendant. Use FORCE_SPMENU(crt_panel, SPI_TPUSER2, 1) before calling the user interface built-in on the CRT.

TPIF-095.remedy: Perform a controlled start (it is not necessary to re-set the new item)

TPIF-097.cause: The execution history of the executing program cannot be displayed
TPIF-097.remedy: Use this screen when the program is paused or aborted.

TPIF-098.cause: The program of $PWR_HOT, $PWR_SEMI or $PWR_NORMAL is not executed
TPIF-098.remedy: Refer to the error cause code. Use the Alarm Log screen.

TPIF-099.cause: The program specified in $PWR_HOT, $PWR_SEMI and $PWR_NORMAL is not executed, when the program is in editing.

TPIF-103.remedy: Press and hold down the DEADMAN, then select FWD execution

TPIF-104.cause: FWD execution is selected while, TP is disabled.

TPIF-105.cause: FWD execution is requested without selection of program.
