TPIF-106.cause: FWD execution is requested when program is running.
TPIF-106.remedy: Abort the running program before requesting FWD execution

TPIF-107.cause: When the Disabled FWD function has been selected, you cannot execute the program by TP
TPIF-107.remedy: Select the Disabled FWD in the function menu, then you can release from the Disable FWD

TPIF-108.cause: The Form Manager detected an error on the specified line with the specified item.
TPIF-108.remedy: Refer to the cause code on the ALARM log screen for the actual error.

TPIF-109.cause: The Form Manager detected an error when displaying a %v item.
TPIF-109.remedy: To specify the %v enumeration type in a form dictionary, use lower case v followed by the dictionary element which specifies the program name and variable name of the variable which contains the display values. For example: "Enum Type: " "-%6v(enum_fkey)" $-,enum_fkey "TPEX" &new_line "CHOICE_ARRAY" In the above example, CHOICE_ARRAY is a KAREL string array variable in program TPEX which contains the enumeration choices. The enumeration choices are displayed in a subwindow.

TPIF-110.cause: The screen you are attempting to use on the TP is currently displayed on CRT or the screen you are attempting to use on the CRT is currently displayed on TP
TPIF-110.remedy: Exit from the screen on the other device

TPIF-116.remedy: Check the spelling and format of the name.

TPIF-117.cause: The default device is not valid for backup
TPIF-117.remedy: Select a valid device and try again

TPIF-118.remedy: Perform a cold start: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot. If the error is not cleared, document the events that led to the error and call your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

TPIF-121.cause: Cannot COPY a file on a Memory device to the same Memory device.
TPIF-121.remedy: Use the MOVE key and try again

TPIF-128.cause: The reverse motion copy function does not support the following motion option instruction. 1. Application command 2. Skip, Quick Skip 3. Incremental 4. Continuous turn 5. Time before
TPIF-128.remedy: Check the above motion option instruction. And modify the copied statement correctly.

TPIF-129.cause: The group motion instruction is copyied. The reverse motion copy function does not supported group motion instruction.
TPIF-129.remedy: Check the group motion instruction. And modify the copied statement correctly.

TPIF-131.cause: This program has no application mask or the equipment mask does not agree with the TP Header Detail.
TPIF-131.remedy: Please set the application mask in the program detail screen. For irCalibration, make sure the selected program used with Program name has no mask.

TPIF-132.cause: Because the data for UNDO can not be saved, this operation can not recover by UNDO function
TPIF-132.remedy: Check the cause code. If the memory is full, please delete program or disable UNDO function.

TPIF-133.cause: Palletizing command and Compliance control command can not be recovered by UNDO function
TPIF-133.remedy: Check the cause code. If the memory is full, please delete program or disable UNDO function.

TPIF-134.remedy: This error is posted because CTRL Upgrade cannot be done while operating robot. Continue with CTRL Upgrade or ABORT

TPIF-135.remedy: This error is posted because CTRL Upgrade is underway. Allow the process to complete. with CTRL Upgrade or ABORT

TPIF-136.remedy: See FRD:REST_LOG.LS for a listing of files and status of attempt to load each. Retry failed files from file menu.

TPIF-137.cause: A user has logged into the teach pendant menuing system.
TPIF-137.remedy: This is for information only. No action is required.

TPIF-138.cause: A user has logged into the teach pendant diagnostic monitoring system.
TPIF-138.remedy: This is for information only. No action is required.

TPIF-139.cause: A user has logged off of the teach pendant menuing system.
TPIF-139.remedy: This is for information only. No action is required.

TPIF-140.cause: An attempt to log into the teach pendant menuing system from an external web browser has failed because the connection limit has been reached.
TPIF-140.remedy: The system variable $UI_CONFIG.$NUM_CONNECT controls the number of external connections allowed. The maximum number of connections is five INCLUDING the teach pendant. Reconnect the external connections in your system so that no more than five exist.

TPIF-141.cause: A user has failed to log into the teach pendant menuing system because not enough RAM memory is available to make the connection. The system might still be usable because the connection requires a predefined amount of available memory to start up.
TPIF-141.remedy: Add RAM memory to your system. You can also lower the memory limit required for login by changing the system variable $UI_CONFIG.$MEM_LIMIT to a lower value.

TPIF-142.cause: Too many user interface menus are active. The iPendant requires three menus which are always available for it to use. External browser onnections require one menu for each window in use. Therefore, a browser connection might use a maximum of three menus - one for each of the three windows in triple window mode.
TPIF-142.remedy: Eliminate some active browser windows or increase the number of menus in $UI_CONFIG.$NUM_MENUS. The total maximum number of menus is eight.

TPIF-143.cause: An external connection to the teach pendant menus has failed.
TPIF-143.remedy: Restart the controller, and try again.

TPIF-145.cause: A change to the iPendant window configuration has taken longer than expected. This can occur on startup or after you make a basic system configuration change. It might also occur in the presence of significant system activity. For example this error could occur if sysvars.sv is being backed up via the Network.
TPIF-145.remedy: When this error occurs, the display might not be what is expected. In this case, change back to Single mode, and try the operation again.

TPIF-146.cause: The firmware version on your iPendant is incompatible with the system software loaded on your controller. In some cases this will cause the iPendant to execute in legacy mode. In this mode it only provides the functionality that is available on an old style teach pendant.
TPIF-146.remedy: You will need to update the firmware to execute all available iPendant functionality. Refer to the Software Installation Manual for more information on how to load iPendant firmware.

TPIF-147.cause: The firmware version on your iPendant is too old to provide all functionality for your system software release. In some cases this will cause the iPendant to execute in legacy mode. In this mode it only provides the functionality that is available on an old style pendants.
TPIF-147.remedy: You will need to update firmware to have all functionality available. Refer to the Software Installation Manual for more information on how to load iPendant firmware.

TPIF-149.cause: You cannot change the focus of the iPendant in the middle of an entry operation. The entry operation must be completed first.
TPIF-149.remedy: Finish the current operation by pressing ENTER, or abort the operation by pressing PREV.

TPIF-150.message: Look mode only, use TP to edit
TPIF-150.cause: No editing is permitted on the device you are using to access a teach pendant program.
TPIF-150.remedy: Select a valid pane for an edit operation. You can only edit teach pendant programs on the iPendant in single or Status/Single mode, or in the left hand pane in Double and Triple modes.

TPIF-151.cause: A popup menu was requested for the pane that does not have focus. This error only occurs in Double, Triple, or Status/Single Display Modes. For instance, if you connect to the iPendant menus from Internet Explorer, bring up a web page that has the ComboBox Control, switch focus to another pane, and then use the mouse to click on the ComboBox Control, you will get this error because the pane does not have focus.
TPIF-151.remedy: Press the DISP key to change the focus to the correct pane before requesting the popup menu.

TPIF-152.cause: The keystroke that was just entered was not accepted by the system because the system does not allow edits. Typically remote operations will be read-only so no changes are allowed from this connection.
TPIF-152.remedy: Make the change from the iPendant instead. Your access to make changes will depend on your security setup. In some configurations there are security procedures on the iPendant.

TPIF-153.cause: You are trying to edit a field that is write protected. This happens if you are editing from an external connection, or if your password privileges do not allow you to change this field.
TPIF-153.remedy: Perform this operation from the teach pendant, or log in.

TPIF-154.cause: The iPendant firmware consists of Teach Pendant Core Firmware and Browser Plugins. The Browser Plugins, also referred to as application code, can be updated independently of the Teach Pendant Core Firmware. However, the major versions must match. For example, Teach Pendant Core Firmware V6.22xx cannot be used with Browser Plugins V6.31xx. When this happens, the iPendant will detect the problem, post this error, and reconnect in legacy mode. The STATUS Version ID menu can be used to show the versions for the Browser Plugins and the Teach Pendant Core Firmware.
TPIF-154.remedy: Update the whole firmware for the iPendant. Refer to the Software Installation Manual for details on updating the iPendant firmware.

TPIF-156.cause: The [TYPE] pullup menu cannot find any other menus to display. The current menu might be the only menu in this category.
TPIF-156.remedy: Press MENUS to select another menu catagory.

TPIF-157.cause: The controller attempted to display a menu that can only be displayed by the iPendant.
TPIF-157.remedy: Another menu will be displayed instead and you can ignore this warning. If you want to display the menu and you have a monochrome teach pendant, contact FANUC America Corporation for information on obtaining an iPendant.

TPIF-158.cause: You are attempting to connect a teach pendant to a robot that already has a teach pendant connected.
TPIF-158.remedy: To log in to a robot remotely with the iPendant, you must configure an iPendant ring. Press MENUS to reconnect to the local robot. If you are attempting to log in to a robot remotely with Internet Explorer, verify that the port number is not specified so that the Web Server's default port of 80 will be used.

TPIF-159.cause: You attempted to log in to a robot remotely with Internet Explorer and the iPendant Controls installed on your PC are not compatible with the robot's version.
TPIF-159.remedy: Install the version of the iPendant Controls that match the robot version. Refer to the application-specific Setup and Operations Manual, Advanced iPendant Functions Appendix, for information on installing the iPendant Controls.

TPIF-160.cause: You attempted to log in to a robot remotely with Internet Explorer and the iPendant Controls installed on your PC are not compatible with the robot's version.
TPIF-160.remedy: Install the version of the iPendant Controls that match the robot version. Refer to the application-specific Setup and Operations Manual, Advanced iPendant Functions Appendix, for information on installing the iPendant Controls.

TPIF-161.cause: The position ID cannot be changed by setting the system variable.
TPIF-161.remedy: Set the system variable $POS_EDIT.$LOCK_POSNUM to FALSE to change the position ID.

TPIF-162.cause: The Edit screen cannot enter the daughter program while the program is paused outside of the daughter program.
TPIF-162.remedy: Abort the program to enter the P-SPS.

TPIF-163.cause: The Edit screen cannot exit the daughter program and enter the parent program while the program is paused inside of the daughter program.
TPIF-163.remedy: Abort the program to exit the daughter program.

TPIF-164.message: This program has no motion group
TPIF-164.cause: This program has no motion group defined. The MOTION instruction cannot be taught.
TPIF-164.remedy: Change the MOTION instruction or set up the motion group in the program DETAIL screen.

TPIF-165.cause: An attempt is being made to resume the daughter program while the parent program is paused.
TPIF-165.remedy: Use BWD to return to the parent program, and then resume.

TPIF-166.cause: When the focus is in the right or bottom window of the Teach Pendant, you cannot execute the program.
TPIF-166.remedy: Change the focus to the primary window. This is the left hand window if split vertically or the top window if split horizontally. You can use DISPLAY menu EDIT<–>EDIT to swap the right hand program with the left hand program or the bottom program with the top program.

TPIF-167.cause: The program you selected is already being edited in the background in another window.
TPIF-167.remedy: Select End_edit in the other window's background edit session.

TPIF-168.cause: You are attempting to connect an iPendant to a remote robot that will not accept your IP address.
TPIF-168.remedy: If you are attempting to log in to a robot remotely with Internet Explorer, verify that the port number is not specified so that the Web Server's default port of 80 will be used. To connect "Jog in Auto Mode" or "Jogging iPendant", use SETUP Host Comm TCP/IP DETAIL screen to set the "PC JOG IP addr" field. It should be set to the IP address of the PC you are trying to connect to the robot. To connect a Shared iPendant to a remote robot, you must configure an iPendant ring. To recover from this operation, press MENU to reconnect to the local robot.

TPIF-169.cause: You are attempting to connect an iPendant to a remote robot that already has a teach pendant connected and enabled.
TPIF-169.remedy: Disable the remote robot's teach pendant. Press MENU to reconnect to the local robot.

TPIF-170.cause: This program cannot be started because the program name is not an allowed program name.
TPIF-170.remedy: Select the correct program, and start the program again.

TPIF-171.cause: The operation cannot be performed because the iPendant system is not initialized.
TPIF-171.remedy: Wait until the iPendant is initialized to do this operation. Typically, this is a force link call from a $PWR_NORMAL program.

TPIF-172.cause: The operation you selected is only available from the teach pendant.
TPIF-172.remedy: Perform this operation from the attached teach pendant.

TPIF-173.message: The pos. can't be handled part repr.
TPIF-173.cause: The position data is wrong. Refer to the cause code for details.
TPIF-173.remedy: Change the position data correctly, and press F5 DONE.

TPIF-174.message: New pos. can't be handled part repr.
TPIF-174.cause: The new position data is wrong. Refer to the cause code for details.

TPIF-175.cause: The shift key and the figure key were pushed at the same time when TP was enable.

TPIF-176.cause: The situation unexpected by the software occured. The index value indicates the reason.
TPIF-176.remedy: Turn off controller power and turn it on again. If the problem persists, document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC technical representative.

TPIF-201.cause: You cannot record motion line using the record button if the next line exists.
TPIF-201.remedy: Move the cursor to the end of the program, and press the record button again.

TPIF-203.message: Format does not match to unified specification
TPIF-203.cause: Record status(TUI default motion) is not written in TUI motion format.
TPIF-203.remedy: Select TUIDFMTN.to and teach J P[ ] R[101]% FINE DB 0.0mm P-SPS as line 1. P-SPS contains no line

TPIF-204.message: There is not specified source program number.
TPIF-204.cause: The input value is not correct.

TPIF-205.message: There is not specified source step number.
TPIF-205.cause: The input value is not correct.

TPIF-206.message: The number of steps of source program doesn't suffice.
TPIF-206.cause: The input value is not correct.

TPIF-207.message: There is not specified destination program number.
TPIF-207.cause: The input value is not correct.

TPIF-208.message: There is not specified destination step number.
TPIF-208.cause: The input value is not correct.

TPIF-209.message: Because destination program is executing, cannot copy.

TPIF-210.message: The number of steps to transfer is 0.
TPIF-210.cause: The number of steps to transfer is 0.

TPIF-211.cause: The copy range is not specified.

TPIF-212.message: The number of steps in the destination exceeds 9999.
TPIF-212.cause: The input value is not correct.

TPIF-213.cause: You cannot Check GO/Back from logic instruction.
TPIF-213.remedy: Move cursor to motion instruction and try again.

TPIF-214.cause: You cannot run or continue from a logic instruction.
TPIF-214.remedy: Move the cursor to a motion instruction and try again.

TPIF-215.cause: An error occurred trying to log in as an iPendant connection.
TPIF-215.remedy: If you are trying to log in from a PC, set Internet Explorer to prevent Windows from blocking communication with the robot controller: 1. The PC must have Microsoft Internet Explorer 5.5 or greater installed. 2. The PC must have the iPendant Controls installed. 3. If there is a firewall between the robot controller and the PC, the robot controller must be able to open a TCP connection to port 60005 on the PC. The PC must also be able to open a TCP connection to port 3002 and a UDP connection to port 60004 on the robot controller. This is in addition to allowing the basic HTTP request from the PC to the robot controller (TCP connection to port 80 on the robot). 4. If you are using a proxy server, make sure that your access to the robot does not go through the proxy server. 5. Verify that cookies are enabled. 6. Try connecting to the robot IP address instead of the robot hostname. 7. If Skype IE plugin is installed, please uninstall it. 8. Try disabling add-on software of Internet Explorer. 9. Please refer to Configuring Internet Explorer section in the Internet Setup & Operations manual for additional details.

VARS-057.remedy: When you load this file you must load all of the individual files created. During loading, the file names will have an index appended to them and you must find all of the files.

VARS-058.cause: You attempted to access a controller that is using an incompatible software version.
VARS-058.remedy: Update the target controller to the same version of software as the source controller.

VARS-059.cause: The program name syntax is invalid.
VARS-059.remedy: Make sure you use UNC compatible naming to access a network robot. For example: \robotnameprogram

VARS-060.cause: The program name syntax is bad.
VARS-060.remedy: Make sure you use UNC compatible naming conventions such as \robotnameprogram to acccess network robots.

VARS-061.cause: All available user types are already being used on this controller.
VARS-061.remedy: You cannot load any additional programs on this controller. You can delete programs and variables to free up types. Be sure that you are properly using the 'FROM' directive in your KAREL programs so that the same type is not defined in multiple programs.

VARS-062.remedy: Make sure you supply a name

VARS-063.cause: The CMOS memory for the named variable was corrupted. This named variable was reallocated as a result of the corruption.
VARS-063.remedy: The named variable will be set to Uninitialized in the process and might need to be set back to a valid initial value. In general, the only way to recover is an initial start. Refer to the application-specific Setup and Operations Manual for more information.

VARS-064.cause: A system variable was changed that requires a cycle power.
VARS-064.remedy: Turn on the Teach Pendant. Press FCTN hardkey and select CYCLE POWER. Or you can also turn off and on the power.

VARS-065.cause: The operation that you are attempting is not allowed while program is running.
VARS-065.remedy: Make the change after program is aborted.

VARS-107.cause: The alarm will occur when you attempt to do a GET_VAR or SET_VAR but the array indices do not match. For example, the variable type is a one dimensional array but you specify two dimensions in the variable name string.
VARS-107.remedy: Be sure that the array indices line up with the variable that you are attempting to access.

VARS-200.cause: System variable data has been corrupted.
VARS-200.remedy: Cycle Start the controller and try the operation again.

VARS-201.cause: System variable data has been corrupted.
VARS-201.remedy: Cycle Start the controller and try the operation again.

VARS-202.cause: An unexpected internal error has occurred
VARS-202.remedy: Document the events that led to the error and contact your FANUC America Corporation technical representative.

VARS-203.cause: Power cycle interrupted the variable file backup.
VARS-203.remedy: The system has attempted to recover. Cycle power to avoid problems.

VARS-204.cause: Power off processing did not complete.
VARS-204.remedy: If the problem persists, replace the hardware.

VARS-205.remedy: Move some variables to DRAM or mark variables NOTSCANNED.

VARS-206.cause: The variable must be reallocated at system initialization.

VARS-207.cause: A file that deferred loading until startup has succesfully loaded.

VARS-208.cause: A file that deferred loading until startup has failed to load. See the cause code.
VARS-208.remedy: Correct the problem in the file and try the operation again.

VARS-209.cause: A path node of a shadowed path has been modified but shadow is disabled.
VARS-209.remedy: Save the PRV file via the SAVE_DRAM built-in to enable shadowing.

VARS-210.message: %s only one shadow path per program
VARS-210.cause: A shadowed path already exists in this program.
VARS-210.remedy: Move the shadow path to its own program.

VARS-211.message: %s Shadow paths exclude other shadow variables
VARS-211.cause: A shadowed path and some other shadow variable cannot exist in the same program.
VARS-211.remedy: Move the shadow path to its own program name.

VARS-212.cause: The program is protected and cannot be cleared or reloaded.
VARS-212.remedy: Unprotect the program from the application.

VARS-214.message: Array element size is too large
VARS-214.cause: The array element size is larger than 32,565
VARS-214.remedy: Defined an variable with smaller array size.

VARS-215.cause: The variable file contains an expanded number of registers.
VARS-215.remedy: Load the expanded registers option R830.

VARS-216.cause: The source and destination represenation do not match.

VARS-218.message: Group number %d is not in valid range
VARS-218.cause: The group number of the variable is not in valid range.
VARS-218.remedy: Define a variable with a group number in a valid range.

WEAV-003.remedy: Remove unneeded loaded variables and programs

WEAV-004.cause: Weave system variables not loaded or initialized

WEAV-006.remedy: Change weave schedule to be in limits

WEAV-008.remedy: Change amplitude to be within limits

WEAV-009.remedy: Change dwell to be within limits

WEAV-012.cause: Stop dwell is specified but the program has multiple groups. Stop dwell is not supported for multiple groups. Moving dwell is executed.

WEAV-013.cause: Weaving vector can not be calcurated because the direction of the weaving vector is not correct.
WEAV-013.remedy: Change the path direction or setting of UTOOL to plan the weaving vector correctly.

WEAV-014.cause: Wrist axes reaches to its limit
WEAV-014.remedy: Change wrist configuration to allow wrist axes away from its limit.

WEAV-015.cause: Joint 5 is too close to zero

WEAV-017.cause: The angles of Weaving direction away from its best direction is larger than allowed tol_ang.
WEAV-017.remedy: Change the torch angle or increase the value of tol_ang.

WEAV-018.cause: The current utool has null value

WEAV-020.cause: The component of all unit vectors is 0.
WEAV-020.remedy: Set the value of component correctly.

WEAV-021.remedy: Change elevation to be within limits

WEAV-022.remedy: Change azimuth to be within limits

WEAV-023.remedy: Change center rise to be within limits

WEAV-024.remedy: Change radius to be within limits

WNDW-001.cause: Format of screen name in DEF_SCREEN, ACT_SCREEN, or ATT_WINDOW_S call is invalid.
WNDW-001.remedy: Screen names must be 1-4 alpla- characters Supply a valid screen name

WNDW-002.cause: Format of window name in ATT_WINDOW_D, ATT_WINDOW_S, or DET_WINDOW call or an OPEN statement is invalid.
WNDW-002.remedy: Window names must be 1-4 alpla- characters Supply a valid window name

WNDW-003.cause: Invalid display device name in DEF_SCREEN or ATT_WINDOW_D call
WNDW-003.remedy: Use TP for teach pendand screen or CRT for KCL screen

WNDW-004.cause: Invalid format of display device name in DEF_SCREEN or ATT_WINDOW_D call
WNDW-004.remedy: Device names must be 1-4 alpla- characters Supply a valid device name

WNDW-005.remedy: n_rows value must be 1 to 50 Correct the value

WNDW-006.remedy: n_cols value must be 1 to 132 Correct the value

WNDW-007.cause: Invalid value of row parameter in ATT_WINDOW_S, AT_WINDOW_D, or SET_CURSOR call
WNDW-007.remedy: For ATWINDOW_S or AT_WINDOW_D calls, row must be in the range 1-(display_device_size-window_size+1) Correct the row parameter value For SET_CURSOR calls, the value must be in the range 1-50

WNDW-008.cause: Invalid value of col parameter in ATT_WINDOW_S, AT_WINDOW_D, or SET_CURSOR call
WNDW-008.remedy: For ATWINDOW_S or AT_WINDOW_D calls, col must be in the range 1-(display_device_size-window_size+1) Correct the col parameter value For SET_CURSOR calls, the value must be in the range 1-132

WNDW-011.cause: Unknown display device name in DEF_SCREEN or ATT_WINDOW_D call
WNDW-011.remedy: Use TP for teach pendand screen or CRT for KCL screen

WNDW-012.cause: Keyboard device specified in a PUSH_KEY_RD or POP_KEY_RD call or OPEN statement is invalid
WNDW-012.remedy: Use 'TP' for teach pendant keys or 'CRT' for KCL keyboard

WNDW-013.cause: Screen name specified in DEF_SCREEN call is already defined
WNDW-013.remedy: If the screen is a system-defined, it cannot be redefined. If the existing screen definition is not being changed, this may not be a problem. Otherwise, it may be necessary to cold-start the controller to delete the existing definition: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot.

WNDW-014.cause: Window name specified in DEF_WINDOW call is already defined
WNDW-014.remedy: If the window is a system-defined window, it cannot be redefined. If the window is a system-defined, it cannot be redefined. If the existing window definition is not being changed, this may not be a problem. Otherwise, it may be necessary to cold-start the controller to delete the existing definition: 1. Turn off the robot. 2. On the teach pendant, press and hold the SHIFT and RESET keys. 3. While still pressing the SHIFT and RESET keys, turn on the robot.

WNDW-015.cause: The screen name specified in a ATT_WINDOW_S, DET_WINDOW, or ACT_WINDOW call is not defined
WNDW-015.remedy: Use the name of a defined screen

WNDW-016.cause: The window name specified in a ATT_WINDOW_S, ATT_WINDOW_D, or DET_WINDOW call or an OPEN statement is not defined
WNDW-016.remedy: Use the name of a defined window

WNDW-017.cause: The window name specified in a ATT_WINDOW_S, ATT_WINDOW_D is ready attached to the specified screen
WNDW-017.remedy: If the present attach is acceptable, this may not be a problem. Otherwise it will be necessary to call DET_WINDOW

WNDW-018.cause: The file name in an OPEN statement begins WD: or KB: but is not a valid format.
WNDW-018.remedy: The following forms are valid: WD:wnam KB:knam WD:wnam/knam KB:knam/wnam where wnam and knam are 1-4 alpha-numberic characters Correct the format of the file name

WNDW-019.cause: A write was issued to a file opened to a keyboard (KB:knam), but not a window
WNDW-019.remedy: Either change the OPEN to specify a window or do not WRITE to the file

WNDW-020.cause: The buffer_size parameter in a INI_DYN_DISI INI_DYN_DISR, INI_DYN_DISS or READ_KB call is invalid
WNDW-020.remedy: Specify a value in the range 10-128 for INI_DYN_DISx calls; for READ_KB calls, specify a range of 1-128, unless the accept mask is zero, when a buffer_size value of zero is permitted.

WNDW-021.cause: The time_out value in a READ_KB call is Invalid
WNDW-021.remedy: The value must be less than 65535000. Use a valid value

WNDW-022.message: Zero term char mask in read
WNDW-022.cause: The terminate character mask in a keyboard read is zero.
WNDW-022.remedy: Use a non-zero value for the terminate character mask

WNDW-023.cause: The init_data value is longer than the buffer size parameter
WNDW-023.remedy: Either increase the value of buffer_size or specify a shorter string for init_value

WNDW-024.message: Attempt to read with no kb
WNDW-024.cause: A READ_KB call or READ statement was executed on a file that was OPENed to a window but not a keyboard
WNDW-024.remedy: Either modify the OPEN FILE statement to specify a keyboard or do not use the file in a READ_KB call or READ statement

WNDW-025.message: Echo window for read not act
WNDW-025.cause: A READ_KB call was executed where the specified file is opened to a window that is not attached to the active screen and the terminate mask included the no_window bit
WNDW-025.remedy: This may be a normal result if the user intended READ_KB requests to fail if the required window is not displayed. Otherwise, either modify the terminate mask or use ATT_WINDOW_D or ATT_WINDOW_S to attach the required window.

WNDW-026.cause: A READ_KB call was executed where the the keyboard for the specified file currently has another READ_KB call or READ statement that accepts some of the same classes of keys and the terminate mask included the kbd_busy bit
WNDW-026.remedy: This may be a normal result if the user intended READ_KB requests to fail if the Keyboard is in use. Otherwise, modify the terminate mask, modify the accept mask of this or the conlicting read, or use a PUSH_KEY_RD call to suspend conficting reads

WNDW-027.cause: The maximum depth of key read PUSH operations has been exceeded.
WNDW-027.remedy: Check for situations in which a PUSH_KEY may be executed and no POP_KEY is exected.

WNDW-028.cause: This indicates that the pop_index specified in a POP_KEY_RD call is not the expected value, indicating that call are being made out of order.
WNDW-028.remedy: Check the logic in use of PUSH_KEY_RD and POP_KEY_RD to ensure that the pop_index values are being suplied in the correct order. If more than one task is issuing PUSH_KEY_RD and POP_KEY_RD calls, extra care is required

WNDW-030.cause: The interval parameter in a INI_DYN_DISI, INI_DYN_DISR, or INI_DYN_DISS call is invalid
WNDW-030.remedy: This must be in the range 1-32767 (ms)

WNDW-032.message: No match on var disp cncl
WNDW-032.cause: There is no currently active dynamic display for variable and window specified in a CNC_DYN_DISI, CNC_DYN_DISR, or CNC_DYN_DISS call.
WNDW-032.remedy: Check the variable and window names. Also check logic to see that dynamic display had been started and not already cancelled.

WNDW-033.cause: The field_width parameter in a call to one of the INI_DYN_DIS builtin routines is invalid.
WNDW-033.remedy: Value must be in the range of 0-255

WNDW-065.cause: The window specified in a DET_WINDOW call is not attached to the specified screen.
WNDW-065.remedy: This is only a warning. It can be ignored or avoided by not detaching windows that are not attached. 3.22 X

XMLF-001.cause: The XML tag string is too long.
XMLF-001.remedy: The XML tag limit is a maximum of 32 characters.

XMLF-002.cause: The attribute data is too long.
XMLF-002.remedy: Limit the length of the attribute data to 64 characters. If a very long attribute string is required use it as the body of the XML for example: <MYTAG> This is a string longer than 64 characters. In fact it could be many pages of text </MYTAG>. There is no limit to the length of the data in this case. A KAREL program can retrieve the data 127 characters at a time from the XML data as the string. Refer to the KAREL Reference manual examples for more information.

XMLF-003.cause: In general the “/” character cannot be used in a tag name. This is a special character.
XMLF-003.remedy: Do not use “/” in tag (or attribute) names. For example, <TAG> </TAG> is valid. However, <TA/G> </TA/G> is not.

XMLF-004.cause: Tag names cannot contain special characters such as &, <, >, /, “, or “.
XMLF-004.remedy: Do not use special characters in tag names.

XMLF-005.cause: There is no value string for an attribute. This error occurs if the attribute is not like the following example: name = “value”.
XMLF-005.remedy: Make sure all attributes are of the form name = “value”.

XMLF-006.message: End tag with no matching start
XMLF-006.cause: An end tag was found with no matching start tag.
XMLF-006.remedy: Start tags and end tags must always balance. That is, for every start tag there must be an end tag <\TAG> or <TAG name=”value”\>.

XMLF-007.cause: An attribute contains an invalid character. Attributes cannot contain the characters <, >, /, ".
XMLF-007.remedy: Change the attribute. For example, <TAG ATT=“val”> is valid. However, <TAG ATT=“val/”> is not.

XMLF-008.cause: The specified file does not exist.
XMLF-008.remedy: Make sure the file you are trying to access exists on the device you are specifying.

XMLF-009.cause: The nesting of tags is limited to 32 levels deep. This error indicates that you have more than 32 tags within tags.
XMLF-009.remedy: Reformulate your XML file to reduce the complexity. Make sure that the file can be edited by a standard PC XML editor.

XMLF-010.cause: The XML source has a badly formed comment.
XMLF-010.remedy: Follow the rules for XML comment delimiters. This means that the comment must begin with <!– – and end with – –>.

XMLF-011.cause: The & is used to denote special characters. Only &, <, >, and " are supported as special characters.
XMLF-011.remedy: If the character is not supported as a special character, you can use the character directly.

XMLF-012.cause: This is returned by the remove tag builtin xml_remtag in the case that the tag was not previously registered.
XMLF-012.remedy: Register the tags before you remove them.

XMLF-013.cause: The XML file ended before the starting tag was closed.
XMLF-013.remedy: Make sure that the last tag in the file closes the first tag in the file.

XMLF-014.cause: The KAREL builtin xml_scan returned because it had scanned as many lines as possible in the time slot.
XMLF-014.remedy: Recall the builtin xml_scan to scan more lines.

XMLF-015.cause: This is returned by the KAREL builtin xml_scan when a registered tag has been found.
XMLF-015.remedy: This indicates that the builtin should process the returned tag.

XMLF-016.cause: The iPendant detected a problem with an XML tag. Most likely an unknown or misspelled tag was used.
XMLF-016.remedy: Correct the XML content, and retry the operation.

XMLF-017.cause: The iPendant detected a problem with an ATTRIBUTE / VALUE pair in the XML content.
XMLF-017.remedy: Correct the XML content, and retry the operation.

XMLF-018.cause: The iPendant detected a syntax error in the XML content.
XMLF-018.remedy: Correct the XML content, and retry the operation.

XMLF-019.cause: There are too many ATTRIBUTE/VALUE pairs with the XML tag.
XMLF-019.remedy: Reduce the number of ATTRIBUTE/VALUE pairs in the XML content and retry the operation.
